file://api-specs/split/Frequently Asked.content: Related Information Manage Entities Manage Dock Appointments App Are you a shipper with a question about your Manage Dock Appointments app? If so, take a look at these FAQs What are the constraints when I reschedule an appointment? You cannot change the activity or duration of an appointment. Also, you cannot reschedule an appointment to any non-business hours. Why can't I find a docking location on the Docking Locations table? To make a docking location visible on the table, you must first define the settings for the docking location and then activate the settings in the Docking Location Settings app. Related Information Manage Dock Appointments Manage Gate Operations App Are you a shipper with a question about your Manage Gate Operations app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. What can I do with the Manage Gate Operations app? As a gate operations manager, you can use this app to view the details of the vehicles that are ready to check-in and checkout of the yard. You can also perform the check-in and checkout process using this app. Who can use this app? Though this app is available for all shipper roles, those shippers who perform the role of gate operations manager can use this app to manage the gate operations. How is the planned check-in date and time calculated? The system calculates the planned check-in date and time based on the appointment details and the Arrival Lead Time that you specify in the gate settings in the Manage Entities app. What is actual check-in date and time? When you start the check-in process for a vehicle, the system updates the actual check-in date and time. What is actual checkout date and time? When you start the checkout process for a vehicle, the system updates the actual checkout date and time. Manage Locations App 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Are you a shipper with a question about your Manage Locations app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Can I create a docking location in the Manage Locations app? No, settings for docking locations are defined in the Docking Location Settings app. Can I have two location master data records with the same Location ID and different object types? No, the Location ID field must be unique. How do I set Source System ID/External ID if I am creating a location that is not copied from any external system? If you are creating a location from scratch, set Source System to LBN, and set External ID to the value of Location ID. Related Information Manage Locations Track Freight Movement App Are you a shipper with a question about your Track Freight Movement app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Note that this app has been deprecated and will be sunset shortly. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. What prerequisite settings are required for using the Track Freight Movement app? The required prerequisite settings are described in the Administration Guide for Shippers. In the guide, see Freight Orders for Tracking in the Configuring Additional Services section. What data can be tracked by the Track Freight Movement app? The Track Freight Movement app tracks and displays the following data for you: The data manually reported by your carrier in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. The manually reported data includes actual events (departure, arrival, proof of pick-up, proof of delivery, and delay) and the attached documents (if any) in actual events. The manually reported data tracked by the app is also synchronized to your SAP TM or TM on S/4HANA system. Automated visibility data from a supported visibility provider, if your carrier provides it. The visibility data includes geographic location data and actual events (departure, arrival, delay, and delay dismissed). In the current delivery, the app only tracks visibility data for events with the DEPARTURE, ARRIV_DEST, POPU, POD, and DELAYED event codes. Only the tracking related data of a freight order is passed into the app, for example, freight order ID, stop locations, and events. The visibility data tracked by the app is also synchronized to your SAP TM or S/4HANA system, and the Freight Orders for Reporting app. In your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system, you can view both of the above data, but the geographic location data is only displayed in the Track Freight Movement app. What is the expected business or technical time window for a planned event? 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- It is a time period between the earliest and latest expected business or technical date and time. By default, the earliest time is 10 minutes before the planned event time and the latest is 10 minutes after the planned event time. If you want to change the default, contact your system administrator to maintain SAP BAdI /SCMTMS/TOR_SE_TRCKPR_OUT. Why can't I see the planned shipping route on the map? The possible causes are: There are no events planned or reported at some stops. The location information for some stops is not specified in the location master data. The freight order was not executed as planned. When we say a freight document was not executed as planned, what does it mean? It means the latest actual event time reported at a stop is later than the earliest actual event time reported at its succeeding stop. What is the impact when a freight document was not executed as planned? The execution flow graphic only shows the events happened or planned at the stops, but there's no lines to connect the stops. All other events are listed in a table beneath the graphic. The map view only shows the actual shipping route, as well as all the events happened or planned in the entire process. I can't track a freight document that I have tracked before. Why? There are two possibilities, as shown below: The freight document was deleted because it reached its retention period. Based on data protection and privacy regulations, there is a retention period for the tracked process of a freight document. You can configure the retention period in the Blocking Store app. The freight document was canceled in your TM system. A cancellation request is sent from the TM system if any of the following conditions is met for a freight document: The value of TOR Lifecycle Status is not In Process or Completed. The value of TOR Execution Status is not Ready for Transportation Execution, In Execution, or Executed. The previously maintained carrier information has been removed. Why can't I find delay dismissed events in the Freight Orders for Reporting app, SAP TM, or SAP S/4HANA system? This is not supported in the current delivery. If an actual event is reported by both the Freight Orders for Reporting app and the visibility provider, which one takes precedence? Currently there is a software limitation on this: In the Track Freight Movement app, the reporting with the latest event time takes precedence. In the Freight Orders for Reporting app, the manually reported data takes precedence over the visibility data synced from the Track Freight Movement app. 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- In the SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system, the latest arrived data takes precedence. Thus, in some cases, the data displayed in the Track Freight Movement app may be inconsistent with the data shown in the Freight Orders for Reporting app, SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system. Related Information Track Freight Movement Manage Freight Execution App (Shipper) Are you a shipper with a question about your Manage Freight Execution app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. What prerequisite settings are required for using the Manage Freight Execution app? The required prerequisite settings are described in the Administration Guide for Shippers. In the guide, see Manage Freight Execution in the Configuring Additional Services section. What data can be tracked by the Manage Freight Execution app? The Manage Freight Execution app tracks and displays the following data for you: The data manually reported by your carrier in the Manage Freight Execution app. The manually reported data tracked by the app is also synchronized to your SAP TM or TM on S/4HANA system. The data reported by your B2B (business to business) carrier using the Provider API for Order Events (FC). The data reported by your visibility provider using the Provider API for Order Events (FC). Note that this option is only for the shippers who are using the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace option. The data manually reported by the shipper in the Manage Freight Execution app. The reported data includes actual planned and unplanned events. For more information on the event types, see Code Lists. You can also view the attached documents (if any) in actual events. You can also see the details of the business partner who reported the event in the Reported By field. What is the expected business or technical time window for a planned event? It is a time period between the earliest and latest expected business or technical date and time. By default, the earliest time is 10 minutes before the planned event time and the latest is 10 minutes after the planned event time. If you want to change the default, contact your system administrator to maintain SAP BAdI /SCMTMS/TOR_SE_TRCKPR_OUT. I can't track a freight document that I have tracked before. Why? There are two possibilities, as shown below: The freight document was deleted because it reached its retention period. Based on data protection and privacy regulations, there is a retention period for the tracked process of a freight document. You can configure the retention period in the Blocking Store app. The freight document was canceled in your TM system. A cancellation request is sent from the TM system if any of the following conditions is met for a freight document: 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- The value of TOR Lifecycle Status is not In Process or Completed. The value of TOR Execution Status is not Ready for Transportation Execution, In Execution, or Executed. The previously maintained carrier information has been removed. If an actual event is reported by the shipper, carrier and the visibility provider, where can I see all the events? If an actual event is reported by the shipper, carrier and the visibility provider, then you can view all these events in the Events History pane. You can view the details of which business partner reported the event in the Business Partner field. Can I update my freight document once the reporting has started? Yes, you can update the freight document once the reporting has started. However, you cannot modify the planned events which have already been reported. Note that the document has to be updated with the option of same or higher precedence. For more information, seeAdministration Guide for Shippers. In the guide, see Manage Freight Execution in the Configuring Additional Services section. Related Information Manage Freight Execution Discover Business Partners App Do you have questions about your Discover Business Partners app? If so, take a look at these FAQs Why companies that match my search conditions are not returned in the Matched Results table? To find out the reason, check the following: Find out which type of SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant you are currently in. Business partners in SAP Business Network for Logistics are categorized in three types: Productive type: tenants created for productive use to conduct real business collaboration Test type: tenants created for test purpose System Integration (SI) type: tenants created by SAP system integration partners To find out which type of business partner tenant you are currently in, open the Manage Business Profile app and take a look at the ID on your company profile page. ID Tenant Type Starting with the prefix 'BNO'. No suffixes. Example: BNO-100000000001111 Productive Starting with the prefix 'BNO'. Ending with the suffix 'T'. Example: BNO-100000000001111-T Test 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- ID Tenant Type Starting with the prefix 'BNO'. Ending with the suffix 'D'. Example: BNO-100000000001111-D System Integration (SI) Make sure the potential business partners that you want to discover and connect already joined SAP Business Network for Logistics, and these companies must set the Make my business profile visible to potential business partners field to Yes in their Manage Invitations app. With the above conditions being met, the Discover Business Partners app restricts the scope of the business partners that you can find based on your own business partner type, as shown below: Your own business partner type Potential business partner type you can discover Productive Test System Integration Productive Yes No No Test No Yes Yes System Integration No Yes Yes Related Information Discover Business Partners Data Protection and Privacy Are you a shipper or a carrier with a question about data protection and privacy in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Why is data protection and privacy important? Data protection and privacy of individual user data is a legal requirement, and every application that collects and distributes user data must be in accordance with statutory data protection laws. How does SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration ensure compliance with the data protection and privacy policies? The solution does the following to ensure compliance with the data protection and privacy policies: Deletes the user data from a business document on the expiry of the applicable retention periods Provides a retrieval function that enables users (data subjects) to find out what personal data is stored about them Logs changes to personal data and provides read access to sensitive personal data Who can retrieve personal data of a user and how? 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The data privacy officer can find the transactions that hold the personal information of the user using the Personal Data Management application. Related Information Data Protection and Privacy Retention Management App Are you a shipper or a carrier with a question about your Retention Management app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. What is the residence period and when does it start? It is the period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set. During the residence period, data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Once the business document reaches the end of business, it enters the residence period. What is the blocking period and when does it start? The blocking period is the period between the end of the residence period and the deletion of the data. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the blocking period, the data is deleted. What is the retention period? The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. It is the period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. What is the end of purpose? The end of purpose for a business document is the point in time at which the primary processing purpose ends, such as a contract being fulfilled. For example, in the Freight Requests for Quotation app, a business partner is an item of master data. The end of purpose of this master data is the point in time at which the data is no longer relevant for business activities. How do I maintain the residence and blocking periods? And can I maintain different residence and blocking periods for each application? You can maintain the residence and blocking periods using the Retention Management app. You can specify the residence and blocking periods in months for an application type. If you do not specify a residence or a blocking period, the system sets it to 12 months by default. Yes, you can maintain different residence and blocking periods for each application. Related Information Retention Management 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Blocking Store App Are you a shipper or a carrier with a question about your Blocking Store app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. How can I view the personal data during the blocking period? You can use the Blocking Store app to view the personal data during the blocking period. Note that you can access the Blocking Store app only if you have the required authorization. What happens to the document once it reaches the end of the blocking period? Once the blocking period is over, all the personal data of the document is deleted permanently. Related Information Blocking Store Manage Business Profile App Are you a shipper or carrier with a question about your Manage Business Profile app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. How do I edit or update the company profile? When you choose the Manage Business Profile tile on SAP Fiori Launchpad, the system opens the company profile page. You can edit or update the profile information by choosing the Edit icon in each section. How do I add multiple company addresses? Follow the instructions on Creating Additional Addresses. Why is it mandatory to maintain a default address? The default address is the address that will be displayed to other business partners in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. The default address is also the address that will be displayed when you launch the Manage Business Profile app. In general, the corporate address is chosen as the default address. My corporate address has changed. What should I do? After you launch the Manage Business Profile app, choose the Edit icon in the first section on your company profile and then enter your new address on the Address tab. Can I add a contact person for each of my addresses? No, you cannot add a contact person for each address. Is it mandatory to maintain sensitive data such as gross revenue in the profile? No, most information that you specify on the company profile page is optional. However, if you specify your business details, the business partner can use this information to analyze your business prospects before connecting with you. What are alternate identifiers and why should I specify them? 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Alternate identifiers are standard industry codes or compliance details, for example the DUNS Number. If you maintain this information, the business partner can verify your credibility and eligibility before connecting with you. Related Information Manage Business Profile Manage Integration Logs App Are you a shipper or a carrier with a question about your Manage Integration Logs app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. One of the messages had a Failed status. Can I reprocess this message? Yes, after you solve the configuration or syntax issues pertaining to that business document, you can choose to reprocess this message. Only messages where the value in the Reprocessable column is set to Yes can be reprocessed. After I reprocessed a message, I am not able to view the log. Why? When you reprocess a message with the status Failed or Escalated, the system updates the status to Reprocessing. After the reprocessing has run, this message is updated to a final status of Failed, Escalated, or Completed. Where can I find the Manage Integration Logs - Integration Message Flow View version 1.0 app? The Manage Integration Logs - Integration Message Flow View (version 1.0) app has been sunset. You must switch to the new Manage Integration Logs (version 2.0) app. To start using the new app (as a shipper, solution owner or network owner), ask your system administrator to add the ManageIntegrationLogsDisplayTemplate and ManageIntegrationLogsTemplate roles to your role collection. If you are a carrier, data contributor or network participant, your role settings are managed by SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app shall be visible in your SAP Fiori launchpad. For any queries or concerns, please report an incident in SAP for Me categorized by component SBN-LBN-INT. Can I reprocess my logs after 30 days? No. The reprocessing of a message is limited to 29 days. After 30 days, you won’t be able to reprocess the message or download the payload. In the app, these messages are highlighted in grey. What is the difference between status and overall status? In the Documents tab, integration logs are aggregated based on the LBN IDs of the parties involved, the document ID, and the scenario. The overall status of an entry in the Documents tab is derived from the latest status of an individual log that's part of the aggregation. The Documents tab is only displayed for shippers, solution owners, and network owners. How can I configure email notifications for failed or escalated messages? You must schedule email notifications for the Integration Error V2 scenario as outlined in Manage Notification Settings (Shipper) and Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- FAQs on Security Are you a shipper or a carrier with a question on security? If so, take a look at these FAQs. How can I monitor the messages that are coming into my system? Shippers and carriers can monitor all incoming and outgoing messages in their SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant using the Manage Integration Logs app. They can also subscribe to notifications to receive alerts in case of message failures. How frequently are the accounts monitored in real-time? Are there any periodic checks? Real-user logins Accounts are monitored in real-time through alert-based mechanisms. API usage Shippers and carriers can define the monitoring frequency as per their needs. How does the system handle unusual login behavior and security threats? SAP Identity Authentication Service triggers alerts at the identity and access layer when it detects unusual behavior, such as excessive requests, failed login attempts, or penetration testing activities. When an alert is generated, the internal operations team is notified and takes corrective actions, such as blocking user access, specific IP addresses, and so on. How does the system detect and flag a compromised carrier account? For real-user logins The SAP Identity Authentication Service triggers alerts for unusual login behavior, prompting further investigation. For API users Shippers and carriers can monitor all incoming and outgoing messages in their SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant using the Manage Integration Logs app and subscribe to alerts for error notifications. What steps are taken once a compromise is identified? If a compromise is detected, the system can perform one of the following actions: For unusual real-user login attempts, the user or IP address may be blocked. For suspicious API usage, shippers and carriers can raise a ticket in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Affected technical user credentials can be disabled, and new credentials issued. To avoid any spurious messages from reaching the shipper, the connection between the shipper and carrier can be temporarily disabled. Are there automated or manual processes to identify suspicious behaviour? A combination of both automated and manual processes are available. For real-user logins, an alert-based monitoring by the SAP Identity Authentication Service team is available. For unusual API usage, manual monitoring options are available to the shippers and carrier. file://api-specs/split/Frequently Asked.content: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) and IP whitelisting These are available but disabled by default. These can be enabled at the tenant-level on request. Encryption All transactional data is encrypted both at rest and in transit. Credential security Credentials are encrypted or hashed according to industry best practices. If a data breach occurs due to a leaked carrier account, who is responsible for handling the situation? In case of a data breach, or any other security incident in the carrier tenants, the carriers are the data owners. They will be responsible for handling these situations, with the necessary support from SAP Business Network for Logistics. What support does SAP provide in case of a security breach? Carriers can raise a support ticket in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Depending on the nature of the breach, the following actions can be taken: Disabling compromised API credentials and issue new ones. Blocking unauthorized user access. Restoring tenant access if valid users lose access due to security issues. Disabling the connection between the shipper and carrier temporarily to isolate the shipper system from the affected system. 5/12/26, 6:42 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction This document describes the APIs provided by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace that are useable by applications. There are two basic types of API: Public cross-tenant APIs These are published by SAP in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub with documentation. They are mostly used by data contributors. In this guide, you can also find detailed instruction on how to use them. Generated tenant-local interfaces These are tenant-specific interfaces used by solution owners. They are also APIs, but differ based on the tenant. Rate Limiting This section describes the rate limit of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace APIs. Rate limiting restricts the number of incoming requests from callers to GTT APIs and within a specific time frame. It’s a protective measure that: prevents the GTT service from crashing due to the excessive load of requests ensures the availability and optimal performance of the GTT service for every client. We have defined the rate limits of following APIs according to tenant type: API Type of Tenant Limit IDOC interface: GTT_V2_EM_IDOC_Ingestion SOAP Message Interface: TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Write Service API: GTT_V2_HTTP_EVENT_INGESTION Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 150 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Read Service API: GTT_V2_OData_Query Production The rate limit per tenant is 200 per minute.  Recommendation Before you start working through this document, ensure that you have the most recent version of this document available from the SAP Help Portal at: help.sap.com/gtt 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- API Type of Tenant Limit Test The rate limit per tenant is 60 requests per minute. When the rate limit is exceeded, you will receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response status code, and your requests are rejected. You can try executing requests again several minutes later. API Payload Limits To prevent APIs from being overloaded by the payload size, we have introduced API payload limits to regulate the API usage per message. The following tables list the size limit of different components in API payload: Public Tracking APIs API Request Body Response Body Provider API for Order Events Less than 40MB N/A Consumer API for Order Tracking Less than 40MB N/A Tenant-local Interfaces API Request Body without Attachment Attachment Response Body IDOC Service Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Read Service API No limit N/A The response body of read service API supports: 256 records at maximum for main entity in a query; 5000 records at maximum for each expanded entity of a single main entity; 20000 records at maximum for sum of each expanded entity for all main entity. Write Service API Less than 2MB Less than 10MB N/A SOAP Message Interface Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Here are examples of requests and responses for you to better understand the Read Service API size limit:  Note This will take effective as of December 13, 2025. There is no limit on API calls to fulfillment tracking apps, such as the "Track Shipments" app.  Example 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Public Cross-Tenant Tracking APIs This chapter describes how solution owners and data contributors exchange messages via the tracking APIs (or tracking interfaces) offered by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides two types of tracking APIs: Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT): enables solution owners to send a tracking request for an order to data contributors. Provider API for Order Events (GTT): enables data contributors (such as network partners or carriers) to post events for a tracked order. You can check out the above APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub . This chapter specifically describes the following two cases: how a solution owner sends a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT), and how a data contributor sends back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Sending Tracking Requests via Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) As a solution owner, you can send a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Request Result Odata Response odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 1 shipment was found and 5100 process events found on this shipment odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 10 shipments were found and 2100 process events were found on each shipment. odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs,stops,trackingUnitTPs 1 shipment was found with 5000 process events, 5000 planned events, 5000 freightUnitTPs, 5000 stops, and 5000 trackingUnitTPs. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have sent the invitation to the data contributor using the Invite Business Partners app. After the data contributor accepts the invitation using the Manage Invitations app, you two will be connected as business partners. 3. You have established a B2B connection to the external systems of the data contributor in the Configure Partner Connections app. 4. But if you want to integrate with your visibility provider in a user model or map user-defined fields in the standard model, do the following: Procedure 1. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Sending Events via Provider API for Order Events (GTT) As a data contributor, you can send back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Prerequisites and Configuration Monitoring Integration Prerequisites and Configuration Prerequisites To perform the tasks described in this chapter, you, as a data contributor, must have the following prerequisites: 1. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have accepted the invitation from the solution owner using the Manage Invitations app. For more, see the application help of Manage Invitations. Configuration You need to use the System Connections app to complete the API implementations. For details, see the Connectivity section of Administration Guide for Logistics Providers. Related Information Provider API for Order Events (GTT) Monitoring Integration On the SAP Fiori launchpad, pen the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting  within the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app. Generated Tenant-local Interfaces This chapter describes how to use the generated tenant-local interfaces in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. These APIs are provided for integration between the GTT system and other systems, which allows solution owners to access GTT services and perform CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations on the GTT system via API requests. API Authentication You can use the following to authenticate your API calls to GTT service interfaces: HTTP Basic Authentication: You must create a technical user and maintain it in the System Connections app. For more, see Maintain Technical User in the System Connections App. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use these APIs, you must fulfill the following prerequisites: 1. Configure API authentication method. For more, see API Authentication. 2. Get the following information required in the API request URI: Server Address: You must provide the server address as the host in the request URI: For basic authentication, server address is the URL of your GTT Fiori Launchpad. It varies from hosted data centers. Do the following to get the server address: a. Go to your subaccount that has subscribed Global Track and Trace b. Click Services Instances and Subscriptions Global Track and Trace Go to Application c. After sign-in, you will see the URL. Model Information: Prepare the following model information needed in the resource path of the request URI: Model Namespace: It’s in the format of “com.<tenant name>.gtt.app.<model name>”. You can find the entire model namespace on the top of your target Model Details page. Write Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>WriteService”. Read Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>Service”. Model Name: You can find it on the target model card. After you finish the above tasks, you are ready to send API requests. In the sections followed, you can find examples of API request and response pair specific to different interface services. Messages with the same hint will be sent to the same message queue and they will be processed in chronological order. file://api-specs/split/GTT_API Documenta.content: Query Option/ Operator Description Official Sample $select https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Products?$select=Price,Name https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Categories? $select=Name,Products&$expand=Products https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Categories? $select=Name,Products&$expand=Products/Suppliers $inlinecount https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Products?$inlinecount=allpages https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Products? $inlinecount=allpages&$top=10&$filter=Price gt 200 $format https://services.odata.org/OData/OData.svc/Products?$format=json Instance-based Authorization Two types of authorization are supported: Read: data contributors can read the tracked process fields that are granted Read authorization. Report: data contributors can report events that are granted Report authorization. To enable the instance-based authorization, you need to: connect with your business partner (via the Invite Business Partners app or the Discover Business Partners app) for the tracked process user model field where you enter LBN ID, add LBN# as the prefix of its value to enable Read or Report authorization. For example, if the LBN ID is 10002424, you need to enter LBN#10002424. Instance-based Authorization Check for Write Service To check if a data contributor has Report authorization for an event, the GTT system will check if the event’s senderPartyId is equal to the tracked process’s partyId or to the LBN ID with the “LBN#” prefix. Not that events reported using Provider API for Order Events (GTT) are an exception, the GTT system won’t do this check for these events. For predefined event types, data contributors can only report GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. Authorization for instances can be inherited and checked through correlation. For example, suppose tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- If you don’t have authorization for tracked process C, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. If tracked process C doesn’t exist, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. Instance-based Authorization Check for OData Read Service 1. Solution owners have Read authorization for their instances. 2. Data contributors can only query user-defined process entities, user-defined event entities, GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. When querying process entities, you cannot filter/expand “QualifiedTrackingId” and user defined process entities. When querying event entities, you cannot filter/expand core entities and user-defined process entities. When querying any process entities, data will be filtered by process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. When querying any event entities, data will be filtered by “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. Notes There are several points to note: 1. It’s not supported that “/”,”//” “;”, “%”, “\” appear in the key of the query entity. 2. It’s recommended to keep the layer of the navigation or expand no more than 3 layers. 3. The max limit of number of records in the response is 256. 4. For $expand, the use of a same entity name is not supported.  Example Unsupported example: https://< Server Address >/api/outbound/odata/v1/com.gttsampleso01.gtt.app.sof.sofService/ SalesOrderItem(id=guid’6d49b8f3-5599-5cbf-b9d0-b06bfb4e24a9', altkey='/;\%-12345678  Example Not suggested example: https://< Server Address >/api/outbound/odata/v1/com.gttsampleso01.gtt.app.sof.sofService/ TrackedProcess(guid'6d49b8f3-5599-5cbf-b9d0-b06bfb4e24a9')? $expand=plannedEvents/lastProcessEventDirectory/event/references 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Response File tp2_20231218083335.zip SOAP Message Interfaces This section introduces SOAP message interfaces used by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out As a solution owner, you can create a freight order in TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA and send it for tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Technical Name TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Description You can use this inbound service provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to create a freight order for tracking from your external system, such as TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA. This will enable you to track a freight order. For detailed configurations, see Using SOAP Messages. Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you are using the tracking APIs. As a solution owner, can I request a new event type in the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You can report an incident on SAP ONE Support Launchpad categorized by component SBN-LBN-GTT to create a new event type. But before reporting the incident, please take a moment to familiarize yourself with the information below: 1. An event type means an action, such as Arrival or Departure. So it should not include any location-related information. 2. Location information could be maintained based on the stop ID (which is provided via the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT)), UNLOCODE, or IATACode. If you want to add an Arrival or Destination event, you can use the ARRIV_DEST event for both of these events. The exact location should then be maintained in the location ID. To foster standardization, please map your events to one of the existing event types. For a complete list of existing event types, see Event Code Descriptions. If you are unsure about which event type you should map with your event, you may also consider mapping it to the OTHER event type and adding a specific description for it. Does SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace support geo location tracking for direct integration with carriers (no visibility provider in between)? Yes. Carriers can also provide geo location updates via the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Note that any event type can contain geo coordinates, such as Arrival, Departure, On Time, Delay, and so on. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- As a solution owner, can I receive attachments from the data contributor as part of the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You have two options to achieve that. Option 1: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName, mimeType, and fileURL that is publicly accessible. The GTT system will save the content from the URL provided as an attachment with the specified event. Option 2: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName and fileContentBinaryObject to upload a Base64- encoded attachment. What is the size limit for attachments such as the proof of delivery that are sent by the data contributor? The total size of the attachment(s) in an event may not exceed 10 MB. As a solution owner, can I send a tracking request to multiple business partners regarding one specific document? Yes. You can achieve this in the Manage Models app by using the event-to-action function sendTrackingRequest. For more, see the corresponding part in the section Event to Action External Functions of Guide for Model Administrators. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 60 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/GTT_Activate Your.content: Activate Your Account Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:47:35 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/8afff0118f9b4f1bb7d29f7b79c8f7d4?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction Welcome to SAP Business Network for Logistics! Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. What is the network and what are the benefits of joining? SAP Business Network for Logistics improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, you – a carrier company – can activate your account on the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, subcontracting, freight settlement, milestone reporting and dock appointment scheduling. SAP Business Network for Logistics is a cloud solution that provides your company with a range of apps which you can use to complete your daily tasks. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . This guide gives you information on how to activate your account for SAP Business Network for Logistics so you can sign in and start using the apps. If you have any issues following the steps, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions. Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process This guide gives an overview of the simplified onboarding process designed for data contributors and carriers who are ready to use SAP Business Network for Logistics. It provides detailed procedures for activating your account on the network, creating your business profile, adding users, and connecting with the business partner that invited you. If you have any issues performing the getting started tasks, see Frequently Asked Questions.  Note Instructions provided in this guide apply to both the production and test environments. If you’re invited by a shipper or solution owner from the production environment, you can follow these instructions to onboard to the production environment. Similarly, if the invitation comes from the test environment, you can use the same steps to onboard to the test environment.  Note Since release 2405, the account activation process for logistics providers has been simplified so that companies without an SAP Store account can also register as a carrier or data contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics. You, as a logistics provider (carrier or data contributor), will receive an invitation from a shipper or solution owner to start your simplified account activation process. However, if the invitation was sent before release 2405 - which is before June 1, 2024, for invitation senders using the Europe data center (EU10), and before July 1, 2024, for those using the United States data center (US20) - the previous account activation process still applies. For more information, see Getting Started (Prior to Release 2405).  Note To help you get started easily, most procedures described in this document are also presented with step-by-step screenshots on the Carrier Learning Portal under Connect With Your Customer: 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Register (for Free) as a Carrier/Data Contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic provides step-by-step instructions on how to complete the registration for SAP Business Network for Logistics. Prerequisites Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. As the administrator of your company, you've received the following invitation email. If you don't receive it, check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take <Company_Name_Of_Inviter> would like to connect with you on SAP Business Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com The email contains a link for registering an account on SAP Business Network for Logistics. See the following procedure. 1. After you received an email invitation from a shipper or a solution owner, click Get started in the email message. When SAP Business Network for Logistics shows the welcome page, click Create new account. 2. If you are creating a new account, verify the auto-populated email address and then click Proceed. 3. Follow the steps in the registration wizard. SAP Business Network asks for basic information about your business, such as your company name, address, and email address. You also create a username and password. The wizard performs automatic address validation to detect and correct any wrong or misspelled portion of a mailing address. A pop-up window shows a recommendation, which you can accept or reject. There is an ISO-based country- or region-specific drop-down list for state/province in the address section of the supplier profile. Select from the drop-down list (where available) instead of entering free text. Getting Started Create Account Connect Existing Account Account Administration Get Support  Note If the shipper or solution owner (inviter) has enabled “Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network” in Profile Settings for cross-data-center connections, you, as the invitee, will be prompted to choose a designated data center where your company profile will initially be maintained. Keep in mind that, to increase the visibility of your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strengths, your company profile will also be replicated to other data centers. If you do not want your profile to be replicated to other data centers, you have the option to abort the registration.  Note 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 4. Read the terms of use, choose the check boxes if you agree to the terms, and then choose Create account. 5. (Optional) Print the Summary page for your records. You can also print the terms of use. Results You’ve registered an account on SAP Business Network. Additionally, you'll receive several emails as described in Follow-up Emails. Follow-up Emails After registering for SAP Business Network for Logistics, you will receive several follow-up emails from SAP Business Network. These emails are sent from noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com. Make sure your email software doesn’t block these email addresses to avoid them going to your SPAM/Junk Mail box. The table below shows the emails you should expect to receive and the actions to take after receiving them. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take Welcome to SAP Business Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com Notifies you that your SAP Business Network account has been created and your company's tenant on the network is ready to use. The email contains the following: Your account information The sign in URL (embedded in the Sign in button) Proceed with the next task Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic explains how to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics by clicking on the URL provided in the email Welcome to SAP Business Network, entering the user credentials, and accepting the terms and conditions. It also mentions that you can change the language displayed in the user interface. Prerequisites You've registered an account on SAP Business Network and received the emails described in Follow-up Emails. Procedure The person whose name is entered in the user account information section becomes the account administrator automatically. Account administrators can transfer the administrator role to another user later.  Note When double byte non-Latin characters (such as Chinese) are detected in an address, a warning is displayed. A Latin character translation must then be provided by the user, which is also validated for correctness. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 4 This is custom documentation. If you don't know your S-User ID, see the next question. To create an incident (report an issue), I need to provide my S-User ID. What if I don't know my S-User ID? If your company didn't have an S-User ID before registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, check the email with the subject " [PRIVATE] Your key to the SAP ecosystem" (see Step 3 in Register (for Free) SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store). The email contains the S-User ID for your company. The password is set when the email receiver activates the account using the link provided in the email. For more information, watch a short video S-Users Management in Carrier Administrative Trainings . It’s also possible that your company already had an S-User ID before registering SAP Business Network for Logistics. In that case, you need to contact a user administrator in your company for S-User sign-in credentials. If you have trouble identifying who the S-User is in your organization, you can contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC). For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Next Steps We recommend that you familiarize yourself with the Administration Guide for Logistics Providers, which contains lots of useful information, including how to administrate your account. When using the apps, you can explore the user assistance by calling up the in-app help via the  Open Help icon on the SAP Fiori Launchpad. You'll also find more useful information on the SAP Help Portal for SAP Business Network logistics providers. The following sections in the user assistance may be of interest to you: Business Area Document Section Administrate your account In the Administration Guide for Logistics Provider: Business Configuration Connectivity: Configuring inbound/outbound connections for implementing APIs and EDIs Automate processes through B2B integration Use the documents in the Integrate section on SAP Help Portal to learn how to integrate via EDI or API. This is an optional way to automate processes. Alternatively, you can use our web UIs. Use web UIs in daily operations Use the documents in the Use section on SAP Help Portal to learn how to use our web UIs to perform freight contracting, dock appointment scheduling, tracking, and freight settlement, etc. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 21 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- This administration guide describes the steps you need to perform as an administrator to set up, configure, and administer SAP Business Network Logistics Provider. This guide addresses the following target audience: administrators, consultants, users and others involved with SAP Business Network Logistics Provider. About SAP Business Network Logistics Provider SAP Business Network for Logistics is an open network that connects business partners for inter-company collaboration. Freight collaboration and milestone reporting support you as a carrier or other logistics service provider to jointly manage the related transactions and exchange documents with your shippers. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . Technical Considerations Note that there are restrictions regarding the overall data volume that can be managed. Before starting your project, discuss your expected data volumes with your SAP technical contact. Browser Support This application only supports the standard browsers supported by SAP Business Technology Platform. For more information, see the Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Root Certificate for End User UI The browser certificate store must contain both the old root certificate ( DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the end user sign-in to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. To check if you are impacted, try to access the following URL: https://digicert-tls-rsa4096-root-g5.chain-demos.digicert.com . If your browser loads the page without warning, it trusts the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 and no further action is required on your end. To ensure a smooth transition, you need to run the check and take action (where applicable) before April 23, 2026. Resolution for user sign-in to the BN4L Fiori Launchpad - How to import the certificate into my browser? The below steps might vary with the browser type and version: Download Root Certificate [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] and Intermediate Certificate [DigiCert G5 TLS RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1 ]. Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Open settings and search for security in the search box and click on it. Click on Manage Device Certificates / Manage Certificates.  Note A logistics provider can be a carrier in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration or a data contributor in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Go to the Trusted Root Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. Go to the Intermediate Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. Ensure that DigiCert Root and Intermediate is added in the list. For more information, see Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5. Product Availability This section describes certain product availability aspects. Availability - Languages The apps provided with SAP Business Network for Logistics support the following languages: English (US) – default Dutch German French Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Russian Simplified Chinese Spanish Turkish Italian Japanese Arabic Bulgarian Czech Danish Greek Finnish Hebrew Croatian Hungarian Korean Malay 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Norwegian Romanian Slovak Serbian Swedish Thai Traditional Chinese In addition, selected documentation on SAP Help Portal supports the languages listed above. Onboarding and User Management A step-by-step guide will lead you through the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, signing in, and adding users. For more information, see Activate Your Account. Business Configuration SAP Fiori Launchpad Integration The SAP Fiori launchpad is delivered with the apps as part of the tenant onboarding process. The users that you have defined can access different applications using the Fiori launchpad. You can sign in to the Fiori launchpad using a URL with the following format: https://<your-subdomain>-site-entry.<domain-name>/sites#Shell-home Set Up Business Profile For your business partners to search and connect with you in the network, you must maintain your business profile using the Manage Business Profile app. For more information, see Manage Business Profile app. Manage Notification Settings You can schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert using the Manage Notification Settings app. The system sends you notifications via emails. For more information, see Manage Notification Settings. Define User Settings You can define defaults that best suit the way you work using the Define User Settings app. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps in your SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, see Define User Settings. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Manage Users As an administrator, you can use the User Management app to manage users in your company tenant, such as adding or deleting administrators or business users. For more information, see User Management. Manage Invitations from Business Partners To perform business in the network and to receive business documents from your business partners, you must first connect with them. An existing or potential business partner can send invitations to connect with you in the network. You can accept or reject the invitations using the Manage Invitations app. Navigate to the Manage Invitations app tile in the Fiori launchpad to access the app. For more information, see Manage Invitations. Freight Contracting You can participate in freight tendering when a known ordering party sends you a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ). You can accept or reject a freight RFQ. The freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a freight quotation and sends it to the ordering party. The ordering party then evaluates your freight quotation and, according to their strategy, may or not award it to you. For more information, see the application help for Freight Contracting. Freight Orders for Confirmation If an ordering party wants to subcontract the transportation of goods to you, you will find the corresponding freight orders in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. This can also be a subsequent step to the tendering process, if your freight quotation was awarded. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) You can review and confirm ocean freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app. Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) You can review and confirm air freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Self-Book Dock Appointments You can book a dock appointment for a freight order in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app when the corresponding vehicle is about to reach a certain stop for loading or unloading. The appointments you booked will then be visualized in the Manage Dock Appointments app. This helps shippers have a precise estimate on the quantity of the upcoming dock appointments. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- For more information, see the application help for the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. Invoice Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for invoicing using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using this app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. For more information, see the application help for the Invoice Freight Documents app. Manage Invoices You can view all the invoices that you created in the freight collaboration option for your ordering party using the Manage Invoices app. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Invoices app. Review Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for self-billing by the ordering party using the Review Freight Documents app. This app displays all the freight documents that you have received from one or more ordering parties. You can view the transportation charges in the freight document based on which the ordering party creates a self-billed invoice. You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs using this app. For more information, see the application help for the Review Freight Documents app. Manage Disputes You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs. Once the system creates a dispute, you can view this document in the Manage Disputes app. In this app, you can newly add a charge line for an additional charge encountered during the transportation or you can propose a change in an existing charge line. The ordering party can accept or reject your changes or propose another change and submit the dispute back to you. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Disputes app. Freight Orders for Reporting You can keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight using the Freight Orders for Reporting app. You can report when planned events in the freight order are completed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a new ETA (expected time of arrival), enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. Note that the Freight Orders for Reporting app has been deprecated and will be sunset on May 16, 2026. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Reporting app. Manage Freight Orders The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of your shipments is delayed on-route, you can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so they can replan if necessary. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For more information, see the application help for the Manage Freight Execution app. Connectivity By implementing the APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your organization can receive and respond to business documents directly from your external system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: 1. Set up Outbound Connections: Choose Manage Details. Enter the communication details and the authentication details to your external system. Then navigate back to Outbound Connections. Configure the supported services in your external system. To do so, choose Create, and select a service name and an operation name from the drop down menu. You can create an API or EDI communication based on the details provided under Manage Details. Activate the operation. 2. Set up Connection Settings: Choose Connection Settings. Under Outbound, in the Integration Platform dropdown list, you can choose between the following values: Neo (old) Multi-Cloud (new) Neo (old) is set as default. To enable outbound communication using the new integration platform, select Multi- Cloud (new). To authorize your inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need an OAuth token. To request the token from SAP, create a BCP ticket and use the component SBN-LBN-INT. Turn on the Enable Inbound Communication toggle and save. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network for Logistics, go to:  Note The System Connections app is available for digital forwarders, carrier subnetworks, network partners, and carriers (B2B carrier/networks).  Note Ensure to allowlist the IP addresses of the integration platform. If you use Neo (old), you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and Hosts Available for the Neo Environment. If you use Multi-Cloud (new) for outbound connections, you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and API Endpoints Available for the Cloud Foundry Environment. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace For more information about EDI integration, see the guides published on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/docs/business- network-logistics-provider?task=integrate_task. Related Information System Connections (Data Contributor) Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 SAP Business Network for Logistics is switching its root Certificate Authority to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 for the domain *.logistics.*.business-network.cloud.sap to enhance security and trust. This is in line with the root certificate replacement in the SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry Environment. To ensure a smooth transition, customers must take action before April 23, 2026. For more information, see SAP Note 3688060 . As part of our ongoing commitment to security and trust, SAP is updating the root Certificate Authority (CA). This update supports the broader adoption of our fifth-generation (G5) root CA and allows additional time for its inclusion in major browser and operating system trust stores, ensuring seamless and trusted connectivity. Am I Impacted? This change could impact B2B Connectivity: The sender systems must trust both the old root certificate ( DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate ( DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the inbound communication to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. For information about a possible impact on the end user UI, see Browser Support. Resolution for B2B Connectivity to BN4L: Case 1: When sender system is S/4HANA (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Upload this Root Certificate to all relevant SSL Client PSEs*. 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 3238733 - How to Import a Certificate Into a STRUST PSE's Certificate List In a NetWeaver AS ABAP. 4. [DigiCert Global Root G2] should remain as is. 5. ICM restart should be necessary post change in STRUST, only if you are running old releases of Netweaver 700/701 and 64x. See SAP KBA 2746647 - SSSLERR_PEER_CERT_UNTRUSTED after importing the target certificate. Since Netweaver AS ABAP 710 and AS ABAP 702, ICM restart is no longer necessary. Case 2: When sender system is SAP NetWeaver PI (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to TrustedCAs view of NetWeaver Java Key Storage. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Particularly, in case of a customer written Java program, JDK version should be higher than the following: SAP JVM 8.1.097 SapMachine 11.0.22 SapMachine 17.0.10 SapMachine 21.0.2 Oracle JDK 8u401 Oracle JDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 21.0.2 For more information, see the following SAP Notes: 3688060 3587968 3566727 3472211 Migration to New Integration Platform (Freemium Customer) SAP Business Network for Logistics is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners for SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and managed by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Freemium customers can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using the System Connections app, and monitor their integration logs using the Manage Integration Logs app. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in the Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note 3351844 ). SAP Cloud Integration is also offered in a multi-cloud foundation in SAP BTP, and this is the new platform that will be used by SAP Business Network for Logistics. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 11 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- In accordance with SAP BTP’s decision to sunset Neo environment, SAP Business Network for Logistics has decided to stop the support of the existing Neo integration platform on July 18, 2025, as part of our July 2025 release. This means that connectivity to your backend transportation management system (TMS) will stop working if you don’t migrate to the new integration platform. This requires some configuration changes in your backend TMS and in your System Connections app in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can read more about this change in this announcement . There is a comprehensive guide capturing the list of changes that a freemium customer must do to migrate from old integration platform to the new one. We understand the critical role that connectivity plays in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The primary focus is not to disrupt the existing integrations between your backend systems and SAP Business Network for Logistics. So, your existing configurations will stay intact and continue to work until you migrate to the new integration platform or till the end of support of the old integration platform. In the meanwhile, we have made it possible for you to migrate from the old integration platform to new one using the configuration apps in SAP Business Network for Logistics. This requires some changes in SAP Business Network for Logistics configuration apps as well as in your backend systems. You might also need to update your firewall/SAP Cloud Connector configurations as the IP range will be different for the new integration platform. We urge you to migrate as soon as possible to leverage the improved log capacity and other new features. For more information, see the Integration Platform Migration Guide for Freemium Users. Based on which data center you’re onboarded to, the IP ranges of our integration platform differs. How to identify your tenant’s datacenter? If you are unsure about your tenant’s data center, this can be identified from the region tag (for example, eu10 ) in the host URL of your SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant. For more information about security on SAP Business Technology Platform, see Data Privacy and Security in the (SAP BTP) documentation on SAP Help Portal. User Administration, Authentication, and Authorizations It's important to consider the security-aspects of creating and configuring users and roles for the applications. Consider the following security aspects: Grant users only the minimum level of authorization that's necessary. Remove a user's authorization as soon as it's no longer required, for example, if an employee leaves the company. Related Information Assign Users to Role Collections Delete Users from Role Collections 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Session Security Protection SAP Business Network for Logistics is restricted to operating with Secure Socket Layer (SSL) and activated cookie handling only in the browser. Network and Communication Security SAP Business Network for Logistics uses the HTTPS protocol to encrypt communication between the browser and the service. Data Storage Security SAP Business Network for Logistics stores data in tenant-specific database schemas. Access to the databases are preconfigured with the infrastructure environment. The databases contain many different types of data including the following: Personal data (for example, user names, email addresses, and so on) Operational business data Preferences and configurations This data is updated continuously whenever required or requested. Data Protection and Privacy Introduction Data protection is associated with numerous legal requirements and privacy concerns. In addition to compliance with general data protection and privacy acts, it is necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries/regions. SAP provides specific features and functions to support compliance with regard to relevant legal requirements, including data protection. SAP does not give any advice on whether these features and functions are the best method to support company, industry, regional, or country-specific requirements. Furthermore, this information should not be taken as advice or a recommendation regarding additional features that would be required in specific IT environments. Decisions related to data protection must be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the given system landscape and the applicable legal requirements.  Note SAP does not provide legal advice in any form. SAP software supports data protection compliance by providing security features and specific data protection-relevant functions, such as simplified blocking and deletion of personal data. In many cases, compliance with applicable data protection and privacy laws will not be covered by a product feature. Definitions and other terms used in this document are not taken from a particular legal source.  Caution The extent to which data protection is supported by technical means depends on secure system operation. Network security, security note implementation, adequate logging of system changes, and appropriate usage of the system are the basic technical requirements for compliance with data privacy legislation and other legislation. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 16 This is custom documentation.
