file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: 5. Save your model configuration. Deploy a Model Context When you have created a model, you can deploy the model directly. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. 2. On the Model Overview page, click the model you want to deploy. The detail page of the model then appears. 3. On the Model Details page, click the Deploy button on the top right. The model is then deployed. Model Header Context In the Header tab, you can fill in the following basic information about the model: Name Description Namespace Correlation Level. Correlation level: is the level of event correlation propagation between tracked processes within a model. is specified as an integer from 1 to 5. Each tracked process has a list of observed tracked processes. You can add a tracked process to the observed tracked process list by the tracked process creation/update event or by some other actual events. For example, suppose there is an event correlation chain between tracked processes A, B, and C, which means that tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If the model is configured to have 1 level of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to B. If the model is configured to have 2 levels of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to both A and B. And so on. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 11 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Note that the event correlation chain between tracked processes breaks up in the following two cases: When tracked processes are of the same type: In this example, if tracked processes A and C are of the same type, then the event correlation chain breaks up between B and A. So events reported to tracked process C are correlated to B, but not to A. When the actual event’s event type is not defined as an admissible planned or unplanned event in this tracked process: In this example, if a Proof of Delivery planned/unplanned event has been defined in tracked processes C and A, but not in B, then when the Proof of Delivery actual event is reported to C, the event correlation chain breaks up between B and C. So the Proof of Delivery actual event reported to C won’t be correlated to B and A, even if there is a Proof of Delivery planned/unplanned event defined in A. Also note that the authorization for instances can also be inherited and checked through correlation. So in this example: If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. If you don’t have authorization for tracked process C, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. If tracked process C doesn’t exist, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. Procedure To complete the model header, do the following: 1. Fill in the mandatory field: Name. It must meet the following requirements: It's unique from other models in the same tenant. It starts with a lowercase letter and then lowercase letters or numbers. It cannot start with letters “gtt”. It's less than 50 characters. 2. When the model name is set, the Namespace will be filled automatically. 3. Fill in the Description. 4. Fill in the Correlation Level in the range from 1 to 5. Tracked Process 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- A tracked process is the main object in the model. Each model must have at least one tracked process. The name of the tracked process must be unique in the model. You can create/edit/delete your own tracked process. You can have at most 200 tracked processes in a model. In the Tracked Process tab, user-defined tracked processes are listed on the left. Select one tracked process in the list. On the right, there are different views of the tracked process: Field Lists Admissible Planned Events Admissible Unplanned Events. Related Information Basic Terms Create Tracked Process Context You can create a tracked process in the Tracked Process tab. Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the Create button above the list. 2. Fill in the following: Name: mandatory and must be unique in this model. Description Tracking ID Type: mandatory and must be unique across models in the whole tenant. Affect Planned Event Status By: mandatory. You can select either the Actual Business Timestamp or Actual Technical Timestamp in the drop-down list. The first one is the default. Your selection decides the timestamp the system uses to process the last reported actual event. In turn, this affects the planned event status. For more, see Timestamps. Sort Planned Events By: mandatory and you can select either First Planned Business Timestamp then Payload Sequence or First Payload Sequence then Planned Business Timestamp in the drop-down list. The first one is the default. Your selection decides the sequence of planned events that is used for the tracked process status calculation. You can see the displayed sequence in the Planned Events tab of the CPE app. 3. Click OK. Edit Tracked Process Context After a tracked process is created, you can edit the tracked process attributes. Procedure 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 13 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the tracked process that you want to change. 2. Click the Edit button above the list. 3. In the pop-up dialog, you can edit its name, description and tracking ID type, and change your selection in Affect Planned Event Status By and Sort Planned Events By. 4. When your editing is complete, click OK. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Tracked Process Context You can delete a tracked process. Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the tracked process that you want to delete. 2. Click the Delete button above the list. 3. Besides, in a standard tracked processes of the standard model "gttft1", you can also see a Standard Model Fields table. It contains the standard fields in this tracked process. Date Timestamp Association to One: associates to a tracked process, or linked to a tracked process. If you choose this type, you must select a process type. Code List: a code list with the string type and a value range. If you choose this type, you must select a code list that you defined in the Code List tab. Attachments: Supported file types are: jpeg, jpg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, and xlsx. The maximum file size limit is 10 MB. Attachments-type fields don’t support IDOC integration mapping. Read: If this field is granted "Read" and the user's LBN ID is equal to this field, then you can read this tracked process where the field exists. Report: If this field is granted "Report" and the user's LBN ID is equal to this field, then you can write this tracked process where the field exists. For more, see the section Specify Attributes in the Role Using “ReadServiceAttributeTemplate” in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Readable When reading the tracked process, this field is readable by the OData service. Writable When writing the tracked process, this field is writable. Visible This attribute controls the visibility of the fields in fulfillment tracking apps: If the box is checked, the field is displayed in the fulfillment tracking apps by default. Actual Technical Timestamp Inherit from Tracked Process: inheriting the configuration from your tracked process definition. Your selection decides the timestamp that the system uses to process the last reported actual event. In turn, this affects the planned event status. 4. In the Match Actual Event tab, you can define how an actual event matches an admissible planned event when the actual event is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Define the Match Location value by clicking the switch control. On: The location is used as a match key between the planned event and actual event. The check box of locationAltKey is then enabled in the Match Planned Event tab. Off: The location is not a match key between the planned event and actual event. The check box of locationAltKey is disabled in the Match Planned Event tab. Below the location match condition, you can define match conditions between planned event extension fields and actual event fields. You can add/edit/delete a match condition. The field you added/deleted here will also enable/disable the check box of this field displayed in the Match Planned Event tab. To add a match condition, do the following: a. Click the Add icon  . b. On the left, choose a planned event extension field you defined in the Planned Event Extension tab, the match operator is set as equal by default. On the right, choose an actual event field. The two match fields must be of the same type. Click the Delete icon on the right to delete a corresponding match condition. 5. In the Match Planned Event tab, you can define how a planned event matches an existing admissible planned event when a planned event update or tracked process update is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can define the match value by using the check box. The check box of eventType is enabled by default and cannot be changed. Fields that are not defined in the Match Actual Event tab won’t be displayed here. If you don't maintain anything here, the system will fall back to the match conditions in the Match Actual Event tab when matching planned events. 6. Click OK to close the dialog and add a planned event if all checks in the dialog pass. 7. Save your model configuration.  Note If a planned event extension field you used here doesn’t exist in the event types that inherit GTTDelayedEvent, then the system will add this extension field to the event types that inherit GTTDelayedEvent.  Note In the GTT standard model “gttft1”, you cannot change the event type, event match key, and standard fields in the Match Actual Event and Match Planned Event tabs for the events below: standard admissible planned events user-defined admissible planned events with a standard event type. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 21 This is custom documentation. All the admissible unplanned events are listed on the right side of this page. By default, the content of Admissible Unplanned Events is displayed with two tables: User Model Unplanned Event Types: This table contains the user-defined unplanned events in this tracked process. You can add/edit/delete these unplanned events. Core Model Unplanned Event Types: This table contains all the unplanned events from the predefined core model's event types. They are: GTTDelayedEvent, GTTOnTimeEvent, GTTDeletionEvent, and GTTUpdatePlanEvent. You cannot modify them. Besides, in a standard tracked process for the standard model "gttft1", you can also see a Standard Model Unplanned Event Types table. It contains the standard unplanned events in this tracked process. You cannot modify them. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 22 This is custom documentation. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Unplanned Events view. 2. In the Match Actual Event tab, you can define how an actual event matches an admissible unplanned event when the actual event is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Here, you can add/edit/delete a match condition between: an actual event field and a string field. Only constants, empty and null fields are allowed. an actual event field and a tracked process field. The two match fields should be of the same type. "Attachments", "Composition", "Association to One" and "Association to Many" types are excluded. If the type is "Code List", the two match fields must come from the same code list. For tracked process fields, only standard and user-defined fields are supported. an actual event field and a sub-field in the tracked process composition field. The match condition works when the actual event field matches one of the sub-fields of the composition field. (Composition field means that the field's type is "Association to One" or "Association to Many".) 5. Click OK to close the dialog and add a unplanned event if all checks in the dialog pass. 6. Save your model configuration. Event Type Event type is used in the planned events and unplanned events of a tracked process. Application Object Type This is a mandatory field. Your entry specifies the application object type in the ERP system for IDOC Integration. Tracked Process / Events table This includes tracked process event and event types. You are free to input your own value or use value help to define IDOC and ERP Event Code. Event code must be unique in a model. User Model Fields table There are Field column, IDOC Segment column and IDOC Field column in the tree table. You are free to input your own values or use value help to define related properties according to your selected ERP Object Type. To Set up IDOC Integration Context To set up the IDOC integration, do the following: Procedure 1. In the IDOC Integration tab, select a tracked process. 2. Set the Integration Switch to ON for IDOC integration. 3. Select an ERP Object Type. 4. Fill in the Application Object Type. 5. For the IDOC column in the Tracked Process / Events table: If your ERP object type value is: “Others”, then use the value help or input a value manually Otherwise, the corresponding is automatically filled in for you. 6. For the Event Code column in the Tracked Process / Events table, use value help or input a value manually. 7. For the IDOC Segment and IDOC Field columns in the User Model Fields table, use value help or manually enter your own values. Visibility Provider Integration Visibility Provider Integration is used for mapping visibility provider generic interface with a tracked process and its actual events. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, you can select a specific tracked process to display or edit related properties. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- On the right of the tracked process selection is an Integration Switch for this tracked process. The default state of this switch is OFF. You can change the state in the edit mode. When the switch state is: OFF, the related configuration view is not visible. These mapping properties are not checked. ON, you can see below the Tracking Indicator, the Generate Event for Tracking Request Failure switch, a Tracked Process / Events table, and a User Model Fields table. When saving a draft model, these selected and filled items are checked before saving or deploying it. Generate Event for Tracking Request Failure switch This switch allows you to automatically generate an event called “GTT Tracking Request Error Event” when your tracking request is rejected by your business partner. The event contains an error message that your business partner sent to you. You can use the information for troubleshooting. The event will be displayed in: the Check Processes and Events app’s Other Events table, which contains a core model field Error Message to display the error. the fulfillment tracking apps’ Events table, which contains a field Event Reason Text to display the error. You can also view this error in the Error Message field of the Event Details page. For more, see Guide for Transportation Planners. Tracked Process / Events table In this table, there are tracked process events and event types. For event types, you can use value help to define the LBN Event Type. To see the full list of supported LBN event types, see Event Code Descriptions in the Code Lists document. Standard/User Model Fields table For the tracked process event, the table includes LBN Tracking Fields column and the tracked process' Fields column. You can select the tracked process field. You cannot input values freely in the edit mode. For the event type events, the table includes the event's user-defined Field column and LBN Tracking Fields column. You can select the LBN tracking field. You cannot input values freely in the edit mode.  Note In the standard model “gttft1”, you can: change the mapping of standard event types with LBN event types. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard model. map user-defined event types with LBN event types. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard model. change the mapping of the tracked process’s standard fields with the LBN tracking fields. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard field mapping of this tracked process. If you change the standard field mapping of the “Shipment” and “TrackingUnit” tracked processes, see Reference: Standard Field Mapping of "Shipment" and "TrackingUnit" Tracked Processes for the upgrades, and manually update the field mapping accordingly. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Set up Visibility Provider Integration Context To set up the visibility provider integration, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, select a tracked process. 2. Set the Integration Switch to ON for visibility provider integration. 3. Use value help to fill in the LBN Event Type for actual events. 4. Use value help to fill in the Field or LBN Tracking Fields. These fields are applied to all the planned events in the model. You can create/edit/delete user defined planned event extension fields in the Planned Event Extension tab. You can have at most 200 planned event extension fields in a model. Create Planned Event Extension Fields Context To create a planned event extension field, do the following: Procedure 1. Click the Create button above the User Model Fields table. 2. Fill in the following: Name: should be unique in the planned event extension Label Type: supports String, UUID, Boolean, Integer, Decimal, Date, and Timestamp 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Visible Readable Writable For more on these attributes, see the relevant information in Create User Model Field. 3. Click OK to create this field. The model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Edit Planned Event Extension Fields Context You can edit the name, label, type, and readable or writable attributes of a planned event extension field. Procedure 1. Select the field that needs to be changed in the table. 2. Click the Edit button above the table. Or click the pencil icon  at the end of the field that needs to be changed in the table. 3. Edit in the pop-up dialog, then click the OK button to save changes. And the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Delete Planned Event Extension Field Context To delete one or more planned event extension user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. Select the fields that you want to delete. Multiple selection is supported. 2. Click the Delete button above the User Model Fields table. 3. The To Be Deleted Objects dialog pops up to ask you if you want to delete the selected fields and all the data in the places where these fields are used. 4. Click OK. Fields you selected are removed immediately, and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Event to Action (Business Rules) Under the Event to Action tab, you can add a script incorporating logic (business rules) to your model. For more information about the script, see Appendix: Event to Action Script. In the standard model “gttft1”, the script is divided into four sections: Standard Declaration, User Script Before Standard Script, Standard Script, and User Script After Standard Script. Standard sections are not editable. You can only edit the user script 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- sections. In the display mode, you can click the eyeglass icon to view the script in a pop-up dialog. Add a Script to Your Model Context To add a script to your model, do the following. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Event to Action tab. 2. You can click Help to open the documentation and find information on writing scripts. 3. Click the Edit button on the top right. Write or paste your script in the window. You can click the pencil icon  to edit the script in a pop-up dialog. 4. Click Validate Code to check your script for errors. If there are no errors, you get a success message. If an error is found, click Open Validation Details to see the line number and type of error. Once you have corrected the error, click Validate Code again. 5. When you have finished your script, you have several options: Cancel: you can choose whether to discard all changes and return to the previous script, or not. Save: to save your script in the model. Translation In the MM app, the following model meta-data fields support multilingual translation: Description of the model Label of user model field in Planned Event Extension, Tracked Process, Field Type and Event Type Description of tracked process Description of event type Name of code in code list Supported Language English (US) is the default language and the default fallback language. To see the full list of supported languages, see the section Product Availability in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Translation Dialog Context 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- The translation dialog allows you to manage the translation of different languages. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Edit button on the top right. 2. Click the Tracked Process tab. 3. To maintain a translation for a tracked process description: a. Select a tracked process from the list. b. Click the Edit button. c. In the pop-up dialog, i. If a translation of the description exists in the current logon language, it is displayed in the Description Input Control. ii. If a translation of description does not exist in the logon language but a fallback language exits, the description in the fallback language is shown as a placeholder in Description Input Control. d. When editing is complete, click Save. 4. To maintain translations for both a tracked process description and fields’ label in a tracked process: a. Click Translate button above the User Model Fields table. b. In the pop-up dialog, a translation of each field is displayed in one line. The first line is a description of this tracked process. Subsequent lines are user fields’ label in this tracked process. In the filter, you can select which language needs to be modified. For example, if you select German in the Language Drop Down List, a new column is added to the table below. c. Add translation in the column of special line. d. Click OK to save your changes. Deployed Models When a model is deployed, two additional views become available: Runtime View: displays deployment information such as API details and deployment history log. Deployed View: displays the deployed version of the model details. Runtime View When a model is deployed, you can see the runtime information of the deployed model. The Runtime view contains the following information: Write Service API Read Service API Write Service 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- In the Runtime view, select the Write Service tab to see the Write Service API details. The Write Service section is displayed in the following order: Tracked process types appear in alphabetical order. And in each tracked process type, the tracked process event is displayed first and followed by user-defined events in alphabetical order. Core events appear at the end in alphabetical order. The Write Service section contains the following information and functions that are offered to consume the Write Service API: API Endpoint: allows you to test the API against the data available in the tenant account. Resources: a list of the resources available for the API. API operations: HTTP POST method can be used to all these resources. Try it out: consume and test the selected API. You can view the response of the API in JSON format in the Response body section. Schemas: The schema for the resources. Trying Out API Context To try out an API, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Servers drop-down, you can see the API endpoint for the Try it out function. 2. In the API documentation, choose the required resource and its HTTP method. To test the API, click Try it out. 3. Enter the request payload in JSON format in the Request body text box. 4. Click Execute to execute the request. 5. In the server response section, it shows the response with the endpoint. Read Service Please see Read Service in API Documentation. Deployed View After a model has been deployed, you can see its deployed version in the Deployed view. On the Model Details page, click the Deployed button on the top right. The Deployed view has the same layout and content as the Draft view. The difference is the deployed view is read-only because you cannot modify the content of the deployed version of the model. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: More Tasks On the top right of Model Details page, there is an Additional Options icon  that contains the following actions: Activate/Deactivate the Model Delete Business Data of the Model Export Business Data of the Model Enable/Disable the Model Cache Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model View the Model History Activate/Deactivate the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can activate/deactivate the model to expose/conceal the Write Service and Read Service APIs for consumption. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select: Activate: to expose the API for consumption Deactivate: not to expose the API for consumption. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The deployed version of the model is then active/inactive. If it’s active, you can read the model metadata and business data, and write the business data. If it’s inactive, you can only read the model metadata. Delete Business Data of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can delete the business data of the logical system you specified, including the tracked processes with corresponding events. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Delete Business Data. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- 4. Select All or Specified Logical System. If you choose the latter, enter the logical system name. 5. Click Delete. Export Business Data of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can export the business data of the model, including the tracked processes with corresponding events, and download the files in the ZIP format. To use this function, you must have the DataModelAdminTemplate role to your role collection. For more, see the Available Roles for Solution Owners section in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Export Business Data. 4. In the pop-up, select a time type that you want the time range of your exported business data to be based on: the Last Changed Time of tracked processes or the Creation Time of tracked processes. 5. Specify the time range for the data you want to export with the Start Time and End Time filters. The duration between the start time and the end time cannot exceed 365 days. 6. Select the tracked process(es) that you want to export. If you don't select any, all tracked processes will be exported. 7. Click Request Export. A confirmation box pops up. Click OK to confirm. A request is then generated under the Requests table. The following columns are displayed: Exported File: displays the request and the file that is exported within this request. Each request is named after the date and time when it is created. You can click  after each request to see the time type, time range and tracked processes you previously specified. If no tracked process is selected in the last step, the Tracked Process field in the pop-over is left empty. But it indicates that all tracked processes are exported. Once the request is completed, expand the request and you can see a list of exported files in the ZIP format that you can download. Each file represents a tracked process and its events. The maximum file size is 100 MB. If the data for a tracked process exceeds this limit, a new file will be created. Completed Time: shows when the request is completed. Status: shows the processing progress of the request: The progress icon  means the request is being processed. The completion icon  means the request is successfully processed. The warning icon  means the request fails to be processed. You must generate a new export request. 8. When the request is completed, select a file that you want to download.  Note The requests will be automatically deleted after 7 days. If the number of requests exceeds 10, only the latest 10 requests are kept. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- 9. Click Download. The file will then be saved to your local device. When you extract the file, you’ll see a collection of JSON files in the resulting folder. Enable/Disable the Model Cache Context When a model is deployed, you can enable/disable the model cache. The default is Enabled. If you change the model cache switch from Enabled to Disabled or from Disabled to Enabled, the change needs at most 15 minutes to take effect. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Enable/Disable Model Cache. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The model cache is then enabled/disabled. If it is Enabled, when you make any changes to the model and redeploy it, the model cache in the runtime needs at most 15 minutes to expire. New changes will take effect thereafter. The same applies to the Configure Partner Connections app. If it is Disabled, when you make any changes to the model and redeploy it, new changes will take effect at once. The same applies to the Configure Partner Connections app. Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can enable/disable the logging of certain items related to your event-to-action script. These items are recorded in message logs and event logs. They include: the Event to Action Log statements the payload sent to the tracking API through the function sendTrackingRequest the payload sent to SAP Transportation Management through the function forwardEventToTM.  Caution In production tenants, enabling the model cache is strongly recommended to ensure optimal message processing performance. Disabling the model cache in production tenants significantly slows down the message processing and could lead to a great number of pending messages in the Manage Message Logs app.  Note This also applies to the Configure Partner Connections API cache. By default, the cache is enabled when calling Configure Partner Connections API internally. When you enable/disable the model cache, the Configure Partner Connections API cache is enabled/disabled at the same time. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The default is Disabled/Off. Once enabled, the system will start logging the above-mentioned items within 15 minutes. You can see the logs on the Correlation Details page of the Manage Message Logs app and the Manage Event Logs app. For instructions, see View Correlation Payload and Logs. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Enable/Disable Event to Action Log. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The Event to Action Log is then enabled/disabled. View the Model History Context When a model is deleted, deployed, activated/deactivated, or meets deployment/deletion error, you can see the history details about the model. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Additional Options icon  and select History. 2. The history log is displayed in chronological descending order by the action time. 3. The history log entries are grouped by weeks. Click the group title to collapse/expand the group. 4. The history log entry contains the information of the administrator who performed the action, action time and description. Check Processes and Events Check Processes and Events (CPE) displays a tracked process with its event data based on a deployed GTT metadata model. The app is used to display all the tracked processes that have been deployed, to test the models, and to check the data displays details of all its events for a selected tracked process displays the data for standard and user-defined fields in the model. When you launch the CPE app, the overview page is displayed that lists all active process types with high-level information about each. Click a specific process type to see its data details on the Process List page. Help and Support There are several ways you can find help and support on the Fiori launchpad of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Built-In Support 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Built-in support provides efficient, simplified and guided support channels, you can search for knowledge, ask for needed information, get help from recommended solutions. Currently, expert chat is not supported. To access the built-in support service on the Fiori Launchpad, click the icon  on the right corner of the screen. You will see a welcome page where you can sign in, and a list of recommended links for the page. To gain full access to the built-in functions, you must activate your S-user. For more, see Activating Built-In Support Services. For more information on how to use this tool, refer to Built-In Support on SAP Help Portal. In-app Help When you launch the app, you can turn on the in-app help that provides on-screen explanations of key fields and areas on the screen. To turn on the in-app help, on the top right on the screen, click the  icon. Once the in-app help is turned on, you can: search the displayed help topics for the text that you type; click the  icon to see the help texts on that topic; click the link tiles to see the documentation of this app on SAP Help Portal; hide the Help Topics panel by clicking the  button on the bottom right. Filters You can apply one or more filters to reduce the number of process types displayed. You can also use value proposal search in selected filters. When you start typing, matching elements are displayed, and you can select them. By default, the following filters are shown: Process Type: the type of a tracked process. Model Namespace: the full unique technical name of the model. Last Deployed At: the range of start to end date that the model was last deployed. When you have completed your filter selection, click Go. You have the following options to alter how filters are displayed: You can hide the filters by clicking the  icon. You can pin the filters to the top of the screen by clicking the pin  icon. You can change the default filters, by clicking the Adapt Filters button. Views You can select a view, also called a variant. The view determines the number of process types listed on the overview page. There are two types, either: 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 45 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Standard: unfiltered so displays all active process types or one of the customized variants, if any have been created. These include some filters that may reduce the number of process types displayed. After you select your view, its name is displayed on-screen. Click Go to display the corresponding process types. An asterisk (*) is displayed after the view name whenever any additional filter selection(s) is made. You can save your selection to create your own view. To create your own view: Click Adapt Filters and the Settings icon  to personalize your filter and table settings respectively. Click the drop-down icon  to the right of the Standard view. Click Save As in the view selector. Enter a name for your view (case sensitive). You can also choose Set as Default and Apply Automatically. Save your view. You can click Manage in the view selector to change the view settings. Process List From the overview page, click a specific process type to see data details of that process type on the Process List page. By default, these filters are displayed: Alternative Key: the unique identifier of the tracked process in SAP Business Network for Logistics. It follows the pattern: scheme:party:system:type:id Scheme: “xri://sap.com/id”, a fixed value Party: LBN ID of the business partner System: name of the logical system that the tracked process comes from Type: business or document type of the tracked process ID: tracking ID of the tracked process Tracking ID: the document number of the tracked process Logical System: an application system in which the applications are coordinated to work in one common database, and from which the tracked process comes from Lifecycle Status: the lifecycle status of the tracked process. Select from the drop-down list one or more of: Business Active: the default value when a tracked process is created. It indicates that the relevant data of the tracked process is used in the ongoing business. End of Business: defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period. When one of the last planned events is reported, the lifecycle status of the tracked process changes to “End of Business” automatically. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Process Status: the actual status of a tracked process, decided by the status of the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned”. Select from the drop-down list one or more of: As Planned: the initial status of a tracked process, also the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is reported on time. Delayed: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is expected to be late. Early: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is early reported. Late: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is late reported. Overdue: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is overdue. Overdue indicates that the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp. You can use the value proposal search in selected filters by clicking the icon . The case insensitive search is supported for the following conditions: “contains” “starts with” “ends with”. When you start typing, matching elements are displayed, and you can select them. To change the default filters, click Adapt Filters. More filters are provided, such as: Estimated Status: the estimated status of a tracked process, decided by the estimated status of the last unreported planned event whose status is not unknown. For details, see Important Terms. ID: the technical key of a tracked process. Party ID: the LBN ID of a solution owner or a data contributor. Tracking ID Type: the equivalent to the tracked process type. In the table of Processes, you can change the default columns with the Settings icon to display the View Settings screen. Select a process to go to the next page: Process Details. Process Details On the Process Details page, the following tabs are displayed: Information You may see the following selectable parts in this tab: Core: core information that is predefined by the GTT system in the model. To see more information, clickShow More. After that, click Show Less to hide the extra information. Standard: standard information that is predefined in the GTT standard model. User-defined: defined by the user in the model Tracking IDs: core composition with table type that is predefined by the GTT system in the model. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can drill down further for more information. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 47 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- External Tracking IDs: core composition with table type that is predefined by the GTT system in the model. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can drill down further for more information. One-Time Locations: core composition with table type that is predefined by the GTT system in the model. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can drill down further for more information. You can use one-time locations for planned events without maintaining the locations in the Manage Locations app. Location geo coordinates will be automatically calculated based on the one-time location information provided, if they’re not maintained. Standard Composition Names: table-typed fields predefined in the GTT standard model. User-defined Composition Names: table-typed fields defined by the user in the model. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings button. You can drill down further for more information. Planned Events The Planned Events table displays all the planned event data for the process in multiple columns including ID, Event Type, Location Alternative Key, Event Match Key, Event Status, Planned Business Timestamp, and Actual Business Timestamp. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can also drill down further for more information. Other Events Other events include: GTTUpdatePlanEvent Unplanned events: display all the actual event data that has been reported without any reference to a planned event. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can also drill down further for more information. Attachments This tab is displayed only when you create a user model field with its type as "Attachments" in the Tracked Process tab of the MM app. A Refresh button is displayed on the top right. Click the button to update the data shown.  Note The field “timeZone” supports the time zone IDs that are defined by IANA Time Zone Database. When setting values for the “timeZone” and “timeZoneId” fields, you should only provide a value for one of them. If you maintain the value of the parameter GTT_OTL_TIMEZONE in the Tracked Process EM IDOC, it will be automatically converted to the corresponding time zone ID. For more information on the mentioned IDOC, see IDOC Service.  Note The "Actual Business Timestamp" is for the planned event’s last correlated event*. *last correlated event: When an actual event is matched with a planned event successfully and the status of this planned event is calculated based on this actual event, then this actual event is considered as the last correlated event of this planned event. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Planned Event Details On the Process Details page, select a planned event from the Planned Events table to see the Planned Event Details page. There are two tabs: Planned Data: It covers the information about the planned event including the core fields, standard fields and the user- defined fields. Actual Data: Only displayed if an actual event is reported with reference to this planned event. The information is held in a table. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. Select an event to see the Event Details page. A Refresh button is displayed on the top right. Click the button to update the data shown. Event Details On the Process Details page, select an event from the Other Events table to see the Event Details page. You can also see this page when you select an event from the Actual Data table on the Planned Event Details page. The following tabs are displayed: Information: with details for the core fields, standard fields, and the user-defined fields. References: displayed in a table with columns such as ID, Event ID, and Reference Type. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can also drill down further for more information. Event Processes: displayed in a table with columns such as Process, Planned Event Location Alternative Key, and Correlation Type. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can click the link to a process in a row to see its Process Details page. You can also drill down further for more information. Estimated Timestamps: displayed in a table with columns such as ID, Event ID, Event Type, Location Alternative Key, Event Match Key and Estimated Timestamp. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings button. Standard Composition Names: table-typed fields predefined in the GTT standard model. Related Information Event Details Appendix: Event to Action Script An event-to-action script allows you to incorporate logic (business rules) into your model. This section explains about the structure and syntax of the script. To add your script to a model, see the section Add a Script to Your Model. To know more about the notification service, see the guide How to Send Notifications. Lexical Structure The lexical structure of a programming language is the set of elementary rules that specifies how you write programs in that language. It is the lowest-level syntax of a language. It specifies such things as what variable names look like, the delimiter characters for comments, and how one program statement is separated from the next. This section documents the lexical structure of the event-to-action script. Character Set Case Sensitivity This script is a case-sensitive language. This means that language keywords, variables, function names, and other identifiers must always be typed with a consistent capitalization of letters. The while keyword, for example, must be typed “while,” not “While” or “WHILE.” Similarly, online, Online, OnLine, and ONLINE are four distinct variable names. Whitespace This script recognizes the following characters as whitespace: space(\u0020) tab(\t) carriage return: (\r) line feed (\n) Comments This script supports the following styles of comments: Any text between a double slash "//" and the end of a line is treated as a comment and is ignored. Any text between the characters "/*" and "*/" is also treated as a comment. These comments may span multiple lines but may not be nested. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Literals A literal is a data value that appears directly in a program. The following are all literals: Identifiers and Reserved Words Identifiers An identifier is simply a name. Identifiers are used to name variables and functions and to provide labels for certain loops in the script code. An identifier must begin with a letter, or an underscore "_". Subsequent characters can be letters, digits, or underscores. The following are all legal identifiers: Reserved Words The script reserves a number of identifiers as the keywords of the language itself. You cannot use these words as identifiers in your programs: actualEvent plannedEvent trackedProcess break function return case do if switch var else continue 12 // The Integer number 1.2 // The float number "hello world" // A string value true // A Boolean value false // The other Boolean value null // A null value [1,2,3,4,5] // An array a a_b_c x11 _test 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 53 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- false while finally true for Semicolons Like many programming languages, we use the semicolon ";" to separate statements from each other. This is important to make the meaning of your code clear. Without a separator, the end of one statement might appear to be the beginning of the next, or vice versa. Values and Variables String Literals To include a string literal in a program, simply enclose the characters of the string within a matched pair of double quotes ("). The maximum size for a string is 10M. Here are examples of string literals: There are three functions for a string literal: 1. Function length() returns the length of a specified string. For example: 2. Function search()searches for a specified string value and returns the position of the match. If no matches are found, the function returns -1. For example: 3. Function substring() extracts the characters in a string from the start character to the end character and returns a new substring. To use this function, the following points should be noticed: The start index is mandatory. If the end index is not specified, the function extracts from the start character to the end of the string. The start character is included in the substring, but the end one is not. Only integers are input as indices. Subtractive integers are recognized as 0. The index 0 suggests the first character. "testing" "π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter" var str = “circle”; str.length(); // returns 6 var str = “π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter”; str.search("is"); // returns 2 str.search("t"); // returns 5 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 54 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- If the start index is greater than the end index, such as str.substring(4, 1), the indices will automatically swap places to str.substring(1, 4). Here are examples: Boolean Values A boolean value represents true or false, on or off, yes or no. There are only two possible values of this type. The reserved words true and false evaluate to these two values. null Value null is a language keyword that evaluates to a special value that is usually used to indicate the absence of a value. Object Value An object is a composite value. It aggregates multiple values (primitive values or other objects) and allows you to store and retrieve those values by name. An object is an unordered collection of properties, each of which has a name and a value. Property names are strings, so we can say that objects map strings to values. This string-to-value mapping goes by various names. The maximum size for an object is 100M. Function containsProperty() checks if an object contains a property. The syntax of this function is: For example: Array Value An array is an ordered collection of values. Each value is called an element, and each element has a numeric position in the array, known as its index. An array element may be of any type, and different elements of the same array may be of different types. Array elements may even be objects or other arrays, which allows you to create complex data structures, such as arrays of objects and arrays of arrays. There are two functions for an array value: 1. Function array.size() returns the size of the array. 2. Function array.push(x) adds the element x to the array as the last element. var str = “π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter”; str.substring(2, 4); // returns “is” str.substring(5); // returns “the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter” object.containsProperty(“propertyName”) o.containsProperty(“x”) 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Numbers A number value can be an integer of float. A number value can be transformed to a string in this way: Timestamp Value There are four functions for a timestamp value: 1. Function timestamp.minusDays(x) subtracts the number of days (x) in the timestamp. 2. Function timestamp.plusDays(x) adds the number of days (x) in the timestamp. 3. Function timestamp.minusMinutes(x) subtracts the number of minutes (x) in the timestamp. 4. Function timestamp.plusMinutes(x) adds the number of minutes (x) in the timestamp. It starts with a function expression that identifies the function to be called. The function expression is followed by an open parenthesis, a comma-separated list of zero or num.toString() expression . identifier var o = toObject(“{x:1,y:{z:3}}”); //An example object o.x; //=>1 o.y.z; //=>3 expression [ expression ] var o = toObject(“ {x:1,y:{z:3}}”); //An example object var a = [o,4,[5,6]]; // An example array that c a[0].x; //=>1 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 56 This is custom documentation. Here are all allowed operators: Operator Operation Example + Positive number +1 - Negate number -1 +,- Add, subtract 1+2 1-2 <,<=,>,>= Compare a>=b == Test for equality a==b != Test for inequality a!=b ^ Power 2^3 == 8 && Compute logical AND true && false || Compute logical OR true || false ! Conditions Conditional statements execute or skip other statements depending on the value of a specified expression. These statements are the decision points of your code, and they are also sometimes known as “branches.” The “if” statement is the fundamental control statement that allows script to make decisions, or, more precisely, to execute statements conditionally. This statement has 3 forms: 1. The first form’s syntax is: 2. The second form of the “if” statement introduces an else clause that is executed when the expression is false. Its syntax is: 3. The third form’s syntax is: Loops (while) The script supports “while” statement for loop. It has the following syntax: To execute a “while” statement, the interpreter first evaluates the expression: If the value of the expression is false, then the interpreter skips over the statement that serves as the loop body and moves on to the next statement in the program. If the expression is true, the interpreter executes the statement and repeats, jumping back to the top of the loop and evaluating the expression again. The continue statement terminates the execution of the statements in the current iteration of the current loop and continues the execution of the loop with the next iteration. The breakstatement terminates the current loop statement and transfers the program control to the statement following the terminated statement. if (expression) statement if (expression) statement1 else statement2 if (expression) statement1 else if(expression2) statement2 else statement2 while (expression) statement 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 5 -- Introduction This guide describes the configurations you need to perform before you can integrate with Ariba Network. After you set up the integration, you can navigate from Ariba Network to the Monitor Inbound ASNs (MIA) app in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to view the inbound delivery details. Perequisites You have purchased SAP Business Network Commerce Automation. You have purchased SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and finished the onboarding process. For more information about the onboarding process, see Onboarding. You have an administrator role of your subaccount and subscribe to the MIA app. You have downloaded and installed sample codes for the MIA app. Procedure To set up for the integration, do the following: Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network Establish Trust Configure Role Collections and Add Ariba Network Buyer Platform Users Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network Context To submit the required information on Ariba Network, do the following: Procedure 1. Download the global track and trace SP SAML Metadata, then submit a Service Request to request enablement. a. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to your subaccount. b. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Trust Configuration in the Security tab in the left-hand navigation area. c. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Trust Configuration page, click SAML Metadata to download the SP SAML Metadata. 2. Create a service request in SAP Ariba a. Go to https://connectsupport.ariba.com/ to create an SAP Ariba Service Request. You create an SAP Ariba Service Request to enable SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace for your Ariba Network account. Sign in with the SAP Ariba credential provided to you.  Note 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 5 -- b. In the Incidents & Service Requests tab on the top, click Create a Service Request. c. In the search box, enter Where is my order enablement and click the Search  icon, then click the Continue to next step popup on the bottom right. d. Click the Issue/Configuration tile to go to the Create a Service Request page. e. Fill in the required information in each step. f. After you complete all steps, click Review at the bottom left to check the information that you filled in. g. Click Submit to create your service request. 3. Download the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata. After your service request has been processed, you will receive a notification that contains the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata from Ariba Support. Establish Trust Context To estabilishe the trust, do the following Procedure 1. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to your subaccount. 2. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Trust Configuration in the Security tab in the left- hand navigation area. 3. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Trust Configuration page, click New Trust Configuration. 4. In the New Trust Configuration popup, click Upload to import the Ariba Network SAML IdP Metadata that you downloaded. 5. Check the validity of the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata by clicking “Show Details”. If one of the following attributes is empty, the SAML Metadata is considered invalid: Origin Key Subject Issuer Entity ID Single Sign-On URL (Redirect Binding) Single Sign-On URL (Post Binding) Single Logout URL (Post Binding) If you do not have permission to create a Support Request, ask your Designated Support Contact to log one for you. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to enable SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace.  Note Upload your global track and trace SP SAML Metadata using the Attachments field. 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 5 -- In this case, you must contact Ariba Support team in step 2 of Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network and ask them to provide a valid one. 6. Fill in the Name (for example: Ariba IDP) and uncheck the Create Shadow Users During Logon box, then click Save. Configure Role Collections and Add Ariba Network Buyer Platform Users Context To configure role collections and add Ariba Network buyer platform users, do the following: Procedure 1. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Role Collections in the Security tab in the left-hand navigation area. 2. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Role Collections page, click the Add icon on the top right. 3. In the pop-up, fill in the Name, then click Create. 4. After creating the role collection, click the name to navigate to its details page, then click Edit. 5. In the Roles tab, select the role with its name and template as AppManageInboundASNsDisplayTemplate, then click Add. 6. In the Users tab, provide the following information as exemplified in the screenshot, then click Save. Fill in ID with the user's E-mail of Ariba Network buyer accounts. Choose the name of the Identity Provider that you configured (which is not "Default Identity Provider"). 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 4 This is custom documentation. TABLE OF CONTENTS INTRODUCTION ............................................................................................................................................... 3 PREREQUISITES .............................................................................................................................................. 3 API OVERVIEW ................................................................................................................................................ 4 MIGRATION OF INTEGRATION PLATFORM ................................................................................................. 4 STEP 1: CONFIGURE OUTBOUND CONNECTIONS ..................................................................................... 5 Special Considerations While Maintaining Communication Details .......................................................... 6 Authenticating Outbound Requests from Network ...................................................................................... 7 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY ............................................................................................... 10 STEP 3: CONFIGURE INBOUND CONNECTIONS ....................................................................................... 11 Provider API Endpoints for Inbound Scenarios ......................................................................................... 13 STEP 4: EMAIL NOTIFICATION FOR INTEGRATION ERRORS ................................................................. 14 OPERATIONAL MONITORING ...................................................................................................................... 15 -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTRODUCTION SAP Business Network for Logistics provides a network for shippers and carriers to collaborate for freight quotation, order confirmation, tracking, invoice, disputes and dock appointment use cases. SAP Business Network for Logistics provides web UI access to carriers for users to act on a defined process. Additionally, if you wish to get these documents in your systems, you may use the public APIs of SAP Business Network for Logistics to get the data and act on it. This document provides information on how to connect to SAP Business Network for Logistics as a carrier using REST APIs. The following subset of processes are supported via APIs: • Freight Tendering (Road) • Freight Subcontracting (Road) • Freight Booking (Ocean and Air) • Order Tracking • External Planning • Settlement For more general information, see the carrier introduction presentation and the carrier introduction video. Note: All activities mentioned in this guide have to be done in both the test and productive environments. PREREQUISITES To set up API integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must meet the following requirements: • Carrier tenant is available in the test and productive environments. For more information about the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, logging on, and adding users, see the Activate Your Account guide. • In case your API server uses IP filtering, you need to add the IP ranges to the allow list as mentioned in the administration guide for logistics providers, to enable SAP Business Network for Logistics integration tenants to connect to your API server. Please make sure the API server is accessible on the internet. • It is expected that a carrier sets up an API server on their side for information exchange. Carriers have to set up the API connection once and shippers can use the same API connection for communication. The following diagram outlines the API communication between the involved parties: -- 3 of 10 -- 4 API OVERVIEW All APIs between the shipper and SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are SOAP. All APIs between SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and the carrier are REST. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides APIs for the following B2B processes: You can find all the carrier-facing REST APIs on the right-hand side of the image. For more information, see the following documents: • Processes in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration • Carrier APIs (Rest APIs) in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration MIGRATION OF INTEGRATION PLATFORM The integration platform used in SAP Business Network for Logistics is announced for sunset, and a new platform is enabled for customers and partners. If you are an existing customer who has setup API connectivity with the network, there are certain migration efforts required from your end. There’s a detailed migration guide explaining the necessary steps required. We urge you to migrate to the new platform as soon as possible. For new customers, we’ve updated the endpoints and other details in our official product documentation on SAP Help Portal, the SAP Business Accelerator Hub documentation and also in this guide. For more information, see the Integration Platform Migration Guide for Freemium Users of SAP Business Network for Logistics relevant for carriers. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 STEP 1: CONFIGURE OUTBOUND CONNECTIONS Precondition: You have developed an API service in your backend server/transportation management system that can receive messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics in the published API format. On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Choose Manage Details in the upper right corner. Under the Communication Details tab, choose Add and select the HTTPS option from the dropdown menu. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 Enter the following data in the New Communication Details window: For more information, see Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. Special Considerations While Maintaining Communication Details Due to disparity in the API designs of earlier SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs, there’s a difference in how destination URLs need to be configured for different scenarios. Earlier designs for ‘Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting’ and ‘Consumer API for Freight Tendering’ capture several pieces of information, such as shipper LBN ID, originator system ID and document ID, in the URL path especially for update, notification and cancellation scenarios. Hence the communication detail only expects the base URL to be maintained for all operation types (including create) of these two APIs. The URL path captured in the standard API documentation will be appended to the base URL configured in the communication details. In the more recent API designs, such as tracking and freight booking, a different approach is followed. All necessary information is captured in the request body. Hence no URL path calculation is required. This means that the entire URL can be configured in the communication details. SAP Business Network for Logistics reads this configuration as-is, and no change is done while sending the request. The difference in handling of communication details during runtime of different APIs is captured below: Consumer API Communication Details - Base URL/Entire URL Freight Tendering Base URL Freight Subcontracting Base URL Freight Booking for Confirmation Entire URL Order Tracking Entire URL Request for Planning in External System Entire URL Examples: Freight Subcontracting create scenario: If your API system is configured to accept a POST request at ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracing’, you need to capture the URL in the communication details as ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/’. Freight Booking create scenario: If your API system is configured to accept a POST request at ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/FreightBookingRequest’, you need to capture the entire URL in the communication details. -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Authenticating Outbound Requests from Network SAP Business Network for Logistics enables carriers to configure either a network-to-network authentication or a shipper-specific authentication for API request from the network to your backend system. • Network-to-network – common authentication for all shippers in the network • Shipper-specific – you expect a unique authentication credential for requests sent by each shipper from the network If you wish to set up a network-to-network authentication, you can follow the steps below. Under the Authentication Details tab, choose Add and select the required option from the dropdown menu and provide the credential details. Go back to the entry page of the System Connections app and create outbound connections for all API services that you provide: For a list of available services, see Assigning Authentication Details and a Base URL to a Service. -- 7 of 10 -- 8 Enter the following data for the new service: Please note that you need to maintain an “Authentication Detail” only if your integration design assumes a network-to-network authentication, this is, if you have a single authentication for all the shippers in SAP Business Network for Logistics. [Image: Configuration where carriers have a network-to-network authentication with SAP Business Network for Logistics] -- 8 of 10 -- 9 If you expect each shipper to send a unique authentication to your API system, you can leave this field blank, and shippers have a different configuration application where they’ll provide the same. [Image: Configuration where carriers expect a shipper-specific authentication from SAP Business Network for Logistics] -- 9 of 10 -- 10 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY After configuration, you should directly perform a connection test to your API server. To test the service, in the Services table, select Post freight order for subcontracting and choose Test Service in the upper-right corner, then select With Default Payload: The system generates a test freight order and attempts to send a call to your API server. The below window is shown with the test freight order ID: Using the ID of the created document (for example API_TEST_xVdlBk8sz6), open the Manage Integration Logs app to view the test result. Please refer to the chapter OPERATIONAL MONITORING for more details. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/How to Integrate.content: 11 STEP 3: CONFIGURE INBOUND CONNECTIONS On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Proceed as follows: 1. Choose Connection Settings in the upper-right corner. 2. Turn on the Enable Inbound Connections toggle. 3. Select the Integration Platform as Multi-Cloud. -- 1 of 5 -- 12 With the new Multi-Cloud integration platform, you can generate OAuth credentials for inbound authentication from the app itself. Proceed as follows: 1. Select the list of Provider APIs that you want to connect to in SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. Choose Save. 3. Generate or view the credentials by choosing Show Service Credentials. It might take a while for the first time as the request is handled asynchronously in the backend authentication service. -- 2 of 5 -- 13 Provider API Endpoints for Inbound Scenarios Depending on the data center that you’re onboarded in, the host URL differs. You can identify the host URL relevant for your tenant ‘Host URL’ in Connection Settings dialog box. Provider API EU US Provider API for Freight Tenderin g https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LbnFreightOrderFo rSubcontracting /{orderingPartyLbnId}/{originatorId}/{freightOr derId}/carrierResponse https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LbnFreightOrderFo rSubcontracting /{orderingPartyLbnId}/{originatorId}/{freightOr derId}/carrierResponse Provider API for Freight Subcontr acting https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LbnFreightQuotatio n https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LbnFreightQuotatio n Provider API for Freight Booking for Confirmat ion https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/FreightBookingCon firmation https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/FreightBookingCon firmation Provider API to Create Planned Freight Documen ts from External System https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/TransportationDoc ument https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/TransportationDoc ument Provider API for Order Events https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/http/v1/tracking/event s https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/http/v1/tracking/event s Provider API for Invoicing https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LogisticsInvoice https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LogisticsInvoice Provider API for Invoice Cancellati on https://api.logistics.eu.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LogisticsInvoiceCa ncel https://api.logistics.us.business- network.cloud.sap/http/v1/LogisticsInvoiceCa ncel -- 3 of 5 -- 14 STEP 4: EMAIL NOTIFICATION FOR INTEGRATION ERRORS You have to configure the Email notification feature in the Manage Notification Settings app so that you are informed in case of integration errors. To do so, enable on-event notification for the Integration Error V2 Scenario. Please refer to the following blog for more details: Email notification for integration error in SAP Business Network for Logistics | SAP Blogs -- 4 of 5 -- 15 OPERATIONAL MONITORING The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics. Messages with status Failed or Escalated can be reprocessed. Please refer to the following link for more details: Manage Integration Logs | SAP Help Portal -- 5 of 5 --

For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction This document describes the APIs provided by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace that are useable by applications. There are two basic types of API: Public cross-tenant APIs These are published by SAP in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub with documentation. They are mostly used by data contributors. In this guide, you can also find detailed instruction on how to use them. Generated tenant-local interfaces These are tenant-specific interfaces used by solution owners. They are also APIs, but differ based on the tenant. Rate Limiting This section describes the rate limit of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace APIs. Rate limiting restricts the number of incoming requests from callers to GTT APIs and within a specific time frame. It’s a protective measure that: prevents the GTT service from crashing due to the excessive load of requests ensures the availability and optimal performance of the GTT service for every client. We have defined the rate limits of following APIs according to tenant type: API Type of Tenant Limit IDOC interface: GTT_V2_EM_IDOC_Ingestion SOAP Message Interface: TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Write Service API: GTT_V2_HTTP_EVENT_INGESTION Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 150 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Read Service API: GTT_V2_OData_Query Production The rate limit per tenant is 200 per minute.  Recommendation Before you start working through this document, ensure that you have the most recent version of this document available from the SAP Help Portal at: help.sap.com/gtt 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 2 This is custom documentation. When the rate limit is exceeded, you will receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response status code, and your requests are rejected. You can try executing requests again several minutes later. API Payload Limits To prevent APIs from being overloaded by the payload size, we have introduced API payload limits to regulate the API usage per message. The following tables list the size limit of different components in API payload: Public Tracking APIs API Request Body Response Body Provider API for Order Events Less than 40MB N/A Consumer API for Order Tracking Less than 40MB N/A Tenant-local Interfaces API Request Body without Attachment Attachment Response Body IDOC Service Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Read Service API No limit N/A The response body of read service API supports: 256 records at maximum for main entity in a query; 5000 records at maximum for each expanded entity of a single main entity; 20000 records at maximum for sum of each expanded entity for all main entity. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Public Cross-Tenant Tracking APIs This chapter describes how solution owners and data contributors exchange messages via the tracking APIs (or tracking interfaces) offered by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides two types of tracking APIs: Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT): enables solution owners to send a tracking request for an order to data contributors. Provider API for Order Events (GTT): enables data contributors (such as network partners or carriers) to post events for a tracked order. You can check out the above APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub . This chapter specifically describes the following two cases: how a solution owner sends a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT), and how a data contributor sends back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Sending Tracking Requests via Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) As a solution owner, you can send a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) .
