This chapter contains the following sections: Prerequisites and Configuration Monitoring Integration Prerequisites and Configuration Prerequisites To perform the tasks described in this chapter, you, as a data contributor, must have the following prerequisites: 1. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have accepted the invitation from the solution owner using the Manage Invitations app. For more, see the application help of Manage Invitations. Configuration You need to use the System Connections app to complete the API implementations. For details, see the Connectivity section of Administration Guide for Logistics Providers. Related Information Provider API for Order Events (GTT) Monitoring Integration On the SAP Fiori launchpad, pen the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting  within the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app. Generated Tenant-local Interfaces This chapter describes how to use the generated tenant-local interfaces in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. These APIs are provided for integration between the GTT system and other systems, which allows solution owners to access GTT services and perform CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations on the GTT system via API requests. API Authentication You can use the following to authenticate your API calls to GTT service interfaces: HTTP Basic Authentication: You must create a technical user and maintain it in the System Connections app. For more, see Maintain Technical User in the System Connections App. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use these APIs, you must fulfill the following prerequisites: 1. Configure API authentication method. For more, see API Authentication. 2. Get the following information required in the API request URI: Server Address: You must provide the server address as the host in the request URI: For basic authentication, server address is the URL of your GTT Fiori Launchpad. It varies from hosted data centers. Do the following to get the server address: a. Go to your subaccount that has subscribed Global Track and Trace b. Click Services Instances and Subscriptions Global Track and Trace Go to Application c. After sign-in, you will see the URL. Model Information: Prepare the following model information needed in the resource path of the request URI: Model Namespace: It’s in the format of “com.<tenant name>.gtt.app.<model name>”. You can find the entire model namespace on the top of your target Model Details page. Write Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>WriteService”. Read Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>Service”. Model Name: You can find it on the target model card. After you finish the above tasks, you are ready to send API requests. In the sections followed, you can find examples of API request and response pair specific to different interface services. file://api-specs/split/How to Send Messa.content: Property Type Mandatory Description LBN-GTT- Partition-Key- Hint String No A hint to determine which message queue the message will be sent to. Report: data contributors can report events that are granted Report authorization. To enable the instance-based authorization, you need to: connect with your business partner (via the Invite Business Partners app or the Discover Business Partners app) for the tracked process user model field where you enter LBN ID, add LBN# as the prefix of its value to enable Read or Report authorization. For example, if the LBN ID is 10002424, you need to enter LBN#10002424. Instance-based Authorization Check for Write Service To check if a data contributor has Report authorization for an event, the GTT system will check if the event’s senderPartyId is equal to the tracked process’s partyId or to the LBN ID with the “LBN#” prefix. Not that events reported using Provider API for Order Events (GTT) are an exception, the GTT system won’t do this check for these events. For predefined event types, data contributors can only report GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. Authorization for instances can be inherited and checked through correlation. For example, suppose tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- If you don’t have authorization for tracked process C, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. If tracked process C doesn’t exist, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. Instance-based Authorization Check for OData Read Service 1. Solution owners have Read authorization for their instances. 2. Data contributors can only query user-defined process entities, user-defined event entities, GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. When querying process entities, you cannot filter/expand “QualifiedTrackingId” and user defined process entities. When querying event entities, you cannot filter/expand core entities and user-defined process entities. When querying any process entities, data will be filtered by process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. When querying any event entities, data will be filtered by “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. Notes There are several points to note: 1. It’s not supported that “/”,”//” “;”, “%”, “\” appear in the key of the query entity. 2. It’s recommended to keep the layer of the navigation or expand no more than 3 layers. 3. The max limit of number of records in the response is 256. 4. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Response File tp2_20231218083335.zip SOAP Message Interfaces This section introduces SOAP message interfaces used by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out As a solution owner, you can create a freight order in TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA and send it for tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Technical Name TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Description You can use this inbound service provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to create a freight order for tracking from your external system, such as TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA. This will enable you to track a freight order. For detailed configurations, see Using SOAP Messages. Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you are using the tracking APIs. As a solution owner, can I request a new event type in the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You can report an incident on SAP ONE Support Launchpad categorized by component SBN-LBN-GTT to create a new event type. But before reporting the incident, please take a moment to familiarize yourself with the information below: 1. An event type means an action, such as Arrival or Departure. So it should not include any location-related information. 2. Location information could be maintained based on the stop ID (which is provided via the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT)), UNLOCODE, or IATACode. If you want to add an Arrival or Destination event, you can use the ARRIV_DEST event for both of these events. The exact location should then be maintained in the location ID. To foster standardization, please map your events to one of the existing event types. For a complete list of existing event types, see Event Code Descriptions. If you are unsure about which event type you should map with your event, you may also consider mapping it to the OTHER event type and adding a specific description for it. Does SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace support geo location tracking for direct integration with carriers (no visibility provider in between)? Yes. Carriers can also provide geo location updates via the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Note that any event type can contain geo coordinates, such as Arrival, Departure, On Time, Delay, and so on. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- As a solution owner, can I receive attachments from the data contributor as part of the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You have two options to achieve that. Option 1: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName, mimeType, and fileURL that is publicly accessible. The GTT system will save the content from the URL provided as an attachment with the specified event. Option 2: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName and fileContentBinaryObject to upload a Base64- encoded attachment. What is the size limit for attachments such as the proof of delivery that are sent by the data contributor? The total size of the attachment(s) in an event may not exceed 10 MB. As a solution owner, can I send a tracking request to multiple business partners regarding one specific document? Yes. You can achieve this in the Manage Models app by using the event-to-action function sendTrackingRequest. For more, see the corresponding part in the section Event to Action External Functions of Guide for Model Administrators. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 60 This is custom documentation. How to connect to Network Partner in Business Network for Logistics as a shipper or Network Owner RavishShettyR Product and Topic Expert 2022 Nov 03 9:39 AM 8 Likes  3,224 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction Business Network for logistics(BN4L) has integration to certain list of the B2B carriers and visibility partners. This document will describe the step by step on how to setup the connection from your account to network partner B2B Carrier – Is nothing but a carrier in your system. Carrier Business users instead of using LBN Web UI, will be using carrier’s IT system. LBN will be integrated to carrier system Network Partner – Also called as a digital forwarder, is another network of carriers. They act on behalf of the carriers for digitally transacting document. LBN will be integrated to Network partner and network partner there on to the carriers.   -- 1 of 10 -- The required configurations for setting up the connections to B2B carriers and Network partners are similar. In this document, we will cover only the steps involved to connect to Network partners. Step1: Discover the Network Partner and establish relationship Step2: Configure connection parameters in BN4L Step3: Testing with Network partners Step1: Discover the Network Partner and establish relationship Pre-requisite: You have established connection to all the carriers, that you wish to collaborate or require tracking information. You can find in the below link on how to establish connection to your carriers. FC:https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_FC_OPTION/185742008f2c477ca789b93675b0ec6c/ a1c5c34037a94fd68fbc24b... GTT:https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/d0802f41861a4f81a3610d873fdcf14 8/a1c5c34037a94fd68fbc24... -- 2 of 10 -- Navigate to Discover Business Partners tile Search for the network partner that wish to connect to. Fourkites, inc. is used as an example -- 3 of 10 -- View detail information for Fourkites, Inc and click on Request for connection. The connection request is routed to the network partner. The network partner will receive a connection request and the network partner will accept/reject depending on your contract with the network partner. To proceed further, the network partner must accept the request. Step 2: Configure connection parameters in BN4L Once the network partner accepted your request, you may proceed with the next steps. In most -- 4 of 10 -- cases, the network partner also would have onboarded you into their systems and would have generated a user credential to access their systems. This credential must be maintained in BN4L for communicating digitally with network partner via BN4L. Maintaining Network Partner Credential Navigate to configure partners connection app Click on Manage credential and maintain the credential provided to you by the network partner -- 5 of 10 -- BN4L support Basic, OAuth and APIkey credentials. Depending on the type of credential provided by the network partner, maintain the entries accordingly . Even for P44, the credential must be maintained as mentioned in the below screenshots. In addition, if you are using tracking for via P44 LTL scenario, you would have to maintain additional values with project44 tab. In P44 terms it is called as capacity provider account. P44 uses the details mentioned in the capacity provider account to retrieve tracking information from carrier system. -- 6 of 10 -- In case you are setting up connection to P44, follow the below mentioned guide: https://help.sap.com/doc/96e23bc983664cc998bd044a66c7b5cd/LBN/en- US/SAP_LBN_FC_p44_guide.pdf Mapping Carriers to Network Partner After maintaining the credential, you must map carriers to network partner. You have an option to map all the carriers to the same network partner for each scenario. -- 7 of 10 -- Depending on the network partner, the list of supported services by the network partner can be seen in drop down. This list will vary from one network partner to another.(These list of services is configured by network partner and integration is built based on supported list). You may select a specific scenario that you wish to setup. BN4L will route the calls to network partner entries endpoints based the transaction data values, mainly transportation Mode( Air , Ocean, Road ) and shipping type( FCL, LCL, FTL, LTL ). -- 8 of 10 -- Note: It is highly recommended to pass the Transportation Mode and Shipping type, if available in the transaction data . Map the network partner credential that was created earlier. After creation, you will have an entry as below. The information can be read as all carriers will be routed to Fourkites for shipment tracking of all modes. -- 9 of 10 -- Step 3: Testing with Network Partners Integration testing must be done on a project basis involving representatives from SAP and network partner organisation. The above setup can be achieved in test and productive environment. In the test environment, you may use one of test carrier tenants in your global account. This test carrier tenant must be mapped to one of the network partner carriers by the network partner. In productive tenants, the carrier that you wish to collaborate must be shared with network partner. Network partner does the mapping between the LBN carriers and the Network partner carriers. In addition, check the logs in Manage Integration Log app for successful communication with network partners Summary By doing above configuration you have enabled connection to Network partner. You can trigger the payload from FC or GTT and see that the calls are going to the network partner. LABELS Technology Updates Add tags Comment -- 10 of 10 --

See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 3 / 10 Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (SAP BN4L) is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners for SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and managed by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Freemium customers can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using the ‘System Connections’ app and monitor their integration logs via ‘Manage Integration Logs’. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note). SAP Cloud Integration is also offered in a multi-cloud foundation in SAP BTP, and this is the new platform that will be used by SAP Business Network for Logistics. In accordance with SAP BTP’s decision to sunset Neo environment, SAP Business Networks for Logistics has decided to stop the support of the existing Neo integration platform on July 18, 2025, as part of our July 2025 release. This means that the connectivity to your backend transportation management system (TMS) will stop working if you don’t migrate to the new integration platform. This would require some configuration changes in your backend TMS and in your System Connections app in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can read more about this change in this announcement. This guide provides a comprehensive list of changes that a premium customer must do in order to migrate from the old integration platform to the new one. We understand the critical role that connectivity plays in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The primary focus is not to disrupt the existing integrations between your backend systems and SAP Business Network for Logistics. So, your existing configurations will stay intact and continue to work until you migrate to the new integration platform or till the end of support of the old integration platform. In the meanwhile, we have made it possible for you to migrate from the old platform to the new one using the configuration apps in SAP Business Network for Logistics. This requires some changes in SAP Business Network for Logistics configuration apps as well as in your backend systems. You might also need to update your firewall/SAP Cloud Connector configurations as the IP range will be different for the new integration platform. We urge you to migrate as soon as possible to leverage the improved log capacity and other new features. Note: We recommend performing the migration activities in your test tenants first and then monitor if all the integration scenarios are working correctly. Proceed with the changes in your productive tenants accordingly. Data Center-Specific Integration Platform There will be a separate integration platform for customers onboarded to EU/US data centers. In this migration guide, you’ll see a mention of endpoints/IP addresses of these two data centers. Please ensure that you update your configurations by referring to the data center where your tenant is hosted. -- 3 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 4 / 10 How to Identify Your Tenant’s Data Center? If you are unsure about your tenant’s datacenter, this can be identified from the ‘eu10’/’us20’ tag in the host URL of your SAP Business Networks for Logistics tenant. URL in SAP Business Network for Logistics Data Center https://carrier01.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/ EU https://lbn-carrier01.lbn.cfapps.us20.hana.ondemand.com/ US Should I Do this Migration? The steps mentioned in this guide are only targeted for B2B carriers/partners of SAP Business Network for Logistics. If you are only using the UI in the network, you need not do any of the below mentioned changes. Why Migrate? Apart from the sunset of the old integration platform, the migration to the new platform has its benefits. Here’s why a B2B carrier should do this migration: • Improved data persistence resources for integration logs: In the current integration platform, resources for database are limited and at the maximum possible limit. Customers rely on integration logs and payload download feature to debug/validate any integration issues. If the DB memory limit is breached, integration scenarios would work fine but there would be discrepancies in the way logs/payloads are stored. Migrating to the new platform will ensure proper log monitoring and payload download. • Improved security for communication between SAP Business Network for Logistics apps: Better authentication protocols will be deployed for communication between the SAP Business Network for Logistics backend apps and the new integration platform (agnostic to customers) • New features: Improvements to platform features will be based on the new integration platform. Some of these upcoming features include hourly auto-reprocessing of failed/escalated logs. • Self-configuration to set up inbound communication for freemium customers: Freemium customers such as ‘carriers’ used to rely on a ticketing process to set up inbound authentication/communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. This was true for both API and EDI communications. Part of the reason was a lack of support from the older integration platform. In upcoming releases, we’ll make these provisionings available via System Connections apps for freemium customers. Configuration Changes for Freemium Users New integration platform means new destination URLs and authentication to connect to SAP Business Network for Logistics. There’ll be no changes to our API/EDI message definitions. So, your existing developments/integrations should work out of the box. -- 4 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 5 / 10 Outbound from SAP Business Networks for Logistics Configurations maintained in your System Connections app are used for the outbound communication from SAP Business Networks for Logistics to your backend system. However, you need to explicitly select the new integration platform for the outbound communication from the network. This is because the new integration platform is hosted in a different cloud infrastructure. Hence, you might need to update your allowlisting rules, if any, at your side to allow communications from the new platform. Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics API Connectivity To use the integration platform for your inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need to change the destination URLs for all provider APIs. The host URL of integration platform varies based on your data center: Data Center Host/Base URL EU10 https://api.logistics.eu.business-network.cloud.sap/ US20 https://api.logistics.us.business-network.cloud.sap/ The URL path remains the same and can be obtained from SAP Business Accelerator Hub documentation. You’d need new OAuth 2.0 credentials to authenticate the calls to the new integration platform. With the latest release of SAP Business Network for Logistics, it’s now possible to provision OAuth 2.0 credentials from the System Connections app directly by selecting the Provider APIs you wish to connect with. -- 7 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Choose Connection Settings. 2. Under Inbound, activate the Enable Inbound Connections toggle. 3. Select Integration Platform as Multi-Cloud. 4. You can create an incident in SAP support portal categorized by component SBN-LBN-INT and title as ‘SAP BN4L Integration Platform Migration: Request for transferring SFTP polling schedulers to new integration platform’ with the following information: • EDI message format (ANSI X12 or EDIFACT) • LBN ID • Polling schedule: Start and end time on the same date (for example, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.). That is, if the start time is on 22 September, the end time cannot be on 23 September, according to your time zone. • Polling frequency (for example, every 30 minutes) Please note that SFTP polling is not yet enabled as a self-service and must be set up by SAP. -- 9 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. We’ve also added a new column to make this clear to customers. The app also supports the reprocessing of messages failed/escalated in both these platforms. Support If you encounter any issues during the migration process, refer to the following blog article. This article summarizes frequently asked questions about the migration: https://community.sap.com/t5/supply-chain-management-blogs-by-sap/faq-neo-to-multi-cloud-cpi- migration-for-business-network-for-logistics/ba-p/14079631 For any further queries, open a ‘Medium’ priority incident in the ‘SBN-LBN-INT’ component with the title – ‘Concerns related to SAP BN4L integration platform migration – <CustomerName>’. -- 10 of 10 --

Start testing integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics without SFTP server aboppre Associate 2023 Jan 26 7:41 AM 11 Likes  1,451 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics provides capabilities of freight tendering, tracking and dock appointment scheduling by connecting business partners in the network. To set up EDI integration with the network carriers need an SFTP server for information exchange. For carriers who are interested in testing EDI integration without such an SFTP server we offer the option to test EDI Outbound messages by sending them as email. This blog describes the required configuration in the System Connections app to use this functionality. Setting up email communication in the System Connections app   -- 1 of 4 -- On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Choose Manage Details in the upper right corner. Under the Communication Details tab, choose Add and select the Email option from the dropdown menu. -- 2 of 4 -- Enter all required data in the New Communication Details window. An email containing an IFTMIN/ANSI 204 message will be sent to each email address in the Recipients field. Go back to the entry page of the System Connections app and create three different outbound connections for the Freight Subcontracting All service, one for each of the following operations: Post freight order for subcontracting cancellation Post freight order for subcontracting Put freight order for subcontracting -- 3 of 4 -- For details how to create these services, see our How-to guides for ANSI or EDIFACT. Here you can also find information how to adjust your configuration for productive usage. Summary By following the above steps, you can start testing the integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics without an SFTP server. You may use the comments section to provide feedback on this article and help in improving the content. Additional you may post your queries in the comment or in the community Q&A. SAP Business Network For Logistics - Carrier Side Integration - API vs EDI Jeff-Gebo Product and Topic Expert 2023 Mar 07 12:39 AM 38 Likes  14,931 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) provides capabilities of freight tendering, subcontracting, settlement, tracking and dock appointment scheduling by connecting business partners in the network. By joining the network, a carrier can connect and transact with any shipper on the network. BN4L comes by default with a web portal that our carriers can use to transact with shippers they are collaborating with. Of course, this often means they have to do the "swivel seat" style of integration, meaning manually copying the data from our portal and pasting it into their own systems...not very fun to be sure but not horrible if you only have a small number of transactions. Most carriers I have met would rather get away from this method of "integration" once the transaction numbers start to increase. BN4L provides two options for building integrations - API and EDI. Both have their pros and cons as you will soon read.   -- 1 of 6 -- API Pros Performance - nothing can beat the speed of a system-to-system API integration. Transactions can flow back and forth between shipper and carrier in a matter of seconds. Functional Coverage - Most functionality in the web portal is also supported with APIs with a couple of exceptions. Invoice Disputes and Dock Appointment Scheduling are only available in the web portal. New processes to the industry like quotes/spot bids and external planning are only available for integration with APIs. API Cons Development Skills Required - APIs require some development and/or robust middleware to implement. On top of that, your own systems must be API enabled to build the integrations. To our SAP customers this might sound trivial, but many carriers are working on older systems that don't support the latest integration possibilities. Takes Time to Implement - building an API integration can take time and requires close collaboration with a shipper who can send test data. A middleware solution can help ease some of this burden, and should be considered, but it will still take time to build a robust API integration. Why does it take a long time? For one, the payloads are large and somewhat complex, it's not enough to be an API developer, you need to also understand the data and the business process. EDI Pros Standards Based - EDI has been around for a long time and is how logistics integrations have operated for decades. There is tons of knowledge in the industry around EDI and even older carrier systems support it. ANSI has defined the North American standard for -- 2 of 6 -- EDI and after that they helped define the UN/EDIFACT standard used in much of the rest of the world. Relatively Easy to Implement - because it is so well known and based on standards it is easier to implement than API. Every carrier I have worked with to date has EDI experts employeed. EDI Cons Performance - BN4L EDI uses SFTP and batch jobs to build the integration, and due to this it is much slower than API. What API can do in seconds EDI can do in minutes to hours. Functional Coverage - BN4L currently only supports EDI for Road tendering (FTL & LTL - 204, 990, 214, 210 & 997). There is no support for quotes (AKA Spot Bids) with EDI for Road as this process wasn't around when EDI standards were defined. Ocean booking EDI support will be rolled out slowly this year starting with the 300 in the March 2023 release. Air booking support is planned but not yet on the roadmap. Above shows our Freight Order APIs and EDI support for Road FTL / LTL. -- 3 of 6 -- Things Shippers Should Know and Consider Not all carriers can build an API integration even if they wanted to, they just aren't there yet. EDI is the best many of them can do. Most carriers can't support API integration for quotes/spot bids and will have to use the web portal to respond to these. There are some exceptions - but only the most technically sophisticated carriers can support this. The LTL industry by and large will not build API integrations, they will only do EDI. Maybe this will change in the future as API standards for LTL are being worked on. Things Carriers Should Know and Consider EDI is a great place to start for integration, but you should start thinking about how to take the next step to support API integration. The speed and functionality over API integration can be a differentiator. New processes that like quotes and external planning are only available for integration over API, and if you don't invest and move forward you could be left behind. Look at the FinTech industry did to banking, the same thing is already starting to happen with CarrierTech. Make sure to invest in your technology as it truly is the new battle ground for carriers. Consider joining a standards body that is defining industry API standards...these will only come about if those with deep industry knowledge make it happen. In Conclusion When it comes to shipper/carrier integrations EDI has dominated for decades and continues to be the most used integration in the industry, and BN4L will continue to grow its support for it. That said, there is no doubt that a well built API integration can be a differentiator in that it can perform orders of magnitude faster, and newer innovative processes like quotes/spot bids and external planning are only supported for integration over API. Carriers who wisely invest in a -- 4 of 6 -- Comments technology platform that can integrate over APIs can now and into the future will certainly have advantages over those who can only do EDI. SAP Business Network For Logistics - Road EDI Integration Tips and Tricks Jeff-Gebo Product and Topic Expert 2023 Jul 26 10:45 PM 16 Likes  12,622 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) provides collaboration capabilities for shippers and carriers - freight tendering, subcontracting, settlement, tracking and dock appointment scheduling can all be collaborated on. A carrier on our network can connect and transact with any shipper on the network. BN4L comes by default with a web portal that our carriers can use to collaborate with shippers they are connected to. Optionally, carriers can build an integration from BN4L to their own systems using EDI or API. If you haven’t yet read my blog on EDI vs API integration I highly recommend doing so. Over the past year and a half, I have worked with hundreds of carriers who are building these integrations, both EDI and API. Over the course of this work with carriers going the EDI integration route I have identified common issues and questions that they have. My hope is that the below list will assist in speeding up EDI integrations for new carrier integrations. Note: I work with North American carriers so I am focused on ANSI EDI, that said we also support EDIFACT for the rest of the world.   -- 1 of 10 -- EDI ANSI Common Issues & Questions 204 The first question I get from a carrier is always this: What are your ISA/GS IDs (AKA sender / receiver IDs)? In BN4L we use the LBN ID of the shipper and carrier. The LBN ID is a unique ID (10 digit numeric value) of the shipper and carrier the uniquely identifies them on the network. Each will typically have two of these. One for the test landscape and another for the production landscape. Like any good integrator you will first build and test your integration on the test landscape then move to production once everything has been successfully tested. Ok, then there is the second related question – what is the qualifier? Ours is “ZZ”. You can find all of this documented in our 204 Spec Guide. PRO TIP: Never download our guides, just bookmark the link – we are making improvements all the time and upgrade our guides regularly. 990 -- 2 of 10 -- The easiest of all the EDI inbound messages but almost everyone misses this one segment, you need to send the Sender System ID! Why? Because a shipper can possibly have multiple systems connected to their BN4L tenant and due to that we need the carrier to send back this segment so we can route the message to the proper system. If only I had a dollar for every time I emailed the below snippet, I could retire. LOL! Learn more in the 990 spec guide. ---------------------------- You are missing the following segment: N9*06*”Sender System ID”~ You can get the sender system ID value from the 204 segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ 210 This one is more complex – the most difficult of all the inbound messages. First you need to send back three N9 segments – the Sender System ID, the Bill From Party and the Purchasing Party. The Bill From Party and Purchase Party are the business partner IDs as maintained in the shippers system. If you don’t get these correct the invoice won’t process successfully. Sometimes carriers forget to send the C3 segment with the currency code. Most difficult about the 210 is how we require the L1 segments to be formatted. I’m not going to go into detail on that in this blog, I will create a separate one just for L1 segment. Suffice to say, take the advice I mention below about the L1 segment – again, I email this snippet out all the time to carriers trying to integrate with the 210: ---------------------------- You are missing the following segments: -- 3 of 10 -- N9*06*Sender System ID~ N9*12*BillFromParty~ N9*CN*PurchasingParty~ You can get these from the 204 in the following segments: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ L11*PurchasingParty*CN~ L11*BillFromParty*12~ With the 210 please pay special attention to how we format the L1 – look at the examples on page 30 of the 210 spec guide. PRO TIP: You need to ask the shipper you are integrating with which BN4L Charge Codes they support for your use case with them. They should be able to send you that list. 214 for Freight Collaboration Tracking (not GTT) This one isn’t too bad, but not used quite as much because a lot of our shippers choose a Visibility Provider (like Project44, FourKites or Shippeo to name a few) to get order tracking data. That said, more and more carriers are setting up the 214 with us…I imagine this will become more popular over time. In addition to the Sender System ID we need the Stop ID or Location ID. Stop ID is just 1, 2, 3 (depends on number of stops), or better yet send the Location ID which can be found in the 204. Below is the email snippet I send out regularly to carriers and as always the 214 Spec Guide which has examples is your friend. -- 4 of 10 -- ------------------------------- You are missing the following segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ You can get the sender system ID value from the 204 segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ You also need to send a Stop ID or Location ID. The location ID can be found in the 204 N1-04 position. Send as: L11*Location ID*LU~ 997 We currently only support the 997 for confirmation of the files you send to BN4L - these are the 990, 214 and 210. It is on our roadmap to support 997 confirmations for a 204 (hopefully will be delivered sometime this year). With our 997 we have one thing that needs to be known by carriers - that is the sender ISA / GS ID is "LBN". Why? Well because we did receive your file, but it may not have been routed all the way to the shipper's TM. This 997 only means that it was received by BN4L. (Why "LBN" and not "BN4L" well, BN4L used to be called Logistics Business Network, LBN for short). Summary -- 5 of 10 -- Comments EDI Integration can be easy if you consider these common issues and answers to common questions listed here. I’ve seen this integration setup as quickly as a day…I’ve also seen it take weeks. My hope is with this info we can get more carriers integrated in days. Feel free to ask any questions below on this in the comments. Happy integrating! PS - we now support the 300 and 301 for Ocean. Are you a carrier interested in this? Let me know! For further questions and feedback related to the blog, please check the Q&A area and feel free to post your questions in the link with the tag SAP Business Network for Logistics. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Application Help Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:36:52 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_FC_OPTION/185742008f2c477ca789b93675b0ec6c?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, a carrier can onboard onto the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, invoicing and milestone reporting. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration runs on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), utilizing one of the following infrastructures: Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia The data used in the solution is also stored in the respective data center. Information for shippers: Collaborative managed transactions supported in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are tailored to the relevant SAP backend systems. For freight collaboration scenarios, SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration offers out-of-the-box connectivity to shippers with the following systems: SAP Transportation Management (on-premise) or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition SAP Logistics Management For more information about supported releases, see SAP Note 2620322 . In addition, out-of-the box connectivity is delivered for truck carrier networks, including project44 for visibility services and B2B carrier connectivity for freight tendering and subcontracting. Selected digital freight forwarders support on-demand road transportation with real-time pricing and subcontracting. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Shipper Apps and APIs With SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, you as a shipper can use the apps to get started on the network, including connecting your systems (for example a transportation management system) to the network. Additionally, you can perform your daily tasks in the areas of dock appointment management, freight order tracking, freight settlement, and dispute handling.  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified.  Note These apps are also suitable for logistics service providers that are performing the role of a shipper. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use a new app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section. Shipper APIs As a shipper, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight contracting, freight booking, freight tracking, dock appointment scheduling, and freight settlement. For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/7ccd8fd6e75249b991c8d62706fe90ff.html. General Settings The General Settings app enables you as the shipper admin to configure the general settings related to freight collaboration at an ordering party level. You can also set up tolerance rules that would enable the settlement clerk at the shipper organization to auto-approve certain amounts by applying the tolerance rules to disputes created from invoices or self-billing documents. When an invoice contains discrepancies that would result in a dispute, you can define and assign tolerance ranges and tolerance groups so that you do not have to check each order manually. The system can then approve charge lines automatically. Lines that are not approved must be reviewed manually by the user. This app contains the following main areas: Define Appointment and Dispute Settings You can configure the appointment and dispute settings for an ordering party in this tab. For more information, see Appointment and Dispute Settings. Define Tolerance Range You can define the tolerance range itself by creating an upper limit and a lower limit. The tolerance values can be specified in either amounts (e.g. lower limit of EUR 10, upper limit of EUR 15) or percentages (e.g. lower limit of 2%, upper limit of 2%). Define Tolerance Groups Once you have defined the tolerance range, you can group them together. You can define item level tolerance ranges for each charge code. You can add a tolerance range for the rate amount and final amount for each charge code. You can also define the tolerance ranges for the total document amount proposed by the carrier. In this scenario, for each currency, you can specify the tolerance range. For more information on how tolerance is applied on dispute documents, see Applying Tolerance Check.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note You must specify a lower limit and an upper limit, either of which can be expressed as an amount or a percentage. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Appointment and Dispute Settings SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to configure the dock appointment and dispute settings for an ordering party. As part of the dock appointment settings, you can also define the guest user access settings. Guest User Access In the General Settings app, in the Define Appointment and Dispute Settings tab, you can choose the Guest Access button to define the type of URL you want to send to the guest carrier user. You can choose one of the following options: Dynamic URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is specific to the document you send to the carrier for dock appointment scheduling. The carrier can enter the document reference to view the document. Static URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is generic. The carrier can enter the following details and view the document: Document Type and ID Email ID User Name Company Name We recommend you to select the dynamic URL by default. If you select the static URL, anyone with the link and valid document reference can access the document. Ordering Party Settings To define the ordering party settings, in the General Settings app, in the Define Appointment and Dispute Settings tab, choose the Add Ordering Party button. Once you add an ordering party, you can define the following settings: Dock Appointment Scheduling You can enable one of the following settings for the dock appointment creation process in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system: On Freight Order Creation  Note The system applies the settings you specify here to all the ordering parties. Once you specify the above settings, the system displays the type of URL you have chosen on the header area in the tab view. In the detailed view, you cannot view this information. If you select the dynamic URL option and later change the setting to static URL, the guest user can use both the dynamic and static URLs to access the document. However, if you select the static URL and later change the setting to dynamic URL, the guest user can only use the latest dynamic URL to access the document.  Note The system only displays those ordering parties that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app with the object type as Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- The system creates an appointment when a freight order is created. In other words, the system creates an appointment for a freight order that is yet to be confirmed. On Freight Order Confirmation The system creates an appointment only when a freight order is confirmed. On Appointment API The system creates an appointment based on the appointment API and not on the freight order. If you select On Freight Order Creation or On Freight Order Confirmation, the system still allows you to create appointments using the Appointment Provider API (GenericAppointment_In). If you select On Appointment API, appointments can only be created using the API. Settlement Dispute Management in External System You can enable or disable dispute management in external system for freight orders and freight bookings. Enable for Freight Order When you enable this setting for freight orders, then the disputes created for the subsequent documents will be created in your external system. Enable for Freight Booking When you enable this setting for freight bookings, then the disputes created for the subsequent documents will be created in your external system. Enable Automatic Submission of Disputes You can enable or disable automatic approval of disputes. If you have enabled this setting, and if the dispute is within the specified tolerance range, the system automatically approves the disputes sent by your carrier. If the dispute is not within the specified tolerance range, you must manually approve the dispute. Note that if you have defined both document tolerance and item tolerance, then both tolerances must be within the specified tolerance range for the dispute to be automatically submitted. If you have defined only document tolerance or item tolerance, then the respective tolerance must be within the specified tolerance range for the dispute to be automatically submitted. Enable Mandatory Attachments for Invoice Submission You can enable or disable mandatory attachments during carrier invoice submission. If you enable this setting, during carrier invoicing, the carrier must mandatorily add attachments before submitting the document. If you disable this setting, adding an attachment is optional for the carriers. Enable Subsequent Invoice with Same Charge Type  Note To add an ordering party, you must have already created a location in the Manage Locations app with the Object Type as Business Partner.  Note It can take up to 15 minutes until any change is reflected in the carrier's Manage Invoices app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- You can enable or disable subsequent invoice with same charge type. When you enable this setting, the carrier can add a subsequent charge for a charge type which has already been invoiced. If you disable this setting, the carrier cannot add a subsequent charge. Reference Documents You can specify whether you want to send reference documents to external system as notes. If you enable this setting, you can also specify the note type for reference documents in the field that appears below. This note type that you specify here will be used to send the reference documents as a note. Enable Tax Code Validation When you enable this setting, if the carrier enters a tax code in the invoice, the system validates this tax code with the tax codes that you have maintained in the Assign Charge Codes app. Tolerance Group Assignment You can assign one tolerance group to each individual carrier that you have onboarded on the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics. When you assign a tolerance group to a carrier, the tolerance group should be sufficient for consumption in terms of charge lines and the respective currencies. For example, if you have a very good relationship with a particular carrier, you can define a group in which all the charge codes are automatically approved. Approval Conditions You can enable a multi-step dispute approval process within your organization before submitting the dispute to the carrier. A dispute document can either be approved in a single step by a basic user at the first level or sent to supervisors or managers at the next levels for review based on the settings that you specify. The additional approval steps are enabled only when the disputed amount exceeds the threshold amount or percentage specified the settings. Based on the range of the disputed amount, you can define multiple approver groups for various dispute amount ranges to approve the dispute. You can specify the approval conditions for an ordering party as follows: 1. Choose Add to add a new approval condition. Add Approver Conditions pane appears on the right. 2. In the Approver Group section, specify the following: Scenario Displays dispute scenario by default. Approver Group Specify the name of the approver group. The name that you specify here must be the same as you have specified in the user group in IAS Portal. You can assign all the users for this approver group to the IAS user group. For more information on assigning user groups, see Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users.  Note Use a note type that is different from the default note type as the system uses the default note type to send the carrier notes to your external system.  Note This is a mandatory field. You can specify alpha numeric values. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Notification Language Select a language, from the drop-down menu, in which you want to receive the email notification. An email notification is sent to the approvers in this group whenever a dispute requires their approval. Notification Emails Specify the email ID to which the email notification must be sent. You can specify multiple email IDs by choosing the add icon. Note that the system only sends email notifications about the dispute approval to these users. Not all these users may have the authorization to approve or reject the disputes. You must maintain those settings in the IAS portal. 3. In the Conditions section, specify the following: Currency Select the same currency that you have specified for the document currency, from the drop-down menu. Threshold Range Select a threshold amount or a threshold percentage from the drop-down menu. Specify a threshold amount or percentage as appropriate. Purchasing Group Specify the name of the purchasing group. Administrative Data Displays the administrative data such as created on, created by, changed on, and changed by. Applying Tolerance Check When a dispute is created or updated in the carrier tenant for a freight order or invoice and then sent to you for review, a tolerance check is applied based on your tolerance settings. You can enable tolerance for the entire document amount or the individual charge item amount. Tolerance Check Formula The system uses the following formulae to check whether the amounts are within the specified tolerance range: For Tolerance Amounts Do not specify commas and spaces. You can only specify _ (underscore) and – (hyphen) special characters.  Note For an ordering party, you must specify the same currency and threshold range factor (amount or percentage) across all approval conditions. In other words, when you create subsequent approval conditions, you must specify the same currency and threshold range factor (amount or percentage) that you specify in your first approval condition. You cannot enter the same combination of condition attributes in two approval groups. In other words, you cannot specify the same currency, threshold range, and purchasing group combination that you specified in the previous entry. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- If you have maintained the tolerance range in amounts, the system uses the following formulae for calculation: Freight Order Amount – Lower Tolerance Amount Freight Order Amount + Upper Tolerance Amount If the amount proposed by the carrier is in between the above values, then the tolerance check is approved. If the freight order amount is USD 50 and the upper limit is USD 5 and lower limit is USD 5, then if the carrier specifies the amount to be within USD 45(50-5) and USD 55(50+5) then it passes tolerance check. For Tolerance Percentages If you have maintained the tolerance range in percentages, the system uses the following formulae for calculation: Freight Order Amount – (Lower Tolerance Percentage * Freight Order Amount) Freight Order Amount + (Upper Tolerance Percentage * Freight Order Amount) If the amount proposed by the carrier is in between the above values, then the tolerance check is approved. For example, if the freight order amount is USD 50 and the upper limit is 5 % and lower limit is 5 %, then if the carrier specifies the amount to be within USD 47.5(50-2.5) and USD 52.5(50+2.5) then it passes tolerance check. Document Tolerances If you have defined document tolerances in your tolerance group for a carrier, a tolerance check is applied on the total document amount proposed by the carrier. In other words, if the carrier sends a disputed document to you and the total freight document amount proposed by the carrier on the header area falls within the defined tolerance range, then the system updates the information button on the header dispute status with this information. Item Tolerances If you have defined item tolerances in your tolerance group for a carrier, the system applies a tolerance check according to the following criteria: If the charge codes listed in a freight document are present in the defined tolerance group, the tolerance check is applied for those charge codes. If the charge codes are not specified in that group, no tolerance check is applied and you must approve those lines manually. For a charge code that matches the group, the currencies are then checked. In the General Settings app, the Rate Amount and the Final Amount, for example, can be maintained in different currencies. If the currencies match, a second check is applied according to a defined formula. For a given currency, you can maintain a limit as either an amount or a percentage, and different formulas are applied accordingly. If the carrier’s proposed value in the invoice lies within the start and end limits according to the respective formula, the charge line is considered to be within tolerance. Every rate amount and final amount that falls within the tolerance limit is assumed to be approved by the system’s tolerance check. The line is then marked with a green bar and receives the status Approved by tolerance check. This means you do not have to approve these lines manually. If the tolerance check does not meet your expectations, you can override it by clicking  (Edit)and entering your changes. If you do so, however, you must consider the following: If you edit the line, the tolerance check will not be applied to that line in subsequent rounds. (However, if you do not edit the line and it does not pass the tolerance check in the first round, the check can be applied in all subsequent rounds of the dispute life cycle process.) 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- If all the lines are approved by the tolerance check, the dispute status remains as For review. (It only changes to Resolved if you click Submit Dispute.) If a line is dependent on other lines and the other lines are approved by the tolerance check, the dependent line is not necessarily approved by the check unless it falls within the tolerance limits. If you add a new line, the same tolerance check is applicable. In this case, however, the freight order value is considered as 0. Only if it matches the currencies and falls within the tolerance limits is the new line also considered as approved by the tolerance check. Combination of Settings If you have specified the settings for both document tolerance and item tolerance, then the system checks the tolerances at both levels in the disputed document and updates the status as follows: For the charge lines within tolerance range, the status is updated as Approved by Tolerance Check. For the charge lines outside tolerance range, there is no status update. For the charge lines for which tolerance is not defined, there is no status update. On the header status, in the information button, a message is displayed whether the tolerance is within the set tolerance range or not. If you have specified the settings only for document tolerance or item tolerance, then the system checks the tolerances as appropriate based on your settings. Example You have specified the following settings in the tolerance group: Document Tolerance Amount Currency Tolerance Definition Selected Tolerance Range EUR Example1 10.00 EUR to 100.00 EUR Item Tolerance Amount Charge Code Rate Amount Tolerance Range Final Amount Tolerance Range ADMIN_FEE 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR INSPECTION_FEE 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR Freight document amount is EUR 100. If the carrier sends a disputed document to you, the system checks the tolerances at both levels in the document as you have maintained both document tolerance and item tolerance. If the total document amount proposed by carrier is within EUR 90 (100-10) to EUR 200 (100+100), the document tolerance check is approved. If both the rate amount and the final amount of the administration fee and inspection fee are within EUR 90 (100-10) to EUR 150 (100+50), then the system updates the status of these charge lines as Approved by Tolerance Check and the charge line is highlighted in green. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps, such as Docking Location Settings, in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see the Business Configuration section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems:  Note If the subsequent invoice contains a charge that is already invoiced, the subsequent invoice is not applicable for document tolerance. If the subsequent invoice contains a charge that is already invoiced, that charge is not applicable for item tolerance.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
