file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Business Working Hours This worksheet contains all the information in the gate Business Hours tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Gate reference Time period reference Start date End date Working days Start time End time Note that you can edit all the fields in this worksheet similar to the edit option in gate in the Manage Entities app. Upload Gates Microsoft Excel To upload the gates in a Microsoft Excel file, perform the following: 1. You can use the gates file that you previously downloaded using the Download option to edit the existing data. Alternatively, you can download the template by choosing Gate Excel Export Template option to add new gates. This template contains the same worksheets and columns similar to the downloaded gates Microsoft Excel file. However, it does not contain any data. Note that you can only use either the template or the downloaded file to upload into the system. 2. Upload the Excel file by choosing Gate Excel Upload . Upload entities dialog box appears. 3. Select the edited file that you want to upload from your computer and choose Proceed. The system displays the confirmation message indicating the number of gate entities that will be uploaded. It will also display the error log if some of the entities are in error state. You can download the error log to investigate the issue. 4. Choose Confirm to upload the entities. Displays whether the entities are uploaded. If they are uploaded, you can view them in the Gate tab in the app. For gate entities in active and inactive statuses, you can only edit the Contact Person, Phone Number, and Arrival Lead Time fields. All the other fields are non-editable similar to the edit option in gate in the Manage Entities app.  Note There are a few columns that are hidden in the worksheets. These columns contain technical information. You cannot edit these columns Adding of Enable Sharing option is currently not available in the Microsoft Excel file. You cannot edit the status of the gate in the Microsoft Excel file. You can only change the status in the Manage Entities app. You can only upload Microsoft Excel files with a maximum of 2500 entries. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 91 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Defining Yard Settings Yard settings define operational parameters such as business hours, gates, and docking locations, crucial for efficient yard management. To define the settings for a yard, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Yard tab on the left pane. 2. Choose the Add Yard button. The create yard pane appears on the right. a. Define settings for the following sections: b. Details c. Business Hours d. Gates e. Docking Locations 3. Choose Save to save the yard settings as a draft. Choose Save and Activate to activate the yard settings. Details Enter the following information in the details section: Location ID Select a location ID. You maintain location master data in the Manage Locations app. Time Zone Enter a time zone. Yard ID Specify a yard ID. Remarks You can enter the additional information about the yard in this section. Business Hours  Note The following fields cannot be changed any longer after the yard was activated: Yard ID Location ID Description Address Time Zone 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 92 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Choose the add icon in this section to add an entry of business hours. Enter the following information: Period Specify the duration for which the entry of business hours is valid. Working Days Specify the working days of the yard. Working Hours Specify the working hours for the specified working days. To add another entry of validity period, choose the add icon. You can create up to 10 entries per validity period. Gates Choose the add icon in this section to add entries of gates. The system displays the list of active gates in the same time zone that you have maintained in the Manage Entities app. You can select the gates that you want to add to the yard. Once you add one or more gates to the yard, you must use the Assign Default button to assign one of the inbound gates and one of the outbound gates as the default gate. Note that if you assign an inbound/outbound gate as the default gate, you need not assign any other gates as the default gate. If you do not assign the default gates, then the system does not allow you to activate the yard. Docking Locations Choose the add icon in this section to add entries of docking locations. The system displays the list of active docking locations in the same time zone that you have maintained in the Manage Entities app. You can select the docking locations that you want to add to the yard. Viewing a Yard Displays detailed information about a yard's status, location, business hours, gates, and docking locations. To view the yard settings, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Yard tab on the left pane. 2. Enter the yard ID in the search bar on the left pane to search for a specific yard. 3. Choose a yard from the results.  Note You can add only one entry of business hours for a yard.  Note The system displays active gates in the same time zone that are either shared with yards or active gates in the same time zone that are yet to be associated with a yard.  Note The system displays only the active docking locations in the same time zone. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The system displays the detail view of the settings on a right pane. The detail view consists of a header and other sections. Header The header section displays the following information: Yard ID Location ID Yard Icon Displays the yard icon. Also displays a shared sign on this icon when a yard has enabled sharing with business partners. You can view the sharing details by choosing this icon. The system displays the Yard ID, Location ID, Shared By, and Permissions. Status Displays one of the following statuses: Draft This status appears after you create a yard and choose the Save button. You can delete a yard only when it is in a draft status. Active This status appears when you activate a draft or an inactive yard or when you choose the Save and Activate button while creating a new yard. Inactive This status appears when you deactivate a yard by choosing the Deactivate button. Note that deactivation may take some time and you may have to refresh your page to get the updated status. You cannot deactivate a yard that is associated with active gates. Decommissioned This status appears when you close a yard by choosing the Decommission button. You can only decommission yards that are in the inactive status. Once you decommission a yard, you cannot activate it or perform any actions. Details The details section displays the following information: Location ID Description Displays the location description. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Address Displays the location address. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Time Zone 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Displays the time zone of the location. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Yard ID Remarks Displays additional information about the yard in this section. Share Entity You can share the yard details with your business partner. Based on the settings you provide here, the business partner can either view or view and edit the yard details. This section displays the following information: Created By Displays the details of who created the yard sharing. Share Entity With Displays the business partners with whom the yard has been shared with. Permissions Displays whether the business partner can only view or edit the yard settings. Business Hours This section displays the business hours of the yard. This section displays the following information: Period Displays the duration for which the entry of business hours is valid. Working Days Displays the working days of the yard. Working Hours Displays the working hours for the specified working days. Gates Displays the list of gates in the same time zone that are associated with the yard. This section displays the following information for each entry: Gate ID  Note You can only share active yards with your business partners. That is, when you create a yard, save, and activate the setting, you can edit the yard settings and add sharing details. As a prerequisite, you must establish a relationship with the business partner (shipper) with whom you want to share your yard. To do so, use the Invite Business Partners app and add a new invitee as a shipper. The shipper must operate in the same data center as you. For more information, see Add New Business Partners. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Description Direction Working Hours Default Gate Displays whether the gate is a default gate Docking Locations Displays the list of docking locations that are associated with the yard. This section displays the following information for each entry: Docking Location ID Description Working Hours Uploading and Downloading Yards SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration enables you to simplify the entity management process especially when you have lot of entities to be processed. You can view, edit, and upload entities using a Microsoft Excel file. This feature enables you to work on multiple entries simultaneously thereby saving a lot of time. You can download and upload the entities in Microsoft Excel format. In the Yard tab, in the worklist area on the left, you can view the Excel button. When you choose this button, you can select one of the following options: Download You can download all the yard entities in Microsoft Excel. Upload You can upload the edited Microsoft Excel template containing the yards that you want to add. Export Template You can download this Microsoft Excel template file to add the yards and upload it in the system. Download Yards Microsoft Excel The downloaded yards Microsoft Excel file contains the following worksheets: Yard This worksheet contains all the information in the yard Details tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Yard reference As the yard information has been split across different worksheets in this Microsoft Excel file, the system has created this reference ID in the Microsoft Excel file. When you switch to another worksheet, you can use this reference ID to logically map the relevant data. Yard ID 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Location ID Time zone Business Working Hours This worksheet contains all the information in the yard Business Hours tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Yard reference Time period reference Start date End date Working days Start time End time Note that you can edit all the fields in this worksheet similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Docking Location Association This worksheet contains the associations between the yard and docking locations. You can view the Yard Reference and the associated Docking Location Reference in this worksheet. Note that you can edit both the above fields are editable. Docking Location This worksheet contains the Docking Location Reference, Docking Location ID, and Description. Note that all the fields in this worksheet are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Gate Association This worksheet contains the associations between the yard and gate. You can view the Yard Reference and the associated Gate Reference in this worksheet. Note that you can edit both the above fields are editable. Gate This worksheet contains the Gate Reference, Gate ID, Description, and Direction. Note that all the fields in this worksheet are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Upload Yards Microsoft Excel To upload the yards in a Microsoft Excel file, perform the following: 1. You can use the yards file that you previously downloaded using the Download option to edit the existing data.  Note For yard entities in draft status, you can edit all the above fields. For yard entities in active and inactive statuses, all the above fields are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Alternatively, you can download the template by choosing Yard Excel Export Template option to add new yards. This template contains the same worksheets and columns similar to the downloaded yards Microsoft Excel file. However, it does not contain any data. Note that you can only use either the template or the downloaded file to upload into the system. 2. Upload the Excel file by choosing Yard Excel Upload . Upload entities dialog box appears. 3. Select the edited file that you want to upload from your computer and choose Proceed. The system displays the confirmation message indicating the number of yard entities that will be uploaded. It will also display the error log if some of the entities are in error state. You can download the error log to investigate the issue. 4. Choose Confirm to upload the entities. Displays whether the entities are uploaded. If they are uploaded, you can view them in the Yard tab in the app. Manage Dock Appointments You, as a shipper, can use this app to manage (view, edit, cancel) the dock appointments that carriers have booked for loading or unloading services in the docking locations of your organization. In this app, you can also apply instance-based authorization. This helps you to restrict the shippers who can access the dock appointments of a certain docking location to only those that are involved in the management of that location. The main features of this app include: Reschedule a dock appointment Cancel a dock appointment Create a dock appointment Reserve a time slot Docking Locations You can view all docking locations in the overview page. The system displays the details of each docking location in a card format. You can filter the docking locations based on the Location ID, Description, and Address.  Note There are a few columns that are hidden in the worksheets. These columns contain technical information. You cannot edit these columns. Adding of Enable Sharing option is currently not available in the Microsoft Excel file. You cannot edit the status of the yard in the Microsoft Excel file. You can only change the status in the Manage Entities app. You can only upload Microsoft Excel files with a maximum of 2500 entries.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Each docking location card displays the following information: Location ID Displays the location ID of the docking location. Note that the system retrieves the docking location details that you have created in the Docking Location Settings app. Description Displays the description for the docking location that you have specified in the Docking Location Settings app. Address Displays the address of the docking location that you have specified in the Docking Location Settings app. Booked Appointments Displays the number of future active appointments booked in this docking location in the current week. Ready for Booking Displays the number of documents that are ready for booking an appointment in the current week. Current Week Slot Utilization Displays the number of appointments in this docking location for the current week. Detail View (Manage Dock Appointments) The detail view of a docking location consists of a calendar view and a table view. Calendar View When you choose a docking location in the worklist page, the system by default opens the calendar of appointments for the docking location. You can view the appointment calendar for the entire docking location in the All tab. You can also view the individual appointment calendar for each loading point available in the selected docking location by choosing the various tabs with the loading point ID. Non- working hours are displayed as greyed-out in 15-minute intervals, based on the validity period of the loading point. You can switch between the day, week, and month view for the loading point calendars. Based on the view that you choose, the system displays the appointments for the specific day, week, or month. Note that the system applies this setting across all the loading point calendars in the docking location. The system displays all the appointments for the day along with the freight order details. Note that in the month view of the calendar, if there is no space to display all the appointments, the system displays some of the appointments in a dialog box. You can also resize this dialog box as desired. In the calendar view, you can view an icon in the upper right corner of the calendar. When you choose this icon, the system displays the details of calendar and appointments color coding. The following are the descriptions of various icons used in the calendar view. Icon Description Arrival 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Icon Description Check-In Begin Check-In On Hold Checked In Loading Unloading Executed Overdue Grouped Blocked Time You can drag and drop an appointment in the calendar to reschedule an appointment. You can use the static search option on the header area to search for booked appointments based on a given freight order ID, appointment ID, or reference document ID. The search is globally conducted for all loading points in the All tab, and separately conducted in the individual appointment calendar for each loading point. The number of matches found in the search is indicated in parentheses, like (1), at the end of the tab name, and the best appointment match is displayed in the Maintain Appointment view. If you have, for example, several appointments that are based on the same freight order, you get several hits for the same freight order, and the system randomly selects one appointment to be displayed as the best match.  Note You can drag and drop to reschedule only those appointments which have time slots in multiples of 30 minutes (for example, 9:00 – 10:00 or 9:30 – 10:30). If the time slots are not in multiples of 30 minutes (for example, 8:45 – 9:45 or 8:15 – 9:15), then you cannot drag and drop to reschedule appointment. However, you can select the appointment and change the time using input boxes. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.title: SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration_BNL_01_Part11
file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Appointments that are not booked or that were canceled, are not displayed in the calendar and therefore cannot be found by the search. You can create a new appointment for the docking location by choosing Maintain Appointment. You can block a time slot for the loading point of a docking location by choosing Block Time. Table View From the calendar view, you can switch to the table view by choosing the table icon in the top right corner. You can filter appointments that are displayed in the Active Appointments and Ready for Booking tabs based on Freight Order, Ordering Party, Carrier, Planned Activity Date, and Appointment Date (as the standard filters). The filters are combined using 'AND'. For example, if you want to search for blocks (blocked time slots), use only the Appointment Date filter and clear the Planned Activity Date filter. Blocks do not have an appointment date. In the table view, you can view the details of the docking location. You can filter appointments that are displayed in the Active Appointments and Ready for Booking tabs based on Freight Order, Ordering Party, Carrier, Planned Activity Date, and Appointment Date (as the standard filters). The system displays the active appointments and the orders that are ready for booking in a worklist view. Active Appointments You can view all the active appointments for the selected docking location. You can filter the appointments based on the loading points of the docking location. When searching for an appointment, you must provide a range either in the Planned Activity Date field or in the Appointment Date field. You can also provide date ranges in both fields. For each active appointment, the system displays the following details: Appointment/Ordering Party Displays the appointment number, ordering party details, and the status of the appointment. The system displays one or more of the following statuses: Check-In Begin Check-In On Hold Checked In Load Begin Load End Unload Begin Unload End Executed Unload Begin - Delayed Load Begin - Delayed For more information about setting statuses, see Appointment Details under Reporting Events. Loading Point Displays the name of the loading point 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 101 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Freight Order ID License Plate Delivery ID Reference Documents Displays the reference document type and the reference document ID Carrier Displays the carrier details Appointment Date Start Time End Time Planned Activity Date Activity Type Displays the type of activity such as loading, unloading, or both Gate ID Gate Location and Description Planned Check-In Time Created By Created On Changed By Changed On Ready for Booking You can view details of the orders that are ready for booking and the appointment requests created by the API. You can view the orders for which there are no appointments in the Not Booked tab. You can view the orders for which there are canceled appointments in the Canceled tab. You can view all the orders in the All tab. When searching for an appointment, you must provide a range in the Planned Activity Date field. For each order that is ready for booking, the system displays the following details: Ordering Party/Reference Document Displays the ordering party ID and the details of the reference document for which the appointment has been created. You can view the reference document type and the reference document ID.  Note You can control the fields that are displayed in the table by choosing the settings icon. The system displays DST STARTS when the day light savings time begins and DST ENDS when the day light savings time ends. You can export this table into a spreadsheet by choosing the export to spreadsheet icon. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Reference Documents When you choose the number of reference documents on the worklist, you can view the type and ID for each reference document. Appointment Status Displays whether the appointment is Not Booked or Canceled. Carrier Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time Carrier Booking Cut-Off Reference Document Source Note that you can control the fields that are displayed in the table by choosing the settings icon. You can select an order and create a new appointment for the order by choosing Maintain Appointment. You can select an order and block a time slot for the order by choosing Block Time. You can export this table into a spreadsheet by choosing the export to spreadsheet icon. Appointment Details The appointment details page consists of the header area and multiple tabs. On the header area, you can view the carrier’s name and the reference document details. You can report events by choosing Report Events. When you choose Manage, you can select whether you want to Edit, Reschedule, or Cancel the appointment. Note that the Reschedule button is visible only in appointments that are reschedulable. That is only when the appointment status is Overdue, Arrival Delayed, or Check-In Canceled. The appointment contains information categorized various sections. Information The system displays the following information under this section: General You can view the following details: Ordering Party Activity Type Reference Documents Reference Document Source Dangerous Goods If the ordering party has provided dangerous goods information, then the system displays Yes. When you choose Yes, the system opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. Other Details 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 103 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Customs Relevant Note that the system displays this field only if the ordering party has maintained this information in their external system. Combined Traffic Note that the system displays this field only if the ordering party has maintained this information in their external system. Incoterm Displays the Incoterm code. You can find the list of standard Incoterm codes supported by SAP Business Network for Logistics here: Incoterm Descriptions. Note that the system displays this field only if the ordering party has maintained this information in their external system. Incoterm Location Displays the location in SAP Business Network for Logistics or the Incoterm location retrieved from the external system. Note that the system displays this field only if the ordering party has maintained this information in their external system. If the location is maintained in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system tries to retrieve the description from the Manage Locations app under Location Details Description . If the location is not maintained in the Manage Locations app, the system displays the incoterm location description retrieved from the external system (for example, TM). Exception: In the Self-Book Dock Appointments app for carriers, the Incoterm Location will always be set to the incoterm location retrieved from the external system (for example, TM). Country of Final Destination Note that the system displays this field only in those appointments that are created through appointment APIs. Booking Details The system displays the following information: Docking Location Loading Point Displays the loading point details for the appointment. When you maintain an appointment from a loading point calendar, the system prefills this field with the respective loading point. Remarks Display additional information that was maintained for a loading point. Planned Start Date and Time Planned End Date and Time Appointment Start Date and Time Appointment End Date and Time Business Hours Preferred Slots (requested dates or acceptable dates) 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 104 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- For more information about the values and their origin, see Integration of Dock Appointment Scheduling with Freight Orders and Provider API for Dock Appointment Scheduling. Active Vehicle Resource You can view the active vehicle resource details such as Transport Means Type, Vehicle Category Code, Vehicle Type Code, and Vehicle Resource ID. Driver Details You can view the driver details such as Driver Name / Language, Additional Driver Name, and Driver Phone Number. Resource Details You can view the License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck), Truck ID, and Trailer ID. Administrative Details You can view the administrative details such as Created By, Created On, Changed By, and Changed On. Guest User You can view the guest user details such as Name, Company Name, and Email ID. Reported Events You can view all events reported by you in the Manage Dock Appointments app and Manage Gate Operations app. You can also view all events reported by the carrier in their Freight Orders for Reporting app. You can view the following information for each event: Event Type Event Date and Time Comment Reference Document You can view the reference document details such as reference document type and reference document ID, stop details, and arrival and departure date and time. Stops Displays the visual representation of the freight order execution flow with the source location, intermediate stop locations, and destination location. You can see the appointment ID created in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the expected dates for departure and arrival, and the activity type performed for the appointment, such as loading or unloading. When you choose a stop, the system displays the following stop details in a dialog box: Arrival Date and Time Displays the expected arrival date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the ExpectedArrivalDateTime field. Departure Date and Time Displays the expected departure date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the ExpectedDepartureDateTime field. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 105 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Requested Start Date and Time Displays the requested start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. Acceptable Start Date and Time Displays the acceptable start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the AcceptableLoadingDateTimePeriod and AcceptableUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. Requested End Date and Time Displays the requested end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and/or RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. Acceptable End Date and Time Displays the acceptable end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. This comes from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or Transportation Management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the AcceptableLoadingDateTimePeriod and/or AcceptableUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. The following Appointment Details are displayed for all appointments created in SAP Business Network for Logistics but not for the currently displayed appointment and not for external appointments: Appointment ID Displays the appointment ID if the appointment was created by SAP Business Network for Logistics . You can use this ID to search for the appointment in its corresponding docking location in the Manage Dock Appointments app. Appointment Start Date and Time Displays the start date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Appointment End Date and Time Displays the end date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Cargo You can view the cargo details such as follows: Cargo Item Displays the description of the cargo item. Type Displays whether the cargo item is a package, product, or a container. Logistical Details Displays the quantity, gross weight, gross volume, and dimensions. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 106 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Equipment Details Displays the equipment type and equipment group. Reference Documents Displays the reference document details. Special Requirements Displays the following: Dangerous Goods The system displays the dangerous goods information that you provided in the freight order in the Cargo section by choosing Yes in the Dangerous Goods column. This opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. Temperature Requirements Other Details Displays the following: Over-Dimensional Non-Stackable High Value Notes You can enter additional information in this section. You can also view the notes added by the carrier. Attachments You can upload attachments in this section. You can also view the attachments uploaded by the carrier. Reporting Events You can report events for confirmed appointments. When you navigate to the details page of the appointment, you can choose the Report Events button to report events. If the appointment contains the activity type loading, you can report the start date and time of loading and the end date and time of loading. You can also report a delay for the loading start event. You can specify a delay date and time, delay reason, and comments. Similarly, if the appointment contains the activity type unloading, you can report the start date and time of unloading and the end date and time of unloading. Rescheduling an Appointment  Note The Executed status is only set in the following cases: Loading end or unloading end is directly reported in the Manage Dock Appointments app. The checkout in the related gate logbook was completed in the Manage Gate Operations app. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration does not receive status updates from external systems. Outside the Dock Appointment Scheduling apps, the status can only be manually reported using the Freight Orders for Reporting app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 107 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- You can directly reschedule an appointment by choosing Manage and Reschedule on the details page of the appointment. The system also displays the Reschedule button on the worklist page and on the warning message that is displayed on the Information tab in the appointment details page. Note that this Reschedule button appears only on appointments that are reschedulable with the appointment status as Overdue or Arrival Delayed. When you choose Reschedule, the system displays the Reschedule Appointment dialog box. The system displays the following information: Appointment ID Ordering Party Loading Point Appointment Date Available Time Slots You can modify the loading point, appointment date, and available time slots and you can reschedule the appointment. You can select whether you want to update all appointments in the group. Note that the system selects this option by default. You can choose NO if you do not want to update all appointments in the group. Maintaining a Dock Appointment Context In most cases, carriers maintain dock appointments for freight orders. However, there are certain scenarios, where you as a shipper may have to maintain dock appointments, for example, when the Carrier Booking Cut-Off Time for the freight order has passed. The Manage Dock Appointments app provides shippers with the flexibility to maintain a dock appointment for a certain freight order. To maintain a dock appointment, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. Select a docking location from the Docking Location table. The dock calendar for the docking location appears. You can also switch to the table view by choosing the table icon. 2. If you are in the calendar view, perform the following: a. Choose Maintain Appointment. The Select Order for Appointment dialog box appears. You can filter the list by Reference Document ID, Appointment Status, Carrier, Arrival Date and Time, and Departure Date and Time. b. Select the order for which you want to maintain an appointment. Maintain appointment pane appears on the right. 3. If you are in the table view, perform the following: a. Navigate to the Ready for Booking tab. b. Select the order for which you want to maintain an appointment and choose Maintain Appointment. Maintain appointment pane appears on the right. 4. Enter the following details: Loading Point (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available) Available Time Slots Note that if you have disabled the time slot option for a loading point in the Manage Entities app, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 108 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- If you have enabled the Restrict Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots and the Use Derived Appointment Duration options in the Manage Entities app, the Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots and Derived Appointment Duration fields are displayed. For more information, see Defining Loading Point Settings. Preferred Slots (shows the requested dates and acceptable dates) For more information about the values and their origin, see Integration of Dock Appointment Scheduling with Freight Orders and Provider API for Dock Appointment Scheduling. Reference Documents Driver Details (Optional) Resource Details (Optional) 5. If there is any additional information about the appointment, enter it in the Notes section. Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. We recommend you to avoid entering sensitive personal data. 6. If there are any attachments that you want to add to the appointment, choose the Add button under the Attachments section. You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files of the formats: jpg, jpeg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, tiff, tiff-fx Image files less than 6MB file size Document files less than 5MB file size File name less than 150 characters including file extension 7. Choose Maintain. Results The system maintains a dock appointment for the order. Maintaining a Grouped Appointment When you select a docking location in the calendar view and switch to the table view, you can select two or more documents from the Ready for Booking tab and maintain multiple appointments in a single group with the same time slot. Note that the system enables you to create a grouped appointment only when the following attributes of the selected documents are same: Location Loading Point (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available) Activity Type Transport Means Description Transport Means Type Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time To maintain multiple appointments in a single group, proceed as follows: 1. Select two or more documents with the similar attributes from the Ready for Booking tab and choose Maintain Appointment. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 109 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- The system creates a grouped appointment. Note that the system displays a confirmation message to notify you that the system creates a grouped appointment and not individual appointments for each document. As of now, you can only select up to 20 documents to create a grouped appointment. 2. You can view grouped appointments in the Grouped Appointments tab. You can perform the following: You can add or remove documents here. When you choose Add, the system displays the list of documents that contain similar attributes. You can select the documents and choose Add to Group. You can choose the appointment ID to switch to a different appointment that is not the current appointment. 3. On the Scheduling tab, specify the Loading Point and Date (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available). 4. Depending on the duration of the loading or unloading activity, choose one or more consecutive time slots from the Time Slot list. Note that if you have disabled the time slot option for a loading point in the Manage Entities app, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. If you have enabled the Restrict Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots and the Use Derived Appointment Duration options in the Manage Entities app, the Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots and Derived Appointment Duration fields are displayed. For more information, see Defining Loading Point Settings. 5. On the Information tab, enter the following under Driver Details: Driver Name Driver Phone Number Additional Driver Name Additional Driver Phone Number 6. On the Information tab, enter the following under Resource Details: License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck) Truck ID Trailer ID 7. Choose Maintain. Results A grouped appointment has been maintained for documents. You can find this appointment on the Active Appointments table. From there, you can access the appointment and view the details. You can also edit or cancel the appointment from there. When you edit or cancel, you can choose whether you want to edit or cancel only the current appointment or all the appointments in the group. Blocking Time Slot You can block one or more of time slots for a selected loading point. The system allows you to configure the reservation capacity, thereby allowing you to either fully block or partially block a time slot.  Note Once you maintain the grouped appointment, you can edit the grouped appointment and add notes and attachments. Note that when you do so, the notes and attachments are added only to the current appointment and not all the appointments in the group. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 110 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Block Time To block time slots, proceed as follows: 1. Select a docking location from the Docking Location table. The dock calendar for the docking location opens. You can also switch to the table view by choosing the table icon. 2. If you are in the calendar view, choose Block Time. If you are in the table view, you can choose Block Time from either Active Appointments tab or Ready for Booking tab. In both the views, block time details pane appears on the right. 3. In the Block Time dialog box, specify the following fields: Description Start Date and Time End Date and Time Disable Appointment Booking Specify whether you want to disable appointment booking only for the carriers or for all. If you select For All, both you and the carriers cannot book appointments during the blocked time. If you select For Carriers, only the carriers cannot book an appointment during the blocked time. The blocked time will be available for you to book an appointment. Max. Capacity When the Max. Capacity toggle is enabled, the maximum capacity is blocked for this loading point, and the loading point capacity is hidden because it is no longer relevant. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Maximum Capacity Blocker . Including Overbooking When the Include Overbooking toggle is enabled, the capacity maintained under Overbooking Limit is blocked for this loading point. Loading Point/Capacity Specify the loading points for which the time slot must be reserved and the corresponding capacity to be blocked. 4. Choose Save.  Note Duration The minimum duration when adding a block is 5 minutes, and the maximum duration is 31 days. Capacity Check If a blocker or appointment already exists, you can only block the remaining capacity, not the maximum capacity. The capacity to be blocked must always be less than or equal to the maximum capacity of the loading point validity period. If a new blocker exceeds the maximum capacity, it cannot be created. To resolve this, you can either reduce the capacity of the blocker or cancel existing blockers or appointments.  Note 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 111 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Results The system blocks the specified capacity for the specified time in the selected loading points. Note that neither you nor the carrier can book an appointment in the blocked time slot. Release Blocked Time Slot To release blocked time slots, click to open a reserved time slot on the dock calendar and then choose Release. If you have created a block for multiple loading points, you can release all blocks created in one go if you choose Release All instead of releasing each time slot individually. In the Manage Dock Appointments app, when you release a single block from a recurring block series, this does not change the recurring block series in the Manage Entities app. Rescheduling a Dock Appointment The Manage Dock Appointments shows you the dock calendar for each docking location of your organization. The calendar visualizes the dock appointments booked at the loading points and the downtimes. You can easily reschedule dock appointments on the calendar page. This also automatically notifies the corresponding carrier about the appointment change. You can reschedule a dock appointment by one of the following ways: Drag-And-Drop 1. Click a docking location on the Docking Location table. The dock calendar of the docking location opens. 2. Locate the appointment that you want to reschedule. You may need to navigate through weeks to locate an appointment that is not displayed in the current one. 3. Drag-and-drop the appointment to the desired time slot. Manual Edit 1. Click a docking location on the Docking Location table. The dock calendar of the docking location opens. 2. Locate the appointment that you want to reschedule. You may need to navigate through weeks to locate an appointment that is not displayed in the current one. You can block the time for a loading point that has been shared with multiple docking locations. When you do so, the system blocks the entire capacity of the loading point for the blocked period across all the docking locations with which the loading point has been shared. If the docking locations that share the loading point are in the same tenant, then the user can release the block. If the docking locations that share the loading point are in different tenants, then only the user who created the time block can release the same.  Note In case multiple people are working in the dock calendar, you can use the Refresh button to retrieve an up-to-date view of the calendar. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 112 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- 3. Double-click the appointment. The details page of the appointment opens. 4. Modify the following fields of the appointment. Loading Point Appointment Start Date and Time Appointment End Date and Time 5. (Optional) You can also modify the driver information of the appointment during rescheduling. 6. Choose Save. Result The dock appointment is rescheduled and an email notification will be sent to the corresponding carrier. Canceling a Dock Appointment To cancel a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click a docking location on the Docking Location table. The dock calendar of the docking location opens. 2. Use the search bar to locate the appointment that you want to cancel. You can also navigate through weeks to locate an appointment that is not displayed in the currently one. 3. Double-click the appointment. The details page of the appointment opens. 4. Choose Cancel Appointment on the upper-right corner of the details page. Result The dock appointment is canceled and an email notification will be sent to the corresponding carrier. Manage Gate Operations As a gate operations manager, you can use this app to view all the freight orders and appointments that are ready to check-in and checkout of the yard. You can find the gate logbook details of the vehicle that arrives at the yard. You can find and verify the details of the appointments and freight orders that are part of this vehicle and perform the check-in process. Once the vehicle checks-in, the system updates the relevant documents. Similarly, you can also find the gate logbook details of the vehicles that leave the yard. You can find and verify the details of the appointments and freight orders that are part of this vehicle and perform the checkout process. Once the vehicle checks-out, the system updates the relevant documents. Prerequisites To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Gate Logbook 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 113 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The gate logbook contains all the freight orders and appointments that are part of the check-in vehicle. As you perform check-in and checkout processes for a vehicle, the system combines the associated documents as a single gate logbook. The system creates a gate logbook when the carrier updates the vehicle license plate details for the associated freight orders and appointments, either during confirmation or appointment booking. If the carrier has not updated the vehicle license plate details, the system creates a gate logbook during the check-in process when the gate operations clerk updates the vehicle license plate details. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- When a carrier confirms an appointment without entering the vehicle license plate number, the system creates a corresponding gate logbook in the Manage Gate Operations app without a vehicle license plate number. The carrier has confirmed two or more appointments without a vehicle license plate number and the carrier executes these appointments in a single vehicle resource. In this scenario, the gate operator can now create a consolidated gate logbook for multiple gate logbooks corresponding to these appointments and perform check-in in the Manage Gate Operations app. Once the system creates a consolidated gate logbook, the individual logbooks are canceled automatically, and the system updates the associated external systems, gates, yards, and business partners with this updated gate logbook ID through API. Example The carrier confirms an appointment APT11. The system creates a corresponding gate logbook GLB11 in the Manage Gate Operations app. Similarly, the carrier confirms an appointment APT22. The system creates a corresponding gate logbook GLB22. The carrier executes appointments APT11 and APT22 in the same vehicle resource. When the vehicle arrives at the gate, the gate operator is aware of the appointments and gate logbooks associated with this vehicle. The gate operator selects the associated gate logbooks and chooses Start Check-In. The gate operator enters the following information and begins the check-in process: Check-In Gate ID Vehicle License Plate Country or Region of Registration Check-In Date and Time The system now creates a consolidated gate logbook GLB33 and cancels the previously created gate logbooks GLB11 and GLB22. The system sends this information to the associated external systems, gates, yards, and business partners through API. The system uses the message code 11200 to send a message that gate logbook GLB11 and GLB22 are canceled as the license plate number was updated and that the user must refer to the new gate logbook GLB33. Enabling Dock Appointment Scheduling for Guest Users SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to interact and schedule appointments with customers and carriers who are not onboarded as business partners in SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a shipper, when you enable your customers to pick up orders from your warehouse, you can associate with both customers who are onboarded and who are not onboarded. When you request for an appointment using the appointment request API, the system sends the appointment request with the email address of your customer or consignee. If the customer or consignee is not onboarded in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system creates an appointment and sends this appointment to the guest customer in an email notification. The guest customer can sign in using the guest URL and can either assign carriers or can decide to execute the transportation on their own. If the guest customer decides to execute the transportation on their own, then they can directly book an appointment. However, if they decide to outsource the transportation to a carrier, then the user can provide the email address of the carrier in the Assign Carrier section available in the guest user UI. When the customer provides the email address, SAP Business Network for Logistics receives the information and sends an email notification to the guest carrier user. The guest carrier user receives an email notification to book an appointment. When the user books an appointment, the system creates a confirmed dock appointment and sends it to your external transportation system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 127 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- For more information on how the customer or carrier can use the guest user URL, see Maintaining a Dock Appointment (Guest User). In the General Settings app, in the Define Appointment and Dispute Settings tab, you can choose the Guest User Access button to define the type of URL you want to send to the guest carrier user. Dynamic URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is specific to the document you send to the carrier for dock appointment scheduling. The carrier can enter the document reference to view the document. Static URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is generic. The carrier can enter the following details and view the document: Document Type and ID Email ID User Name Company Name We recommend you to select the dynamic URL by default. If you select the static URL, anyone with the link and valid document reference can access the document. For more information, see Appointment and Dispute Settings. For more information on the appointment API implementation considerations, see the Guest User Access section in Provider API for Dock Appointment Scheduling. Carrier's automated visibility data (including real-time location, estimated ETA (expected time of arrival), and time of event completion) from a supported visibility provider, if available. Note that this app has been deprecated and will be sunset shortly. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution.  Note Only those business partners who are onboarded in SAP Business Network for Logistics have an LBN ID. The guest carrier user or the guest customer will not have an LBN ID as they are not onboarded in SAP Business Network for Logistics.  Note If you select the dynamic URL option and later change the setting to static URL, the guest user can use both the dynamic and static URLs to access the document. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- The following table provides descriptions of the attributes that can be displayed in the Freight Documents list. Execution Status, Process Status, and Event Status The following describes the concepts of execution status, process status, and event status of a freight document. Execution Status Execution status shows the execution progress of a freight document. See the below table for status description. Execution Status Description Ready for Execution When a freight document is set to ready for transportation execution in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system, the execution status is Ready for Execution in the Track Freight Movement app. This is the original execution status of a freight document. Execution Started When the visibility provider reports an event at the source location, the execution status changes to Execution Started. In Transit When the visibility provider reports a departure, the execution status changes to In Transit. Arrived at Intermediate Location When the visibility provider reports an arrival at an intermediate location, the execution status changes to Arrived at Intermediate Location. Arrived at Destination When the visibility provider reports an arrival at the destination location, the execution status changes to Arrived at Destination. Executed When the visibility provider reports an event that matches the last expected event, for example, arrived at destination, configured in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system, the execution status changes to Executed. Process Status The Track Freight Movement app tracks business process for each freight document. The status of business process is determined by the status of the most recently occurred event within the process. See the below table for process status description. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 134 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Process Status Description As Planned The original status of a process. Early When an actual event is reported to occur earlier than the expected time window*, the process status changes to Early. Late When an actual event is reported to occur later than the expected time window*, the process status changes to Late. Overdue When the expected time window* for a planned event is overdue, but no actual event has been reported, the process status changes to Overdue. Delayed When a Delay event is reported, the process status changes to Delayed. * The expected time window is a time period between the earliest and latest expected business or technical date and time. By default, the earliest time is 10 minutes before the planned event time and the latest is 10 minutes after the planned event time. If you want to change the default, contact your system administrator to maintain SAP BAdI /SCMTMS/TOR_SE_TRCKPR_OUT. Event Status The Track Freight Movement app tracks business process for each freight document, and the business process includes planned and unplanned events. Each event has a status, as described below. Event Status Description Planned The original event status. Reported On Time The event has been reported and the reported event time is within the expected time window*. Reported Early The event has been reported and the reported event time is earlier than the expected time window*. Reported Late The event has been reported and the reported event time is later than the expected time window*. Overdue When there is no actual event reported within the expected time window* for a planned event, the event status changes to Overdue. Delayed When it is estimated that a planned event cannot be executed on time, a Delay event can be reported as a reference to the original planned event, and the status of the original event changes to Delayed. The Delay event itself is shown in the execution flow and map view with the event status Unplanned. If the delay is dismissed, which means the expected event can be executed on time based on new estimation, then the status of the original event changes from Delayed back to Planned, and the status of the Delay event changes from Unplanned to Dismissed. * The expected time window is a time period between the earliest and latest expected business or technical date and time. By default, the earliest time is 10 minutes before the planned event time and the latest is 10 minutes after the planned event time. If you want to change the default, contact your system administrator to maintain SAP BAdI /SCMTMS/TOR_SE_TRCKPR_OUT. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 135 This is custom documentation. Tracking Harmonization Tracking harmonization provides a harmonized tracking experience in SAP Business Network for Logistics by clearly distinguishing the capabilities provided in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. As of now, capabilities are distributed amongst SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration (that primarily focuses on order management and dock appointment scheduling), and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. In terms of tracking, SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration now supports basic tracking of milestone events and ETA. On top of these capabilities, SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace supports advanced tracking that also includes: geo position updates map view Here is the comparison of the tracking capabilities before and after tracking harmonization in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration: Capability Mode of Transport Business Partner Before Tracking Harmonization After Tracking Harmonization Milestone and ETA reporting via Web UI Road Carrier ✓ ✓ Milestone and ETA reporting via Web UI Ocean Carrier × ✓ Milestone and ETA reporting via Web UI Road, Ocean Shipper × ✓ Map view (in ʻTrack Freight Movement’ application) Road, Ocean Shipper ✓ × Milestone and ETA reporting via API Road, Ocean Carrier ✓ ✓ Milestone and ETA reporting via API Road, Ocean Visibility Provider ✓ ✓ 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 152 This is custom documentation. It has a central table for tracking information and a common look and feel. As a result, the following apps will be deprecated in 2026: Track Freight Movement Freight Orders for Reporting Benefits It has the following benefits to different users: Shippers gain insights into shipment execution and can now report logistics execution events via the new Manage Freight Execution app. Carriers can report all supported planned and unplanned events and view events reported by other business partners in the new Manage Freight Execution app. Previously, they could only report a small subset of events. Impact If you have subscribed to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, you only need to switch to the new app before May 2026, as the Freight Orders for Reporting and Track Freight Movement apps will be deprecated then. If you have subscribed to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and want to use advanced tracking, you must do the following: 1. Subscribe to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and onboard. For more, see Solution Owner Onboarding. 2. Set up carrier manual reporting via Web UI. For more on how to set up, see Enable Manual Reporting For Carriers. Events: All milestone events are supported except for “location update”, “carbon emission” and “overdue” events. Applying Instance-Based Authorization You can use Authorization Management of SAP Cloud Identity Service to apply instance-based authorization for the Manage Freight Execution app. You need to create custom authorization policies in which a collection of rules are defined. After you assign them to users, they can view documents that match the rules maintained in the policy. Prerequisites You must migrate from SAP Authorization and Trust Management (XSUAA) to SAP Identity Authentication Service (IAS) at tenant level. For more information, see Migration of Authentication from XSUAA to IAS. You must enable policy-based authorizations in SAP Cloud Identity Service. For more information, see Configure Authorizations Based on Policies. This ID is maintained in your backend SAP S/4HANA system. You can use the value help to select ordering parties. The value help only displays those ordering parties that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app with the object type as Business Partner. You can also enter free texts. restrictWithTransportationMode This policy allows you to segregate documents based on transportation modes. You can use the value help to select transportation mode codes. These are the transportation mode codes that are available in the Assign Codes app. You can also enter free texts. restrictWithTransportMeans This policy allows you to segregate documents based on transport means. You can use the value help to select transport means codes. These are the transportation means codes that are available in the Assign Codes app. You can also enter free texts. Manage Disputes As an ordering party, you can view the disputes that have been created for invoices that the carrier has submitted based on your freight documents, or you can view the disputes which the carrier has raised on self-billed freight documents. When the system receives an invoice from the carrier, it checks the invoice against the freight document. If it detects inconsistencies, the system raises a dispute and informs you accordingly. You can then either accept the invoice as it is, or you can engage in dialog with the carrier with the aim of reaching a mutual agreement. You can also have a self-billing process in place with the carrier, wherein the carrier does not submit an invoice for the transportation services. Instead, you settle automatically based on the information in your freight document. In this process, you can have differences and potential disputes between what you expect to pay against what the carrier expects to be paid. To keep good business relationships, you need to work closely with the carrier to resolve these differences in a collaborative way. You need to get clarification on the differences and converge on an agreement with the carrier on how to resolve the differences. A dispute can be raised based on either the carrier invoice or the self-billing freight document. Once the dispute has been resolved, the freight document charges are updated and it is sent back to your SAP Transportation Management system. An application-to- application (A2A) message is also sent from your LBN tenant to your SAP Transportation Management system. So when the invoice then reaches your SAP Transportation Management system, the system does not detect any discrepancies as the charges have been updated and it has been informed accordingly, so ideally no further dispute is created. The freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics enables your carriers to create disputes against your freight documents for additional unplanned freight costs. The carrier can create dispute against the freight document and submit the dispute for your review. Once the carrier submits the dispute, you can collaborate on the dispute with the carrier either from the Manage Disputes app in SAP Business Network for Logistics or from your external transportation system. You can select one of these options from the General Settings app. You can enable a multi-step dispute approval process within your organization before submitting the dispute to the carrier. A dispute document can either be approved in a single step by a basic user at the first level or sent to supervisors or managers at the next levels for review based on the settings that you specify. Based on the range of the disputed amount, you can define multiple approver groups for various dispute amount ranges to approve the dispute. You can specify the approval conditions in the General Settings app. For more information, see Internal Approval Process.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Internal Approval Process SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to have a multi-step dispute approval process within your organization before submitting the dispute to the carrier. A dispute document can either be approved in a single step by a basic user at the first level or sent to supervisors or managers at the next levels for review based on the settings that you specify. The additional approval steps are enabled only when the disputed amount exceeds the threshold amount or percentage specified the settings. Based on the range of the disputed amount, you can define multiple approver groups for various dispute amount ranges to approve the dispute. You can specify the approval conditions in the General Settings app. When a carrier sends a dispute document for review to you, any user from your organization that has the required roles and scope can edit and submit the document. If the disputed amount is greater than the threshold amount or threshold percentage, the dispute is sent to the users from the appropriate approval group. You define the approver groups and the users in an approver group in the General Settings app. When a higher approver is working on the dispute document, the document does not go for any further approval processes. The system sends an email notification to all the email addresses specified in the appropriate user group. Approvers can perform one of the following actions: Approve When the supervisor or manager selects the approve icon in the dispute document, all the changes proposed by the first-level user are accepted. The dispute is submitted to the carrier or your transportation management system if all the charges are resolved. Edit The supervisor or manager can edit the changes proposed by the first-level user and submit the document. For the disputed charge lines, the user can either accept, edit, or reject the charges. Once the document is submitted, the system checks if the amount proposed by the supervisor is within the threshold of the current approver group. If the amount exceeds the threshold of the current approver group, the system then sends the document to the next level approver group that you have specified in the General Settings app. If it does not exceed, the system submits the dispute document to the carrier. Reject When the supervisor or manager selects the reject button in the dispute document, the status of the document becomes rejected. For the disputed charge lines, the user can either accept, edit, or reject the charges. The system prompts you ro specify a rejection note that is submitted to internal users in your organization. Acknowledgement Message After Dispute Resolution A dispute is resolved when the shipper or the carrier accepts all charges proposed by the other party. For example, the carrier proposes charges and the shipper accepts these charges. When the party that has the document accepts all the charges, then the system updates these charges in the freight document in the shipper's SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system and the dispute status is updated as Submitted for confirmation. When the resolved charges that have been agreed upon by the shipper and the carrier in the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics are updated in the shipper's SAP TM system, the system displays an acknowledgment message that the charges have been updated. If the charges are not updated, the system displays a failure message. Success message When a successful acknowledgment message is received in the freight collaboration option, the status of the shipper's dispute is set to Resolved. Then, the carrier dispute is set to Resolved, after which the carrier invoice status is updated to Submitted (for an invoicing dispute) and the carrier invoice is submitted to the SAP TM system. When the system receives an acknowledgment message from the SAP TM system, it sets the dispute status changed as Resolved. Failure message If the SAP TM freight document update fails, TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In will fail with errors, and the acknowledgment message (TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out) will not be triggered. The shipper must process this error in Forward Error Handling (FEH), which has already been registered and implemented on the inbound side for TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. FEH is configured to perform error handling. Therefore, the error message is forwarded to FEH post-processing, which the shipper can access by choosing the red flag. You user launches the transaction sxi_monitor in the shipper's system and provides the interface name as TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. Error message If TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out message contains any error, it will set the dispute status as In Error. The error must be addressed in the SAP TM system and the dispute can be re-triggered. This will resend the TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In message to update the charges again. Dispute Inconsistencies During Freight Document Updates Updates in self-billed freight documents are reflected in the dispute document in the carrier's system and are marked as inconsistent. When a carrier, creates a dispute on a self-billed freight document and the ordering party also makes changes to the self-billed freight document in their SAP Transportation Management system, the system notifies the carrier that the carrier is disputing on a document 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 168 This is custom documentation. The system displays the following message to the carrier: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. Also, the system highlights the relevant lines and indicates as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The carrier can accept the new charges or create a new dispute with the new frame of reference. When the carrier chooses Merge charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process. However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the carrier submits the document, the dispute status changes to Submitted for confirmation. If the document is with the ordering party, the disputed line is highlighted and marked as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The document is editable in the ordering party's system but not in the carrier's system. If there are disputed lines that are inconsistent, the system displays the following message to the ordering party: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. When the ordering party accepts the charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute, and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process. However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the document is submitted by the ordering party, the dispute status changes to To be reviewed and is sent to the carrier for approval. The carrier can view the updated charges. Applying Instance-Based Authorization You can apply instance-based authorization in the Manage Disputes app to segregate dispute documents based on the purchasing organization. In other terms, you can assign purchasing organizations to a user ID. When you do so, the user can view only those dispute documents that belong to the purchasing organizations assigned to a specific user ID. As the purchasing organization has a business partner representation as the ordering party, you must assign the users to the ordering party instead of a purchasing organization. To enable instance-based authorization, proceed as follows: 1. Create a role using the AttributedOrderingPartyTemplate role template You can find this role template under the lbn-live!t1590 application identifier. 2. For the newly-created role, set the party_id attribute in AttributedOrderingPartyTemplate to <Business Partner ID> of your purchasing organization, for example LBNPO01. You can find the business partner ID of your purchasing organization in you SAP Transportation Management system. 3. Add this role to the role collection that has been assigned to you. Manage Integration Logs The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can view the integration logs using this app. This can be integration logs between SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP S/4HANA or any other backend SAP system (such as SAP Transportation Management) or any API or EDI system of carriers, network partners, network participants, or similar. Since SAP Business Network for Logistics follows a single integration system design for all customers and other partners, the Manage Integration Logs app aims to provide a visibility into integration logs for a particular customer or partner. Only the technical parties involved in an integration log can view the same in the app, ensuring data separation across all customers. The app also provides access to customer-facing payloads and enables the reprocessing of failed integration logs. The app provides standard SAP Business Network for Logistics integration logs only. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting . Shippers and solution owners can use the following features: You can search based on document ID and date/time. You can use separate tabs for Logs and Documents: In the Logs tab, there are two predefined filters: All (includes all messages in all statuses) and Failed (includes messages in status Failed or Escalated). Individual messages sent to or from SAP Business Network for Logistics are listed here. The Documents tab provides an aggregated view based on predefined scenarios. Each scenario is a collection of document types based on SAP Business Network for Logistics apps. For more information about available scenarios, see Scenarios. For each scenario, the Manage Integration Logs app provides an overall status. The status in the Documents tab is the status of the latest integration log within the aggregated scenario. You can reprocess escalated messages from either of the tabs. You can sort and filter on column level. You can download the table content to a Microsoft Excel file. You can view the payloads and error logs within the app. You can download the payloads.
