For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Scenario Message Type Tracking ANSI - 214 Tracking IFTSTA Available Statuses A message in the Manage Integration Logs app can have different statuses. The following statuses are available: Completed: The system assigns this status to a message when SAP Business Network for Logistics was able to process the document successfully. Failed: The system assigns this status to a message when there is a validation error that occurred during the first step of processing of the message. This can happen if there is a payload issue, missing mandatory fields, or a missing configuration. Retry: Depending on the nature of the error and the settings in the consuming application, an integration log can go to retry mode. In such cases, the log retries for a couple of times ranging from a couple of minutes to 30 minutes, after which the status goes into a final status – Completed or Escalated. Escalated: The system assigns this status to a message when the processing failed in backend of an app, or in an external API, or in the customer’s backend SAP system. This usually denotes a connectivity failure at any of the above mentioned places. Reasons could be that a service is not available for a long period, or that there is an authentication issue, or some basic connectivity failure due to misconfigurations, or technical failures in a backend system. You can find a more detailed error information when you click the icon in the Log Details column. The Error column displays the error code and description that the affected app sends when a call to SAP Business Network for Logistics fails. The description provides you with a more concrete context of the issue. You can sort or filter by error code to identify the logs with common failures, and take corrective actions (such as reprocessing the messages, fixing the root cause of the issue, informing SAP support about the error). Reprocessing: The system assigns this status to a message while it's being reprocessed. After you solve the configuration or connectivity issue in SAP Business Network for Logistics and select the Reprocess button, the system moves the message to this status. While a message has this status, you should just wait for it to complete reprocessing. The overall status is derived from the latest status of an individual log associated with the scenario. Contact your visibility provider or carrier. 5002 Request body format error 5003 Time zone format incorrect Reprocessing Integration Messages When integration messages fail to reach the target system, this is reported in a message log. Depending on the kind of error, it can help to reprocess an integration message. However, not all integration messages can be reprocessed. You can manually reprocess integration messages with the status Failed or Escalated. To do so, proceed as follows: 1. Select a message, or multiple messages, in the table. 2. Choose Reprocess. When an escalated/failed message is reprocessed, newer logs are created in the internal integration system. When you try to reprocess an already reprocessed message, the Manage Integration Logs app refers to the latest logs in the internal integration system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 183 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The reprocessing of a message is limited to 29 days. After 30 days, you won’t be able to reprocess the message or download the payload. Log details are available to be viewed for 90 days. For reprocessing purposes, there are two columns available: Reprocessed: Indicates whether an integration message has already been reprocessed or not. Reprocessable: Indicates whether a message log can be reprocessed or not. Not all messages with status Failed or Escalated are eligible for reprocessing. This is usually determined by a uniqueness check of a combination of several fields such as Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. In certain cases, the check is also extended to additional information, such as Event Type or Reported Time. An integration message with status Failed or Escalated is the latest one in chronological order when grouped together with Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. Example: A subcontracting request (TransportationOrderRequest) is sent from the transportation management (TM) system of a shipper to SAP Business Network for Logistics and fails. The same document is updated in the TM system and sent again. In such cases, SAP Business Network for Logistics would allow the reprocessing of the latest message only. The older integration messages will have the Reprocessable value set to No. The same applies when the latest integration message from the TM system has the status Completed. Older messages with status Failed or Escalated are not eligible for reprocessing. Hence, the Reprocessable value is set to No. In certain cases, such as an event notification in a tracking scenario, the event type and the reported time are also considered. Example: If multiple events reported by a carrier or a carrier system fail in SAP Business Network for Logistics, all of these are relevant for reprocessing. In the uniqueness check, event type and reported time information is considered too. Thus, for the same freight order ID, shipper, document type (TransportationEventBulkNotification), and source system, it’s possible to reprocess escalated logs for DepartureEvent, ArrivalEvent, etc. And for all these event logs, the Reprocessable value is set to Yes. Auto-reprocessing is not supported for test tenants. The messages failed with an error code that is eligible for auto-reprocessing. Processes in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration In this section, you can view the details of the end-to-end business process scenarios for various functionalites in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. For example, the Freight Order Contracting Process elaborates on all the activities that need to be performed for the freight contracting process such as, ordering party sending a a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) to the carrier, carrier confirming or rejecting the freight RFQ, ordering party receiving the carrier's response and so on. Freight Contracting The ordering party has a requirement to transport goods from one location to another. The ordering party wants to execute this transportation with the help of the carriers in their network. The freight order serves as the transportation document for the means of transport as Road. In the Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4 HANA system, SAP Logistics Management, or the external transportation system, the ordering party performs the freight planning to select from the list of contracted carriers and later sends the freight order to get the confirmation from the carrier. 1 – Receive Freight Request for Quotation The ordering party then receives the Freight Requests for Quotation in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the SOAP interface from external backend system, TransportationOrderQuotationCreateRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create Freight Request for Quotation . 2 - Forward Freight Request for Quotation In the SAP Business Network for Logistics system, the carrier can receive and process the quotation in the Freight Requests for Quotation app. Alternatively, the carrier can receive and process the freight request for quotation using the POST 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 185 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- LbnFreightRequestForQuotation service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Tendering . The carrier can use this API to also send the quotation details to their carrier network. 3 – Receive Response to Freight Request for Quotation The carrier can view, accept, or reject freight requests for quotations that the ordering party has sent in the Freight Quotations app. Alternatively, the carriers can also use the POST LbnFreightQuotation service in the public REST API Provider API for Freight Tendering to accept or reject a freight request for quotation. As part of accepting a freight request for quotation, the carrier provides the price proposal or currency change depending on the permissions set by the ordering party. 4 - Send Quotation The ordering party receives the carrier’s response in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from external backend system, TransportationOrderQuotationConfirmation_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Create or Update Freight Quotation . 5 - Receive Award Notification In the external transportation system, the ordering party decides whether they want to award or reject the transportation request received from the carrier. The ordering party uses the SOAP interface from external backend system, TransportationOrderQuotationNotification_Out to send a notification about the status of the freight quotation to the carrier. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Notify Freight Quotation . 6 - Forward Quotation Award / Reject The carrier receives this response in the Freight Requests for Quotation app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST LbnFreightQuotation service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Tendering to receive the response. The carrier can use this API to also send the quotation details to their carrier network. 7 - Receive Freight Order for Confirmation The ordering party creates a freight order from their external transportation system and sends it to the carrier using the SOAP interface from external backend system, TransportationOrderRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create Freight Order for Subcontracting . 8 - Forward Freight Order The carrier receives this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracting service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting to receive and process the freight order. The carrier can use this API to also send the freight order details to their carrier network. 9 - Receive Confirmation/Rejection for Freight Order The carrier responds to this freight order by confirming or rejecting the freight order in their SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The carrier can confirm or reject the freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracting service in the public REST API, Provider API for Freight Subcontracting to confirm or reject the freight order and send the response to the ordering party. 10 - Send Confirmation / Rejection The ordering party receives the carrier’s response in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from external backend system, TransportationOrderConfirmation_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Confirm Freight Order for Subcontracting . 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 186 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Only applicable to freight orders from TM on SAP S/4HANA: Post confirmation and follow up in the ordering party’s external transportation system, the execution status of the freight order is set to Ready for Execution. If the ordering party has enabled tracking for this freight order, then upon setting this status, the SOAP message TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out is triggered to SAP Business Network for Logistics. This creates a tracking process or tracking request for the freight order in SAP Business Network for Logistics that enables reporting or tracking of events for the freight order. For more information, see Track Freight Movement. Freight Booking Similar to the order process for means of transport Road explained in the Freight Contracting, for the means of transport Ocean and Air, the freight booking document is the primary transportation document. The ordering party performs the freight planning and creates a freight booking for confirmation for ocean freight or air freight in their Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4HANA system or the external transportation system. Booking Creation Scenario 1 - Receive New Freight Booking The ordering party sends the freight booking request to the SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create Freight Booking Request . 2 - Forward New Booking Request The carrier receives new ocean freight booking requests in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app and air freight booking requests in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. The carrier can review and confirm freight bookings sent by the ordering parties in these apps. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST FreightBookingRequest service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Booking for Confirmation to view and manage the freight booking. 3 - Receive response to Freight Booking 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 187 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The carrier can respond to the freight booking and either confirm or reject the booking in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) or Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Alternatively, the carrier send their response to the ordering party using the POST FreightBookingConfirmation service in the public REST API, Provider API for Freight Booking for Confirmation . 4 - Send Booking Confirmation / Rejection The ordering party receives the carrier’s response in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingConfirmation_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Confirm Freight Booking . Booking Update Scenario 5 - Receive Freight Booking Update To send the updated booking request to the SAP Business Network for Logistics, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingRequest_Out. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST FreightBookingRequest service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Booking for Confirmation to view and manage the freight booking. 7 - Receive response to Freight Booking The carrier can respond to the freight booking and either confirm or reject the booking in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) or Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Alternatively, the carrier send their response to the ordering party using the POST FreightBookingConfirmation service in the public REST API, Provider API for Freight Booking for Confirmation . 8 - Send Booking Confirmation/Rejection The ordering party receives the carrier’s response in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingConfirmation_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Confirm Freight Booking . Sending Waybill Notification 9 - Receive Waybill (Only for Ocean Scenario) The ordering party can send a notification to the carrier about a waybill that is to be issued by a carrier. The information in the notification enables a carrier to issue a waybill with reference to a confirmation of a freight booking. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingWaybillNotification_Out. 10 - Forward Shipping Instructions and VGM The carrier receives the shipping instructions and verified gross mass (VGM) details in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app and air freight booking requests in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST FreightBookingWaybillNotification service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Booking for Confirmation to receive and process the freight booking. Booking Cancellation Scenario 11 - Receive Booking Cancellation 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 188 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- The ordering party can send a freight booking cancellation request to the carrier using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderBookingCancellationRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Cancel Freight Booking . 12 - Forward Booking Cancellation The carrier receives the cancellation request from the ordering party in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app for ocean freight bookings and Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app for air freight bookings. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST FreightBookingRequestCancellation service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Booking for Confirmation to view and manage the freight booking cancellation request. Post confirmation of the freight booking, the ordering party can go ahead with the follow up processes in the external transportation system. The freight booking can send a track process creation request for reporting and tracking of events. For more information, see Track Freight Movement. Track Freight Movement (Deprecated) The carriers can provide updates to the ordering parties about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of the delivery trucks is delayed on-route, the carrier can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival), so the ordering party can replan if required. Additionally, the carriers can upload and send documents, such as proof of deliveries, to their ordering parties. The ordering parties can view the status of the execution of their freight documents in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The ordering parties can view the planned and unplanned events in a freight document and the carrier's automated visibility data. 1 - Receive Freight Document for Tracking To enable reporting of events by carriers and tracking of events by the ordering party, the ordering party can create a freight order for tracking and send it to the SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the SOAP interface from Transportation Management (TM) on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create or Update Track Process .  Note This process is deprecated and replaced by the new process: Manage Freight Execution. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 189 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To enable reporting of events by carriers and tracking of events by the ordering party, the ordering party can create a freight document for tracking and send it to the SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the SOAP interface from Transportation Management (TM) on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create or Update Track Process . 2 - Send Freight Document for Tracking In the SAP Business Network for Logistics system, the carrier receives the create or update tracking request and can view and manage the request in the Manage Freight Execution app. The carrier can create a tracking request in their carrier network using the POST LbnOrderforTracking service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Order Tracking (FC) . The carrier can receive the real- time event status and predictive estimated time of arrival information from their carrier network. 3 - Receive Events and ETA The carrier can send this information to their SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the Manage Freight Execution app. Alternatively, the carrier can use the Events service in the public REST API, Provider API for Order Events (FC) to report these events. 4 - Update Freight Document with Events The ordering parties can view the status of the execution of their freight documents in the Track Freight Movement app. The ordering parties can view information sent by the carrier. The ordering party can also update the freight order with the event information in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationEventBulkNotification_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Notify Events . Post tracking, during the execution process, the execution status of the freight order is set as In Execution. On calculation of charges, the calculation status is set as Calculated. At this point, the freight order is sent to the carrier for settlement. Outsourced Planning of Freight Units The ordering party on Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4HANA system can create freight units and outsource the planning of freight units externally to a forwarder. SAP Business Network for Logistics has enabled the possibility of receiving such freight units from the ordering party and forwarding the same to the forwarder (onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics) using the public REST API. Post planning the freight units, the forwarder can send the planned freight document to SAP Business Network for Logistics using the public REST API which would be routed to the original ordering party’s backend TM on S4HANA system. Post creation of the freight order or freight booking in the ordering party’s S4HANA system, the freight document processing takes place. In this end-to-end process, SAP Business Network for Logistics acts as the integration platform for the ordering party and forwarder. Transportation Requirements Creation Scenario  Note For road freight orders, if the shipper has enabled tracking via TransportationOrderRequest_Out, the reporting of events can be enabled automatically after the carrier confirms the freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. However, in this case, the carrier can only report events on the freight order manually in the Manage Freight Execution app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 191 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 8 -- 1 - Receive Freight Unit The ordering party creates transportation requirements from a sales order, purchase order, or delivery documents in their TM on SAP S/4HANA system or the external transportation system. The ordering party can send these transportation requirements or freight units to the carrier or forwarder and request the forwarder to perform planning activities in the carrier’s system. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_Out. 2 - Forward Transportation Requirement The carrier receives the transportation requirements or freight units in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The carrier can receive and process the requirements using the POST TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Consumer API to Request for Planning in External System . 3 - Receive Planned Transportation Document Once the carrier creates a planned freight document in their system, they can send the planned transportation document such as the freight order or a freight booking containing the transportation requirements back to the ordering party. To do so, the carrier uses the POST TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Provider API to Create Planned Freight Documents from External System . 4 - Send Freight Document The ordering party receives the planned freight document from the carrier and updates their external system. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_In. Subsequent Subcontracting Process 5 - Send Subcontracting request The ordering party creates a freight order from their external transportation system and sends it to the carrier using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create Freight Order for Subcontracting . The external ID for the planned freight document must be sent as a document reference with type code 1122 (Transportation Order). 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 192 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 8 -- 6 - Send Freight Orders for Subcontracting The carrier receives this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracting service in the public REST API, Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting to receive and process the freight order. The carrier can use this API to also send the freight order details to their carrier network. The external ID for the planned freight document must be sent as a document reference with type code 1122 (Transportation Order). 7 - Receive Freight Document Confirmation The carrier responds to this freight order by confirming or rejecting the freight order in their SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The carrier can confirm or reject the freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Alternatively, the carrier can also use the POST LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracting service in the public REST API, Provider API for Freight Subcontracting to confirm or reject the freight order and send the response to the ordering party. 8 - Send Freight Confirmation The ordering party receives the carrier’s response in their external transportation system using the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderConfirmation_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Confirm Freight Order for Subcontracting . Transportation Requirements Update Scenario 1 - Receive Updated Freight Unit The ordering party can update the transportation requirements or updated freight units and send them to the carrier. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_Out. 2 - Forward Updated Transportation Requirement The carrier receives the updated transportation requirements or updated freight units in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The carrier can receive and process the updated requirements using the POST TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Consumer API to Request for Planning in External System . 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 193 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 8 -- 3 - Receive Update on Planned Transportation Document Once the carrier updates the planned freight document in their system, they can send the document back to the ordering party. To do so, the carrier uses the POST TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Provider API to Create Planned Freight Documents from External System . 4 - Send Freight Document The ordering party receives the updated planned freight document from the carrier and updates their external system. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_In. Transportation Requirements Cancellation Scenario 5 - Receive Freight Unit Cancellation The ordering party can send a cancellation request to the carrier to cancel the freight unit planning request. To do so, the ordering party uses the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_Out. 6 - Forward Cancelled Transportation Requirement The carrier receives the cancellation request from the ordering party and manages it using the DELETE TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Consumer API to Request for Planning in External System . 7 - Receive Cancellation on Planned Transportation Document Once the carrier cancels the planned freight document in their system, they can send the cancellation back to the ordering party. To do so, the carrier uses the DELETE TransportationDocument service in the public REST API, Provider API to Create Planned Freight Documents from External System . 8 - Send Freight Document Cancellation The ordering party receives the cancellation of the planned freight document from the carrier and the freight document is cancelled in their external system. To do so, the ordering party can use the SOAP interface from TM on S/4HANA, TransportationOrderGenericRequest_In. Freight Settlement SAP Business Network for Logistics enables the carriers to settle the freight documents with their customers. The carrier receives and processes the freight documents that are ready for settlement in the Invoice Freight Documents app and can create an invoice for a freight document from this app. The created invoice contains the planned charges sent by the ordering party. The created invoices can be further processed before submitting the invoice to the shipper in the Manage Invoices app.  Note The planning in the external system is managed only using the API scenario. When a transportation requirement is cancelled by the ordering party, the carrier may cancel the associated planned freight document or update the planned freight document to remove the cancelled transportation requirement.  Note In this document, the term Shipper refers to the company that has onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. The term Ordering Party refers to the multiple purchasing organizations of the shipper in their backend system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 194 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 8 -- In case of discrepancies, the system creates disputes, which can be collaboratively resolved by the shipper and the carrier using the Manage Disputes app. Based on the system in which the shipper handles the dispute process, the settlement process differs. For more information, see Dispute Management in SAP Business Network for Logistics and Dispute Management in SAP TM on S/4HANA. Dispute Management in SAP Business Network for Logistics In this scenario, the ordering party handles the dispute process in SAP Business Network for Logistics. 1 – Send Freight Document Ready for Invoicing The ordering party sends the freight document ready for invoicing that is, when the status of freight order is In Execution and the charges are calculated, from the Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4 HANA system to the SAP Business Network for Logistics system using the SOAP interface, TransportationOrderRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Create Freight Order for Settlement . 2 – View Freight Document with Charges In the SAP Business Network for Logistics system, the carrier can receive and process the freight document with charges in the Invoice Freight Documents app. From the Invoice Freight Documents app, the carrier can create invoices and manage them in the Manage Invoices app. 3 – Submit Carrier Invoice The carrier can manage and submit invoices in the Manage Invoices app. Alternatively, the carriers can also use the POST LogisticsInvoice service in the public REST API Provider API for Invoicing to submit invoices. When the carrier submits an invoice, the system checks the invoice against the data contained in the freight document. If it detects inconsistencies between the invoice and the freight document, the system automatically creates a dispute. The shipper can view the disputes in the Manage Disputes app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 195 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 8 -- 4, 5 – Collaborate on Disputes The ordering party can then either accept the invoice or the ordering party and the carrier can engage in a dialog until the dispute is resolved. The carrier can manage the disputes in the Manage Disputes app for carriers. 6 – Send Resolved Dispute Lines Once the dispute is resolved, the freight document charges in TM on SAP S/4 HANA system are updated using the SOAP interface, TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Update Freight Order with Dispute Charges . 7 - Send Update Confirmation Once the charges are updated, the system sends the confirmation to the carrier from their TM on SAP S/4 HANA system using the SOAP interface, TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_Out. For more information on the API, see Provider API to Confirm Freight Order Dispute Charges . 8 - Re-Submit Carrier Invoice Once the confirmation is received, the dispute is set as Resolved and the carrier can re-submit the invoice with the updated charges using the Manage Invoices app. If the invoice is created via API, then the earlier invoice is rejected and the carrier must submit the new invoice with the updated charges using the POST LogisticsInvoiceservice in the public REST API, Provider API for Invoicing . 9 - Send Carrier Invoice The submitted invoice is sent to the ordering party’s TM on SAP S/4 HANA system using the SOAP interface, InvoiceRequest_In. For more information on the API, see Consumer API to Create Invoice . Dispute Management in Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4 HANA In this scenario, the ordering party handles the dispute process from their Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4 HANA system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 196 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Post-Event Notifications Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after your CPI certificate has expired. You can schedule post-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the end of the period, for example, 30 days after the event, which means the notification period starts from the end of the previous period or the event time, to 30 days after the event. Notification frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Within the period from 30 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. Note that for the CPI certificate expiry scenario, the notifications stop as soon as the certificate that will expire is deleted in the System Connections app. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 15 days Every 3 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 60 days Every 10 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 30 days after the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 30 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Note that for the CPI certificate expiry scenario, the notifications stop as soon as the expired certificate is deleted in the System Connections app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 21 This is custom documentation. In the scenario list, select the scenario for which you want to set notifications. 3. To activate on-event notification, for On-Event Notification, set the toggle to Yes. To deactivate, set it to No. 4. To configure pre-event or post-event notifications, do the following: a. Expand the Pre-Event Notifications or Post-Event Notifications area. b. To add a notification period, choose the Add button. Then in the Add Notification Period dialog box, specify the start (pre-event) or end (post-event) of the period and the frequency, and choose Save. You can add multiple periods according to your needs. c. To edit or delete a notification period, choose the Edit or Delete button. To deactivate a period, set Activated for User to No. Assign Codes SAP Business Network for Logistics offers out-of-the-box connectivity with SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) standalone or Transportation Management (TM) embedded in SAP S/4HANA. As a shipper, you can maintain mappings for LBN-defined code lists (such as packaging material type). When a business document is sent from a TM system to SAP Business Network for Logistics, the LBN system converts the code lists to LBN standard and displays the correct value on the UI of the corresponding app. You have the following possibilities to define your code list mappings: Take over standard LBN code lists and their values Upload a spreadsheet with your customized code list values Add values manually In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 60 days Every 10 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note SAP Business Network for Logistics only supports a one to one mapping of codes. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 22 This is custom documentation. To do so, choose Add, enter the system ID and the internal ID in the free text fields, and select a carrier LBN ID from the input help. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Downloading and Uploading Code Lists Overview You can download a spreadsheet with the standard code lists from SAP Business Network for Logistics, enter the required code list values to be mapped and then upload your customized spreadsheet to LBN. SAP Business Network for Logistics provides a standard spreadsheet for each code list. Prerequisites Only spreadsheets with the *.xlsx format are supported. Procedure To upload your code lists to SAP Business Network for Logistics, proceed as follows: 1. In the Assign Codes app, on the left-hand side, choose the code list whose mappings you want to edit. 2. Mark all standard LBN codes and delete them. (Optional) 3. Download the spreadsheet with the standard LBN codes. 4. Edit the spreadsheet according to your needs. There are two sheets with columns described below. Sheet 1 contains the mapping of source code to LBN code. Source Code: The source code from the external system, such as a TM system. LBN Code: The LBN code (such as CIF – Cost and Freight). Deletion Indicator: Provide value Y if this mapping should be deleted and N to include or retain it. Sheet 2 contains the code list with LBN codes and corresponding descriptions. 5. Upload your spreadsheet to LBN. 6. Upon saving, LBN checks your entries and displays any errors or mismatches found during validation. 7. Solve the errors. 8. If required, you can add values manually. 9. Save your entries. Assign Charge Codes You use this app to perform the following: In a carrier invoicing scenario, you can assign charge types and condition types that you use in your transportation system to a set of predefined charge codes in the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics. Alternatively, you can also create and use a custom charge code. In a self-billing scenario, you can assign charge types that you use in your transportation system to a set of predefined charge codes in the freight collaboration option.  Note Ensure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non-purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 25 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Alternatively, you can also create and use a custom charge code. Because the charge types in freight orders play an important role in the calculation of transportation charges, it is important that these charge types are easily identifiable. When you use unified charge codes in the freight collaboration option, the carriers can easily interpret the charge types specific to your transportation system in freight orders. Prerequisites If you are using Transportation Management (TM) on SAP S/4 HANA 1809 onwards, you have made the following basic settings in your TM system. You must use the InvoiceRequest_In interface to process a carrier invoice that refers to a document such as a freight order, a service order, or a freight booking in TM. When the invoice is submitted and sent from the freight collaboration option to TM, the charge codes are converted to condition types to suit the message interface InvoiceRequest_In. To enable the carrier to submit an invoice, you must maintain the following Customizing activities: In Customizing for Transportation Management under Integration Enterprise Services Carrier Invoice Integration Assign Carrier Condition type to SAP TM Charge Type In Customizing for Transportation Management under Integration Enterprise Services Carrier Invoice Integration Assign Carrier Tax Types to SAP TM Tax Charge Type Note that if you do not maintain these Customizing activities, the system does not create an invoice in the TM system. You can use the Assign Charge Codes app to map the following entities based on the scenario type: Charge types These are the charge types that you have agreed with your carriers in the freight agreement. You maintain these charge types in your transportation system. Condition types These are the condition types which the carrier sends in the invoice via business to business (B2B) communication method. You map these condition types in your transportation system with the charge types. Charge codes You can choose a charge code that is predefined by the freight collaboration option charge codes from the input help. Alternatively, you can choose a custom code that you have created in the Assign Charge Codes app. You can also create a custom code from the input help. To do so, perform the following: 1. Choose Create Custom Code from the input help. A create custom code dialog box appears. 2. Enter a unique custom code that begins with Y or Z. Note that it must not contain any spaces or special characters, except underscore. 3. Enter the language in which you want to provide a description. Note that you can add multiple descriptions in different languages after you create a custom code, using the Manage Custom Codes feature.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 26 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- 4. Choose Save and Select. A new custom code has been created and it has been assigned in the charge type mapping. Enabled for carrier If you select this checkbox, the system displays the charge type to the carrier while creating an unplanned charge in an invoice. If you deselect this checkbox, the system does not display the charge type to the carrier. Carrier Invoicing Scenario The carrier generates the invoice in their transportation system and submits the invoice via the freight collaboration option. The charges in their transportation system invoice are represented by condition types. These condition types are mapped to specific charge types in your transportation system. When you map the charge types and condition types to charge codes, in the freight collaboration option, the carrier views the charge codes in the charges table in the freight order and the invoice documents. These charge codes provide a uniform representation of the charge types across the entire network. Hence, you must map your charge types and condition types to charge codes in the Assign Charge Codes app. However, when the carrier submits and sends the invoice to your transportation system, you must receive condition types in place of business network charge codes. To enable this, replaces the business network charge codes with the corresponding charge types and condition types specific to your transportation system. Self-Billing Scenario In a self-billing scenario, you must map the charge types that the shipper maintains in the TM system to standard freight collaboration option charge codes. You could download the charge types from the charge type customizing from TM and upload the same in the freight collaboration option in this app. Please note that the first row is ignored by the system during upload. Similarly, only the first column is read by the app.  Note You cannot assign multiple combinations of charge types and condition types to a single charge code. If you cannot find a predefined code, you can create a new custom code.  Note If you are using TM on SAP S/4 HANA 1809 onwards, the charge type and condition type values that you maintain in the Customizing activity Assign Carrier Condition type to SAP TM Charge Type must match the values that you specify in the Assign Charge Codes app. If the values do not match, the inbound and outbound communication between the invoice and the freight order will be erroneous.  Note If you are using TM on SAP S/4 HANA 1809 onwards and a freight order is sent from TM system to the freight collaboration option, the TM charge types are converted to charge codes. In the carrier tenant, the system fetches these charge codes from your tenant and the charge types and condition types are converted to the respective charge codes. When the invoice is submitted and sent from the freight collaboration option to TM, the charge codes are converted to condition types to suit the message interface InvoiceRequest_In. For more information on processing a carrier invoice using a B2B interface, see SAP Library for SAP S/4HANA on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/s4hana. In SAP Library, under Product Assistance, select the preferred language and choose Enterprise Business Applications Supply Chain Transportation Management (TM) Settlement Freight Settlement Dispute Management for Freight Settlements Carrier Invoice Processing of a Carrier Invoice Using a B2B Interface . 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 27 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Manage Codes Custom Codes When you choose the Manage Codes Custom Codes button in the Assign Charge Codes app, you can view, edit, and create custom codes. Creating a Custom Code To create a custom code, perform the following: 1. Choose the Create button on the top right corner of the screen. A create custom code dialog box appears. 2. Enter a unique custom code that begins with Y or Z. Note that it must not contain any spaces or special characters, except underscore. 3. Enter the language in which you want to provide a description. Note that you can create multiple descriptions in different languages after you create a custom code. 4. Choose Create. A new custom code has been created Adding, Editing, and Deleting Descriptions To add a new description in a different language, choose the add icon in the Actions column. You can also delete or edit an existing description using the edit and delete icons respectively in the Actions column. You can revert the deletion of a description using the undo icon in the Actions column. Note that you must maintain at least one description for a custom code in any language. Deleting a Custom Code To delete a custom code, you can use the delete icon in the Actions column. Saving the Changes  Note Only after you assign charge codes to charge types and condition types that you use in your transportation system, can you create freight orders and invoices. When you choose the Scenario as Both in the Assign Charge Codes app, you can add a mapping common to both the carrier invoicing and self-billing scenarios. As of now, the freight collaboration option only supports these assignments only for the road mode of transportation.  Note You can only delete a custom code that does not have the In Use indication. This indication appears when you have used the custom code in a charge type mapping. If you want to delete a custom code with In Use indication, you must first delete the charge type mapping in the worklist page and then delete the custom code. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 28 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- When you create or delete a custom code, or when you add, modify, or delete a description, you must choose Save on top right corner of the screen to save your changes. Tax Codes When you choose the Manage Codes Tax Codes button in the Assign Charge Codes app, you can view, edit, and create tax codes. The carrier can you use these tax codes and percentage values in their invoicing app when they add a tax line. Adding a Tax Code To create a tax code, perform the following: 1. Choose the Add button on the top right corner of the screen. A new tax line appears. 2. Enter a tax code of up to 3 characters. 3. Enter a tax percentage and choose Save. A new tax code has been created. Deleting a Tax Code To delete a tax code, you can use the delete icon. Note that once you delete a tax code, you can undo the delete action by using the undo icon. Saving the Changes When you create or delete a tax code, you must choose Save on top right corner of the screen to save your changes. Uploading and Downloading Charge Code Assignments Downloading Charge Type Assignments You can download the charge types and condition types assignments in the Assign Charge Codes app in a Microsoft Excel file using the Download button. The downloaded Microsoft Excel file contains the charge code assignments in the first sheet. You can view the charge codes description in the second sheet. Uploading Charge Type Assignments If you have already maintained the charge types and condition types mapping in your transportation system, you can avoid the effort of manually entering them in the Assign Charge Codes app. You can upload the charge types and condition types mapping from your transportation system in the Assign Charge Codes app using the Upload button.  Note In the General Settings app, a new toggle Enable Tax Code Validation has been introduced. When you enable this setting, if the carrier enters a tax code in the invoice, the system validates this tax code with the tax codes that you have maintained here in the Assign Charge Codes app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 29 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- You can do the following: 1. Scenario Code Enter scenario code referring to the possible values provided in the column header. 2. Charge Code (SAP Business Network for Logistics) Enter the appropriate charge code by referring to the second sheet. 3. Enabled for Carrier If you select this checkbox, the system displays the charge type to the carrier while creating an unplanned charge in an invoice. If you deselect this checkbox, the system does not display the charge type to the carrier. Downloading Charge Type Assignments from TM on SAP S/4 HANA System If you are using TM on SAP S/4 HANA 1809 onwards, you can download the charge type and condition types mapping in Microsoft Excel format using the following procedure: In Customizing for Transportation Management under Integration Enterprise Services Carrier Invoice Integration Assign Carrier Condition type to SAP TM Charge Type , choose Table View Print . In the print view, choose the spreadsheet icon. A select spreadsheet dialog box appears. Choose Select from All Available Formats Excel – Office Open XML Format (XLSX) and choose Continue. Save the file. File Format and Contents The system allows you to upload only Microsoft Excel files of xlsx format. The first column in the Microsoft Excel file must contain the condition types and the second column must contain the charge types. The system ignores the first row of the Microsoft Excel file.  Note You can only upload Microsoft Excel files of xlsx format. The Microsoft Excel file that you want to upload must be of the same format as the file that you download from the Assign Charge Codes app. To avoid any formatting changes, you can choose to download, edit and then upload the Microsoft Excel file here.  Note You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. If the uploaded Microsoft Excel file contains mappings from your transportation system that exists already in the Assign Charge Codes app, the system ignores such entries and uploads only new entries from the file. The system adds the new entries to the app along with the existing entries. The Assign Charge Codes app contains a charge type to charge code mapping for a self-billing scenario and the uploaded Excel file contains a mapping for the same charge type with condition type for the carrier invoicing scenario. In this case, the system changes the scenario as Both in the app and includes the condition type mapping as well to this entry. If the uploaded Microsoft Excel file contains a different mapping for a charge type or a condition type that exists already in the app, the system does not upload the entire file. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 30 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Discover Business Partners Finding the right business partners is always a challenge. However, this will be easier once your partners-to-be have joined SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a simple yet powerful app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, Discover Business Partners helps you search the network for logistics service providers, then from the results, invite suitable ones to be your business partners. Prerequisites To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Search for Business Partners To search for business partners on the network, enter a key word, for example the company name, in the search box and then press Enter . You can also use faceted search on the left pane to narrow down your search results. When using faceted search, you can even leave the search box empty. This is useful if you want to explore your potential partners in a specific region or industry. Result A set of matched results are returned. You can click to open the details page of a matched result. Send Request for Connection To send a request for connection to your potential business partners, proceed as follows: 1. Click to select the company to which you want to send the request for connection from the Matched Results table. 2. Choose Request for Connection. The request for connection is sent to the selected companies. Results A request for connection is sent to the selected company. Once the company accepts your request, you will become business partners. After you’ve set up a partnership with a business partner via this app, you must update the business partner’s LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). To do this, see Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID. References If the uploaded Microsoft Excel file contains the same charge type or a condition type repeated more than once, the system does not upload the entire file.  Note If the business partners you are trying to connect with operates in a different data center, you must first ensure that your company profile is available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, refer to Profile Settings.  Note If the companies that match your search conditions are not found, see Discover Business Partners App and refer to "Why companies that match my search conditions are not returned in the Matched Results table?" 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Manage Business Profile Manage Invitations Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID To update the LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) for a logistics service provider who’s become your business partner, proceed as follows in SAP TM: 1. Go to the Manage Business Partner transaction (transaction BP). 2. Set the filter criteria to find the business partner for which you want to update the LBN ID and then double-click the business partner to open its Display Organization page. 3. Navigate to the Identification tab. In the Identification Numbers section, IDType field, enter LBN001. 4. In the Identification Number field, enter the LBN ID and save your changes. Invite Business Partners The Invite Business Partners app is designed for managing all the business partners that you want to be part of your network. You can use this app to select and invite business partners to join your business network and check their participation status. If you have access, you can navigate to the Discover Business Partners app to find more potential business partners. You may have business with many partners in your system and you may want to persist your business with them in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can download the Excel template available in the app and fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload the template back in the app. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can download these business partners from SAP TM system and upload them in Invite Business Partners. For more information, see Downloading Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). You can select one or more of these business partners from your system and invite them to join your network. When you submit these partners, a back-end team manages your connection invitation. For more information, see Connection Invitations. When a business partner accepts an invitation to connect with your network, the system updates the unique LBN ID of the partner. If you are using SAP TM system, you can update these LBN IDs of partners in SAP TM system by downloading the partner list from the  Note To use these apps, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. The file size of each business partners Excel cannot be larger than 2MB, and the maximum number of rows in each file is 5000. A digital freight forwarder is managed as a business partner in both the SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP Transportation Management system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Discover Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). The Discover Business Partners app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the business partner based on one more of the filter options (Business Partner ID and Business Partner) that appear on the header area. Worklists by status The business partners are categorized based on their invitation response status: To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Business Partners) There are different ways to manage all the business partners and to set filters. To search for a specific business partner, you can use the filter bar in the header. The system also displays preconfigured worklists (To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, Rejected) based on the business partner's invitation response status. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for business partners. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper-left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. To Be Submitted The To Be Submitted worklist displays all the business partners that you have uploaded or added in the app but have not yet submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitations. This worklist also displays connection invitations that have been rejected. The worklist displays the following details for each invitation: System ID Business Partner ID Invitee Company Role SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code)  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Phone number Email Language City Country/Region Zip code Status In Progress The In Progress worklist displays all the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team to manage the connection invitations. These business partners have not yet responded to your invitation to connect with your network. You can recall your invitation in this worklist if needed. The In Progress worklist has the same columns as the To Be Submitted worklist. Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the business partners who have accepted your invitation to join your business network. You can select one or more business partners in the Accepted tab and download them in Microsoft Excel format. The Accepted worklist has the same columns as the In Progress worklist along with the unique LBN ID of the business partner. Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the business partners who have rejected your invitation to join your business network via Discover Business Partners. The Rejected worklist has the same columns as the Accepted worklist. Using the settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected tabs. You can also sort and filter the business partners in these worklists based on various attributes. Add New Business Partners You can add new business partners to the Invite Business Partners app in one of the following ways: Manual entry  Note A rejected invitation is displayed on the To Be Submitted worklist with the status "Returned by LBN OPS team" if it was submitted via the Invite Business Partners app. A rejected invitation is displayed on the Rejected worklist if it was submitted via the Discover Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- On the To Be Submitted tab, you can manually add a new business partner to the Invite Business Partners app by choosing Add Invitee Business Partner . You can also add a shipper to the app by choosing Add Invitee Shipper . When adding a shipper, you must provide the shipper's LBN ID. Using this method, you can specify the language of your connection invitations. Supported languages are: English Arabic Bulgarian Chinese Simplified Chinese Traditional Croatian Czech Danish Dutch Finnish French German Greek Hebrew Hungarian Italian Japanese Korean Malay Norwegian Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Romanian Russian Serbian Slovak Spanish Swedish Thai Turkish Manual entry with an Excel template 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- You can download the Excel template available in the Invite Business Partners app by choosing the Download Excel Template button. You can fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload this template back in the Invite Business Partners app. Downloading business partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system You can download the list of business partners in your SAP TM system and upload the Excel file in the Invite Business Partners app. For more information, see Download Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management System. You can select one or more business partners in the To Be Submitted worklist and delete them from the Invite Business Partners app. Note that you cannot delete the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. Connection Invitations Once you have a list of business partners added to the Invite Business Partners app, you can select one or more partners from the To Be Submitted worklist and choose Submit. Once you choose Submit, the system instantaneously sends a request to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. The system moves the submitted business partners to the In Progress worklist. Shippers in both production and test environments can use the Invite Business Partners app to send connection invitations to business partners. If the invitees are not yet on the network, they can activate their accounts via a simplified account activation process and collaborate with the inviter in the respective environment (either production or test). You can refer your invitees to the following resource for their account activation: Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process. Note that business partners need your contact information when you send them an invitation to join your business network. If you have not maintained a default address in the Manage Business Profile app, the system does not allow you to submit business partners. For more information on adding a default address, see Edit Company Profile. The back-end team sends an invitation to the business partners requesting them to connect with your network. The business partner can view this connection invitation using the Manage Invitations app and choose to accept or reject the invitation. For more information, see Manage Invitations. When the business partner accepts or rejects an invitation, you will be notified of the same and the system moves the business partner to the accepted or rejected worklist as appropriate. If a partner accepts your invitation, the partner connects with your network and you can perform business transactions with this partner. If a business partner rejects your invitation, the partner is not connected with your network and you cannot perform any business transactions with this partner. You can find the rejected invitation from the To Be Submitted worklist and resend it if you want to.  Note When you upload a business partner Excel in the Invite Business Partners app, the system automatically filters out the erroneous business partner records and selects only the correct business partner records. For example, in the downloaded Excel file, if there are business partners that already exist in the Invite Business Partners app with the status as In Progress, Accepted or Rejected, or if some of the entries do not contain any of the mandatory fields, the system ignores such entries and uploads all the other entries. When you upload a business partner Excel, the system performs a validation. If there are no validation errors, the business partner Excel is uploaded. If there are validation errors, the system displays the erroneous entries in an error log. The system allows you to download this error log. You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The system updates the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted your connection invitation. You can view this LBN ID in the Accepted worklist for each business partner. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can update these LBN IDs of business partners in SAP TM system by downloading the business partner list from the Invite Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). Recall Invitations You can recall a submitted invitation as long as its status remains "In Progress". To recall the invitation, switch to the In Progress worklist, click to open the invitation that you want to recall, and then choose Recall on the details page. After being recalled, the invitation returns to the To Be Submitted worklist and becomes editable. The business partner cannot view the recalled invitation using the app until you submit it again. Downloading Business Partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can download the business partners from the SAP TM system and upload them to the Invite Business Partners app. Context In SAP TM system, you must perform the following steps to download the business partner Excel: Procedure 1. Execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_CARR_LIST_DWNLD in transaction SE38. 2. Enter your SAP TM organization ID in the Organizational ID field and execute. The system determines the hierarchy of this organization and retrieves all the freight agreements that are valid at the time of searching. The system then determines the valid business partners from these agreements. Note that if you select the Show Application Log checkbox, the system displays the detailed information about the business partner determination process. 3. Alternatively, instead of entering an organization ID and retrieving multiple business partners, you can also enter the business partner IDs in the Carrier IDs field and execute. The system retrieves the details of all the business partners that you have entered. 4. Select all the business partners that you want to download and then choose Download. The system downloads the Excel file. Next Steps Once you download the Excel file, in the Invite Business Partners app, choose the Upload Business Partners button to upload this Excel. Once you upload the Excel file with a list of partners, the system updates the To Be Submitted worklist in the app with the partner details in the Excel.  Note You can't recall an invitation when its status is "Invitation email sent to business partner". 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can update the SAP TM system with the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted to connect with your business network. Context To do so, you must perform the following: Procedure 1. Download the list of business partners with their LBN IDs from the Accepted worklist in the Invite Business Partners app. The system downloads the list of partners in a CSV format. 2. In the SAP TM system, execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_ID_BP_UPD in transaction SA38. 3. Browse for the CSV file that you have downloaded and upload the file. The system updates the business partner IDs for the partners in the system. Note that you can choose whether you want the system to process the upload job in the background or foreground. If you choose to process the upload job in the foreground, the system displays the error logs if there are any. Configure Partner Connections You can use the Configure Partner Connections app to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners. Using this configuration, SAP Business Network for Logistics can directly send documents to your partner’s external systems. Prerequisites SAP Business Network for Logistics must support the desired business partner for B2B connectivity. This means that your company must agree on B2B integration with your carrier. Then, you must invite your network partner to join SAP Business Network for Logistics using the Invite Business Partners app. Only then will the network partner be visible in the Configure Partner Connections app. The process of using the Configure Partner Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Manage Credential Details 2. Create Partner Connection  Note System IDs may consist of alphanumerical characters and the underscore ( _ ) character. You can check the Specification tab of the Excel for further guidance. The system checks all records when you upload your Excel, and displays the errors on the Upload Business Partners screen. You can correct the errors in your Excel and upload it again.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Create Partner Connection Context Using the Configure Partner Connections app, you now need to map the connection details with your business partners and establish a B2B connection. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Create. 2. Provide the following information: Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Business Partner ID Type* ID type of your individual connected business partner or of all connected business partners. A business partner is an entity with which the LBN customer does business (freight contracting, and order execution). You can maintain the following ID types: LBN ID SCAC P44_EU Motor Carrier Number US DOT GLN VAT SAPBPID – SAP Business Partner Number You can choose between general ID types (Any LBN ID or Any Alternate ID) and specific ID types (such as LBN ID, SCAC, or GLN) for a connection with your business partners. Any LBN ID applies this setting to all business partners that are onboarded in the network and connected to your tenant. You can configure alternate business partner ID types to initiate tracking for your shipments. Onboarding of these business partners to SAP Business Network for Logistics is not required. Business Partner ID Value* Unique identifier representing the business partner. Based on the business partner ID type, you choose the business partner ID value: If you choose LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner (LBN ID). If you choose a different ID than LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner ID Value. Network Partner (LBN ID) LBN ID of your network partner. A network partner is an entity which does data transfer/integration to business partners. Network partners will have many business partners in their network and have built integrations to business partner systems. You must provide this information if you receive the data via a network partner. Service* A service is defined based on the combination of the following information coming from a shipper: SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the transportation modes Road and Ocean with the following services: 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Tracking type: Specifies if the tracking is based on a device or vehicle (such as the vehicle’s license plate) or based on a shipment indicator (such as a bill of lading) Transportation mode (such as Road) Scenario (such as tracking) Shipping type (such as LTL - less than truck load, or FTL - full truck load) Resource Road Tracking FTL (Removed) Shipment Road Tracking LTL Shipment Tracking All Shipment Road Tracking FTL Resource Road Tracking LTL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking FCL Resource Ocean Tracking FCL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking LCL Resource Ocean Tracking LCL (Removed) Resource Tracking All (Removed) Freight Tendering All Freight Subcontracting All Supply Chain Risk Freight Ocean Booking All Freight Air Booking All Freight Road Subcontracting FTL Freight Road Subcontracting LTL Freight Road Tendering FTL Freight Road Tendering LTL Freight External Planning All Business Partner Credential Credential provided to you by your business partner, which is maintained in the Manage Credential Details view. You must maintain this field if you communicate directly with your business partner’s system. Network Partner Credential Credential provided to you by your network partner, which is maintained in the Manage Credential Details view. You must provide this information if you are communicating with your business partner via a network partner.  Caution Resource tracking related services have been removed on August 17th, 2024. You can use the shipment tracking related services instead.  Note Only those services that are supported by your business partner will be shown in the dropdown box. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
