file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: * mandatory fields You can either save or save and activate your changes. 3. (Optional): Provide the following information under Custom Headers: Fields Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Key Value Additional information provided by you to your business partners or network partners as key value pairs. It will be sent as header parameters in a Consumer API. Depending on your scenario, you can agree with your business partners or network partners to provide additional information. 4. Save your entries. Manage Credential Details Context The Manage Credential Details view is a secure storage for you to maintain all the credentials that you receive from your business partner or network partner with whom you would like to enable B2B communication. A network partner can consist of a network of business partners (in this case of carriers) that provides services like tracking, freight tendering, and subcontracting. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following credential types: Basic OAuth 2.0 API Key project44 For more information, see the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 add-ons. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Manage Credential Details. 2. Select the tab with the credential type that you want to use for maintaining the credential details. 3. Choose Add and complete the dialog. 4. (Optional): To change the credential details, select the row and choose Edit. System Connections (Shipper) Use the System Connections app for shippers to create a connection and to authenticate inbound and outbound messages between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA.  Note This feature is only available for SAP Business Network for Logistics standard APIs and not for custom API integrations. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You can use the app in combination with each of the following exchange infrastructures between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system: SAP Cloud Integration SAP Process Integration Direct integration using SOA Manager The process of using the System Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Creating a Connection. 2. Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. Authenticating Outbound Messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics. 4. Activating the Connection. Creating a Connection By creating a connection in the System Connections app, you can then specify the details required for authenticating inbound and outbound messages between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system. If you need to connect multiple backend systems, create a connection for each system. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Add in the Connections column. 2. In the New Connection dialog box, select a connection type from the list. The following connection types are available: ABAP-based SAP system Qualtrics SAP Analytics Cloud SAP Cloud ALM 3. Enter the following information for the new connection. a. Connection ID: meaningful name of the connection b. System ID: ID of the system you’re connecting, for example, QW9.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note Specify the source system ID as it appears in your external system (such as SAP Transportation Management). The format must be specified exactly as it appears in the external system. For example, QM7_910. If you use another system ID or change the system ID afterwards, this can have severe consequences. Your processes might stop working.  Caution 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- c. Logical System ID: logical system ID of the system you’re connecting, for example, QW9CLNT170. The Logical System ID field is only available to the ABAP-based SAP system connection type. This setting helps users using both the freight collaboration and global track and trace solutions avoid duplicated tracking records. 4. Click Add. Related Information Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics Maintaining Qualtrics Connection Maintaining SAC Connection Maintaining SAP Cloud ALM Connection Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics To authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your SAP backend system, complete the following steps in the System Connections app. Prerequisites You've acquired a client certificate that's signed by SAP or a third-party certification authority: You’re recommended to use an SAP client certificate, which you can request from your Identity Authentication account on SAP BTP. The certificate is signed by SAP Passport Certification Authority. For more information, see Configuring a Certificate for API Authentication. Alternatively, you can use a client certificate that’s signed by one of the following third-party certification authorities. Third-party certification authorities AddTrust External CA Root Baltimore CyberTrust Root Certum CA DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CA DigiCert Global Root CA GeoTrust Global CA GeoTrust Primary Certification Authority - G3 GlobalSign GlobalSign Root CA Go Daddy Class 2 Certification Authority Go Daddy Root Certificate Authority - G2 Entrust Root Certification Authority If you use both the freight collaboration and global track and trace for tracking harmonization purposes, you must enter the system ID in the following format: <System>_<Client ID>. For example, QW9_170. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Entrust.net Certification Authority (2048) Entrust Root Certification Authority - G2 Equifax Secure Certificate Authority QuoVadis Root CA 2 TC TrustCenter Class 2 CA II SwissSign Gold CA - G2 SwissSign Platinum CA - G2 SwissSign Silver CA - G2 Thawte Primary Root CA Thawte Primary Root CA - G3 VeriSign Class 1 Public Primary Certification Authority - G3 VeriSign Class 3 Public Primary Certification Authority VeriSign Class 3 Public Primary Certification Authority - G5 VeriSign Universal Root Certification Authority Context When you have a client certificate, complete the following steps to authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, select the connection and on the Inbound to Network tab, click Add. 2. In the Add Certificate dialog, enter a meaningful name for the certificate details, and upload the client certificate. a. Note, you can use a certificate for only one connection. b. Make sure you upload the same client certificate to your SAP backend system. This step establishes trust between the systems. 3. When the certificate expires, you need to get a new one and repeat these steps to upload it. To receive notifications about certificate expiration, subscribe to the system notification service. For more information, see Subscribing to System Notifications. Locate the leaf certificate in the Certificate Hierarchy section and click Export to export it as a .cer file. 5. Open the .cer file in a text editor and copy the content. 6. Select Process Integration Runtime in the Service dropdown list, select Integration-flow in the Plan dropdown list and then specify the instance name. b. In the newly created integration instance, click Create in the Service Key section to create a service key that applies the new client certificate: a. Set the Key Type to External Certificate. b. Paste the content you copied in step 5 into the External Certificate field. c. Save the service key. Configure Survey Delivery Settings You as a shipper, may want to send event-based experience management surveys on a regular basis to your customers and carriers to get their feedback on the event execution experience. SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to configure the delivery settings for the surveys that you maintain in the Qualtrics system. Note that to maintain a connection from your SAP Business Network for Logistics system to the Qualtrics system, you must maintain the appropriate settings in the System Connections app. For more information, see Maintaining Qualtrics Connection. You can create a user account in Qualtrics and create surveys based on the templates provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information on creating surveys in Qualtrics, see Customer Delivery Experience Management with Qualtrics . In the Configure Survey Delivery Settings app, based on the settings you have defined, the system sends emails to the email IDs that you have maintained at regular intervals. You can also assign a survey to a specific scenario, location, carrier, and trigger condition. Once the recipients receive the email, fill and submit the survey, the Qualtrics system collates all the feedback and provides the information on their experience. You can use this information to evaluate their experience. The Configure Survey Delivery Settings app consists of the following areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the survey configurations using one or more of the following filters: Location Carrier Survey Name Trigger Condition Delivery Schedule Survey Delivery Configuration Worklist You can view the list of survey configurations that you have already created. When you choose a configuration, the system displays the details on the right pane. Note that when you choose the location name and carrier name you can view the additional details of the location in a dialog box. If you have chosen All Carriers in the carrier setting, you cannot view the additional details. Defining a Survey Delivery Configuration To define a survey delivery configuration, choose Create. The Create New Survey Delivery Configuration pane appears on the right. On this pane, enter the following information: Scenario  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Select a scenario from the drop-down menu that contains the list of pre-defined business scenarios. Note that as of now, Customer Delivery is the only available scenario. Location Select a location from the input help. Note that these are the locations that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app. Carrier Select either All Carriers or a carrier from the input help that contains the list of carriers. Note that the system selects All Carriers by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. Trigger Condition Specify on what event you want the delivery to be triggered. Select one or more events from the drop-down menu that contains the pre-defined events. When you select more than one event, the system triggers email delivery on the occurrence of each event based on the delivery schedule and delivery frequency settings. Survey Name Contains the list of survey names. These are the surveys that you have created in the Qualtrics system. Select a survey that must be sent for this scenario. Recipients Enter the list of email addresses to which the survey email must be sent. When you choose the input help, the system displays the list of email addresses that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app for the selected location. You can select one or more email addresses from the input help to which the survey email must be sent. Delivery Schedule Specify whether you want the delivery to be done every n events or every n days. You define the value of n in the Delivery Frequency field. Note that the system selects Every N Events by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. Delivery Frequency Specify a number. The value that you specify here aligns with the Delivery Schedule. For example, if you have selected the Delivery Schedule as Every N Events and specified the Delivery Frequency as 10, then the system schedules the survey email to be sent on completion of every 10 events. Note that the system selects 1 by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. When you choose Save, the system saves the survey delivery configuration.  Note All the above fields are mandatory. You cannot maintain more than one survey delivery configuration for a specific combination of scenario, location, and carrier. For example, if you have created a survey delivery configuration with the scenario as Customer Delivery, location as Location A, and carrier as Carrier X, you cannot create another survey delivery configuration with the same attributes. However, you can create a configuration with the scenario as Customer Delivery, location as Location A, and carrier as All Carriers. In this case, when a survey must be sent to the carrier X, the settings with the carrier as Carrier X takes precedence over the settings for all carriers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 59 This is custom documentation. Integration with external systems like SAP EWM and SAP TM is possible, and APIs are available for appointment creation and cancellation. As a shipper, you can use dock appointment scheduling functionality in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to book dock appointments for a loading point on behalf of the carrier for loading or unloading services in the docking locations of your organization. You can create dock appointments for confirmed freight orders in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can also integrate dock appointment scheduling functionality in SAP Business Network for Logistics with external systems such as SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM), Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) on SAP S/4HANA, SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM), and Transportation Management on SAP S/4HANA. For this integration, SAP offers APIs to trigger appointment creation and cancelation from an external system to SAP Business Network for Logistics system and send the appointment confirmation from SAP Business Network for Logistics system to your external system. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Prerequisites Before shippers can start booking dock appointments, they need to take some settings in other apps, such as the Manage Locations or General Settings app. You must create a location master data in the Manage Locations app. For more information on creation of a location, see Creating a Location Settings to Enable Appointment Booking To book appointments with the Manage Dock Appointments app and to enable the carriers to self-book dock appointments, you must enable certain settings. The carrier can create a dock appointment before or after confirming a freight order based on your settings. To enable you and the carrier to book dock appointments for a confirmed freight order, you must perform the following: 1. In the Manage Locations app, you must create a location with the following settings: Specify Object Type as Business Partner. Specify the source system ID as it appears in your SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system. Note that the format must be specified exactly as it appears in the SAP TM system. For example, QM7_910. In the External ID field, enter the business partner ID of the business partner associated with the purchasing organization as it appears in the SAP Transportation Management system. Note that in the General Settings app, the system represents the ordering party ID in the format <source system ID>: <external ID>. For more information, see Creating a Location. 2. In the Docking Location Settings app, you must maintain this location as a loading or unloading point and as an active location. For more information, see Manage Entities. You can also enable a carrier or a warehouse operator to create an appointment for a freight order that has not yet been confirmed. To do so, along with the above-mentioned settings, in the General Settings app, you must perform the following: 1. In the Define Appointment Settings tab, add the ordering party by selecting the entry with the system ID and external ID that you created. 2. For this ordering party, under the Maintain Appointment setting, enable the option On Freight Order Creation button. Enabling Role-Based Access Role-based access configuration for the Manage Dock Appointments app involves creating a role from a role template and setting specific location attributes. To enable role-based access of Manage Dock Appointments app and Manage Gate Operations app, proceed as follows: 1. Create a role using the AttributedLocationTemplate role template. You can find this role template under the lbn-live!t1590 application identifier. 2. For the newly-created role, set the location_id attribute in AttributedLocationTemplate to <Source System>:<External ID> of the docking location that you want the shipper to access, for example QM7_910: LBN_WDF. You can find the Source System and External ID of a location in the Manage Locations app. 3. Add this role to the role collection that has been assigned to the shipper. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 61 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Result In the Manage Dock Appointments app, shippers who have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can only access the dock appointments in the docking location that matches the location_id attribute set in AttributedLocationTemplate. In the Manage Gate Operations app, shippers who have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can only access gate logbooks associated to the yard location that matches the location_id attribute set in AttributedLocationTemplate. Integration of Dock Appointment Scheduling with Freight Orders Integration of dock appointment scheduling with freight orders in the transportation management (TM) system streamlines logistics by automatically creating and updating appointments based on changes in freight order details. The dock appointment scheduling functionality is integrated with the freight orders from your external systems such as your transportation system. The system uses an inbound message from your transportation system to create a freight order for the carrier in your SAP Business Network for Logistics system. If you have maintained the relevant settings for the carrier in the General Settings app, the system created appointment requests for this freight order. For more information on the settings, see General Settings. Confirming a Freight Order When a carrier confirms a freight order using the Freight Orders for Confirmation app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system creates appointment requests for this freight order. When you make any changes to a confirmed freight order in your transportation system or in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system updates the appointments accordingly. The following table describes what happens when you update a freight order: Freight Order Update Type Appointment Status Notification Change of arrival or departure dates System updates the open and provisional appointments System cancels the confirmed appointments Exception: If the changed dates match the start and end date of the scheduled appointment, the appointment will not be canceled. System triggers notification on cancellation Change of docking location or loading point System updates the open and provisional appointments System cancels the confirmed appointments System triggers notification on cancellation Change of document references No change in status. System updates the document references.  Note In the Manage Dock Appointments app, shippers who do not have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can access all docking locations. In the Manage Gate Operations app, shippers who do not have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can access all gate logbooks. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 62 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Freight Order Update Type Appointment Status Notification Other changes No change in status. System updates the changes. Canceling or Rejecting a Freight Order When you cancel a freight order from your transportation system or when a carrier rejects a freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system cancels the relevant appointment requests and the booked appointments. The appointments will not be visible on the Self-Book Dock Appointments app for the carrier and the Manage Dock Appointments app. In addition, an appointment is automatically canceled if one of the following is changed: Arrival dates Departure dates Loading point Docking location Reconfirming a Freight Order When you reconfirm a canceled freight order from your transportation system or when a carrier reconfirms a rejected freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system reopens the relevant appointment requests for booking. Preferred Slots / Slots Preferred by Shipper If the shipper provides the relevant acceptable and requested date and time information, it will be displayed when you maintain an appointment. The requested dates correspond to the Loading of Cargo Start Date/Time and Loading of Cargo End Date/Time fields of the respective stop in the transportation management (TM) system. The UI fields are related to the TransportationOrderRequest message type in TM where start date time and end date time are inside the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod tags. The acceptable dates correspond to the Start Date/Time Confirmed by Carrier and End Date/Time Confirmed by Carrier fields of the respective stop in the transportation management (TM) system. The UI fields are related to the TransportationOrderRequest message type in TM where start date time and end date time are inside the AcceptableLoadingDateTimePeriod and AcceptableUnloadingDateTimePeriod tags. Additional Address to Fix Loading Point The subcontracting process passes the loading point ID and unloading point ID from the transportation management system (TM) to SAP Business Network for Logistics. This is done through the Location field under Additional Address at Source Location or Additional Address at Destination Location in TM, which is sent through the InternalID fields under  Note If the changed dates match the start and end date of the scheduled appointment, the appointment will not be canceled. If the start and end date of the scheduled appointment is within the range of the new acceptable start and end date, the appointment will also not be canceled. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 63 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- DetailedLoadingLocation or DetailedUnloadingLocation in the Provider API to Create Freight Order for Subcontracting (TransportationOrderRequest_Out). If the internal ID matches an existing loading point ID, the system preselects and fixes this loading point. It then cannot be changed by the shipper or carrier in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Manage Entities Manage Entities app allows users to define and manage attributes for loading points, docking locations, gates, and yards. You can use this app to define and view the following settings: Loading Point You can define the attributes of a loading point and manage the business hours and block time. Docking Location The loading points situated in the same geographical location are grouped into one docking location. You can define the attributes of a docking location and manage the corresponding loading points. Gate You can define the attributes of a gate and manage the business hours. Yard You can define the attributes of a yard and maintain the corresponding gates and docking locations. Defining Loading Point Settings Loading point settings define operational parameters such as business hours, capacity, and time slot booking for efficient management of loading and unloading activities. To define the settings for a loading point, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Loading Point tab on the left pane. 2. Choose the Add Loading Point button. The create loading point pane appears on the right. 3. Define settings for the following sections: Details Business Hours Block Time 4. Choose Save to save the loading point as a draft. Choose Save and Activate to activate the loading point settings.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 64 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Details Enter the following information in the Details section: Loading Point ID Enter the loading point ID. The loading point ID is the identification of a single loading point for differentiation. You must always book a dock appointment for a specific loading point. That’s why you need to create a loading point. A loading point can have several areas (for example, doors), which are represented by the capacity. You must always assign the loading point to a docking location in order to select a loading point for appointment booking. Location ID Select a location ID (optional). You maintain location master data in the Manage Locations app. The location ID is composed of the source system and the external ID as follows: app. The location ID is composed of the source system and the external ID as follows:<Source System>: <External ID>. It is retrieved from the location master data one time at the beginning. After activation it cannot be changed anymore even if the values in the Manage Locations app change. Capacity Specify the number of loading/unloading activities that can be performed concurrently at the loading point. In a logistics setting, a capacity value of 10 typically indicates that there are 10 doors available in the loading area, allowing 10 trucks to be loaded or unloaded simultaneously. However, the exact meaning of capacity depends on how your operational entities – such as loading points and docks – are defined and modeled within your system. For instance, if each door is represented as a loading point in your configuration, then the capacity assigned to each loading point is 1. Address The following fields cannot be changed any longer after the loading point was activated: Under Location Details: Loading Point ID Location ID Description Address Capacity Activity Type Under Time Details: Time Zone Time Slot Booking Time Slot Duration  Note The location ID of the loading point is not used to determine the loading point of the appointment. Instead, the location ID of the docking location is used to determine the docking location for appointment booking. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 65 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Activity Type Specify whether you can perform loading, unloading, or both activities in this loading point. Time Zone Appointment Date Change If you enable this indicator, the carriers can change the date of a dock appointment. You can specify a range for the loading point so that carriers can change the date within the specified range. Note that a date change is only possible before the cut-off time. Advance Up To Specify the number of days up to which the carrier can advance the dock appointment date. Postpone Up To Specify the number of days up to which the carrier can postpone the dock appointment date. Time Slot Booking Time slot booking is disabled by default so that you cannot specify a time slot duration. While booking an appointment, you do not have to select a time slot and the appointment is valid at any time of the day of the appointment date. The time slot duration is set to 0. If you enable time slot booking for this loading point, you can define the time slot duration for which this loading point can be booked. Time Slot Duration You can select a time slot duration for which the loading point can be booked. You can enter a duration between 5 minutes and 23:59 hours. Restrict Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots You can define whether the maximum duration of all consecutive time slots is restricted. This setting ensures that the sum of time slots to be booked by your carrier cannot exceed the maximum consecutive duration of all adjacent time slots. This restriction only affects the booking for the carrier when they select more than one time slot. They can always book at least one time slot. As the shipper, you can always exceed the maximum duration. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . Maximum Consecutive Duration You can define the maximum duration of all adjacent time slots. Use Derived Appointment Duration If you enable the Use Derived Appointment Duration toggle, the system forces carrier users to book appointment durations based on input from an external system. 1. This can, for example, come from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or transportation management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and/or RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. 2. Additionally or instead, you can add a custom implementation and provide the LoadingDuration and UnloadingDuration fields within the TransporationStage. As a prerequisite, you must implement the  Note This setting that you maintain for a loading point, takes precedence over the settings you specify for the Enable Appointment Date Change in the docking location. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 66 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- following SAP Notes: 3680384 - Scheduling Settings Simulation Interface 3662698 - Loading and Unloading Duration in TransportationOrderRequest_Out 2474555 - Additional SOA Documentation for Enterprise Services "Transportation Order" If both options are implemented, the LoadingDuration and UnloadingDuration fields take precedence. 3. Another option is through the Provider API for Dock Appointment Scheduling (GenericAppointment_In), using the RequestedStartDateTime and RequestedEndDateTime fields. For more information about the setup and the underlying processes, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . Overbooking You can enable or disable overbooking for this loading point. When you enable overbooking, the system allows the user to book appointments even after the available slots are booked. If you enable overbooking, the system displays the following: Overbooking Limit If you enable the overbooking setting, you must specify the overbooking limit. Overbooking limit refers to the number of appointments that can be booked once the available slots are booked. Note that as of now you can set the overbooking limit up to 50. Overbooking for Carriers If you enable the overbooking setting, you must either enable or disable the overbooking option for the carriers. When you enable the overbooking option for carriers, the carriers can book appointments even after the available slots are booked. Note that the overbooking limit that you set here applies for the carriers as well when you enable this setting Capacity and Time Slot At You can specify the level at which you want to enable the capacity and time slot settings. You can select one of the following options: Loading Point Level Validity Period Level Working Hours Level Based on the setting you specify here, you can maintain the capacity and time slot at the respective levels. Assignment Details Assignment with Docking Locations If you enable this setting, the loading point can be associated with multiple docking locations in the same time zone. If you disable this setting, the loading point can be associated with only one docking location in the same time zone. Assigned Docking Locations You can select the docking locations in the same time zone with which you want to share the loading point.  Note After loading point activation, this field can only be changed to a lower level ( Loading Point Validity Period Working Hours , and the settings defined for the newly selected level will be used. It can't be changed back to a higher level.  Note The Microsoft Excel upload feature only works if you have selected the Loading Point Level option. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 67 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- After selecting the relevant docking locations, you can assign the loading point to these additional docking locations. To do so, you need to edit the docking location, choose the + icon, and select the loading point from the list under Add Loading Point. Remarks You can enter the additional information about the loading point in this section. Validity Period Choose the add icon in this section to add an entry of validity period. Enter the following information: Period Specify the duration for which the entry of validity period is valid. Working Days Specify the working days of the loading point. Working Hours Specify the working hours for the specified working days. To add another entry of validity period, choose the add icon. You can create up to 10 entries per validity period. It is recommended that you specify the working hours in accordance with the time slot that you have maintained for this loading point. Deleting Validity Periods To delete an entry of validity period, choose the delete icon that appears next to the entry. You can also choose Delete from the details pane that appears on the right when you select the entry of validity period. Note that you cannot delete an entry of validity period if the entry contains appointments in the future. You can only delete an entry that either does not contain any future appointments or contains appointments in the past. Modifying Validity Periods You can select an entry of validity period and modify the details on the right pane. Modifying Periods You can increase or reduce the period.  Note You can add multiple entries of validity period per working day for a loading point. However, the combination of period and working days specified in an entry of validity period must not overlap with the consecutive entries.  Note You can only reduce a period that does not contain any future appointments or contains appointments that are in the past. You cannot reduce the period, if the period that you are reducing contains appointments that are in the future. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 68 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Modifying Working Days You can add a working day for the selected entry of validity period. Note that the system allows you to delete a working day for a time period only when the deleted working day does not contain any future appointments. Modifying Working Hours You can increase or reduce the working hours. Block Time You can block time for special occasions, such as public holidays, maintenance, or cleaning. Choose the add icon in this section to add a time block. The system displays the block time pane on the right. Description Specify a description for the time block. Disable Appointment Booking Specify whether you want to disable appointment booking only for the carriers or for all. If you select For All, both you and the carriers cannot book appointments during the blocked time. If you select For Carriers, only the carriers cannot book an appointment during the blocked time. The blocked time will be available for you to book an appointment. Max. Capacity When you enable the Max. Capacity toggle, the maximum capacity is blocked for this loading point, and the capacity in the dropdown above is disabled because it is no longer relevant. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Maximum Capacity Blocker . Including Overbooking When you enable the Include Overbooking toggle, the capacity maintained under Overbooking Limit is blocked for this loading point. You can only enable this toggle when the Max. Capacity toggle is enabled. Capacity In the dropdown menu, you can view the capacity that you have specified for this loading point. You can select a capacity that you want to block from the dropdown menu. If you have enabled Capacity and Time Slot At as Validity Period Level, you can view and modify the Capacity and Time Slot Duration in this pane.  Note When you modify the working hours, there might be inconsistencies in the start and end time of the time slots. Hence, it is recommended that you modify the working hours in multiples of the time slot duration. You cannot modify the working hours, if the selected entry of validity period contains appointments that are in the future. If you have enabled Capacity and Time Slot At as Working Hours Level, you can view and modify the Capacity and Time Slot Duration in this pane. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 69 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Date and Time You can specify the start and end date and time, and you can choose between single blocks and recurring blocks. Single Block: Creates a single occurrence of the time block. Recurring Block: Creates multiple occurrences based on the specified recurrence interval and the recurrence end date. You can specify a daily, weekly or monthly recurrence interval, such as every third week on a specific day of the week. For monthly recurrence intervals, you can choose between the following options: Day: A specific day of the week, such as every first Monday of the month. Date: A calendar date, such as 1 for the first day of the month. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Announcing Recurring Block Times . All Day Event When you enable the All Day Event toggle, you can create a block for an entire day or for several days in a row. Note: When creating an All Day Event, ensure that the duration of the appointment is less than the chosen recurrence interval. For instance, if your appointment lasts two days, the earliest possible recurrence is every three days or more. This means the recurrence interval must always be longer than the appointment duration. Start Date and Time Specify the start date and time for the time block. End Date and Time Specify the end date and time for the time block. View History When you enable the View History toggle, the system also displays the appointments that are in the past. By default, time blocks in the past are hidden. You can block the time for a loading point that has been shared with multiple docking locations. When you do so, the system blocks the entire capacity of the loading point for the blocked period across all the docking locations with which the loading point has been shared.  Note Duration The maximum duration of a single block is 31 days. If you want to block your loading point for more than 31 days, you can use the Deactivate option of the loading point or use a recurring block. For more information, see the status Inactive under Header on this page. The maximum duration of a recurring block depends on the recurrence pattern: Daily: The maximum duration is 31 days, and it can occur up to every 31 days. The duration must be shorter than the recurrence frequency. The recurrence end date can be set up to one year from the start date. Weekly: The maximum duration is 24 hours, and it can occur up to every 6 weeks. The recurrence end date can be set up to one year from the start date. Monthly: The maximum duration is 24 hours, and it can occur up to every 12 months. It must be shorter than the recurrence frequency. The recurrence end date can be set up to three years from the start date. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 70 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

If the docking locations that share the loading point are in different tenants, then only the user who created the time block can release the same. Viewing a Loading Point Loading point settings provide detailed information about the configuration and status of loading points, including capacity and time slots. To view the loading point settings, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Loading Point tab on the left pane. 2. Enter the loading point ID in the search bar on the left pane to search for a specific loading point. 3. Choose a loading point from the results. The system displays the detail view of the settings on a right pane. The detail view consists of a header and other sections. Header The header section displays the following information: Loading Point ID Shared Displays Shared when this loading point has enabled sharing with multiple docking locations Loading Point Icon Displays the loading point icon. Also displays a shared sign on this icon when a loading point has enabled sharing with business partners. You can view the sharing details by choosing this icon. The system displays the Loading Point ID, Location ID, Shared By, and Permissions. Location ID Capacity Displays the number of loading/unloading activities that can be performed concurrently at the loading point Status Displays one of the following statuses: Draft Capacity Check If a blocker or appointment already exists, you can only block the remaining capacity, not the maximum capacity. The capacity to be blocked must always be less than or equal to the maximum capacity of the loading point validity period. If a new blocker exceeds the maximum capacity, it cannot be created. To resolve this, you can either reduce the capacity of the blocker or cancel existing blockers or appointments. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, a carrier can onboard onto the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, invoicing and milestone reporting. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration runs on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), utilizing one of the following infrastructures: Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia The data used in the solution is also stored in the respective data center. Information for shippers: Collaborative managed transactions supported in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are tailored to the relevant SAP backend systems. For freight collaboration scenarios, SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration offers out-of-the-box connectivity to shippers with the following systems: SAP Transportation Management (on-premise) or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition SAP Logistics Management For more information about supported releases, see SAP Note 2620322 . In addition, out-of-the box connectivity is delivered for truck carrier networks, including project44 for visibility services and B2B carrier connectivity for freight tendering and subcontracting. Selected digital freight forwarders support on-demand road transportation with real-time pricing and subcontracting. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Data Protection and Privacy You use the Data Protection and Privacy apps to manage personal and sensitive personal data of employees, individual customers, and contacts. Data processing systems store master data or transactional data used to perform business processes and to document them. In many cases, it involves the personal data of employees, individual customers, and contacts. In many countries, the storage, disclosure, and removal of such personal data from data storage systems must be in accordance with statutory data protection  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- laws. One requirement in many countries is that the personal data can only be stored if a clear business reason for this data retention exists. Most data protection legislation proscribes fixed retention periods, defining how long data can be stored in data systems, after which it must be deleted. In addition, legislation in many countries stipulates that the data protection officer must disclose the personal data of individuals, when requested for it. Retention Management SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration restricts the access of personal data on completion of its business purpose. That is, not all the user groups can access the personal data after the expiration of originally defined residence period. The Retention Management app enables you to define rules for residence and blocking of personal data for apps that belong to a specific application group. These rules restrict the usage of documents containing personal data. In the Retention Management app, you define the residence period and the blocking period. The residence period and blocking period are together called as the retention period. Defining Residence and Blocking Periods To define the residence period and blocking period of various applications, perform the following: 1. Sign in to the Fiori Launchpad and choose the Retention Management tile. 2. Select an application type.  Note You must familiarize yourself with the following important definitions relevant for using the Retention Management app: Residence Period The period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Blocking Period The period between the residence period and the deletion of the data is the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. Retention Period The period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. For example, in the Freight Requests for Quotation app, business partner is a master data and the end of purpose of this master data is until the business partner is in the network. The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. Data Subject An identified or identifiable natural person. An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 3. Enter a residence period. The residence period is the period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Note that if you do not specify a residence period, the system by default assigns a residence period of 12 months for the application type. 4. Enter a blocking period. The blocking period is the period between the residence period and the deletion of the data is the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a Data Protection Officer (DPO), can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. Note that if you do not specify a blocking period, the system by default assigns a blocking period of 12 months for the application type. 5. Choose Save. The system stores the residence and blocking periods for the specific application type. Blocking Store Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can log into the Fiori Launchpad and choose the Blocking Store app to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format by choosing the Download button. Identifier Displays the unique identifier for the document. Status Displays the status of the document, for example, in blocking period. End of business Displays the date when the document got into the end of business state. App name Displays the name of the app with which the data is associated. Administration information Personal Data Record  Note For the Define User Settings application type, the system displays only the Data Subject ID field. You must enter the identifier of the person in which the system stores the personal settings. When you choose Delete, the system deletes the personal settings of the individual from the system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Data subjects have the right to receive information regarding their personal data undergoing processing. The personal data record feature helps you to comply with the relevant legal requirements for data protection by allowing you to search for and retrieve all personal data for a specified data subject. The search results are displayed in a comprehensive and structured list containing all personal data of the data subject specified, organized according to the purpose for which the data was collected and processed. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration uses Personal Data Manager for information and retrieval of personal data. A user with the right role can access the Fiori Launchpad of Personal Data Manager and search for the transactions that have the data of the data subject. To access the Fiord Launchpad of Personal Data Manager, use an URL of the following format: https://<your-subdomain>- pdm-portal.<domain-name>/sites For more information about Personal Data Manager, see the Administration Guide for Shippers. Audit Log Personal data is subject to frequent changes. Therefore, for review purposes or as a result of legal regulations, it may be necessary to track the changes made to this data. When these changes are logged, you should be able to check which employee made which change, the date and time, the previous value, and the current value, depending on the configuration. It is also possible to analyze errors in this way. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration supports change and audit log. When you change any personal information, the system updates the audit log. Users with the required authorization can request for the change log. To request for a log, the authorized user must create an SAP support message in the component BC-NEO-AUDITLOG. For more information about how to request for audit logs, see Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. Manage Business Profile Whether you are a shipper, solution owner, or logistics provider, you will land on the company profile page in SAP Business Network when opening the Manage Business Profile app. On this page, you can manage and adjust your company information as per your needs. This enables potential partners and relevant stakeholders to know more about your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strength. You can maintain the basic information about your company. This includes but is not limited to the type of organization, year founded, and annual revenue to help shippers and solution owners evaluate you as a potential logistics provider. The Product and Service Categories, Ship-to or Service Locations, and Industries sections of your company profile allow you to provide detailed information about the products or services you offer, the locations you ship to or provide services, and the industries you serve. This information is critical because shippers and solution owners usually discover your company based on the product and service categories and ship-to or service locations. The Additional Addresses section provides you with an effective and intuitive way to add and manage addresses beyond the primary business address, such as branch offices, regional offices, warehouses, or other physical sites associated with your company. Including these addresses provides a comprehensive overview of your company's geographical reach and operational scope. The Contacts section enables you to create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or multiple roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, and Technical Contact, designating them as companywide contacts. This guarantees that their contact details are readily available to all current and potential trading partners on the network. More Information 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 5 This is custom documentation. On the Company Profile page, click a pencil icon to edit the information in a section, and enter or revise values as necessary. Note the following constraints and guidelines when you edit your company profile: Company D-U-N-S Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a D-U-N-S number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Supplier Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. Year Founded—Enter the year in yyyy format. Number of Employees—The approximate number of people who work for your organization. Annual Revenue—Select a currency range. If you prefer not to state your annual revenue, scroll to the bottom of the list and select Contact Company for Information. Business Type—Check the business types that apply to your company. Product and Service Categories—Select your company's products and services by clicking Add Category. Ship-to or Service Location—Select the locations your company ships to or serves by clicking Add Locations. Industries Served—Select the industries your company serves. 2. For detailed information, see Creating Additional Addresses. 4. To add contact information to your company profile, select Contacts from the left navigation pane. For detailed information, see Managing Contact Information. Creating Additional Addresses To add an additional address to your company profile, follow these steps: 1. Select Additional Addresses from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. On the Additional Addresses page, click Create. 3. On the Create Address page, specify the following fields: Address Name (Mandatory): Give a unique name to easily identify this address. Address Type: Specify the type of address. Country/Region (Mandatory): Specify the country or region where the address is located. Address Line 1 (Mandatory): Enter the primary address information. Address Line 2 (Optional): Include additional address details, if applicable. Address Line 3 (Optional): Include further address details, if necessary. City (Mandatory): Specify the city where the address is located. State (Mandatory): Provide the state or region where the address is situated. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Zip (Mandatory): Enter the postal or ZIP code for the address. Contact: You can add contact details associated with this address, including: Phone Number: This field is mandatory. Mobile Number: Optionally provide a mobile contact number. Fax Number: If applicable, provide a fax number. Email: This field is mandatory for email communication regarding this address. 4. Once all required information is entered, click Save. The new address will appear in the Addresses table. 5. Repeat the process to add more addresses. Managing Contact Information Companywide Contact Companywide contacts have their contact information accessible to both current and potential business partners on the network. Assign individuals in your company as companywide contacts. This ensures that your business partners know the right people to contact for various issues or questions. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. Click Create in the upper right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 3. On the Create Contact Personnel Entry page, specify the basic information and address of the contact. The basic information includes Contact Name, Email, Business Title, Phone, Fax, and Company Assignment. Each contact must have a name, phone number, and email. The Company Assignment field specifies the companywide roles assigned to a contact. If this field is specified, the contact is designated as a companywide contact for the selected role, and their contact information is accessible to all business partners on the network. Each contact personnel can be assigned with multiple companywide roles. 4. After providing the necessary information, click Create. 5. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 6. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table. After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Profile Settings You can specify the visibility and availability of your company profile on the Profile Settings page. If you are a shipper or solution owner, before trying to connect with business partners that operate in a different data center, you must first make your company profile available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Steps to Configure Profile Settings 1. Open your company profile. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- 2. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 3. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile to appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to potential business partners in their search results. Once your company profile becomes visible, shippers or solution owners can discover your company on the network and send you connection requests for further partnership. Default value: Yes b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to allow profile data replication across data centers. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers in SAP Business Network for Logistics. For carriers and data providers, this setting is enabled by default. Shippers and solution owners need to enable it manually. 4. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results Once Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will become searchable and visible to potential business partners. Otherwise, your company profile will not be shown in any search results, and thus, no business partners can reach you for further connections. Once Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network is enabled, your company profile data will be replicated across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Future updates to your profile will also be automatically synchronized across all data centers. For shippers and solution owners, enabling this setting allows for establishing cross- data-center connections. If this setting is not enabled, your company profile will be only available in the data center where you initially onboarded. As a result, no cross-data-center connections can be established. Carrier Apps and APIs With SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, you as a carrier can use the the apps to get started on the network and to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight tendering, subcontracting, dock appointment scheduling, milestone reporting and freight settlement. The SAP Business Network Logistics Provider, basic membership page is the central entry point for logistics providers (carriers and data contributors) to find all relevant assets regarding activation, integration and operation of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Carrier APIs As a carrier, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight contracting, freight booking, freight tracking, and freight settlement.  Note Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed.  Note These apps are also suitable for logistics service providers that perform the role of a carrier who receives freight requests for quotation or freight orders from an ordering party. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/15db9545fb79453c90e49ebad6cc57fc.html. Define User Settings (Carrier) The Define User Settings app allows you to define defaults that best suit the way you work. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. Distance In this section, you can define the default unit of measurement for distance. The system uses this setting in other apps in your area. Notification Subscriptions In this section, you can subscribe to notifications for various scenarios and specify the email address and preferred language for receiving the notifications. Note that you cannot subscribe to a scenario without maintaining an email address. When you subscribe to notifications for a scenario, the system can send email notifications based on the settings you make in the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information on managing notification settings, see Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). Manage Notification Settings (Carrier) You can use this app to schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert. The system sends you notifications via emails. The Manage Notification Settings app consists of the following areas: List of scenarios This area displays the scenarios for which you can configure alerts. Filter You can use this filter to filter the scenarios. When you select a scenario from this drop-down menu, the system displays only that specific scenario. Configuration details The system displays the following in this area: Configurations The system displays notification types and the settings that you can configure for each type. On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. Upload Locations You can fill the details of locations using an Excel template and then upload this template back to the app. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Choose Upload to open the Upload Locations page. 2. Click Upload on the up-right corner, then download the Excel template available by choosing Download Excel Template. 3. Fill the details of the locations you want to upload in the template. 4. In Choose File, locate the modified Excel template and then choose Upload. Editing a Location To edit a location, proceed as follows: 1. Use the following fields to filter locations: Location ID Description Location Type Country/Region City 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. 3. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner of the details page.  Note You can enter the geographical coordinates for the location records in the Longitude and Latitude columns manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you upload your file. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location records you are uploading is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo- coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. The detail view of the location consists of a header and other sections. Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. This includes the business purposes, the longitude/latitude coordinates, and the revision history. Geographical Coordinates and Map This section displays the geographical coordinates of the location. Define Additional Information The Additional Information section contains a list of additional information associated to a location record. This section enables you to define necessary custom characteristics or references by adding your information items. An information item comprises a name, the type of the item, and the corresponding value. Type: Type of the additional information item. It can be either Text or Alternative ID. Name: Name of the additional information item. If you set Type to Alternative ID, the name of the item must be set to one of the following values: GLN DUNS UN/LOCODE IATA Airport Code Value: Value that corresponds to this additional information item. Manage Custom Codes You can use the manage custom codes feature to extend the drop-down list for the following fields: Country/Region State Location Type Time Zone Role of Contact  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For example, you do not find the region code you need in the drop-down list of Country/Region. To create a custom code, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Manage Custom Codes button. 2. On the Manage Custom Codes page, select the field for which you want to extend the list, and then choose Create. 3. Specify the name, language, and description of the code, and then choose Save. Results After you create a custom code, you can find it from the Custom category when you expand the corresponding drop-down list. If needed, you can also remove it or edit its description on the Manage Custom Codes page. Global settings for Geo-Coordinates You can use Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box to define how the system handles geo- coordinates for all location records. In Generate geo-coordinates automatically, you have the following options: Off (Default): Do not generate geo-coordinates automatically even if they are missing. Generate: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. (Applies to all locations including the existing ones) Overwrite: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when coordinates are missing or overwrite them if they already exist. (Applies to locations created after you enable this option) Enable Risk Monitoring If you have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections, you can determine whether or not to use the service provider to monitor risks at a certain location in Manage Locations. Prerequisites  Note Options in Generate geo-coordinates automatically only take effect for location records where you leave Calibrate coordinates when saving with the default option Apply global settings. The Calibrate coordinates when saving setting in location records takes precedence over Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box. For example, when you set Calibrate coordinates when saving to No in a location record, the system does not generate or calibrate coordinates for the record even if Generate geo-coordinates automatically is set to Generate or Overwrite.  Note Risk information is not displayed in Manage Locations. Instead, it’s displayed on the map view of the Logistics Execution Insights app. You use Manage Locations to specify a group of target locations where you want to monitor risks. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 94 This is custom documentation. Procedure To enable risk monitoring for a specific location, follow these steps: 1. Click the location record for which you want to monitor risks to open its details page. 2. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner. 3. Click to select the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox and then choose Save. Alternatively, you can enable risk monitoring for multiple locations at once. To do this, select the location records, and then choose Risk Monitoring Enable . Results The risk monitoring service provider starts monitoring risks at the location. If you’ve subscribed for the intelligent insights add-on, you can view the risk information on each target location in the Logistics Execution Insights app. To notify the service provider to stop monitoring risks at a location, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in the corresponding location record. To stop using the risk monitoring feature for all locations in your supply chain, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in each location record where you previously enabled the feature in Manage Locations and then deactivate the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. More Information Editing a Location Creating a Location Self-Book Dock Appointments You, as a carrier, can use this app to book a dock appointment for a freight order when the corresponding vehicle is about to reach a certain stop for loading or unloading. The appointments you booked will then be visualized in the Manage Dock Appointments app. This helps shippers have a precise estimate on the quantity of upcoming dock appointments. Process When you confirm a freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system updates the Self-Book Dock Appointments app with this freight order, so that you can create an appointment for this freight order. Note that to perform this, the ordering party must have enabled the relevant settings. Alternatively, the ordering party can enable you to update the Self-Book Dock Appointments app with a freight order that has not yet been confirmed. In other words, once the ordering party sends the freight order from SAP Transportation Management system, the freight order is updated in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, with the status as New. Before you confirm this order, the  Note You can also configure this setting when creating a new location record. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- system lists this freight order in the Ready for Booking table in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. You can select and create an appointment for this order. Note that the system allows you to cancel only those appointments for which the associated gate logbooks are in the status Ready for Check-In or Cancelled. Worklist (Self-Book Dock Appointments) The Self-Book Dock Appointments app consists of the Ready for Booking tab and the Booked Appointment tab. Ready for Booking The Ready for Booking tab consists of all freight documents that are ready for maintaining an appointment. You can view the following information on this tab: Location Loading Point Ordering Party / Reference Document License Plate Activity Type Displays whether you can perform loading, unloading, or both activities. Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time Appointment Status Displays whether the document has a canceled appointment or the appointment is yet to be booked Means of Transport Booking Cut-Off Displays the cut-off date and time for booking an appointment Location ID Freight Order Reference Documents Booked Appointment The Booked Appointment tab consists of all freight documents with an appointment. You can view the following information on this tab: Loading Point  Note For more information, you can watch the following video: How to Self-Book Dock Appointments (English only). 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 96 This is custom documentation.
