View History When you enable this toggle, the system also displays the appointments that are in the past. Personalization You can choose the personalization icon to manage your settings. You can perform the following: Columns You can add or remove columns that are displayed on the table. Sort You can do an ascending or descending sort of a column in the table. Filter You can filter the documents for appointment based on the loading type values. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Group You can group the documents for appointment based on one or more of the attributes specified in the input help. Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the dock appointments in Microsoft Excel format. This feature is available in both Ready for Booking and Booked Appointment tab. Maintaining a Dock Appointment Context The Ready for Booking table lists documents for which you can maintain an appointment. These include: Documents that have a stop matching of one of active loading points but do not have an appointment booked Documents whose appointment has been canceled To maintain a dock appointment, select an eligible document from the list, and then choose Maintain Appointment to proceed with the appointment creation process. You cannot update appointments in the past. For more details, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. Select the document from the Ready for Booking table, and then choose Maintain Appointment. You can also click the document to view its details page. Additionally, booking cut-off times that are less than 24 hours away are highlighted in orange. This helps you better prioritize your appointment booking. 2. On the Maintain Appointment page, specify the Loading Point and Date fields (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available). The system displays a list of available time slots and the slots preferred by your shipper (acceptable and requested ones). If the shipper does not allow carriers to change the appointment date, you are not able to edit the Date field. Note that the system displays DST STARTS when the day light savings time begins and DST ENDS when the day light savings time ends. 3. Depending on the duration of the loading or unloading activity, choose one or more consecutive time slots from the Time Slot list. Note that if the shipper has disabled the time slot option for a loading point, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. The shipper can restrict the maximum duration of consecutive time slots. This ensures that the sum of bookable time slots cannot exceed the total duration of all adjacent time slots. However, you can always book at least one time slot. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . If your shipper uses the Derived Appointment Duration feature, the following applies: When you book an appointment, the booked time slots must match the calculated duration from the shipper. If an exact match is not possible, you must ensure that the booked time is not exceeded by more than one time slot. Example: If the derived appointment duration is set to 27 minutes, and a single time slot has 15 minutes, you must select two consecutive time slots of 15 minutes. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . 4. On the Information tab, enter the following under Driver Details: Driver Name Driver Phone Number Additional Driver Name Additional Driver Phone Number You can also click the Ordering Party link to open the quick view page. Hyperlinks on the quick view page enable you to perform various operations. For example, you can click Email to launch an email program. 5. On the Information tab, enter the following under Resource Details: License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck) Truck ID Trailer ID 6. If there is any additional information about the appointment, enter it in the Notes section. Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. We recommend you to avoid entering sensitive personal data. 7. If there are any attachments that you want to add to the appointment, choose the Add button under the Attachments section. You can only upload files that meet the following criteria: Files of the formats: jpg, jpeg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, tiff, tiff-fx Image files less than 6MB file size Document files less than 5MB file size File name less than 150 characters including file extension 8. Choose Maintain. Results A dock appointment has been maintained for the document. You can find this appointment on the Booked Appointments table. From there, you can access the appointment and view the details. After you maintain a dock appointment, shippers can view your appointment using the Manage Dock Appointments app. Maintaining a Grouped Appointment When you select a docking location in the calendar view, you can select two or more documents from the Ready for Booking tab and maintain multiple appointments in a single group with the same time slot. Note that the system enables you to create a grouped appointment only when the following attributes of the selected documents are same: Location Loading Point (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available) 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Activity Type Transport Means Description Transport Means Type Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time To maintain multiple appointments in a single group, proceed as follows: 1. Select two or more documents with the similar attributes from the Ready for Booking tab and choose Maintain Appointment. Note that as of now, you can only select up to 20 documents to create a grouped appointment. 2. You can view multiple appointments that are created under the Grouped Appointments tab. You can perform the following: You can add or remove documents here. When you choose Add, the system displays the list of documents that contain similar attributes. You can select the documents and choose Add to Group. You can choose the appointment ID to switch to a different appointment that is not the current appointment. You can choose the freight order under the Freight Order column to navigate to the freight order in SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. On the Scheduling tab, specify the Loading Point and Date (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available). Note that if the shipper has disabled the option to change the appointment date for carriers, you may not be able to edit the Date field. 4. Depending on the duration of the loading or unloading activity, choose one or more consecutive time slots from the Time Slot list. Note that if the shipper has disabled the time slot option for a loading point, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. The shipper can restrict the maximum duration of consecutive time slots. This ensures that the sum of bookable time slots cannot exceed the total duration of all adjacent time slots. However, you can always book at least one time slot. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . If your shipper uses the Derived Appointment Duration feature, the following applies: When you book an appointment, the booked time slots must match the calculated duration from the shipper. If an exact match is not possible, you must ensure that the booked time is not exceeded by more than one time slot. Example: If the derived appointment duration is set to 27 minutes, and a single time slot has 15 minutes, you must select two consecutive time slots of 15 minutes. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . 5. On the Information tab, enter the following under Driver Details: Driver Name Driver Phone Number Additional Driver Name Additional Driver Phone Number 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: 6. On the Information tab, enter the following under Resource Details: License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck) Truck ID Trailer ID 7. Choose Maintain. Results A grouped appointment has been maintained for documents. You can find this appointment on the Booked Appointments table. From there, you can access the appointment and view the details. You can also edit or cancel the appointment from there. When you edit or cancel, you can choose whether you want to edit or cancel only the current appointment or all the appointments in the group. After you maintain a dock appointment, shippers can view your appointment using the Manage Dock Appointments app. Viewing an Appointment You can access the list of maintained appointments in the Booked Appointment tab. When you select an appointment, the system displays the appointment details. The detail view of an appointment consists of a header and several sections. Header The system displays the following information in this section: Location Note that when you choose the location, the system displays the additional details of the location that is assigned to the docking location, such as time zone, address, and remarks. Loading Point Appointment Start Date and Time Appointment End Date and Time Information The system displays the following information under this section: General You can view the Ordering Party, Activity Type, Dangerous Goods, Incoterm, and Incoterm Location. Note that when you choose the ordering party, the system displays the additional details of the ordering party. Booking Details  Note Once you maintain the grouped appointment, you can edit the grouped appointment and add notes and attachments. Note that when you do so, the notes and attachments are added only to the current appointment and not all the appointments in the group. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 101 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You can view the Loading Point, Remarks, and Business Hours of the loading point. Active Vehicle Resource You can view the active vehicle resource details such as Transport Means Type, Vehicle Category Code, Vehicle Type Code, and Vehicle Resource ID. Driver Details You can view the driver details such as Driver Name, Additional Driver Name, and Driver Phone Number. Resource Details You can view the License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck), Truck ID and Trailer ID. Admin Data You can view the Created By, Changed By, Created On, and Changed On details. Guest User You can view the guest user details such as Name, Company Name, and Email ID. Reference Documents You can view the reference document details such as reference document ID, stop details, and arrival and departure date and time. When you choose a freight order, the system navigates to the freight order in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The link is only available if the appointment was created based on a freight order that exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Stops Displays the visual representation of the freight order execution flow with the source location, intermediate stop locations, and destination location. You can see the appointment ID created in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the expected dates for departure and arrival, and the activity type performed for the appointment, such as loading or unloading. When you choose a stop, the system displays the following stop details in a dialog box: Arrival Date and Time Displays the expected arrival date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Departure Date and Time Displays the expected departure date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Requested Start Date and Time Displays the requested start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Acceptable Start Date and Time Displays the acceptable start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Requested End Date and Time Displays the requested end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Acceptable End Date and Time Displays the acceptable end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- The following Appointment Details are displayed for all appointments created in SAP Business Network for Logistics but not for the currently displayed appointment and not for external appointments: Appointment ID Displays the appointment ID if the appointment was created by SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can use this ID to search for the appointment in its corresponding docking location in the Manage Dock Appointments app. Appointment Start Date and Time Displays the start date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Appointment End Date and Time Displays the end date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Cargo You can view the following cargo details: Cargo Item Displays the description of the cargo item. Type Displays whether the cargo item is a package, product, or a container. Logistical Details Displays the quantity, gross weight, gross volume, and dimensions. Equipment Details Displays the equipment type and equipment group. Reference Documents Displays the reference document details. Special Requirements Displays the following: Dangerous Goods If the ordering party has provided dangerous goods information, you can view this information from the Cargo section by choosing Yes in the Dangerous Goods column. This opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. Temperature Requirements Other Details Displays the following: Over-Dimensional Non-Stackable High Value 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 103 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Notes You can view the additional information about the appointment that you have added. Attachments You can view the attachments that you have added. You can edit or cancel the appointment by choosing the Edit and Cancel Appointment buttons respectively. Note that the system allows you to cancel only those appointments for which the associated gate logbooks are in the status Ready for Check-In or Cancelled. Enabling Docking Location-Based Access You can apply location-based authorization in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app to control user access to appointments belonging to a specific docking location. In other terms, you can assign a docking location to a user ID. When you do so, the user can view only those documents for appointment that belong to the docking location ID. To enable location-based authorization, navigate to the User Management app. Create and assign a user group to control user access to specified docking locations in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. For more information, see Create a User and Assign User Groups. Maintaining a Dock Appointment (Guest User) You as a customer or a carrier, who is not on SAP Business Network for Logistics (but your shipper is on the network), may want to pick up a shipment from a shipper’s warehouse. You may also want your carrier to do this on your behalf. To do so, you must maintain the dock appointment details in the SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration system. The shipper can provide a guest user access to you and can enable you to maintain the appointment details in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration using an API. Once the shipper provides you a guest user access, the system generates an URL and sends it to you in an email. To validate the authenticity of the accessing personnel, when you navigate to the URL, the system prompts you to enter additional appointment information such as the purchase order number. Once you pass the security validation, you can view the appointment details. You can select the time slots yourself and save the appointment. You can also invite your carrier to access this appointment and select the time slots. To do so, you must perform the following: 1. Choose the Add Carrier button. A dialog box appears. 2. Enter the carrier details in this dialog box and proceed. The system sends an email to the carrier with the URL for guest user access of the appointment. The carrier can navigate to the URL, access the appointment details, and select the time slots. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 104 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Note that only the URL that you receive as a customer contains the Add Carrier button. The URL that the carrier receives does not contain this button. Freight Orders for Reporting The Freight Orders for Reporting app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of your delivery trucks is delayed on-route, you can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so they can replan if necessary. Additionally, the app lets you upload and send documents, such as proof of deliveries, to your ordering parties. Note that this app has been deprecated and will be sunset shortly. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. The reporting app contains the track relevant freight orders irrespective of whether the orders are relevant for confirmation or not. In the Freight Orders for Reporting app, you can view the events that you reported manually and the events reported by the visibility provider. The manually reported data and the events reported by the visibility provider are synchronized to the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app and SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or SAP S/4 HANA system. The Freight Orders for Reporting app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you open the app, the main view is displayed. It has two screen areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight orders by one or more of the following options: Freight Order Ordering Party Reporting Status Displays one of the following statuses: Ready for Reporting When you confirm a freight order, the system sends this freight order to the Freight Orders for Reporting app with this status. Reporting in Progress  Note As of now, in the Freight Orders for Reporting app, you can report only arrival and departure events. Alternatively, you can keep your ordering parties in the loop during the transportation of their freight by sending them visibility data (including real-time location, estimated ETA, event status, and time of event completion) via a supported visibility provider. For more information about supported visibility providers, visit the SAP Community wiki for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration , and the homepage for SAP Business Network for Logistics . You can report events for a freight order even when you have not reconfirmed a freight order that has been updated by the ordering party. In the worklist, you can view the tag Updated for such updated freight orders. Also, a message appears on the worklist when there are freight orders updated by the ordering party and you have not yet confirmed these freight orders. You can use the link in the message to navigate and view the list of freight orders with pending reconfirmation. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 105 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- When you start reporting the events in the freight order then the system sets the status of this freight order as Reporting in Progress. Reporting Completed When you have reported all planned events in the freight order, then the system sets the status of this freight order as Reporting Completed. Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required) After you start reporting the events in the freight order, if any changes are done to this freight order, then the system sets this status. Canceled If the freight order is canceled, the system updates the status of this freight order as Canceled. Driver Name License Plate Delay Departure Date Arrival Date Source Location Destination Location Received On Orders Pending Reconfirmation Consignee Party Name Destination Address Source Address Vendor ID Proof of Delivery Status You can select one of the following options: Reported at Last Stop When you select this filter option, you can view all freight orders for which you have reported the proof of delivery at the last stop. Not Reported at Last Stop When you select this filter option, you can view all freight orders for which you have not reported the proof of delivery at the last stop. Worklists You can use the following worklists Events to Report, Skipped Events, and All. From each worklist, you can click on a freight order to navigate to its detail view. The detail view has two screen areas: Header 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 106 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The header displays information such as the freight order ID, ordering party, and the reporting status of the freight order. Sections In the Reporting section, you can report the planned events in freight order, as well as upload both proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents. You can also display extra details in the Information, Contacts, Notes, and Drivers and License Plate sections. Worklists (Freight Orders for Reporting) To restrict the number of freight orders that are displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (Events to Report, Skipped Events, All). All The All worklist displays the information available on the Events to Report and Skipped Events worklists. Additionally, the All worklist lists freight orders that you have finished reporting, as well as canceled freight orders. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status Driver and license plate Number of reference documents Event type and location of the current event that you must report Scenario type Planned time of the current event that you must report By how long the event is delayed Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location The number of skipped events within the freight order Events to Report The Events to Report worklist displays the freight orders – and the events within the freight order – that you must report. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 107 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Reporting status Drivers and license plate Number of reference documents Event type and location of the current event that you must report Scenario type Planned time of the current event that you must report By how long the event is delayed Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location Skipped Events The Skipped Events worklist displays freight orders that include one or more events that you’ve skipped. This means when you skip an event on the Events to Report worklist, you can easily find the freight order later on when you’re able to report the skipped event. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status Drivers and license plate Number of reference documents Scenario type The number of skipped events within the freight order Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the dock appointments in Microsoft Excel format. This feature is available in both Ready for Booking and Booked Appointment tab. Detail View (Freight Orders for Reporting) The detail view of a freight order consists of a header and several sections. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 108 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Header The header displays information about the freight order. The following fields may be of interest to you: Freight order details You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status (Ready for reporting, Reporting in progress, Reporting in progress (freight order reconfirmation required), Reporting completed, Canceled) The status of a freight order changes from Ready for reporting to Reporting in progress when you report any event (or if you skip an event or mark an event as unable to report). The status changes from Reporting in progress to Reporting completed only when you have reported the final time (the time of completion) for all events or marked any events that you cannot report to unable to report. Contact details of the ordering party Information The Information section displays general data about the freight order. Reporting The Reporting section displays all the events in the freight order. Report Final Time You can report a final time for the event Report Delay You can report a delay to the shipper. You can specify the duration of delay, reason for delay, and additional details. Report Proof of Pickup For a departure event, you can report a proof of pickup. Note that you must upload a minimum of one attachment. Report Proof of Delivery For an arrival event, you can report a proof of delivery. Note that you must upload a minimum of one attachment. Report Exception You can report exceptions to the shipper in case of unforeseen events such as damages or other issues. Note that you have an option to upload an attachment. Unable to Report When you are unable to report an event, you can notify the shipper by choosing this option. Note that you can select any time zone when you report a final time. However, the system converts it to the local time zone of the respective source or destination location while displaying it in the Freight Orders for Reporting app and the shipper’s Track Freight Movement app. Contacts 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 109 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- If provided by the ordering party, the Contacts section displays the company name of the ordering party along with the phone number and the email address of the contact person. This section also displays the contact details for each individual stop (stop number and location). Notes The Notes section displays comments left by the ordering party. Drivers and License Plate The Drivers and License Plate section displays the driver and vehicle license plate information that was provided in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting Events in a Freight Order While your company transports freight for an ordering party, use the Freight Orders for Reporting app to report when planned events in the freight order are completed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a new ETA (expected time of arrival), enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. Prerequisites Before you can report the events of a freight order, the freight order must be confirmed in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Once the system creates a freight order in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app, this freight order is also available in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. Context You can report an event from both the Events to Report worklist and from the Reporting section in the detail view of the freight order. Using the worklist is useful for reporting the events of multiple freight orders while they are executed during the day. Whereas, using the Reporting section is useful for reporting several events for one freight order. If you don't have the information required to report an event, you can skip the event and report it later. For more information, see Skipping an Event. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Orders for Reporting app. 2. On the Events to Report worklist, report the first event of the freight order. a. Optional: If the event cannot be completed at the planned time due to a delay, you can inform the ordering party. To do so, select Report Delay from the inline menu of the freight order and enter the details of the delay in the Report Delay dialog box. Note, if you don’t know the duration of the delay, you can leave the Expected Time and Delay fields empty. b. When the event is complete, select Report Final Time from the inline menu of the freight order and complete the Report Final Time dialog box. Enter the final time, time zone, reason for delay, and additional details. Note, if you report a time that is earlier than when the freight order was received in the app, the time may not be saved by the shipper's system. After reporting the final time of the event, the data for the next planned event is displayed on the worklist. 3. Repeat step 2 for all events in the freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 110 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To see an overview of the events you have reported for the freight order, click the freight order to display the Reporting section. Next Steps When you receive electronic copies of the proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents, you can use the app to upload and send them to the ordering party. For more information, see Sending Proof of Delivery and Proof of Pickup Documents to the Ordering Party Skipping an Event If you don't have the information to report an event that is listed on the Events to Report worklist, you can skip the event and report it later. This enables you to carry on reporting the rest of the events in the freight order. To skip an event, on the Events to Report worklist choose Skip Event from the inline menu of the freight order.  Note When the ordering party makes any changes, subcontracts, and executes the freight order in the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, the system does the following: Updates the reporting app with these changes. Sets the status of the reporting app to Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required). To report events in the reporting app, you must reconfirm this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When the ordering party sends the freight order for subcontracting, you can confirm the order in Freight Orders for Confirmation app and start reporting events in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. The freight order status is set to Ready for Reporting in the reporting app. Meanwhile, if the ordering party changes the order details in SAP TM and executes it, System creates the order in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app. In this case, the status of freight order in the reporting app becomes Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required). In this scenario, the ordering party must perform the subcontracting process again in the SAP TM system. Only after this is done, you can view the updated freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you reconfirm this freight order, the system updates the status Ready for Reporting in the reporting app. When the ordering party creates a freight order and subcontracts the order in SAP TM, the system updates this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you confirm this order, it appears in the reporting app and also in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app. After this is done, when the ordering party makes any changes to this freight order in SAP TM system and executes the freight order, the system updates the order only in the Track Freight Movement app and not the reporting app. However, the status of this freight order becomes Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required) in the reporting app. In this scenario, the ordering party must perform the subcontracting process again in the SAP TM system. Only after this is done, you can view the updated freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you reconfirm this freight order, the system updates the status Ready for Reporting in the reporting app.  Note You can skip an event even after you have reported a delay. You cannot skip the last event of a freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 111 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When you skip an event, the freight order is listed on the Skipped Events worklist. This ensures that you don’t forget to report the event. When you’re able to report the final time of the skipped event, click the freight order to display the Reporting section and enter the final time for the event. If you'll never be able to provide the final time of the skipped event, you can mark the event as unable to report. By doing so, the freight order will no longer be listed on the Skipped Events worklist. And, if the skipped event is the only outstanding unreported event in the freight order, the reporting status will change to Reporting completed. To mark an event as unable to report, go to the Reporting section in the details view of the freight order and select Unable to Report from the inline menu of the event. Sending Proof of Delivery and Proof of Pickup Documents to the Ordering Party To upload and send the ordering party proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents, go to the Reporting section in the details view of the freight order and upload the documents to the relevant events. For a proof of delivery document, choose Upload Proof of Delivery from the dropdown menu of the relevant arrival event. Enter the final date and time, time zone, and upload relevant attachments and choose Report. Note that the time zone that you specify while uploading a proof of delivery, will be converted to the local time zone of the destination location while the system displays it in the shipper’s Track Freight Movement app. For a proof of pickup document, choose Upload Proof of Pickup from the dropdown menu of the relevant departure event. Enter the final date and time, time zone, and upload relevant attachments and choose Report. Note that the time zone that you specify while uploading a proof of pickup, will be converted to the local time zone of the source location while the system displays it in the shipper’s Track Freight Movement app. When you upload an electronic copy of a proof of pickup and proof of delivery, the system updates these documents in ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app. Note that only when the ordering party updates the proof of pickup and delivery as planned events in the SAP Transportation Management system, the ordering party can view the documents in the Track Freight Movement app. Manage Freight Execution The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if a shipment is delayed, you can provide a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so the ordering party can replan if necessary. Also, you can perform the following in this new app: Planned milestone events You can view the milestones planned by the ordering party. Planned and unplanned events You can report various planned and unplanned events. The ordering party is not informed when you skip an event.  Note The ordering party is not informed when you mark an event as unable to report. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 112 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Estimate You can report an estimate for any planned event. Delay You can report delays at both the document-level and at an event-level. Proof of pick-up and delivery You can submit proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. Additional events You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. Event history You can view all the events reported by you and all other business partners. You can also view the event history for a specific planned event. Attachments You can view all the attachments specific to the freight execution in the Attachments tab. This app contains the track relevant freight documents irrespective of whether the documents are relevant for confirmation or not. In this app, you can view the events that you reported manually and the events reported by other business partners. The manually reported data and the events reported by the APIs are synchronized to the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or SAP S/4 HANA system. Note that you can report events for a freight order even when you have not reconfirmed a freight order that has been updated by the ordering party. This app consists of a main view and a detailed view. When you open the app, the main view is displayed. It consists of two screen areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight documents by one of the following criteria to restrict the number of freight documents displayed: Freight Document Freight Document Type Ordering Party Departure Location Arrival Location Departure State Arrival State Departure Date Arrival Date Created On 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 113 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Reference Documents Mode of Transport Category of transportation, for example, road, ocean, air, and so on. Reporting Status Displays the reporting status based on the documents that are ready for reporting. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Execution Status Displays whether the freight is Ready for Execution or In Transit. For more information, see Freight Execution Statuses. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Estimated Status Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is as running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. For more information on estimated status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Arrival Country The last arrival location of a freight document. It consists of the three letters "IMO" followed by unique seven-digit numbers. Worklists You can use the following worklists: All, Documents for Reporting, and Reporting Completed. From the main view, you can navigate to the detailed view of a freight document. Worklist (Manage Freight Execution) 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 114 This is custom documentation. All The All worklist displays all the freight documents that are in the system. You can view the following information for each freight document. Note that you can add one or more of the following fields to the worklist from the settings icon in the worklist: Freight Document/ Document Type Displays the ID of the freight document and the type of the freight document for which the execution has been planned. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. Ordering Party Arrival Country The last arrival location of a freight document. Cargo Quantity and UoM Cargo quantity of a freight document and unit of measure. Cargo Volume and UoM Cargo volume of a freight document and unit of measure. Cargo Weight and UoM Cargo weight of a freight document and unit of measure. Changed On Container Created By Created On Dangerous Goods 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 115 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- An indicator that shows whether the cargo contains substances and objects that are a threat to humans, animals, or the environment when they are transported. Departure Country Estimated Status Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is as running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. It consists of the three letters "IMO" followed by unique seven-digit numbers. Incoterm An international commercial term that defines the terms of sales and the passing of risks for import and export of merchandise. Incoterm is published by the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) and widely used in commercial transactions. Incoterm Location A geographical location (harbour name, railway station name, transfer-cargo-terminal name, and so on) that is entered in conjunction with an Incoterm to uniquely identify the point from which the division of costs and transfer of risks are assumed between two commercial parties (purchaser and seller). License Plate Number Mode of Transport Planned Gross Duration Planned Net Duration Planned Total Distance and UoM Proof of Delivery Status Reference Documents Shipping Type Stops Truck ID Vessel ID Departure State The state as specified in the departure address. Arrival State The state as specified in the arrival address. Documents for Reporting 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 116 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The Documents for Reporting worklist displays all the freight documents for which the reporting is yet to be completed. This worklist displays the same fields as the All worklist. Reporting Completed The Reporting Completed worklist displays freight documents for which the reporting status is set as Reporting Completed or marked as Unable to Report. That is, when all the planned events have either been reported or marked as unable to report. This worklist displays the same fields as the All worklist. Reporting an Event You can select a freight document and report planned and unplanned events or mark all the pending planned events as unable to report directly from the worklist page using the Report button. For more information on reporting an event, see Reporting Events. Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the freight documents in Microsoft Excel format. This feature is available in all tabs. Detail View (Manage Freight Execution) The detail view of a freight document consists of a header and several sections. Header You can view the following important information about the freight document: General Details Displays the freight document ID, departure and arrival location details. You can also view the following information: Ordering Party Displays the ordering party identifier. Mode of transport Category of transportation, for example, road, ocean, air, and so on Execution status Displays whether the freight is Ready for Execution or In Transit. For more information, see Freight Execution Statuses. Reporting status Displays the reporting status based on the documents that are ready for reporting. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Departure Location In this sub-section, you can view the departure location details along with the departure date and time. When you choose the departure location, you can view the location address in a dialog box. Arrival Location 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 117 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- In this sub-section, you can view the arrival location details along with the arrival date and time. When you choose the arrival location, you can view the location address in a dialog box. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Note that if an estimated time has been reported for the latest planned event, the estimated status appears below the current status. Reporting Overview You can view the total number of planned events. When you choose the number of events, you can view the number of reported events, events unable to be reported, skipped events, and pending events in a dialog box. Information The information tab contains the General Data section and the Events Overview section. You can view the following details in these sections: General Data General data Displays the carrier details, bill of lading, and mode of transport. Terms and conditions Displays the incoterm location, movement type, shipping type, and traffic direction. Cargo information Displays the cargo details such as the weight, volume, quantity, container ID, and dangerous goods. Voyage Displays the voyage details such as the voyage number, vessel ID, and IMO number. Transportation Displays the transportation details such as the planned total distance, planned gross duration, planned net duration, number of visits, number of loading stops, and number of unloading stops. Events Overview Displays all the planned event details for each stop in a card format. You can report a planned event for the specific event directly from the card using the Report button. You can perform one of the following actions: Report When you choose the Report button, you can report the final time and estimated time for that specific planned event. You can also add a reason code, description, and add an attachment. For more information on reporting an event, see Reporting Events. Skip Event If you do not have the information to report an event, you can choose this option and report it later. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 118 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Unable to Report You can choose this option if you will never be able to provide the final time of the planned event. View History When you navigate to additional options and choose the View History button in the card, you can view all the events that have already been reported for that specific planned event on the right pane. Reference Documents In this tab you can view all the reference documents along with the date and time it was created. Attachments In this tab, you can view the attachments that you have uploaded while reporting a planned or an unplanned event. You can also view the attachments uploaded by the other business partners while reporting an event. For each attachment, you can view the following details: File name Event Displays for which event the file has been uploaded. Location Displays the event location. File size Uploaded by and uploaded on Contacts In this tab, you can view the contact details of business partners and stops. You can view the name, address, phone number, and the email address of the contact person for each of these contacts.  Note Attachment file type must be base 64 You can attach documents related to the business document or business process in this section. You’re recommended to avoid attaching sensitive personal data. You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpeg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx. Image files must be less than 6MB file size. Document files must be less than 5MB file size. When you mention the file path, you must mention the file name along with the extension. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 119 This is custom documentation. Freight Execution Statuses You can view the detailed information about the various statuses and the transition of the statuses that occur in the Manage Freight Execution app during the freight execution process. Execution Status Displays the execution progress of a freight document. You can view one of the following statuses: Ready for Execution When a freight document is set to ready for transportation execution in the ordering party’s external system, the execution status is set as Ready for Execution. This is the initial execution status of a freight document. Execution Started When an event is reported at the source location, the execution status is set as Execution Started. In Transit When a departure is reported, the execution status is set as In Transit. Arrived at Intermediate Location When the vehicle arrives at an intermediate location, the execution status is set as Arrived at Intermediate Location. Arrived at Destination When the vehicle arrives at the destination location, the execution status is set as Arrived at Arrived at Intermediate Location. Executed When the last planned event has been reported, the execution status is set as Executed. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 120 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Reporting Status Displays a status based on the event reporting in a freight document. You can view one of the following statuses: Ready for Reporting When a freight document is made available in the Manage Freight Execution app, the initial status is set as Ready for Reporting. Reporting in Progress When the carrier starts reporting events in the freight document then the reporting status is set as Reporting in Progress. Reporting Completed When the carrier has reported all planned events in the freight document or marked the remaining events as Unable to Report, then the reporting status is set as Reporting Completed. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. You can view one of the following statuses: As Planned This status appears when no event has been reported for the freight document and the reporting deadline has not yet lapsed. Early This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred ahead of time. On Time This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred on time. Late This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred late. Overdue This status appears when the latest planned event has not been reported by the reporting deadline. Delayed This status appears when a delayed event is reported on either the latest planned event or at the document-level. Estimated Status Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. You can view one of the following statuses: Running Early 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 121 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen before time. Running on Time When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen on time. Running Late When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen late. Proof of Delivery Status Displays whether the proof of delivery has been reported at the last stop. You can view one of the following statuses. Reported at Last Stop Not Reported at Last Stop Reporting Events While your company transports freight for an ordering party, you can use the Manage Freight Execution app to report planned and unplanned events in the freight document. You can also perform the following when you report an event: Report an estimate for any planned event, enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a delay at both the document-level and at a planned event-level. You can report proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. You can report an event directly from the worklist page or the detailed view page for a freight document. When you choose the Report button, you can choose one of the following options. Planned Event You can report a planned event as follows: 1. Select an event for which you want to report. You can view the list of events planned by the ordering party for you. Note that the system pre-selects the next planned event. You can change the selection as required. 2. Enter the final time or estimated time along with the time zone. 3. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 4. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 5. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. Unplanned Event You can report an unplanned event as follows: 1. Select an event from the supported event types. 2. Optionally, select a stop at which this unplanned event must be reported. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 122 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- 3. Enter the final time along with the time zone. 4. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 5. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 6. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. Unable to Report Remaining Events You can choose this option if you will never be able to provide the final time of the event. Events History Header When you choose the View Events History button in the detailed view page, you can view all events reported during the freight execution in a card format. This includes all the planned and unplanned events that have been reported multiple times. For each event, you can view the following information in a card format: Event type Current status When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated status When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Location Planned on Final time When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated time When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Business partner Attachment Reason Code When a reason code is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Reason Code Description When a reason code description is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Events Overview When you navigate to additional options in the Events Overview sub-tab and choose the View History button in the planned event card, you can view all the events that have already been reported for that specific planned event on the right pane. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 123 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Invoice Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for invoicing using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using this app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. The Invoice Freight Documents app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you launch the app, the system displays the main view with the following areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight documents to restrict the number of freight documents displayed. You can filter based on freight documents based on one or more of the following attributes: Freight document Departure date Ordering Party Arrival date Arrival location Document status Customer account Reference document ID Reference document type Changed on Created on Departure location Gross amount Gross amount currency Purchasing group Mode of transport Worklists You can use the following worklists: To be Invoiced, Invoicing in Process, Awaiting Ordering Party's Response, Completely Invoiced, and All. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view of a freight document. The detail view has the following areas: Header You can view information such as the general details, freight document amount, invoiced amount, and invoice status. Sections You can view further details of the freight document in the following sections: Information 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 124 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Cargo Stages Charges Business Partners Notes Attachments Worklist (Invoice Freight Documents) To restrict the number of freight documents displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (To be Invoiced, Invoicing in Process, Awaiting Ordering Party's Response, Completely Invoiced, All) that are based on the invoice status of the freight document. All The All worklist displays all freight documents that are settlement relevant. The system displays the following information for each freight document: Ordering party and freight document Displays the ordering party details and the freight document ID. Also displays a warning message if the freight document contains zero amount. Customer account Displays the customer account ID. Departure date and time Arrival date and time Departure location Arrival location Arrival location time zone Mode of transport Purchasing group Reference documents To be Invoiced The To be Invoiced worklist displays all freight documents that are not yet invoiced. This worklist displays the same information as the All worklist. Invoicing in Process The Invoicing in Process worklist displays all freight documents for which you have already created an invoice. This worklist displays the same information as the To be Invoiced worklist. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 125 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Awaiting Ordering Party's Response The Awaiting Ordering Party's Response worklist displays those freight documents which are not yet responded by the ordering party. This worklist displays the same information as the Invoicing in Process worklist. Completely Invoiced After an invoice has been created for a freight document in your Transportation Management (TM) system (TM in SAP S4 HANA 1809 onwards), the status of the freight document becomes Completely Invoiced. These invoices are displayed in the Completely Invoiced worklist in the Invoice Freight Documents app. This worklist displays the same information as the Awaiting Ordering Party's Response worklist. Document Statuses You can view the document statuses Updated, Settled Outside, and Cancelled, as appropriate, as a label in the worklist. When the ordering party makes any changes to a freight document with the status as Invoicing in Process in their transportation system, these changes are updated and the freight document status is set as Updated. When the ordering party cancels a freight document in their external system, you can view the Cancelled label for the freight document in the worklist. In the ordering party's external system, when a freight order that has been sent for confirmation to the carrier has been cancelled, the corresponding freight order is cancelled in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean), and the Invoice Freight Documents app. Note that the freight document can be cancelled only when there is no active dispute or an invoice document corresponding to the freight document. When you settle a freight document outside of SAP Business Network for Logistics in your external system, you can view the Settled Outside label for the freight document in the worklist. Create Invoice You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice for your ordering party using the Create Invoice button. For more information, see Creating Invoices from Freight Documents. Note that this button is available only in the following tabs: All To be Invoiced Completely Invoiced Create Collective Invoice You can select two or more of these freight documents and create a collective invoice for your ordering party using the Create Collective Invoice button. For more information, see Creating a Collective Invoice. Note that this button is available only in the following tabs: All To be Invoiced 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 126 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Completely Invoiced Mark or Unmark as Settled Outside You can settle a freight document outside of SAP Business Network for Logistics in your external system. When you do so, you can select one or more relevant freight documents and choose the mark or unmark as settled outside icon. From the drop down menu, you can choose the option Mark as Settled Outside. Note that once you mark a freight document as settled, it no longer appears in the To be Invoiced tab. You can use the Document Status filter to view the marked documents in the All tab. You can also undo this action by choosing the Unmark as Settled Outside option from the drop down menu. Note that you can only select up to 100 freight documents from the worklist while choosing one of these options. Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the freight documents in Microsoft Excel format. Note that when you use this feature, the applied filters are considered for data selection. Detail View (Invoice Freight Documents) The detail view of a freight document for settlement consists of a header and several sections. Header You can view the following important information about the freight document: General Details Displays the freight document ID, document status, contact details, delivery date, and purchasing group. When you choose the contact, the system displays the phone number, email, and address of the ordering party. Freight document amount Displays the sum of all amounts in the freight document Invoiced amount Displays the total amount of charges that are currently invoiced in the freight document. Note that this amount does not include the charges that are yet to be invoiced. Invoicing status Displays the status of the invoice, that is, whether the invoice is yet to be invoiced, in process, awaiting ordering party's response, completely invoiced, or submitted. Information The Information section displays the following subsections: General Displays the total distance, duration, service level, and freight agreement details. Departure Location Displays the date and time and address. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 127 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Arrival Location Displays the date and time and address. Active Vehicle Resource Displays the mode of transport, means of transport, vehicle code, vehicle type code, and vehicle resource ID. Administrative Data Displays the administrative information. Invoice Details Section You can view the following information for each invoice associated with the freight document: Invoice Displays the invoice IDs of the included invoices. You can navigate directly to the displayed invoices from this section. Invoice Date Gross Amount Displays the total gross invoice amount of the invoice. That is, if you have a collective invoice, the gross invoice amount is the total of gross amounts from all the included freight documents. Note that the gross amount is the sum of net amount and tax amount. Document Status Displays the status of the invoice, that is whether it is a draft or if it has been submitted. Disputes Reference Documents Section Displays the document type and document ID of the reference documents. Cargo The Cargo section displays information on the cargo items involved, such as type, locations, quantity, gross weight, net weight, dimensions, and gross volume. Stages You can view the transportation stages in this tab. You can view the details such as item, type, locations, quantity, gross weight, net weight, dimensions, and gross volume for each stage.  Note You can view the details of all cargo item types such as container, package, product, and service. You can navigate through the entire cargo item hierarchy. For example, from a container to the packages, package to the products or services and so on to view the respective details. The ordering party can implement a business add-in (BAdI) to display only the main cargo items. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 128 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Charges The Charges section displays the following information: Charge description Displays the charge type details for each stage in each freight document. Charge types are the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. Charge type (Transportation System) Classification of charge line that indicates the type of charges such base rate, surcharge, or discount, as specified in the ordering party's SAP Transportation Management system. Rate amount/unit Displays the flat rate amount or rate amount per unit, for example, USD 20 per 1 kg. Quantity Displays the total quantity relevant for calculating the final amount. Final amount Displays the final amount that has been derived from the rate amount, quantity, and calculation method. When you select a charge line, you can view the following additional details specific for the selected charge: Transportation charges You can view the charge details such as line number, charge type, calculation methods, and payment terms. Line number Charge description Displays the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. These are the transportation mode- specific codes that are predefined by SAP Business Network for Logistics. Calculation method Displays the logic with which the system calculates the charges. Payment terms Displays the conditions of payment you agreed with your ordering party with respect to goods supplied or services provided. Logistical reference Displays the item or stage information for a charge line (for container, package, product, or stage) from which the system obtains the logistical data. Calculation basis Displays the actual base or factor with which the system calculated the charges. You can view the calculation basis for rates belonging to a rate table. Exchange rates Displays the exchange rate information that is used as the basis for currency conversion. Notes 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 129 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Displays the notes specified for the charge line. Business Partners You can view the various business partners associated with the freight document. The system displays the role of the business partner (whether the business partner is a carrier or an ordering party). The system also displays the address of the business partner. Notes You can view the comments added by the ordering party. Attachments You can view the attachments added by the ordering party. Creating Invoices from Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. To create an invoice or a collective invoice from freight documents, perform the following: Creating an Invoice To create an invoice, you must select a freight document from the worklist page and choose Create Invoice. Alternatively, you can also choose Create Invoice on the header area of the detail view of a freight document. You can also select multiple freight documents from the worklist page and choose Create Invoice. The system creates individual invoices, one each for all the selected freight documents. Creating a Collective Invoice  Note You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx Image files must be less than 6MB file size Document files must be less than 5MB file size File name must be less than 150 characters including file extension  Note If you already have an invoice in draft version for a freight document, you cannot create a new invoice. You cannot create an invoice or a collective invoice for a freight order with the document status as Cancelled. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 130 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To create a collective invoice, you must select two or more freight documents from the worklist page and choose Create Collective Invoice. For more information about collective invoice creation, see Creating a Collective Invoice. Note that if you already have a collective invoice in draft version for the selected freight documents, you cannot create a new collective invoice. Exclusion of Zero Charges When you create an invoice from a freight document that includes a planned charge with a zero amount, these zero charges are excluded by default in the invoice document. Also, in the Manage Invoices app, you can view a message in the Charges tab that indicates the same. You can review and manually include these charges if needed. Note that this exclusion applies only to planned charges and not unplanned charges. Creating a Collective Invoice When you select two or more freight documents and create a collective invoice, the system attempts to combine multiple freight documents that you have selected into a single invoice document. However, if certain conditions are different between the selected freight documents, the system cannot create a combined invoice. In this case, the system creates multiple invoices. Split and Consolidation Criteria The system uses the following split and consolidation criteria when it attempts to create a collective invoice: Account Invoicing party Payee Document currency Calculation level Payment terms Item currency Note that the system makes a split with no specific document of priority. Example You have two freight documents for invoicing for which you want to create a collective invoice. You select the freight documents in the worklist screen and choose Create Collective Invoice. However, the document currency in the first freight document does not match the document currency in the second freight document. In this case, the system creates two invoices.  Note If a freight document is being invoiced item wise or stage wise, and if an invoice has been created only for some items or stages, then you can create an invoice for the remaining items or stages. However, you can create a subsequent invoice only after the ordering party accepts or rejects the first invoice. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 131 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Creating Subsequent Invoices A carrier can submit subsequent invoices for an individual freight document. A carrier may want to invoice only a few charge lines for the charges he has actually incurred and then submit a second invoice for the remaining charges he has subsequently incurred. Alternatively, the carrier may want to charge all the lines in one invoice and then later add his unplanned charges in a subsequent invoice. In the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics, multiple invoices can be created for the same freight document. A subsequent invoice can only be created for an individual freight document on the following conditions: There is no active invoice for that given freight document. If the carrier creates an invoice but does not submit it to SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) and then tries to create a second invoice, an error message is returned informing him that an invoice already exists. An invoice has already been submitted to the SAP TM system. Only when the first invoice has been submitted to the SAP TM system can a second invoice be created, but the invoicing cannot be done for the lines that have already been invoiced. When the subsequent invoice is submitted from the freight collaboration option, it creates the subsequent invoice in SAP TM after the previous invoice has been transferred for Accruals. The carrier can choose to exclude certain lines from an invoice – either because he wants to invoice it later or he has not incurred that charge – by clicking the cross icon. This will ensure that only a few charge lines are invoiced but not others. Excluded lines can be part of a subsequent invoice. A further condition of subsequent invoicing relates to parent and child lines. If a parent line is part of one invoice, all its dependent lines are also expected to be part of the same invoice, so parent and child lines always appear as part of one invoice. They cannot be split and invoiced in different invoices. If the carrier chooses to exclude a child line but not the parent line, a warning message is displayed informing the carrier that the excluded line has a reference in that invoice and that after the invoice has been submitted, it will no longer be possible to invoice the excluded child line. Adding a Subsequent Charge When you create a subsequent invoice, you can add a subsequent charge for a charge type which has already been invoiced. In the Charges tab, for each charge line, you can choose the icon to add a subsequent charge. When you choose the icon, you can enter a new subsequent charge and the old invoice amount is displayed below. The rate amount has been disabled for subsequent charges. You can add the additional amount in the Final Amount field and submit the invoice. For example, if the already invoiced amount for the charge type Basic Freight is EUR 100, and you enter EUR 50 as the subsequent charge, then the final invoiced amount for Basic Freight will be EUR 150. Review Freight Documents You can have a billing process in place with your ordering party where you do not submit an invoice to your ordering party for the transportation services you provide. Instead, your ordering party pays you automatically in a self-billing process, based on the information in the freight document.  Note This feature is available only if the ordering party has enabled the necessary settings for you. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 132 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- You can view all the freight documents that are ready for self-billing by the ordering party using the Review Freight Documents app. This app displays all the freight documents that you have received from one or more ordering parties. You can view the transportation charges in the freight document based on which the ordering party creates a self-billed invoice. The Review Freight Documents app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you launch the app, the system displays the main view with the following areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter freight documents based on one or more of the following attributes: Freight document Departure date Ordering party Arrival date Arrival location Reference document ID Reference document type Changed on Created on Departure location Dispute status Gross amount Gross amount currency Purchasing group Mode of transport Worklists You can use the following worklists: No Disputes, In Dispute, and All. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view of a freight document. The detail view has the following areas: Header You can view information such as the general details, freight document amount, and dispute status. Sections You can view further details of the freight document in the following sections: Information Cargo Stages Charges 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 133 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Business Partners Notes Attachments Worklist (Review Freight Documents) To restrict the number of freight documents displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (No Disputes, In Dispute, and All) that are based on the dispute status. No Disputes This worklist displays all freight documents for which there are no active disputes. The system displays the following information for each freight document: Freight document ID and ordering party Displays the freight document ID and ordering party details. Also displays a warning message if the freight document contains zero amount. Customer account Departure date and time Arrival date and time Departure location Arrival location Arrival location time zone Purchasing group Reference documents Viewed and Not Viewed In the No Disputes tab, you can toggle between the Not Viewed and Viewed sub-tabs to view the documents that you have not viewed and viewed respectively. You can select one or more documents in the not viewed tab and choose Mark as Viewed. The system marks these documents as viewed and moves them to the Viewed tab. Similarly, you can select one or more documents in the viewed tab and choose Mark as Not Viewed. The system marks these documents as not viewed and moves them to the Not Viewed tab. Note that you can also perform these actions from the details view page of a freight document. In Dispute This worklist displays all freight documents for which the disputes are in progress (the dispute document will be in one the statuses – New, Submitted, For your approval). This worklist displays the same information as No Disputes worklist along with the count of number of disputes. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 134 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- All This worklist displays all the freight documents for reviewing. This worklist displays the same information as In Dispute worklist. Detail View (Review Freight Documents) The detail view consists of a header and several sections.
