Resubmitting Invoices You can reopen a submitted invoice to make any necessary changes and then resubmit the invoice. Context If an invoice for a freight document contains certain errors such as, an incorrect tax charge type, the invoice might not appear in the SAP Transportation Management system when you submit it. In this case, the customer can inform the carrier that the invoice has not been created in SAP Transportation Management and then ask the carrier to reopen the invoice, make the necessary changes and resubmit the invoice. Procedure 1. Go to the Submitted worklist tab to reopen an invoice that has already been submitted. 2. Choose the Reopen button. The system then changes the invoice status to Error to indicate that the invoice is in progress again and the invoice appears on the Error worklist tab. 3. Make the necessary changes, such as excluding all 0 amounts or adding tax codes, and choose Save to save the invoice. The invoice status remains as Error. 4. Choose Submit to resubmit the invoice. The invoice status then changes to Submitted. Results Once the invoice has been corrected and resubmitted, it is created in the SAP Transportation Management system.  Note You only need to reopen an invoice if the invoice has failed in SAP Transportation Management. Otherwise, you should not reopen invoices that have already been submitted. If you reopen an invoice that was created in the SAP Transportation Management system without any errors and then try to resubmit it, the system rejects the invoice as the invoice ID is identified as a duplicate. This ensures that the process is not interrupted.  Note The invoice ID is read-only, but you can modify the Charge fields, and Notes and Attachments can also be edited. Manage Disputes As a carrier, you can have a self-billing process in place with the ordering party, wherein you do not submit an invoice for the transportation services. Instead, the ordering party settles automatically based on the information in the freight document. In this process, you can have differences and potential disputes between what the ordering party expects to pay against what you expect to be paid. To keep good business relationships, you need to work closely with the ordering party to resolve these differences in a collaborative way. You need to get clarification on the differences and converge on an understanding with the ordering party on how to resolve the differences. You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned charges, rates, quantities, and final amounts. Invoice Ordering Party Displays the ordering party details. Customer Account Displays the customer account ID. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Invoice Process Settings You can select the invoice process settings. On dispute resolution, when you submit the dispute to the ordering party, a dialog box appears and you can choose one of the following options for the invoice: Submit the invoice with updated charges to the ordering party If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice with the updated charges related to this dispute will be submitted to the ordering party. If there are taxes in the invoice, you can modify the taxes before resolving the dispute so that the invoice is submitted to the ordering party with the appropriate tax amounts. Update the invoice and set the status as Ready for Submission If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice related to this dispute will be updated and the status will be set as Ready for Submission. You can navigate to the invoice in the Manage Invoices app and submit it. Set the invoice status as Rejected by Dispute If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice related to this dispute will be set as Rejected by Dispute. You can create and submit a new invoice. An information message indicating the status of the invoice after dispute resolution appears on the header area of the dispute details page. If you want to modify the invoice process settings, you can do so using the link available in the information message. Acknowledgement Message After Dispute Resolution A dispute is resolved when the shipper or the carrier accepts all charges proposed by the other party. For example, the carrier proposes charges and the shipper accepts these charges. When the party that has the document accepts all the charges, then the system updates these charges in the freight document in the shipper's SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system and the dispute status is updated as Submitted for confirmation. When the resolved charges that have been agreed upon by the shipper and the carrier in the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics are updated in the shipper's SAP TM system, the system displays an acknowledgment message that the charges have been updated. If the charges are not updated, the system displays a failure message. Success message When a successful acknowledgment message is received in the freight collaboration option, the status of the shipper's dispute is set to Resolved. Then, the carrier dispute is set to Resolved, after which the carrier invoice status is updated to Submitted (for an invoicing dispute) and the carrier invoice is submitted to the SAP TM system. When the ordering party rejects a dispute document, you can re-submit the dispute document by adding a note for the rejected charge line without modifying the rate amount. Note that this is relevant only for disputes from SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. The ordering party has rejected the dispute document with the reason as attachment missing. In this scenario, you can add an attachment without modifying the rate amount and submit the dispute document.  Note This setting is applicable only when there is a change in the invoice post dispute process. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 161 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 3 -- When the system receives an acknowledgment message from the SAP TM system, it sets the dispute status changed as Resolved. Failure message If the SAP TM freight document update fails, TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In will fail with errors, and the acknowledgment message (TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out) will not be triggered. The shipper must process this error in Forward Error Handling (FEH), which has already been registered and implemented on the inbound side for TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. FEH is configured to perform error handling. Therefore, the error message is forwarded to FEH post-processing, which the shipper can access by choosing the red flag. You user launches the transaction sxi_monitor in the shipper's system and provides the interface name as TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. Error message If TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out message contains any error, it will set the dispute status as In Error. The error must be addressed in the SAP TM system and the dispute can be re-triggered. This will resend the TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In message to update the charges again. Dispute Inconsistencies During Freight Document Updates Updates in self-billed freight documents are reflected in the dispute document in the carrier's system and are marked as inconsistent. When a carrier, creates a dispute on a self-billed freight document and the ordering party also makes changes to the self-billed freight document in their SAP Transportation Management system, the system notifies the carrier that the carrier is disputing on a document that has recently been changed. The system displays the following message to the carrier: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. Also, the system highlights the relevant lines and indicates as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The carrier can accept the new charges or create a new dispute with the new frame of reference. When the carrier chooses Merge charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process. However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the carrier submits the document, the dispute status changes to Submitted for confirmation. If the document is with the ordering party, the disputed line is highlighted and marked as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The document is editable in the ordering party's system but not in the carrier's system. If there are disputed lines that are inconsistent, the system displays the following message to the ordering party: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. When the ordering party accepts the charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute, and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process.  Note The system does this only for disputes on self-billed freight documents. Also, the system does this only for disputes that are managed by the ordering party in their SAP Business Network for Logistics system and not in their external transportation system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 162 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 3 -- However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the document is submitted by the ordering party, the dispute status changes to To be reviewed and is sent to the carrier for approval. The carrier can view the updated charges. APIs for Planning in External System As a carrier, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration for planning in external system. The ordering party creates transportation requirements from a sales order, purchase order, or delivery documents in their SAP Transportation Management system and sends it to you and requests you to perform planning activities in your system. Once you create a planned freight document in your system, you can send the document containing the transportation requirements back to the ordering party. You can perform these activities using the following APIs: Consumer API to Request for Planning in External System Provider API to Create Planned Freight Document from External System For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/e3d67b2e9ec847a5b6942021a74b2523.html. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 163 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 3 --

The carrier can then review the invoice, adjust the tax lines (if needed) based on the resolved amount, and submit the invoice. Invoice Submission Pending The system sends an email notification to you when the invoice document is not yet submitted to your shipper as the corresponding freight document is not available in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Update Freight Booking The system sends an email notification to you when a shipper sends an updated freight booking. Related Information Define User Settings (Carrier) Configure Notification Settings (Carrier) Prerequisites To enable reminder notifications, make sure you also maintain an email address and subscribe to the notification(s) you need in the Define User Settings app. For more information, see Define User Settings (Carrier) Context You can configure the following types of notifications in the Manage Notification Settings app, where applicable. On-Event Notification On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. You can activate or deactivate on-event notification by setting the activation toggle to Yes or No, respectively. Pre-Event Notifications Pre-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive before the target event happens, for example, before dock appointment booking cut-off. You can schedule pre-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the start of the period, for example, 30 days before the event, which means the notification period starts from 30 days before the event till the start of the next period or the event time.  Note To enable email notifications for the above scenarios, you need to activate the settings in this app and subscribe to notifications for the scenarios in the Define User Settings app. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 13 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Post-Event Notifications Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. You can schedule post-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the end of the period, for example, 30 days after the event, which means the notification period starts from the end of the previous period or the event time, to 30 days after the event. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 15 days Every 3 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 30 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 30 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 15 days Every 3 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days.  Example The schedule shown below 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 14 This is custom documentation. In the scenario list, select the scenario for which you want to set notifications. 3. To activate on-event notification, for On-Event Notification, set the toggle to Yes. To deactivate, set it to No. 4. To configure pre-event or post-event notifications, do the following: a. Expand the Pre-Event Notifications or Post-Event Notifications area. b. To add a notification period, choose the Add button. Then in the Add Notification Period dialog box, specify the start (pre-event) or end (post-event) of the period and the frequency, and choose Save. You can add multiple periods according to your needs. c. To edit or delete a notification period, choose the Edit or Delete button. To deactivate a period, set Activated for User to No. User Management Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 60 days Every 10 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 30 days after the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 30 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Note that for the invitations scenario, the notifications stop as soon as the invitation is accepted or rejected. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 60 days Every 10 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days.  Note 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Prerequisite To access the User Management app, you must be an administrator user of SAP Business Network for Logistics. If you don’t know who is your company’s administrator user, create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB and provide your company’s subdomain in the incident. The subdomain can be found in your sign-in URL as follows: https://<subdomain>.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/sites About the app The User Management app allows an administrator to perform user management tasks including the following: Add or delete users in your company's tenant Add users to user groups Manage additional user groups to control user access to specified docking locations in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. The User Management app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the users based on one or more of the filter options, such as First Name, Last Name and Email that appear in the header area. Worklists Include an All Users list and other user lists categorized by user groups. Worklist (User Management) There are different ways to work on the users and to set filters. To restrict the number of users displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the worklists for different user groups. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for users. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. This app is only available for carriers in the productive environment. It is not applicable for a test-type carrier that subscribed Carrier Apps for Freight Collaboration (plan: test or si). 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 16 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Worklists All Users The All Users worklist contains all the users in the current tenant. This worklist displays the following details for each user: First name Last name Email User group(s) The system displays all the user groups to which the user belongs. This worklist contains the option to change user information, including first and last names, and the assigned user groups. You can do so by clicking the  Edit icon in the worklist. You can also add a user by choosing the Add button and delete a user by selecting the user and choosing Delete Delete User . User Lists by User Groups Each worklist displays all the users that belong to a specific user group. These worklists display the same user information as the All Users worklist. The worklists contain the option to change user information, delete a user, and remove a user from the current user group. To edit a user, click the  Edit icon for the user. To delete a user, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete User . To remove a user from the current user group, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete Mapping . For example, by choosing Delete Mapping in the ABC worklist, you remove the user from the ABC user group. Create a User and Assign User Groups Prerequisites You are a tenant administrator, that is, you have already been assigned to the admin user group either by the system or by another administrator in your company. Context As an administrator, you can create users in your company's tenant and assign users to user groups so that they have access to relevant apps. Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. 2. In the All Users worklist, choose the Add button.  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 17 This is custom documentation. System Connections (Carrier) Use the System Connections app for carriers and partners to complete the implementation of SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs. By implementing the freight tendering, subcontracting and tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, your organization can receive and respond to freight tendering documents, subcontracting documents, and tracking requests directly from your system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: Specify the authentication details and base URLs for your system’s endpoints. Assign authentication details and a base URL to each API operation that you’ve implemented. Enable inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app has the following areas: Outbound Connections This area lists the outbound-from-network API services to which you can assign authentication details and a base URL. In addition, you can see the active or inactive status of the operations. Manage Details This area enables you to manage (create, edit and delete) your base URLs (communication details) and your authentication details (OAuth 2.0 and basic credentials). Connection Settings This area enables you to call LBN endpoints for inbound and outbound connections. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, go to SAP Business Accelerator Hub . Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 21 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Configure communication and authentication details for your system's API or EDI endpoints by specifying base URLs, protocols (HTTPS/SFTP/Email), and authentication methods (Basic, API Key, OAuth 2.0) to enable secure integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Manage Details. 2. In the Communication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. You can choose between the following options: HTTPS (for API) SFTP (for EDI) Email (for EDI) 3. In the Authentication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. When creating API communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details Base URL The endpoint URL for the communication The API call made to your system uses the HTTPS protocol. When creating EDI communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Address Enter the host name or IP address of the SFTP server and an optional port, for example, my.host.org:22. You can configure this parameter by entering a dynamic expression such as ${property.property_name} or ${header.header_name}. Message Format You can choose EDIFACT or ANSI X12 from the drop-down list. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 22 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Attribute Description Message Type For EDIFACT, you can choose between the following options: IFTMIN All Inbound Messages For ANSI X12, you can choose between the following options: 204 213 300 303 997 All Inbound Messages Known Host Key Enter a base64-encoded string of your SFTP server. This is used to authenticate your server. SAP Business Network for Logistics can also retrieve the known host key and insert it for you. As a prerequisite, you must have entered the address (including the port) of the SFTP server. Message Version The D96A message version is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT. The V4010 message version is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12. No version will be displayed for message type All Inbound Messages. Description The Instructions of Transport description is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT message type IFTMIN. The Load Tender description is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12 message type 204. The description will not be shown for message type All Inbound Messages. Directory Enter the relative path to write the file to a directory. Example: parentdirectory/childdirectory File Name Enter the name of the file to be written. The entry is valid only for LBN outbound message types. Additional allowed placeholders: %DOCUMENT_ID% %MESSAGE_TYPE% %TIMESTAMP% %SHIPPER_LBN_ID% %CONTROL_NUMBER% The placeholder %CONTROL_NUMBER% is only available for ANSI X12 997 messages. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Attribute Description You can combine these placeholders with any fixed strings and in any order (<string 1><placeholder 1><string 2><placeholder 2> <string 3>). Examples: LBN_%MESSAGE_TYPE%_%DOCUMENT_ID%_%TIMESTAMP%.edi %TIMESTAMP%_%SHIPPER_LBN_ID%.edi When creating Basic authentication details, the provided user name and password are used for authentication during the API call to your system. When creating API Key authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details API Key Attribute Enter the key for the request header. API Key Value Enter the token to be used for authentication. The API key represents the name of the token that a client provides when making API calls. The token is sent as request header. When creating OAuth 2.0 authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Grant Type Valid values are: Client Credentials (default) and Client Certificate. Authentication URL Enter the URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization server that issues the access token. Client ID Enter the ID of the client that you’re connecting to. Client Secret Secret key of the client that you’re connecting to. OAuth 2.0 uses a multiple-step authentication pattern: Client credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) are used by the client application to initially request an access token. The access token is then used to authorize the client (for as long as the token is valid) to access the server’s resources (for example, the resources that are used in the associated integration flow). In many OAuth 2.0 scenarios, the access token is issued (or generated) by an authorization server. Client Authentication Select Send as Body Parameter or Send as Request Header. This enables access to your system. If you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent in the request body to the authentication server. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Attribute Description If you select Send as Request Header, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent as a part of the authorization header to the authentication server. Valid values are: client credentials and client certificate. Client Certificate When you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID goes in the request body to the authentication server. If you choose Send as Request Header, the Client ID becomes part of the authorization header sent to the authentication server. Specify the path of the client certificate (key pair file) in the Key Pair File field. Enter its password in the Password field. Include Scope Select the checkbox to provide the OAuth 2.0 scope information that will be included in the request body. Scope Enter the scope that you defined for the endpoint. Content Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded is selected by default. Assigning Authentication Details and a Base URL to a Service Prerequisites You have specified the communication details (base URL) and authentication details (basic or OAuth 2.0 credentials, or API key). To test the service, select it in the table and choose one of the two methods from the Test Service drop down. With Default Payload An internal shipper tenant is used to trigger the payload. The payload content is static with the intention of testing the connection from SAP Business Network for Logistics to your carrier system. With Custom Payload An internal shipper tenant is used to trigger the payload. You can modify the payload content to the extent of changing the order details with the intention of testing various scenarios. However, the order ID and the shipper LBN ID will always be fixed by SAP Business Network for Logistics. The test service will not work with any other shipper tenant. You will find a sample payload shippers would send from their system here . The service test is only available for test tenant types for the following operations: Post freight request for quotation Post freight request for quotation cancellation Post freight quotation notification Post freight order for subcontracting Post freight order for subcontracting cancellation 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 28 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Post freight booking request Freight booking shipping instruction Delete order for tracking Post freight booking request cancellation Put order for tracking Put freight order for subcontracting Post freight order for subcontracting Post freight document generic request Put location data Delete location data Automating EDI Pulling This feature allows you to schedule automated EDI pulling operations for ANSI and EDIFACT inbound messages. You can run the pulling job during a specific time period each day or on specific days of the week. Prerequisites Ensure you set the Service Name to EDI Inbound All and the Operation Name to Pull EDI in the Create Service dialog when using the System Connections app to create a connection service. Procedure 1. Specify the recurrence type of the EDI pulling service by using the Recurrence toggle. Daily (default): The service runs every day. Weekly/On Days: The service runs on selected days of the week. 2. Set the time period during which the service runs based on the selected recurrence type by specifying the Recur Start Time and Recur End Time. 3. Choose the interval for the service from the Interval drop-down list. 4. Choose your time zone from the Timezone drop-down list. This setting applies to the time period you set in step two. Enabling Inbound Communication Context To call the provider APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, complete the following steps. In the System Connections app under Connection Settings, you can enable inbound connections for Multi-Cloud and generate OAuth 2.0 authentication credentials on your own without creating a support ticket. To enable inbound connections for Multi-Cloud, proceed as follows: 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 29 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Manage Alternate IDs (Carrier) You can maintain alternate identifiers of your other accounts in the network. These identifiers shall be used in specific integration scenarios or in specific transaction flows in the network. Additionally, the LBN ID of your tenant can be seen above the Alternate IDs table as a read-only field. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following alternate identifiers (alternate IDs): DUNS ID (Data Universal Numbering System ID) SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Registration Number USDOT (US Department of Transportation) MC Number (Motor Carrier Number) Others GLN (Global Location Number) Technical User To create your own alternate IDs, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select an alternate ID type from the dropdown menu and type in the required value. 3. Choose OK. You can also delete or change existing entries. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: The app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the invitations based on one or more of the filter options, such as inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear in the header area. Worklists by status The invitations are categorized based on the invitation statuses: New, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Invitations) There are different ways to work on the invitations and to set filters. To restrict the number of invitations displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the preconfigured worklists (New, Accepted, Rejected) based on the status of the invitation. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for invitations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists New The New worklist displays all invitations that you have not yet responded to. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- City Country/Region Address Accept and reject options Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the invitations that you have accepted. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Administration information such as Accepted On and Accepted By Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the invitations that you have rejected. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Administration information such as Rejected On and Rejected By  Note Using the  Settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the New, Accepted, and Rejected worklists. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- You can schedule alerts for the invitations that you receive from potential business partners. On the event of receiving or automatically accepting an invitation, you can specify whether you want to receive a notification in an email using the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information, see Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). Viewing an Invitation Context To view an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. 2. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. (Optional) You can retrieve a specific invitation or a set of invitations using the various search filter options such as the inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear on the header area. The system also categorizes the invitations based on various attributes and displays them in the following tabs: New: Displays all new invitations from potential business partners. Accepted: Displays invitations that you have accepted. Rejected: Displays invitations that you have rejected. Accepting or Rejecting an Invitation Context You can accept or reject the invitations from potential business partners to connect with their business network. When rejecting, you can indicate a rejection reason to the inviter. If you accept an invitation, you can connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. If you reject an invitation, you cannot connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. To accept or reject an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. You can directly accept or reject the invitations in this worklist. 2. Alternatively, you can search for and retrieve a specific invitation using search filter options in the header. Once you retrieve the invitation, you can respond to the invitation by choosing the Accept or Reject button. Results Once you accept or reject an invitation, you can view the details of the invitation in the Accepted or Rejected worklist as appropriate. You cannot view this invitation anymore in the New worklist.  Note 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Settings on Invitations You can specify the visibility of your company profile and how you process connection requests in the app. To do this, click Settings on Invitations on the upper-right concern then specify the followings: Automatically accept connection requests (invitations) Determines whether you want the app to automatically accept connection requests from potential business patterns. Default value: No Freight Contracting You can participate in freight contracting when a known ordering party sends you a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ). Subsequently, if the freight quotation was awarded, then you can find the corresponding freight documents in the Freight Orders for Confirmation, Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean), and Confirm Freight Bookings (Air). Your options for responding to the received freight RFQ are determined by the tendering setup implemented by the ordering party. Your response options depend on the following settings: Is the price negotiable? If so, you can propose a new price. Are the dates and times negotiable? If so, you can propose new dates and times. Does the ordering party require you to respond? If a response is unrequired (indicated by Accept Automatically: Yes) then the freight RFQ will be automatically accepted when the response time runs out, unless you reject it beforehand. If a response is required and you want the job then you must accept the freight RFQ before the response time runs out. When you accept or reject a freight RFQ, the SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a freight quotation and sends it to the ordering party. The ordering party then evaluates your freight quotation and, according to their strategy, may or not award it to you. Integration with SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC) LE-TRA Shipments If you want the system to automatically accept all invitations, select Automatically accept connection requests (invitations) in the Manage Business Profile app. For more information, see Edit Company Profile. To get email notification each time when an invitation is automatically accepted, subscribe the Invitation Auto-Accepted notification scenario in the Manage Notification Settings app.  Note Your response options change depending on how the ordering party sets up the tendering. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Logistics has integrated with the SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC) LE-TRA shipments for the subcontracting process. You can view these SAP ECC shipments in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can view the shipments sent from your shipper’s SAP ECC system in your SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The system receives the shipment document from SAP ECC and performs the following: If the Means of Transport of the shipment is Road, freight order with Document Category as Shipment is created in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. If the Means of Transport of the shipment is Ocean, freight booking with Document Category as Shipment is created in the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app for ocean freight. You can consume the APIs in SAP API Hub to send these shipments from your SAP Business Network for Logistics system to your external system. You can use the following APIs: Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting for road shipments Consumer API for Freight Booking for ocean shipments Integration with SAP Logistics Management Requests for Quotation (RFQs) and Consignment Orders SAP Business Network for Logistics has integrated with the SAP Logistics Management RFQs and consignment orders for the tendering and subcontracting process respectively. You can view the RFQs and consignment orders sent from your shipper’s SAP Logistics Management system in your SAP Business Network for Logistics system. The system receives the RFQs and consignment orders from SAP Logistics Management and performs the following: If the document is an RFQ, the document will be visible in the Freight Requests for Quotation app. If the document is a consignment order, the document will be visible in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. You can consume the APIs in SAP API Hub to send these shipments from your SAP Business Network for Logistics system to your external system. You can use the following APIs: Consumer API for Freight Tendering for RFQs Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting for consignment orders Freight Requests for Quotation The Freight Requests for Quotation app allows you to accept or reject freight requests for quotations (freight RFQs) that ordering parties have sent to you. SAP Business Network for Logistics has integrated with the SAP Logistics Management RFQs. Freight Requests for Quotation app allows you to view them. The Freight Requests for Quotation app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you first open the app, the main view is launched. It has two screen areas: 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the RFQs by one or more of the following attributes: Freight RFQ Ordering party Departure date Departure location Tendering status Shipping type Transport means description Transport means type Acceptable loading start date time Acceptable loading end date time Arrival date Arrival location Arrival state Currency Departure state Freight order ID Price Requested loading start date time Requested loading end date time Vendor ID Worklists You can use the following worklists: New, Responded To (Open), and All. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view of the selected freight RFQ. The detail view has two screen areas: Header You can display data such as the price, the remaining time, the contact details of the ordering party and your latest response. Sections You can display further details in the Information, Cargo, Tour, Contacts, Notes, and Attachments sections. Email notifications are sent to carriers when the following events are triggered in tendering and subcontracting: Create RFQ – when a new request for quotation is sent to the carrier by the shipper Cancel RFQ – when the shipper cancels the request for quotation for the carrier (which is sent earlier) 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The notifications include a link that the user can click to view the relevant status or perform any action they need to carry out. The email also includes a request to perform the necessary action on or before a specific date. Worklist (Freight RFQs) To restrict the number of freight requests for quotation (freight RFQs) displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (New, Responded To, All) according to the status of the freight RFQ. New The New worklist displays all freight RFQs that you've not yet responded to. For each freight RFQ, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight RFQ Remaining time Departure date and time Departure location Arrival date and time Arrival location Stops Price Freight Order Acceptable loading start date time Acceptable loading end date time Arrival state Departure state Mode of transport Requested loading duration Requested loading start date time Requested loading end date time Shipping type Transport means description Transport means type Vehicle resource ID Vendor ID The freight RFQs are only displayed if the response due date and time has not yet been reached and the tendering is still open. When there is no remaining time, the freight RFQs are moved to the All worklist. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Responded To (Open) The Responded To (Open) worklist displays all freight RFQs that you've already responded to and for which a freight quotation has been created. The Responded To (Open) worklist displays the same information as the New worklist. The freight RFQs are only displayed if the response due date and time has not yet been reached. All The All worklist displays the same information as the New worklist. Detail View (Freight RFQ) The detail view of a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) consists of a header and several sections. Header The Header section displays important data about the freight RFQ as well as data related to the response you can send to your ordering party. Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation If you agree with the price and the dates given by the ordering party, you can accept a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) without proposing a change. Context You can also accept a freight RFQ that you previously rejected or accepted with a change, as long as the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party. If you want to propose a new price or new dates, see Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation with a Change. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight RFQs (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). To accept a single freight RFQ, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Accept. Note that if one or more of the selected freight RFQs contain zero prices from the ordering party and if you have not maintained any price, the system displays a warning message before you proceed to Accept. The ordering party expects you to enter a price before you accept. Next Steps Your ordering party will now evaluate your freight quotation and reply to it. If they award it to you, they will ask you to confirm the related freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation with a Change You can accept a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) with a change. Context If the ordering party wants to receive proposals for alternative prices or dates to those which they specified in the freight request for quotation (freight RFQ), then you can make a proposal by accepting the freight RFQ with a change. And, as long as the remaining time has not run out and the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party, you can accept a freight RFQ and make a date or price proposal for freight RFQs that you previously rejected or accepted.  Note The ordering party can maintain a setting in their transportation management system to either enable or disable you from modifying the price proposal currency. Based on this setting, when you accept a freight request for quotation with change, the system either enables you to modify the price proposal currency or does not allow you to do so. You can view these details in the information icon next to the price proposal currency, in the dialog box, which appears when you choose the Accept with Change button in the freight request for quotation. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), look for the open freight RFQ for which you want to enter changes (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). Alternatively, you can also open the detail view of the freight RFQ. 3. Choose Accept with Change. 4. Enter your your proposal price and the currency. 5. Enter your date proposals. For each stop, the earliest start and the latest end for all activities at that location are displayed, such as driving on the premises, loading, completing paper work. These dates might be prefilled by your ordering party. In the proposal fields in the middle, you can see if the ordering party would prefer a timeframe for your activities. If these are empty, you can enter your own proposal in these fields. 6. Choose Accept with Change. Next Steps Your ordering party will now evaluate your freight quotation and reply to it. If they award it to you, they will ask you to confirm the related freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Rejecting a Freight Request for Quotation You can reject a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) if you are unable to or do not want to take over this transport. Context As long as the remaining time to respond hasn't ran out and the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party, you can reject a freight RFQ, even if you previously accepted it. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight RFQs (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). To reject a single freight RFQ, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Reject and select a rejection reason. Note, the reject reason will be assigned to all selected freight RFQs and recorded in each automatically generated freight quotation. 4. Choose Reject. Freight Quotations The Freight Quotations app allows you to see if the ordering party awarded or rejected the freight requests for quotation (freight RFQs) that you submitted to them. The Freight Quotations app consists of a main view and a detail view: When you first open the app, the main view is launched, which has two screen areas: Filter bar Note that when you change the price proposal currency, the system automatically updates the settlement currency to be the same as the updated price proposal currency. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 42 This is custom documentation. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view, which has two screen areas: Header You can display data such as the latest submitted price, your latest response and the response of the ordering party. Sections You can display further details in the Information, Cargo, Tour, Contacts, Notes, and Attachments sections. For each freight quotation, the following information is displayed: 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 43 This is custom documentation. Administrative data section Displays the date and time the freight order was received, details of the last responded person and time. The following fields may be of particular interest to you: Freight quotation ID along with your response (Accepted, Accepted with Change, Rejected, Accepted Automatically) Price Response of the ordering party (Award Pending, Awarded, Rejected) Start and end dates For each stop within the stop sequence, the following dates for all activities at that location are displayed: Earliest start and latest end (this is, the hard borders given by the ordering party) Proposed start and proposed end (this is, either the more narrow timeframe entered by your ordering party, or your own new proposal) Cargo The Cargo section displays data about the cargo items involved, such as weight, quantity, and special transport requirements. Dangerous Goods If the ordering party has provided dangerous goods information, you can view this information from the Cargo section by choosing Yes in the Dangerous Goods column. This opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. If the ordering party has entered dangerous goods information in their SAP Transportation Management (TM) system, this information is transferred to SAP Business Network for Logistics. To view this information, in the Information section, choose Yes under Dangerous Goods, which opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, temperature control, and emergency temperature. You can choose to display the dangerous goods information in any language that the ordering party has specified previously in the TM system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For each stop, you can view data such as the address location, the dates and times, and the loading or unloading activity at the location. Contacts If provided by the ordering party, the Contacts section displays the company name of the ordering party along with the phone number and the email address of the contact person. This section also displays the contact details for each individual stop (stop number and location). Notes The Notes section displays the comments previously left by the ordering party and yourself. Attachments The Attachments section displays the files the ordering party sent you with the freight request for quotation as well as the attachments you sent to the ordering party when you responded. Freight Orders for Confirmation The Freight Orders for Confirmation app allows you to confirm freight orders that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting. SAP Business Network for Logistics has integrated with the SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC) LE-TRA shipments, and SAP Logistics Management consignment orders. Freight Orders for Confirmation app allows you to view them. The Freight Orders for Confirmation app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you first open the app, the main view is launched. The email also includes a request to perform the necessary action on or before a specific date. The Award Freight Order notification is already covered by the confirmation notification. New Version You can now use the latest version of the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you login and use the app for the first time, you will automatically be navigated to the new version of the app. You can also switch to the old version using the button in the dialog box that appears automatically when login for the first time. You can also view whether you need to respond to the freight order. The same information also appears on the details page on the header area. New Worklist Tabs You can view the following tabs in the worklist: All New Confirmed Rejected Cancelled 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 49 This is custom documentation. Cancellation Confirmed All and Updated Subtabs In the worklist page, in the New tab, you can view the All and Updated subtabs. In the All subtab, you can view all new and updated freight orders that are active to respond and whose planned arrival time at the final destination has not yet passed. In the Updated subtab, you can view all freight orders that have received an update from the ordering party after your response and whose planned arrival time at the final destination has not yet passed. New Message for Updated Freight Orders A message appears on the worklist page if the ordering party has updated a confirmed or rejected freight order and sent it to you. This message provides information on how many confirmed or rejected freight orders have been updated today. You can use the link in this message to directly navigate and view all the updated freight orders. Worklist (Freight Orders for Confirmation) To restrict the number of freight orders displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (New, Responded To (Open), All) according to the status of the freight order. Freight Order Worklist Transition Based on the Status When the ordering party updates or cancels a confirmed freight order in their SAP Transportation Management system and sends it you, the system displays it in the New tab. When the arrival or departure date and time of a freight order is in the future, the system displays it in the New tab. When you confirm this freight order from the New tab, the system moves it to the Responded To tab. If the ordering party updates this freight order again in their SAP Transportation Management system, the system again moves it to the New tab. If the departure or arrival date and time of a freight order is in the past, or if the remaining time to respond has expired, the system displays it in the All tab. Open the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight orders. Confirming a Freight Order with a Change You can confirm a freight order with a change. Context If the ordering party wants to receive proposals for alternative prices to those which they specified in the freight order, then you can make a proposal by confirming the freight order with a change. And, as long as the remaining time has not run out and the freight order has not been closed by the ordering party, you can confirm a freight order and make a price proposal for freight orders that you previously rejected or confirmed. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), look for the open freight order for which you want to enter changes. Alternatively, you can also open the detail view of the freight order. 3. Choose Confirm with Change. 4. Enter your price proposal. 5. Choose Confirm with Change. Rejecting a Freight Order You can reject a freight order if you are unable to or do not want to take on the transportation. Context As long as the remaining time to respond hasn't run out and the freight order has not been closed by the ordering party, you can reject a freight order, even if you previously confirmed it. You can reject a freight order as long as the arrival date and time has not passed.  Note The ordering party can maintain a setting in their transportation management system to either enable or disable you from modifying the price proposal currency. Based on this setting, for the direct tendering scenario, when you confirm a freight order with change, the system either enables you to modify the price proposal currency or does not allow you to do so. You can view these details in the information icon next to the price proposal currency, in the dialog box, which appears when you choose the Confirm with Change button in the freight order. Note that when you change the price proposal currency, the system automatically updates the settlement currency to be the same as the updated price proposal currency. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 60 This is custom documentation. Depending on the type of stop, the system displays the date and time information. Detail View (Confirm Freight Bookings (Air)) The detail view of a freight booking for confirmation consists of a header and several sections. Header The Header section displays the following information: Booking Details Displays the Document Category, Ordering Party, Consignee Party, Departure Location, and Arrival Location information. Document category displays whether the document is a freight booking or a shipment. When you choose the ordering party, consignee party, departure location, or arrival location, you can view the address, and address details. Airport Details Displays the Airport of Departure and Airport of Destination information. When you choose the airport of departure or destination, you can view the address and contact details. Status Displays one of the following confirmation statuses: New New (Updated) Displays this status when the ordering party sends an update on a freight booking that you have not yet confirmed. Updated 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 79 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Displays this status when the ordering party sends an update on a freight booking that you have already confirmed. Confirmed Rejected Cancelled Displays whether the freight booking is in New, Confirmed, Rejected, or Cancelled status. Information The information section displays the following details: General Displays the following information: Freight Booking Master Airway Bill House Airway Bill Contract Basis Displays one of the following values: Allotment Blocked space Charter Spot quote Shipping Type Note that as of now, you can only view bookings with the shipping type as loose cargo. Cargo Displays the following information: Requested Cargo Weight Requested Cargo Volume Requested Cargo Quantity Dangerous Goods Cargo Quantity Temperature Controlled Journey You can view the flight code details. Transportation Displays the following information: Number of Visits 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 80 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Displays one of the following values: Door to Door Door to Port Port to Door Port to Port Administrative Data Displays the date and time you received the freight booking and the details of the person who last modified the booking and the modified time. Enter the document type and document ID of the reference document. You can also download the reference document details in a spreadsheet. You can view the following details in this document: Document ID Document Type Code Document Type Description 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Cargo The Cargo section displays the following data about the cargo items involved: Item ID Displays the cargo item ID. Cargo Type Displays whether the cargo item is a package, product, or a container. Container Type Displays the container type code. Cargo Details Quantity Gross Weight Gross Volume Nature of Goods Displays the nature of goods description specified by the ordering party. Special Requirements Displays one or more icons for the following special requirements: Dangerous Goods Temperature Control Stackable Over Dimensional When you choose the special requirement icon for dangerous goods, you can perform the following: View the dangerous goods information in a dialog box Select the language in which you want to view the dangerous goods details View the dangerous goods details for all the cargo items in this dialog box. When you navigate from a specific cargo item, you can view the dangerous goods of that cargo item. Search the dangerous goods details for a specific cargo item using the search bar When you select the details icon from a cargo item, the system displays the cargo information in a new page. The system displays the following information: Header Booking Details On the header area, you can view the following booking information: Ordering Party Departure Location 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 82 This is custom documentation. Commodity Code Displays the commodity code type and the code. Stages This tab displays the following information: Stage Means of Transport Mode of Transport 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 83 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Note that in the Assign Codes app, if you do not maintain the mapping between Code in External System and LBN Code for the values in the below table, then the system does a default mapping to the respective value. Mode of Transport SAP Transportation Management System SAP Business Network for Logistics System 03 - Ocean 01 - Ocean 01 - Road 03 - Road 05 - Air 04 - Air Departure Location Departure IATA Arrival Location Arrival IATA Activity Cargo Type Activity Location Planned Start Date of Activity Planned End Date of Activity Planned Departure Date and Time Planned Arrival Date and Time Locations For each stop, the system displays the following information: Stop Number Location Planned Arrival Date and Time Planned Departure Date and Time Activities Overview  Note The ordering party can implement a business add-in (BAdI) to display only the main cargo items. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. You can view the aggregated dangerous goods information for the filtered items at the main cargo item level. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 84 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Distance to Next Stop Time to Next Stop Date and Time Displays the date and time details for each stop. Depending on the type of stop, the system displays the date and time information. The following are the different types of stops: Pick-Up Location Indicates the source location of the first pre-carriage stage. Delivery Location Indicates the destination location of the last on-carriage stage. Airport of Departure Indicates the source location of the first main carriage stage. Airport of Destination Indicates the destination location of the last main carriage stage. The system displays these dates and times in the time zone of their respective stop location. Note that the system receives this time zone information for a location from the transportation management system. If there is no time zone associated with a location in the transportation management system, then the system receives this time zone information from the location master in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system. If there is no time zone associated with a location in the location master, then the system by default displays the time zone as UTC for that location. Stages Displays the following information: Stage Type Displays whether the stage is a pre-carriage, on-carriage, or main carriage stage. Transport Specifies the mode of transport and means of transport details. The mode of transport specifies one of the following values: Maritime transport Road transport Air transport The mode of transport specifies one of the following values: Sea Road Air Departure Location 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 85 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- If the ordering party has sent the departure location details, you can view the IATA airport code and the location of departure with the address and contact details. If not, you can enter the IATA airport code and update the freight booking. Arrival Location If the ordering party has sent the arrival location details, you can view the IATA airport code and the location of arrival with the address and contact details. If not, you can enter the IATA airport code and update the freight booking. Date and Time Displays the planned arrival and planned departure date and time. Journey Displays the flight code. Note that the flight code is the combination of the airline code (for example, LH for Lufthansa), followed by the flight number. Note that the journey details are editable only in main carriage stages. When you select the details icon from a stage, the system displays the stage details in a new page. You can view the following information: Transport Details Displays the means of transport and mode of transport details. Location Details Displays the departure and arrival location details. Journey Details Displays the flight code. Expected Date and Time Displays the expected arrival and departure date and time. Cargo Items Table Displays the following details of the associated cargo items in a table format: Item ID Cargo Type Cargo Details Quantity Gross Weight Gross Volume Special Requirements Contacts The Contacts section displays the following information for a contact in a card format: Contact Type Name 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 86 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Address Phone Number Email You can view different icons in these tiles for the following: Various business partners such as shipper party, consignee party, forwarding agent, customs agent, and notify party Important locations such as, departure location, airport of departure, airport of arrival, and arrival location. Attachments In the Attachments tab, you can upload attachments that you want to send to the ordering party and view the attachments sent by the ordering party to you. You can also toggle the view between the attachments that you have uploaded, the attachments from the ordering party, and the all the attachments. Notes The Notes section displays the notes the ordering party has sent you. You can as well enter your own notes. Managing an Air Freight Booking  Note Attachment file type must be base 64 You can attach documents related to the business document or business process in this section. You’re recommended to avoid attaching sensitive personal data. You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpeg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx Image files must be less than 6MB file size Document files must be less than 5MB file size When you mention the file path, you must mention the file name along with the extension.  Note Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. You’re recommended to avoid entering sensitive personal data. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. You can enter notes when you reject a freight order. The ordering party can view these rejection notes in their transportation system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 87 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- You can perform the following actions on a freight booking: Confirming a Freight Booking You can confirm a freight booking with the status as New. You can confirm a freight booking either from the worklist page or the freight booking details page. You can select one or more freight bookings from the New worklist and choose Confirm. You can also enter information in the editable fields in the freight booking details page and then confirm a freight booking. Note that once you confirm a freight booking, the status of the freight booking changes to Confirmed. Updating a Freight Booking You can update a freight booking with the status as Confirmed. In the details page of a confirmed freight booking, you can update the information and choose Update. In the Stages tab, you can now specify an IATA code for a location for which there is no location details or IATA code specified. Rejecting a Freight Booking You can reject a freight booking with the status as New or Confirmed. You can reject a new freight booking from the worklist page or the freight booking details page. You can select one or more freight bookings from the New worklist and choose Reject. You can also reject a confirmed booking from the freight booking details page. Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps, such as Docking Location Settings, in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see the Business Configuration section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 88 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 89 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. If you are importing a location from SAP Transportation Management (TM), set the Source System to the business system name of your TM system and set the External ID to the location ID in TM. For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name. Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. The Logical System field is is optional in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. If you’ve only purchased the freight collaboration solution, leave this field empty. If you’ve purchased both freight collaboration and global track and trace, refer to the configuration for global track and trace to maintain the logical system ID. (Optional) Address: Country/Region State City District Street/House Number Zip Code (Optional) Geographical Coordinates And Map: Longitude: Longitude coordinate of the location Latitude: Latitude coordinate of the location (Optional) Time Zone (Optional) Alternative Location ID: Type: Type of the alternative ID. ID: Alternative ID in the specified type.  Note You can enter the coordinates in the Longitude and Latitude fields manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you save your changes. You can also choose Generate Longitude and Latitude Coordinates to create the coordinates according to the address information you’ve entered. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location record you are working on is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo-coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 90 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
