file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Application Help Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:52:37 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/98d177f964dc42f8916622380de9d0c3?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace The aim of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is to capture, process and store tracking information about tracked business processes. Then, it allows business users to get real-time transparency of the execution of those processes. They can query any tracked process and display its retrieved data from end to end. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is a cloud service solution based on SAP Business Technology Platform. It's integrated with the following SAP S/4HANA systems: SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition Both two systems have the Transportation Management (TM) component embedded, which can work with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Solution Owner Apps This chapter provides application help on all the apps used by solution owners as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Overview The following apps are available for Solution Owners: Model Management App Description Manage Models to create and deploy a GTT metadata model that meets the business requirements for events and logic Check Processes and Events to display, dynamically and in a user-friendly way, a tracked process with its event data, based on a deployed GTT metadata model Business Operations  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified.  Note The apps provided with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace run on desktops, as well as tablet devices that have a screen format wide enough to display the overview section and the detailed section of the screen, side-by-side. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- App Description View Logs to have an at-a-glance overview of the available logs and their statuses Manage Message Logs to view all the technical logs for all the message data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger certain events or their correlations for the message Manage Event Logs to view all the technical logs for all the event data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger one or multiple events or their correlations Manage Integration Logs to monitor the inbound and outbound integration messages related to location replication and visibility providers that are processed by SAP Business Network for Logistics Fulfillment Tracking App Description Track Shipments to monitor the real-time execution status of LE-TRA shipments and freight documents from SAP S/4HANA and report events manually Monitor Inbound ASNs to monitor the fulfillment status of inbound ASNs/deliveries Monitor Outbound Deliveries to monitor the fulfillment status of outbound deliveries Track SO Fulfillment to monitor the fulfillment status of sales orders Track PO Fulfillment to monitor the fulfillment status of purchase orders For more information on the Fulfilment Tracking apps, see Fulfillment Tracking Apps. In addition, SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace incorporates apps that are, or will be, standard across SAP Business Network for Logistics, including: Manage Network App Description Invite Business Partners to invite business partners already known to join their business network and check their participation status System Connections to create a connection and to authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA Configure Partner Connections to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners Manage Business Profile to view and edit your company profile such as contact details and business partner type Manage Notification Templates to create a template for a notification email of an event, such as that a sales order has been created, for use with the notification service Manage Locations to manage location master data either manually copied from another system or created from scratch 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- App Description Discover Business Partners to search onSAP Business Network for Logistics and select suitable business partners, they may or may not already know, to invite to join their business network Retention Management App Description Blocking Store to access restricted data during its blocking period Retention Management to define rules that determine the residence and blocking periods of personal data Further, the Reminder service is introduced that allows you to create a template email for an event, such as that a sales order has been created, and automatically send to the involved parties of a tracked process, an email based on the template. It uses the Manage Notification Templates app to create the template and the Manage Models app to set up the notifications. Fulfillment Tracking Apps Fulfillment tracking apps monitor the fulfillment status of: sales orders, purchase orders, outbound and inbound deliveries, shipments in SAP S/4HANA freight units and freight orders in TM in SAP S/4HANA. Fulfillment tracking apps are ready-to-consume standard apps based on the GTT standard model. The standard model allows extensibility to add user-defined tracked processes, field types, event types, code lists, planned event extensions, and event-to- action scripts. If you want to send documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to How to Send Documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and make sure that you meet the requirements for the product version mentioned in its Prerequisites section. The sample codes for the fulfillment tracking apps are available in the following GTT repository in the SAP Samples organization on GitHub.com: https://github.com/SAP-samples/logistics- business-network-gtt-standardapps-samples . You can find a document explaining how to download and install the sample codes in the repository. On the contrary, If you want to send documents from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to other SAP systems, refer to How to Send Documents from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to Other Systems. Based on your business needs, you can perform the following configuration tasks to enhance the functionality and the usability of fulfillment tracking apps: Adapting the UI  Note The sample codes are not provided as part of standard delivery, but only as an example to show you how to set up the SAP S/4HANA extractors for use with fulfillment tracking apps. They are not standard codes and you can customize them for your business scenarios. You should determine what documents with certain condition need to be sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace for tracking. You don't need to send unnecessary ones. For example, if you only need the sales order, then you don't have to implement the purchase order. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Navigate to Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems Define My Tracking Status. Track Shipments App A standard app : for transportation planners to monitor the real-time execution status of LE-TRA shipments from SAP S/4HANAand freight documents from TM in SAP S/4HANA and report events manually. To know how to synchronize actual events back to TM in SAP S/4HANA in the Fulfillment Tracking apps, see Synchronize Actual Events Back to TM in SAP S/4HANA. For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Transportation Planners. Monitor Inbound ASNs App A standard app : for receiving specialists to monitor the inbound ASN/delivery fulfillment status. To know how to integrate with Ariba Network, see How to Integrate SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace with Ariba Network. To know how to synchronize ETA of the inbound delivery to yourSAP S/4HANA system, see Synchronize ETA of the Inbound Delivery Back to SAP S/4HANA. For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Receiving Specialists. Monitor Outbound Deliveries A standard app : for shipping specialists to monitor the fulfillment status of outbound deliveries For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Shipping Specialists. Track SO Fulfillment App A standard app : for internal sales representatives to track the fulfillment status of sales orders with integration to SAP S/4HANA, TM in SAP S/4HANA and visibility providers. For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Internal Sales Representatives. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Track PO Fulfillment App A standard app : for purchasers to track the purchase order fulfillment status with integration to SAP S/4HANA, TM in SAP S/4HANA and visibility providers. For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Purchasers. Track Shipments For information on how to use this app, see Guide for Transportation Planners. Monitor Inbound ASNs For information on how to use this app, see Guide for Receiving Specialists. Monitor Outbound Deliveries For information on how to use this app, see Guide for Shipping Specialists. Track SO Fulfillment For information on how to use this app, see Introduction. Track PO Fulfillment For information on how to use this app, see Guide for Purchasers. Adapting the UI This section describes how to adapt the UI of the fulfillment tracking apps. When you are in the adaptation mode, you have many options to adapt the UI to your liking. You can also adapt and save certain views. The content in this section is an excerpt from Adapting SAP Fiori UIs at Runtime - Key User Adaptation, and adapted for the use in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. It might not be updated timely. You can check out more details and timely updates on this function with the link provided. Prerequisites You have added the roles of fulfillment tracking apps and and two flexible UI configuration roles “UIConfigureTemplate” and “FlexKeyUser”to the role collection in SAP BTP cockpit. For the role templates and application identifiers, see Available Roles for Solution Owners. You have started the UI Adaptation mode. To do that, click Adapt UI in the user actions menu. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Overview Header Bar Version History If the user interface of the current app has been adapted previously, you can switch to a recent version or to the original app. Just click on the title of the current version to expand the version history, then select a version from the dropdown list to display it. Activate New Version Use  to activate the current draft or a selected version that is not currently active, so it becomes a new version. Discard Draft This option is only available when you display a draft that has not yet been activated. Use  to discard all UI changes that you did in draft mode. You can then start adapting the UI again, based on the last activated version. Publish Version This option is only available when you display an unpublished version. Use  (Publish Version) to publish a version of a changed app to a target subaccount. UI Adaptation and Navigation modes When UI Adaptation is activated, you can edit the current screen on which you started the adaptation mode, but you cannot navigate using a button (for example, to another list item, screen, or dialog box triggered by the button). To interrupt the adaptation mode and reach these "hidden" elements, choose Navigation. Now you can navigate on the UI as usual, for example to reveal other areas. Please note: Any changes you make while you're in the Navigation mode (for example setting a filter) will not be saved later. So make sure you choose UI Adaptation again before you make further changes that you want to preserve. Visualization mode This highlights all or certain supported key user changes that have been made on the UI and are part of the current UI. When you click on a highlighted change, you see details about all changes made to this element, including a timestamp for when the changes were saved. When you're in this mode, you will also see a dropdown list in the header bar that lets you filter for certain change types. By default, you see All Changes. More Actions Use  (More Actions) to display a menu containing additional actions. This menu contains actions for translating UI changes. These actions, as well as the  icon are only visible if you have the AdminFlexKeyUser role. Undo and Redo Use  to undo and  to redo the changes you made during your current session. Feedback Use  (Feedback) to share your feedback on key user adaptation with the development team at SAP. Save Draft Use  (Save Draft) to save your UI changes. The changes are saved as drafts and are not visible to end users until you activate them. Exit When you're done with your UI changes, use  (Exit) to exit the UI adaptation mode and return to your running app. For the specific kinds of changes you can make on the UI, check the subpage of this chapter. Security UI adaptation should not be used as a means to fulfill security requirements. UI changes affect only the visibility of the respective elements on the UI. Example: If you remove a field, it doesn't show up on the UI any longer. However, no other security measures 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- are applied that prevent a user from accessing the data associated with the removed field. If you want to restrict access to certain data for security reasons, this has to be done in the back-end system via roles and authorizations. Making UI Changes When you're in the adaptation mode of a worklist page or detail page, you can edit all UI elements (such as fields, groups of fields, or sections) that get highlighted when you hover over or select them. The optional changes that you can make on the elements appear in the context menu after you select them. You can also move a UI element by dragging and dropping. Check out the following video for an overview of how to make UI changes: Open this video in a new window Moving a UI Element To move a UI element, just drag and drop it. When you drag a UI element, dashed boxes indicate where you can drop it. Drag the element to its new location (indicated by a space) and drop it. You can also cut and paste UI elements: Right-click the UI element and choose Cut from the context menu. The element gets grayed out and a dashed box indicates where you can paste it. Right-click within the dashed box at the position where you want to paste the cut element and choose Paste from the context menu.  Note Different fields, groups or sections may support different kinds of changes depending on the apps’ predefined settings. For example, you can rename one certain field, but for others, you may not be able to rename them. You can also make changes on the elements on the popups and dialogues. After you add a field that is created in the standard model "gttft1" with Adapt UI, deleting it or marking it unreadable in the standard model will lead to errors and improper display of the field. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Removing a UI Element Select a UI element it and press Delete or choose Remove from the context menu. The element is then removed from the UI, it's not permanently deleted from the app. You can add it again at any point within its original container. Exception: When you delete a group of fields, the grouping information (group title and order of fields) gets lost, but the fields are still available and can be added. Resetting Changes By clicking  in the header bar, you can discard all the UI changes you made and return to the current activated version where you can make the changes again from the start. To do this, select Public when you create a view and save. Click Save & Exit to exit the UI Adaptation mode and return to the running app where you can see the created view in your view list. Data Contributor Apps This chapter provides application help on all the apps used by data contributors as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Overview Data contributors have access to a SAP Fiori Launchpad that offers various apps including the following: Manage Network App Description Manage Business Profile to view and edit your company profile such as contact details and business partner type User Management to manage your users such as to add/delete users and assign users to groups  Sample Code setMapConfiguration: function (sProvider) { var sProtocol = "https"; var sHereHost = "maps.hereapi.com"; var appLanguage = sap.ui.getCore().getConfiguration().getLanguageTag().slice(0, 2); var servicePattern = "{0}://{1}/v3/base/mc/'{LOD}'/'{X}'/'{Y}'/png8?apiKey={2}&lang={3}&lang2=en"; var sUrl = formatMessage(servicePattern, sProtocol, sHereHost, this.keys.HERE, appLanguage var oConfiguration = { "MapProvider": [{ "name": "HERE", "type": "", "description": "", "tileX": "256", "tileY": "256", "maxLOD": "22", "copyright": "Copyright © HERE", "Source": [{ "id": "s1", "url": sUrl, }], }], "MapLayerStacks": [{ "name": "DEFAULT", "MapLayer": { "name": "layer1", "refMapProvider": sProvider, "opacity": "1.0", "colBkgnd": Constants.COLORS.DELAYED_OVERDUE, }, }], }; this.oMap.setMapConfiguration(oConfiguration); this.oMap.setRefMapLayerStack("DEFAULT"); }, 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 92 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- App Description Manage Locations to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app System Connections to receive and respond to order and event tracking documents directly from your system by implementing the order and event tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Manage Invitations to manage all the invitations you receive from the solution owners to connect with their business network Settings App Description Define User Settings to define the default settings in various other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Retention Management App Description Blocking Store to access restricted data during its blocking period Retention Management to define rules that determine the residence and blocking periods of personal data Business Operations App Description Manage Integration Logs to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions User Management Prerequisite To access the User Management app, you must be an administrator user of SAP Business Network for Logistics. If you don’t know who is your company’s administrator user, create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB and provide your company’s subdomain in the incident. The subdomain can be found in your sign-in URL as follows: https://<subdomain>.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/sites About the app The User Management app allows an administrator to perform user management tasks including the following: Add or delete users in your company's tenant Add users to user groups  Note This app is available for data contributors only. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The User Management app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the users based on one or more of the filter options, such as First Name, Last Name and Email that appear in the header area. Worklists Include an All Users list and other user lists categorized by user groups. Worklist (User Management) There are different ways to work on the users and to set filters. To restrict the number of users displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the worklists for different user groups. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for users. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists All Users The All Users worklist contains all the users in the current tenant. This worklist displays the following details for each user: First name Last name Email  Note The user groups are pre-defined and you are not able to modify them.  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- User group(s) The system displays all the user groups to which the user belongs. This worklist contains the option to change user information, including first and last names, and the assigned user groups. You can do so by clicking the  Edit icon in the worklist. You can also add a user by choosing the Add button and delete a user by selecting the user and choosing Delete Delete User . User Lists by User Groups Each worklist displays all the users that belong to a specific user group. These worklists display the same user information as the All Users worklist. The worklists contain the option to change user information, delete a user, and remove a user from the current user group. To edit a user, click the  Edit icon for the user. To delete a user, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete User . To remove a user from the current user group, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete Mapping . For example, by choosing Delete Mapping in the ABC worklist, you remove the user from the ABC user group. Create a User and Assign User Groups Prerequisites You are a tenant administrator, that is, you have already been assigned to the admin user group either by the system or by another administrator in your company. Context As an administrator, you can create users in your company's tenant and assign users to user groups so that they have access to relevant apps. Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. 2. In the All Users worklist, choose the Add button. A new empty row is added at the top of the list table. 3. In the new row, enter the user names, user email, and select the user group(s) you want to assign to the user. Users assigned to the “…Admin” user group are administrators. They can perform administrative tasks using the following apps: Manage Business Profile Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings System Connections Manage Invitations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- User Management Manage Integration Logs Users assigned to the “…All_Function” user group can access the following apps: Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings Manage Invitations Manage Disputes Freight Orders for Confirmation Freight Orders for Reporting Review Freight Documents Invoice Freight Documents Freight Quotations Freight Requests for Quotation Manage Invoices Self-Book Dock Appointments Manage Freight Execution 4. Choose the Save button. Results The new user is created and added to the specified user groups in your company's tenant. The system will send an activation email to the user for setting the password.  Note When assigning user groups, consider the following security considerations: Grant the user only the authorization that is necessary. Ensure that authorization is removed as soon as it is no longer needed (for example, if an employee leaves the company).  Note If the new user's email domain is different from yours, you'll be prompted to confirm it.  Note If the user already exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics, no activation email will be sent because the user was already activated for the network. Users must sign out and sign in again to see the apps respective to their newly assigned user groups. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You need to send the network URL to the newly added users so they can sign in to the network with their own user credentials (after they’ve activated their user accounts). Edit User Information You, as a tenant administrator, can change the information for existing users in your company's tenant. Context The following user information can be changed: First and last names User group assignments Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. You can view all your users in the current tenant in the All Users worklist. To narrow down the list, use the filter bar, search box, or go to the worklist for a specific user group. 2. To edit a user, in any worklist, click the  Edit icon for the user, make your changes, and choose Save. Results If the user group assignment for an existing user is changed, the system will send an email to the user to notify the change. Users must sign out and sign in again to see the apps respective to their newly assigned user groups. Delete a User Context You, as a tenant administrator, can delete a user from the current tenant. The deleted user can no longer access the apps in your company's tenant. Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. You can view all the users in the All Users worklist. To narrow down the list, use the filter bar or search box. 2. To delete a user, in any worklist, select the user and choose Delete Delete User . 3. In the confirmation dialog box, click OK.  Note You can't delete your own account.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see Configurations for Location Replication. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Viewing a Location To view a location, proceed as follows: 1. By default, you can use the following fields to filter locations: External ID Source System Object Type Description Country/Region City Data Processing Status If the user also exists in other tenants of SAP Business Network for Logistics, the deletion only removes the user from the current tenant.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Additional Information You can also adjust the filter bar by chooosing Adapt Filters. 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. The detail view of the location consists of a header and other sections. Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. This includes the business purposes, the longitude/latitude coordinates, and the revision history. Geographical Coordinates and Map This section displays the geographical coordinates of the location. It also identifies the location on the map. Alternative Location IDs This section displays a list of type-specific alternative IDs of the location. Contact Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. Additional Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. More Information You can do the following with the filter bar: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for locations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. The default Standard view cannot be changed.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name. Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. This is a mandatory field if you want to use the location in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. The logical system ID you enter here must be the same one that you used when configuring the replication of location master data via the Data Replication Framework. For more information, see Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF). Make sure you enter the logical system ID correctly so that it matches the source system of the location. Otherwise, there can be duplicate records in your location master data. (Optional) Address: Country/Region State City District Street/House Number Zip Code (Optional) Geographical Coordinates And Map: Longitude: Longitude coordinate of the location Latitude: Latitude coordinate of the location (Optional) Time Zone (Optional) Alternative Location ID: Type: Type of the alternative ID. ID: Alternative ID in the specified type.  Note You can enter the coordinates in the Longitude and Latitude fields manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you save your changes. You can also choose Generate Longitude and Latitude Coordinates to create the coordinates according to the address information you’ve entered. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location record you are working on is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo-coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 101 This is custom documentation. Use the following fields to filter locations: Location ID Description Location Type Country/Region City 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. 3. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner of the details page. System Connections (Data Contributor) Use the System Connections app for data contributors to complete the implementation of SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs. By implementing the tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your organization can receive and respond to tracking requests directly from your system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: Specify the authentication details and base URLs for your system’s endpoints. Assign authentication details and a base URL to each API operation that you’ve implemented. Enable inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app has the following areas: Outbound Connections This area lists the outbound-from-network API services to which you can assign authentication details and a base URL. In addition, you can see the active or inactive status of the operations. Manage Details 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- This area enables you to manage (create, edit and delete) your base URLs (communication details) and your authentication details (OAuth 2.0 and basic credentials). Connection Settings This area enables you to call LBN endpoints for inbound and outbound connections. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, go to https://api.sap.com/package/LbnGlobalTrackAndTrace?section=Overview . Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints Configure communication and authentication details for your system's API or EDI endpoints by specifying base URLs, protocols (HTTPS/SFTP/Email), and authentication methods (Basic, API Key, OAuth 2.0) to enable secure integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Manage Details. 2. In the Communication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. You can choose between the following options: HTTPS (for API) SFTP (for EDI) Email (for EDI) 3. In the Authentication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. When creating API communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details Base URL The endpoint URL for the communication The API call made to your system uses the HTTPS protocol. When creating EDI communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Address Enter the host name or IP address of the SFTP server and an optional port, for example, my.host.org:22. You can configure this parameter by entering a dynamic expression such as ${property.property_name} or ${header.header_name}. Message Format You can choose EDIFACT or ANSI X12 from the drop-down list. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 103 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Attribute Description Message Type For EDIFACT, you can choose between the following options: IFTMIN All Inbound Messages For ANSI X12, you can choose between the following options: 204 213 300 303 997 All Inbound Messages Known Host Key Enter a base64-encoded string of your SFTP server. This is used to authenticate your server. SAP Business Network for Logistics can also retrieve the known host key and insert it for you. As a prerequisite, you must have entered the address (including the port) of the SFTP server. Message Version The D96A message version is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT. The V4010 message version is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12. No version will be displayed for message type All Inbound Messages. Description The Instructions of Transport description is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT message type IFTMIN. The Load Tender description is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12 message type 204. The description will not be shown for message type All Inbound Messages. Directory Enter the relative path to write the file to a directory. Example: parentdirectory/childdirectory File Name Enter the name of the file to be written. The entry is valid only for LBN outbound message types. Additional allowed placeholders: %DOCUMENT_ID% %MESSAGE_TYPE% %TIMESTAMP% %SHIPPER_LBN_ID% %CONTROL_NUMBER% The placeholder %CONTROL_NUMBER% is only available for ANSI X12 997 messages. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 104 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Attribute Description You can combine these placeholders with any fixed strings and in any order (<string 1><placeholder 1><string 2><placeholder 2> <string 3>). Examples: LBN_%MESSAGE_TYPE%_%DOCUMENT_ID%_%TIMESTAMP%.edi %TIMESTAMP%_%SHIPPER_LBN_ID%.edi When creating Basic authentication details, the provided user name and password are used for authentication during the API call to your system. When creating API Key authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details API Key Attribute Enter the key for the request header. API Key Value Enter the token to be used for authentication. The API key represents the name of the token that a client provides when making API calls. The token is sent as request header. When creating OAuth 2.0 authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Grant Type Valid values are: Client Credentials (default) and Client Certificate. Authentication URL Enter the URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization server that issues the access token. Client ID Enter the ID of the client that you’re connecting to. Client Secret Secret key of the client that you’re connecting to. OAuth 2.0 uses a multiple-step authentication pattern: Client credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) are used by the client application to initially request an access token. The access token is then used to authorize the client (for as long as the token is valid) to access the server’s resources (for example, the resources that are used in the associated integration flow). In many OAuth 2.0 scenarios, the access token is issued (or generated) by an authorization server. Client Authentication Select Send as Body Parameter or Send as Request Header. This enables access to your system. If you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent in the request body to the authentication server. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 105 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Attribute Description If you select Send as Request Header, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent as a part of the authorization header to the authentication server. Valid values are: client credentials and client certificate. Client Certificate When you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID goes in the request body to the authentication server. If you choose Send as Request Header, the Client ID becomes part of the authorization header sent to the authentication server. Specify the path of the client certificate (key pair file) in the Key Pair File field. Enter its password in the Password field. Include Scope Select the checkbox to provide the OAuth 2.0 scope information that will be included in the request body. Scope Enter the scope that you defined for the endpoint. Content Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded is selected by default. Assigning Authentication Details and a Base URL to a Service Prerequisites You have specified the communication details (base URL) and authentication details (basic or OAuth 2.0 credentials, or API key). Context Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, on the Outbound Connections view, choose Create and complete the Create Service dialog. The table below provides more information. In the System Connections app, on the Configuration Settings view, activate the Enable Inbound Connections toggle. For new users, the toggle is disabled by default. 2. Select the integration platform. You can choose between Multi-Cloud and Neo (deprecated). Neo is selected by default. 3. (For Multi-Cloud only) Select the Provider APIs to which you want to have access, and save. You can update the Provider API selection later. 4. View the service credentials (client ID, client secret, authentication URL, and host URL). You can copy them and enter them when you create the OAuth 2.0 authentication details. For more information, see: Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. For more information, refer to the instructions in the provider API specification of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, under https://api.sap.com/package/LbnGlobalTrackAndTrace?section=Overview . To enable inbound connections for Neo, proceed as in step 1. By default, inbound communication is authenticated with OAuth 2.0. To acquire the OAuth 2.0 credentials for Neo (deprecated), create an incident with component SBN-LBN-INT. Manage Alternate IDs (Data Contributor) You can maintain alternate identifiers of your other accounts in the network. These identifiers shall be used in specific integration scenarios or in specific transaction flows in the network. Additionally, the LBN ID of your tenant can be seen above the Alternate IDs table as a read-only field. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following alternate identifiers (alternate IDs): DUNS ID (Data Universal Numbering System ID) SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Registration Number USDOT (US Department of Transportation) MC Number (Motor Carrier Number) Others GLN (Global Location Number) Technical User To create your own alternate IDs, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select an alternate ID type from the dropdown menu and type in the required value. 3. Choose OK. You can also delete or change existing entries. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps for .SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Distance In this section, you can define the default unit of measurement for distance. The system uses this setting in other apps in your area. Notification Subscriptions In this section, you can subscribe to notifications for various scenarios and specify the email address and preferred language for receiving the notifications. Note that you cannot subscribe to a scenario without maintaining an email address. When you subscribe to notifications for a scenario, the system can send email notifications based on the settings you make in the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information on managing notification settings, see Manage Notification Settings. Manage Invitations The Manage Invitations app allows you to manage all the invitations you receive from potential business partners to connect with their business network. The app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the invitations based on one or more of the filter options, such as inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear in the header area. Worklists by status The invitations are categorized based on the invitation statuses: New, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Invitations) There are different ways to work on the invitations and to set filters. To restrict the number of invitations displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the preconfigured worklists (New, Accepted, Rejected) based on the status of the invitation. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for invitations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists New The New worklist displays all invitations that you have not yet responded to. Launch the Manage Invitations app. 2. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. (Optional) You can retrieve a specific invitation or a set of invitations using the various search filter options such as the inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear on the header area. The system also categorizes the invitations based on various attributes and displays them in the following tabs: New: Displays all new invitations from potential business partners. Accepted: Displays invitations that you have accepted. Rejected: Displays invitations that you have rejected. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Context You can accept or reject the invitations from potential business partners to connect with their business network. When rejecting, you can indicate a rejection reason to the inviter. If you accept an invitation, you can connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. If you reject an invitation, you cannot connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. To accept or reject an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. You can directly accept or reject the invitations in this worklist. 2. Alternatively, you can search for and retrieve a specific invitation using search filter options in the header. Once you retrieve the invitation, you can respond to the invitation by choosing the Accept or Reject button. Results Once you accept or reject an invitation, you can view the details of the invitation in the Accepted or Rejected worklist as appropriate. You cannot view this invitation anymore in the New worklist. Default value: No Manage Notification Settings You can use this app to schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert. On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. Subscribers The system displays the list of users who have subscribed to notifications for the current scenario. The subscription is made in the Define User Settings app. Scenarios As a data contributor, you can schedule email notifications for the following scenario: Scenario Group Scenario For receiving email notifications when, before or after ... Business Operations Integration Error V2 The system now sends an email notification to you when an integration error occurs. Related Information Define User Settings Configure Notification Settings Prerequisites To enable reminder notifications, make sure you also maintain an email address and subscribe to the notification(s) you need in the Define User Settings app. For more information, see Define User Settings Context You can configure the following types of notifications in the Manage Notification Settings app, where applicable. On-Event Notification On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. You can activate or deactivate on-event notification by setting the activation toggle to Yes or No, respectively. Pre-Event Notifications  Note To enable email notifications for the above scenarios, you need to activate the settings in this app and subscribe to notifications for the scenarios in the Define User Settings app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 116 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Pre-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive before the target event happens, for example, before dock appointment booking cut-off. You can schedule pre-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the start of the period, for example, 30 days before the event, which means the notification period starts from 30 days before the event till the start of the next period or the event time. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Post-Event Notifications Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. You can schedule post-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 15 days Every 3 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 30 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 30 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 15 days Every 3 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 117 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- You only specify the end of the period, for example, 30 days after the event, which means the notification period starts from the end of the previous period or the event time, to 30 days after the event. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Notification Settings app. 2. In the scenario list, select the scenario for which you want to set notifications. 3. To activate on-event notification, for On-Event Notification, set the toggle to Yes. To deactivate, set it to No. 4. To configure pre-event or post-event notifications, do the following: a. Expand the Pre-Event Notifications or Post-Event Notifications area. b. To add a notification period, choose the Add button. Then in the Add Notification Period dialog box, specify the start (pre-event) or end (post-event) of the period and the frequency, and choose Save. You can add multiple periods according to your needs.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 60 days Every 10 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 30 days after the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 30 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Note that for the invitations scenario, the notifications stop as soon as the invitation is accepted or rejected. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 60 days Every 10 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. To deactivate a period, set Activated for User to No. Manage Freight Execution The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to view the execution of the freight documents by tracking planned and unplanned events that occurred during freight execution. You can also report various planned and unplanned events. Also, you can perform the following in this new app: Planned milestone events You can view the milestones planned by the ordering party Planned and unplanned events You can report various planned and unplanned events. Estimate You can report an estimate for any planned event. Delay You can report delays at both the document-level and at an event-level. Proof of pick-up and delivery You can submit proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. Additional events You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. Event history You can view all the events reported by you and all other business partners. You can also view the event history for a specific planned event. Attachments You can view all the attachments specific to the freight execution in the Attachments tab. This app contains the track relevant freight documents irrespective of whether the documents are relevant for confirmation or not. This app also contains documents that are ready for tracking from the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. In this app, you can view the events that you reported manually and the events reported by other business partners. The manually reported data and the events reported by the APIs are synchronized to the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or SAP S/4 HANA system. Note that you can report events for a freight order even when you have not reconfirmed a freight order that has been updated by the ordering party. Execution Status Displays the execution progress of a freight document. You can view one of the following statuses: Ready for Execution When a freight document is set to ready for transportation execution in the ordering party’s external system, the execution status is set as Ready for Execution. This is the initial execution status of a freight document. Execution Started When an event is reported at the source location, the execution status is set as Execution Started. In Transit When a departure is reported, the execution status is set as In Transit. Arrived at Intermediate Location When the vehicle arrives at an intermediate location, the execution status is set as Arrived at Intermediate Location. Arrived at Destination 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 126 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- When the vehicle arrives at the destination location, the execution status is set as Arrived at Arrived at Intermediate Location. Executed When the last planned event has been reported, the execution status is set as Executed. Reporting Status Displays a status based on the event reporting in a freight document. You can view one of the following statuses: Ready for Reporting When a freight document is made available in the Manage Freight Execution app, the initial status is set as Ready for Reporting. Reporting in Progress When the carrier starts reporting events in the freight document then the reporting status is set as Reporting in Progress. Reporting Completed When the carrier has reported all planned events in the freight document or marked the remaining events as Unable to Report, then the reporting status is set as Reporting Completed. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. You can view one of the following statuses: As Planned This status appears when no event has been reported for the freight document and the reporting deadline has not yet lapsed. Early This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred ahead of time. On Time This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred on time. Late This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred late. Overdue This status appears when the latest planned event has not been reported by the reporting deadline. Delayed This status appears when a delayed event is reported on either the latest planned event or at the document-level. Estimated Status 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 127 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. You can view one of the following statuses: Running Early When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen before time. Running on Time When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen on time. Running Late When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen late. Proof of Delivery Status Displays whether the proof of delivery has been reported at the last stop. You can view one of the following statuses. Reported at Last Stop Not Reported at Last Stop Reporting Events While your company transports freight for an ordering party, you can use the Manage Freight Execution app to report planned and unplanned events in the freight document. You can also perform the following when you report an event: Report an estimate for any planned event, enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a delay at both the document-level and at a planned event-level. You can report proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. You can report an event directly from the worklist page or the detailed view page for a freight document. When you choose the Report button, you can choose one of the following options. Planned Event You can report a planned event as follows: 1. Select an event for which you want to report. You can view the list of events planned by the ordering party for you. Note that the system pre-selects the next planned event. You can change the selection as required. 2. Enter the final time or estimated time along with the time zone. 3. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 4. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 5. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 128 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Unplanned Event You can report an unplanned event as follows: 1. Select an event from the supported event types. 2. Optionally, select a stop at which this unplanned event must be reported. 3. Enter the final time along with the time zone. 4. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 5. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 6. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. Unable to Report Remaining Events You can choose this option if you will never be able to provide the final time of the event. Events History Header When you choose the View Events History button in the detailed view page, you can view all events reported during the freight execution in a card format. This includes all the planned and unplanned events that have been reported multiple times. For each event, you can view the following information in a card format: Event type Current status When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated status When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Location Planned on Final time When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated time When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Business partner Attachment Reason Code When a reason code is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Reason Code Description 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 129 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- When a reason code description is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Events Overview When you navigate to additional options in the Events Overview sub-tab and choose the View History button in the planned event card, you can view all the events that have already been reported for that specific planned event on the right pane. Common Apps This chapter provides application help on the apps used by both solution owners and data contributors as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Manage Business Profile Whether you are a shipper, solution owner, or logistics provider, you will land on the company profile page in SAP Business Network when opening the Manage Business Profile app. On this page, you can manage and adjust your company information as per your needs. This enables potential partners and relevant stakeholders to know more about your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strength. You can maintain the basic information about your company. This includes but is not limited to the type of organization, year founded, and annual revenue to help shippers and solution owners evaluate you as a potential logistics provider. The Product and Service Categories, Ship-to or Service Locations, and Industries sections of your company profile allow you to provide detailed information about the products or services you offer, the locations you ship to or provide services, and the industries you serve. This information is critical because shippers and solution owners usually discover your company based on the product and service categories and ship-to or service locations. The Additional Addresses section provides you with an effective and intuitive way to add and manage addresses beyond the primary business address, such as branch offices, regional offices, warehouses, or other physical sites associated with your company. Including these addresses provides a comprehensive overview of your company's geographical reach and operational scope. The Contacts section enables you to create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or multiple roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, and Technical Contact, designating them as companywide contacts. This guarantees that their contact details are readily available to all current and potential trading partners on the network. More Information Company information was once maintained via the Manage Business Profile app. Although the Company Profile page in SAP Business Network uses a similar user interface to the app, a few differences can be noticed. Note the following constraints and guidelines when you edit your company profile: Company D-U-N-S Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a D-U-N-S number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Select Additional Addresses from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. On the Additional Addresses page, click Create. 3. On the Create Address page, specify the following fields: Address Name (Mandatory): Give a unique name to easily identify this address. Address Type: Specify the type of address. Country/Region (Mandatory): Specify the country or region where the address is located. Address Line 1 (Mandatory): Enter the primary address information. Address Line 2 (Optional): Include additional address details, if applicable. Address Line 3 (Optional): Include further address details, if necessary. City (Mandatory): Specify the city where the address is located. State (Mandatory): Provide the state or region where the address is situated. Zip (Mandatory): Enter the postal or ZIP code for the address. Contact: You can add contact details associated with this address, including: Phone Number: This field is mandatory. Mobile Number: Optionally provide a mobile contact number. Fax Number: If applicable, provide a fax number. Email: This field is mandatory for email communication regarding this address. 4. Once all required information is entered, click Save. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 132 This is custom documentation. Managing Contact Information Companywide Contact Companywide contacts have their contact information accessible to both current and potential business partners on the network. Assign individuals in your company as companywide contacts. This ensures that your business partners know the right people to contact for various issues or questions. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. Click Create in the upper right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 3. On the Create Contact Personnel Entry page, specify the basic information and address of the contact. The basic information includes Contact Name, Email, Business Title, Phone, Fax, and Company Assignment. Each contact must have a name, phone number, and email. The Company Assignment field specifies the companywide roles assigned to a contact. If this field is specified, the contact is designated as a companywide contact for the selected role, and their contact information is accessible to all business partners on the network. Each contact personnel can be assigned with multiple companywide roles. 4. After providing the necessary information, click Create. 5. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 6. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table. After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Profile Settings You can specify the visibility and availability of your company profile on the Profile Settings page. If you are a shipper or solution owner, before trying to connect with business partners that operate in a different data center, you must first make your company profile available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Steps to Configure Profile Settings 1. Open your company profile. 2. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 3. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile to appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to potential business partners in their search results. Once your company profile becomes visible, shippers or solution owners can discover your company on the network and send you connection requests for further partnership. Default value: Yes 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 133 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to allow profile data replication across data centers. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers in SAP Business Network for Logistics. For carriers and data providers, this setting is enabled by default. Shippers and solution owners need to enable it manually. 4. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results Once Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will become searchable and visible to potential business partners. Otherwise, your company profile will not be shown in any search results, and thus, no business partners can reach you for further connections. Once Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network is enabled, your company profile data will be replicated across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Future updates to your profile will also be automatically synchronized across all data centers. For shippers and solution owners, enabling this setting allows for establishing cross- data-center connections. If this setting is not enabled, your company profile will be only available in the data center where you initially onboarded. As a result, no cross-data-center connections can be established. Manage Integration Logs The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can view the integration logs using this app. For solution owners, to navigate to this app, you need to launch the View Logs app first on the SAP Fiori launchpad. Then click Manage Integration Logs in the Quick Links section. This can be integration logs between SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP S/4HANA or any other backend SAP system (such as SAP Transportation Management) or any API or EDI system of carriers, network partners, network participants, or similar. Since SAP Business Network for Logistics follows a single integration system design for all customers and other partners, the Manage Integration Logs app aims to provide a visibility into integration logs for a particular customer or partner. Only the technical parties involved in an integration log can view the same in the app, ensuring data separation across all customers. The app also provides access to customer-facing payloads and enables the reprocessing of failed integration logs. The app provides standard SAP Business Network for Logistics integration logs only. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting . Shippers and solution owners can use the following features: You can search based on document ID and date/time. You can use separate tabs for Logs and Documents:  Note Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed.  Note To use the app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Solution Owners section and the Available Roles for Data Contributors section of the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 134 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- In the Logs tab, there are two predefined filters: All (includes all messages in all statuses) and Failed (includes messages in status Failed or Escalated). Individual messages sent to or from SAP Business Network for Logistics are listed here. The Documents tab provides an aggregated view based on predefined scenarios. Each scenario is a collection of document types based on SAP Business Network for Logistics apps. For more information about available scenarios, see Scenarios. For each scenario, the Manage Integration Logs app provides an overall status. The status in the Documents tab is the status of the latest integration log within the aggregated scenario. You can reprocess escalated messages from either of the tabs. You can sort and filter on column level. You can download the table content to a Microsoft Excel file. You can view the payloads and error logs within the app. You can download the payloads. Carriers and data contributors can only view the Logs tab. The following statuses are available: Completed: The system assigns this status to a message when SAP Business Network for Logistics was able to process the document successfully. Failed: The system assigns this status to a message when there is a validation error that occurred during the first step of processing of the message. This can happen if there is a payload issue, missing mandatory fields, or a missing configuration. Retry: Depending on the nature of the error and the settings in the consuming application, an integration log can go to retry mode. In such cases, the log retries for a couple of times ranging from a couple of minutes to 30 minutes, after which the status goes into a final status – Completed or Escalated. Escalated: The system assigns this status to a message when the processing failed in backend of an app, or in an external API, or in the customer’s backend SAP system. This usually denotes a connectivity failure at any of the above mentioned places. Reasons could be that a service is not available for a long period, or that there is an authentication issue, or some basic connectivity failure due to misconfigurations, or technical failures in a backend system. You can find a more detailed error information when you click the icon in the Log Details column. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 137 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The Error column displays the error code and description that the affected app sends when a call to SAP Business Network for Logistics fails. The description provides you with a more concrete context of the issue. You can sort or filter by error code to identify the logs with common failures, and take corrective actions (such as reprocessing the messages, fixing the root cause of the issue, informing SAP support about the error). Reprocessing: The system assigns this status to a message while it's being reprocessed. After you solve the configuration or connectivity issue in SAP Business Network for Logistics and select the Reprocess button, the system moves the message to this status. While a message has this status, you should just wait for it to complete reprocessing. The overall status is derived from the latest status of an individual log associated with the scenario. Flow Direction Systems involved in message flow The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are being sent between the different systems involved. The following flow directions are available: SAP S/4HANA to Network Network to SAP S/4HANA Network to External System External System to Network Network to Network Error Codes The Manage Integration Logs app categorizes and displays error codes for communication failures between different systems. The Manage Integration LogsSAP Business Network for Logistics app displays error codes when the communication between the different systems involved (SAP Business Network for Logistics, SAP S/4HANA or any other backend SAP system, such as SAP Transportation Management, or any API or EDI system) fails. The Manage Integration Logs app can categorize integration log errors based on the error response captured. When an error occurs in a backend SAP Business Network for Logistics app, this app provides an error code in the response, which can then be shown in the Manage Integration Logs app under Error along with their translated descriptions. SAP Business Network for Logistics tries to capture the HTTP response codes while communicating to an external system, and for internal systems where it doesn’t find a category code. We categorize the error messages as far as possible. You can sort or filter by error code to identify the logs with common failures, and take corrective actions (such as reprocessing the messages, fixing the root cause of the issue, informing SAP support about the error).  Note SAP S/4HANA can be either SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. Both two systems have the Transportation Management (TM) component embedded, which can work with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Network refers to a product or solution within the SAP Business Network family. External System refers to a non-SAP system. This can, for example, be an API system or an EDI server. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 138 This is custom documentation.
