Contact your visibility provider or carrier. 5002 Request body format error 5003 Time zone format incorrect Reprocessing Integration Messages When integration messages fail to reach the target system, this is reported in a message log. Depending on the kind of error, it can help to reprocess an integration message. However, not all integration messages can be reprocessed. You can manually reprocess integration messages with the status Failed or Escalated. To do so, proceed as follows: 1. Select a message, or multiple messages, in the table. 2. Choose Reprocess. When an escalated/failed message is reprocessed, newer logs are created in the internal integration system. When you try to reprocess an already reprocessed message, the Manage Integration Logs app refers to the latest logs in the internal integration system. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 148 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- The reprocessing of a message is limited to 29 days. After 30 days, you won’t be able to reprocess the message or download the payload. Log details are available to be viewed for 90 days. For reprocessing purposes, there are two columns available: Reprocessed: Indicates whether an integration message has already been reprocessed or not. Reprocessable: Indicates whether a message log can be reprocessed or not. Not all messages with status Failed or Escalated are eligible for reprocessing. This is usually determined by a uniqueness check of a combination of several fields such as Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. In certain cases, the check is also extended to additional information, such as Event Type or Reported Time. An integration message with status Failed or Escalated is the latest one in chronological order when grouped together with Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. Example: A subcontracting request (TransportationOrderRequest) is sent from the transportation management (TM) system of a shipper to SAP Business Network for Logistics and fails. The same document is updated in the TM system and sent again. In such cases, SAP Business Network for Logistics would allow the reprocessing of the latest message only. The older integration messages will have the Reprocessable value set to No. The same applies when the latest integration message from the TM system has the status Completed. Older messages with status Failed or Escalated are not eligible for reprocessing. Hence, the Reprocessable value is set to No. In certain cases, such as an event notification in a tracking scenario, the event type and the reported time are also considered. Example: If multiple events reported by a carrier or a carrier system fail in SAP Business Network for Logistics, all of these are relevant for reprocessing. In the uniqueness check, event type and reported time information is considered too. Thus, for the same freight order ID, shipper, document type (TransportationEventBulkNotification), and source system, it’s possible to reprocess escalated logs for DepartureEvent, ArrivalEvent, etc. And for all these event logs, the Reprocessable value is set to Yes. Automatic Reprocessing of Integration Messages In addition to the conditions mentioned above, integration messages must meet the following prerequisites to be auto- reprocessed: The messages are reprocessable. The messages have not been reprocessed earlier (either manually or automatically). Either the sender or the receiver of the message has a tenant of type Default (productive tenant). Auto-reprocessing is not supported for test tenants. The messages failed with an error code that is eligible for auto-reprocessing. Automatic reprocessing is supported for the following error codes: Error Codes Eligible for Auto-Reprocessing Error Code Description 102 Missing necessary connectivity configurations at customer side 107 Missing necessary tenant configurations 108 Missing necessary connectivity configurations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 149 This is custom documentation. After a downtime, we automatically reprocess failed and escalated messages. Retention Management SAP Business Network for Logistics restricts the access of personal data on completion of its business purpose. That is, not all the user groups can access the personal data after the expiration of originally defined residence period. The Retention Management app enables you to define rules for residence and blocking of personal data for apps that belong to a specific application group. These rules restrict the usage of documents containing personal data. In the Retention Management app, you define the residence period and the blocking period. The residence period and blocking period are together called as the retention period. Business Activity The relevant data is used in ongoing business, such as contract creation, delivery or payment. End of Business Defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period.  Note You should familiarize yourself with the following important definitions before using the Retention Management app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 150 This is custom documentation. Residence Period The period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. For the settings of residence period in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to Defining Residence and Blocking Periods. End of Purpose The point in time when the processing of a set of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose, for example, when a contract is fulfilled. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorizations (for example, tax auditors). In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the value of end of purpose is calculated by the blocking store background job: End of Purpose = End of Business + Residence Period When the residence period is finished, the tracked process and event lifecycle reach end of purpose. Blocking Period The period between the residence period and the deletion of the data. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a Data Protection Officer (DPO), can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. For the settings of blocking period in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to Defining Residence and Blocking Periods. Retention Period The period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. Retention Period = Residence Period + Blocking Period Deletion The data is deleted and no longer exists in the database. In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the value of date of deletion is calculated by the blocking store background job: Date of Deletion = End of Business + Residence Period + Blocking Period Notes Blocking store background job operates automatically once a day at 12 a.m. UTC. So any changes of the life cycle status of tracked processes and events take effect after 12 a.m. UTC each day. End of Business is updated if an event is reported to a tracked process. The end of business dates of this tracked process and its correlated tracked processes are also updated and consistent with the end of business date of the latest reported event. The life cycle status of tracked process is not updated if you directly change the “lifeCycleStatus_code” value of this tracked process. It is only updated by the blocking store background job. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 151 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 3 -- When considering compliance with data protection regulations, it is also necessary to consider compliance with industry- specific legislation in different countries/regions. A typical potential scenario in certain countries/regions is that personal data shall be deleted after the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for the processing of personal data has ended, but only as long as no other retention periods are defined in legislation, for example, retention periods for financial documents. Legal requirements in certain scenarios or countries/regions also often require blocking of data in cases where the specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes for the processing of this data have ended, however, the data still has to be retained in the database due to other legally mandated retention periods. In some scenarios, personal data also includes referenced data. Therefore, the challenge for deletion and blocking is first to handle referenced data and finally other data, such as business partner data. Defining Residence and Blocking Periods Context To define the residence period and blocking period of various applications, do the following: Procedure 1. Login to the SAP Fiori Launchpad and choose the Retention Management tile. 2. Select an application type. 3. Enter a residence period. Note that if you do not specify a residence period, the system by default assigns a residence period of 12 months for the application type. 4. Enter a blocking period. Note that if you do not specify a blocking period, the system by default assigns a blocking period of 12 months for the application type. 5. Choose Save. Results The system stores the entered residence and blocking periods for the specific application type. Blocking Store Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with appropriate authorization, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can log into the SAP Fiori Launchpad and choose the Blocking Store app to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format by choosing the Download button. Identifier: Displays the unique identifier for the document. Status: Displays the status of the document, for example, in blocking period. End of business: Displays the date when the document reached the end of business state. App name: Displays the name of the tracked process type / event type with which the data is associated.  Note If you have any questions, log your incident in SAP Support Launchpad with component “SBN-LBN-BP-OB”. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 152 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 3 -- Administration information Help and Support There are several ways you can find help and support on the Fiori launchpad of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Built-In Support Built-in support provides efficient, simplified and guided support channels, you can search for knowledge, ask for needed information, get help from recommended solutions. Currently, expert chat is not supported. To access the built-in support service on the Fiori Launchpad, click the icon  on the right corner of the screen. You will see a welcome page where you can sign in, and a list of recommended links for the page. To gain full access to the built-in functions, you must activate your S-user. For more, see Activating Built-In Support Services. For more information on how to use this tool, refer to Built-In Support on SAP Help Portal. In-app Help When you launch the app, you can turn on the in-app help that provides on-screen explanations of key fields and areas on the screen. To turn on the in-app help, on the top right on the screen, click the  icon. Once the in-app help is turned on, you can: search the displayed help topics for the text that you type; click the  icon to see the help texts on that topic; click the link tiles to see the documentation of this app on SAP Help Portal; hide the Help Topics panel by clicking the  button on the bottom right.  Note If you have any questions, log your incident in ServiceNow with component “SBN-LBN-BP-OB”. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 153 This is custom documentation. In the navigation URLs, the filtering settings should be defined as the URL parameters,and the filtered results would be automatically displayed as you navigate to these pages. Typically, the pattern of this navigation URL is: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key>=<value> If you want to specify multiple filters or multiple values for one filter, the navigation URL patterns are as follows: For multiple filters: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key_1>=<value_1>&<key_2>=<value_2> For one filter with multiple values: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key_1>=<value_1>& <key_1>=<value_2> For detailed instructions on how to define the URL parameters for the navigation, see Define the URL Parameters for Filtering the Worklists of Fulfillment Tracking Apps. You can also find some URL Parameters examples in List of URL Parameters Examples. Define the URL Parameters for Filtering the Worklists of Fulfillment Tracking Apps Context To define the URL parameters for filtering the worklists of fulfillment tracking apps, do the following: Procedure 1. Decide on a filter to be defined in the navigation URL. 2. Define the key of the parameter. It is the field name of the filter. Generally, each filter in the apps corresponds to one user model field, standard model field or core model field in the standard model “gttft1”. To find the field name, do the following: Go to the standard model in the Manage Models app. Click the target tracked process or field type and find the corresponding field in the User Model Fields, Standard Model Fields or Core Model Fields sections. Use the field name, not the description. The type of the field may influence the name of the key. For details, see List of URL Parameters Examples. 3. Define the value of the parameter. It consists of the operator and the field value, for example, “>2021”. The type of the field supports different operators. For details, see List of URL Parameters Examples. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Context “My Tracking Status” is a non-standard field that can reflect how your tracking process goes. You can display it in the Track Shipments, Monitor Inbound ASNs and Monitor Outbound Deliveries apps to identify shipments, inbound and outbound deliveries with exceptional tracking status. You can define it in a way that better meets your individual business needs. Procedure 1. Open the Manage Models app. 2. Go to the standard model “gttft1”. 3. In the Code List tab, click one of the following code lists: “ShipmentCustomTrackingStatus” code list for the shipment. "TrackingUnitCustomTrackingStatus" code list for the tracking unit. “InbDlvCustomTrackingStatus” code list for the inbound delivery. “OutbDlvCustomTrackingStatus” code list for the outbound delivery. 4. Click the Add button above the table. A new row with two empty inputs will be added on the bottom of the table. 5. Fill in code and name. If the code is left empty, this line will not be saved to model. 6. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- GoodsReceipt Delivered Return ManifestReady ReceivedFromShipper ConsigneeNotified Stage-Level Observation Between Tracked Processes Introduction When a tracked process observes another tracked process at stage level, the event correlation follows the following rules: For actual events that can match a planed event in the observing tracked process, they can be correlated to the observing tracked process from the observed tracked process. For actual events that cannot match a planned event in the observing tracked process, only those of the observed stages can be correlated to the observing tracked process from the observed tracked process. In such case, the correlation starts after the first planned event is reported for the observed tracked process, and the actual event must: be correlated to the observing tracked process. match a planned event of the observing tracked process. The correlation stops once the Arrival event on the last stop of the observed stages is reported for the observed tracked process. In the fulfillment tracking apps, those correlated events from the observed tracked process can be displayed in the timeline or events table of the observing tracked process. The stage-level observation applies to the following observation scenarios: FreightUnit observes Shipment FreightUnit observes TrackingUnit Shipment observes TrackingUnit OutboundDelivery observes Shipment InboundDelivery observes Shipment 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Here is an example that helps you better understand the event correlation for the stage-level observation: In this example, tracked process A is assumed to observe tracked process B. For tracked process A, there are two stops, each has a planned event. For tracked process B, there are three stops. There are two planned events (planned Arrival and Departure events) on stop 2. The observed stage is from stop 1 to stop 2. Case 1 The Departure event is reported on stop 1 of tracked process B. This Departure event can be correlated to tracked process A because the Departure event of tracked process B can match a planned event in tracked process A. Case 2 After departure, an unplanned Location Update event is reported on stop 1 of tracked process B. This unplanned Location update can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A, because: This Departure event matches the Departure event on stop 1 of tracked process A. The Departure event has already reported and correlated to tracked process A. Case 3 The Arrival event on stop 2 of tracked process B is reported. This Arrival event can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. Meanwhile, tracked process A stops getting actual events that cannot match its planned events from tracked process B because its Arrival event on the last stop of the observed stage has been reported. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Case 4 The Departure event on stop 2 of tracked process B is reported. This Departure event cannot be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A because this Departure event cannot match a planned event of tracked process A, and this actual event is not on the observed stage. As a result, All actual events on the observed stage (from stop 1- stop 2) can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. All actual events from stop 2 to stop 3 cannot be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. Deactivating Stage-Level Observation By default, the stage-level observation is activated. You can use the flag “gttft1_StageLevelObserveSwitchOn” in the event-to-action script to deactivate it. As a result, the observing tracked process receives all actual events correlated from the observed tracked process. To deactivate the stage-level observation, do the following: 1. Go to the standard model “gttft1” of the Manage Models app. 2. In the User Script before Standard Script section of the Event to Action tab, set the value of “gttft1_StageLevelObserveSwitchOn” to “false”. By default, the value is set to “true”. Delay Status Shows if a tracked process or an event is delayed or not. A tracked process is shown as Delayed when one of its planned events is delayed. Event Status Event status is determined by comparing the planned business timestamp with that of the actual. Event Status Description As Planned The initial status for the planned event. Delayed At least one "Delay" event or an event that inherits "GTTDelayedEvent" is reported with reference to the unreported planned event, without the "on-time" event to restore its status. Reported Early The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is earlier than the earliest planned business time. Reported On Time The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is between the earlier and latest planned business time. Reported Late The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is later than the latest planned business time. Reported An unplanned event has been reported. Overdue The planned event is not reported but the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp. Process Status The actual status of the tracked process, decided by the status of the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned”. See the following table for status description. Process Status Description As Planned The initial status of a tracked process, also the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported. Delayed A tracked process is "Delayed" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is expected to be late. Early A tracked process is "Early" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported and its actual business time is earlier than the earliest planned business time. Late A tracked process is "Late" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported and the actual business time is later than the latest planned business time. Overdue A tracked process is "Overdue" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is overdue. It indicates that the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp, but the last planned event hasn't been reported. Invite Business Partners The Invite Business Partners app is designed for managing all the business partners that you want to be part of your network. You can use this app to select and invite business partners to join your business network and check their participation status. If you have access, you can navigate to the Discover Business Partners app to find more potential business partners. You may have business with many partners in your system and you may want to persist your business with them in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can download the Excel template available in the app and fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload the template back in the app. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can download these business partners from SAP TM system and upload them in Invite Business Partners. For more information, see Downloading Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). You can select one or more of these business partners from your system and invite them to join your network. When you submit these partners, a back-end team manages your connection invitation. For more information, see Connection Invitations. When a business partner accepts an invitation to connect with your network, the system updates the unique LBN ID of the partner. If you are using SAP TM system, you can update these LBN IDs of partners in SAP TM system by downloading the partner list from the Discover Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). The Discover Business Partners app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the business partner based on one more of the filter options (Business Partner ID and Business Partner) that appear on the header area. Worklists by status The business partners are categorized based on their invitation response status: To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Business Partners) There are different ways to manage all the business partners and to set filters. To search for a specific business partner, you can use the filter bar in the header. The system also displays preconfigured worklists (To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted,  Note You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. The file size of each business partners Excel cannot be larger than 2MB, and the maximum number of rows in each file is 5000. A digital freight forwarder is managed as a business partner in both the SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP Transportation Management system. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Rejected) based on the business partner's invitation response status. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for business partners. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. To Be Submitted The To Be Submitted worklist displays all the business partners that you have uploaded or added in the app but have not yet submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitations. This worklist also displays connection invitations that have been rejected. The worklist displays the following details for each invitation: System ID Business Partner ID Invitee Company Role SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Phone number Email Language City Country/Region Zip code Status  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed.  Note A rejected invitation is displayed on the To Be Submitted worklist with the status "Returned by LBN OPS team" if it was submitted via the Invite Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- In Progress The In Progress worklist displays all the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team to manage the connection invitations. These business partners have not yet responded to your invitation to connect with your network. You can recall your invitation in this worklist if needed. The In Progress worklist has the same columns as the To Be Submitted worklist. Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the business partners who have accepted your invitation to join your business network. You can select one or more business partners in the Accepted tab and download them in Microsoft Excel format. The Accepted worklist has the same columns as the In Progress worklist along with the unique LBN ID of the business partner. Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the business partners who have rejected your invitation to join your business network via Discover Business Partners. The Rejected worklist has the same columns as the Accepted worklist. Using the settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected tabs. You can also sort and filter the business partners in these worklists based on various attributes. Add New Business Partners You can add new business partners to the Invite Business Partners app in one of the following ways: Manual entry On the To Be Submitted tab, you can manually add a new network data contributor to the Invite Business Partners app by choosing Add Invitee. Using this method, you can specify the language of your connection invitations. Supported languages are: English Arabic Bulgarian Chinese Simplified Chinese Traditional Croatian Czech Danish A rejected invitation is displayed on the Rejected worklist if it was submitted via the Discover Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Dutch Finnish French German Greek Hebrew Hungarian Italian Japanese Korean Malay Norwegian Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Romanian Russian Serbian Slovak Spanish Swedish Thai Turkish Manual entry with an Excel template You can download the Excel template available in the Invite Business Partners app by choosing the Download Excel Template button. You can fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload this template back in the Invite Business Partners app. Downloading business partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system You can download the list of business partners in your SAP TM system and upload the Excel file in the Invite Business Partners app. For more information, see Download Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management System.  Note When you upload a business partner Excel in the Invite Business Partners app, the system automatically filters out the erroneous business partner records and selects only the correct business partner records. For example, in the downloaded Excel file, if there are business partners that already exist in the Invite Business Partners app with the status as In Progress, Accepted or Rejected, or if some of the entries do not contain any of the mandatory fields, the system ignores such entries and uploads all the other entries. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- You can select one or more business partners in the To Be Submitted worklist and delete them from the Invite Business Partners app. Note that you cannot delete the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. Connection Invitations Once you have a list of business partners added to the Invite Business Partners app, you can select one or more partners from the To Be Submitted worklist and choose Submit. Once you choose Submit, the system instantaneously sends a request to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. The system moves the submitted business partners to the In Progress worklist. Solution owners in both production and test environments can use the Invite Business Partners app to send connection invitations to business partners. If the invitees are not yet on the network, they can activate their accounts via a simplified account activation process and collaborate with the inviter in the respective environment (either production or test). You can refer your invitees to the following resource for their account activation: Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process. Note that business partners need your contact information when you send them an invitation to join your business network. If you have not maintained a default address in the Manage Business Profile app, the system does not allow you to submit business partners. For more information on adding a default address, see Edit Company Profile. The back-end team sends an invitation to the business partners requesting them to connect with your network. The business partner can view this connection invitation using the Manage Invitations app and choose to accept or reject the invitation. For more information, see Manage Invitations. When the business partner accepts or rejects an invitation, you will be notified of the same and the system moves the business partner to the accepted or rejected worklist as appropriate. If a partner accepts your invitation, the partner connects with your network and you can perform business transactions with this partner. If a business partner rejects your invitation, the partner is not connected with your network and you cannot perform any business transactions with this partner. You can find the rejected invitation from the To Be Submitted worklist and resend it if you want to. The system updates the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted your connection invitation. You can view this LBN ID in the Accepted worklist for each business partner. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can update these LBN IDs of business partners in SAP TM system by downloading the business partner list from the Invite Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). Recall Invitations You can recall a submitted invitation as long as its status remains "In Progress". When you upload a business partner Excel, the system performs a validation. If there are no validation errors, the business partner Excel is uploaded. If there are validation errors, the system displays the erroneous entries in an error log. The system allows you to download this error log. You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 45 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- To recall the invitation, switch to the In Progress worklist, click to open the invitation that you want to recall, and then choose Recall on the details page. After being recalled, the invitation returns to the To Be Submitted worklist and becomes editable. The business partner cannot view the recalled invitation using the app until you submit it again. Downloading Business Partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can download the business partners from the SAP TM system and upload them to the Invite Business Partners app. Context In SAP TM system, you must perform the following steps to download the business partner Excel: Procedure 1. Execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_CARR_LIST_DWNLD in transaction SE38. 2. Enter your SAP TM organization ID in the Organizational ID field and execute. The system determines the hierarchy of this organization and retrieves all the freight agreements that are valid at the time of searching. The system then determines the valid business partners from these agreements. Note that if you select the Show Application Log checkbox, the system displays the detailed information about the business partner determination process. 3. Alternatively, instead of entering an organization ID and retrieving multiple business partners, you can also enter the business partner IDs in the Carrier IDs field and execute. The system retrieves the details of all the business partners that you have entered. 4. Select all the business partners that you want to download and then choose Download. The system downloads the Excel file. Next Steps Once you download the Excel file, in the Invite Business Partners app, choose the Upload Business Partners button to upload this Excel. Once you upload the Excel file with a list of partners, the system updates the To Be Submitted worklist in the app with the partner details in the Excel. Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM)  Note You can't recall an invitation when its status is "Invitation email sent to business partner".  Note System IDs may consist of alphanumerical characters and the underscore ( _ ) character. You can check the Specification tab of the Excel for further guidance. The system checks all records when you upload your Excel, and displays the errors on the Upload Business Partners screen. You can correct the errors in your Excel and upload it again. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You can update the SAP TM system with the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted to connect with your business network. Context To do so, you must perform the following: Procedure 1. Download the list of business partners with their LBN IDs from the Accepted worklist in the Invite Business Partners app. The system downloads the list of partners in a CSV format. 2. In the SAP TM system, execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_ID_BP_UPD in transaction SA38. 3. Browse for the CSV file that you have downloaded and upload the file. The system updates the business partner IDs for the partners in the system. Note that you can choose whether you want the system to process the upload job in the background or foreground. If you choose to process the upload job in the foreground, the system displays the error logs if there are any. Assign Technical User Roles to Data Contributor's Technical User Prerequisites You must have the administrator role for your subaccount on SAP BTP. Context If you are using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your connected data contributor will send you the email address of its technical user after accepting your connection request. You need to grant the technical user the technical user roles. This needs to be performed for each data contributor that's connected with you. Procedure 1. Go to your subaccount in the SAP BTP cockpit. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Role Collections under Security. 3. Choose the technical user role collection (you've created it in the task Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users). 4. Go to the Users section and choose Edit. 5. Enter the email address of the technical user and select Default identity provider. 6. Save your changes. Related Information Assign Users to Role Collection  Note Make sure the role collection contains all the technical user roles as listed in Available Roles for Solution Owners. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 47 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- System Connections (Solution Owner) Use the System Connections app for solution owners to create a connection and to authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA. You can use the app in combination with each of the following exchange infrastructures between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system: SAP Cloud Integration SAP Process Integration Direct integration using SOA Manager The process of using the System Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Creating a Connection. 2. Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. Activating the Connection. Configurations for Location Replication To replicate locations, you need to do some configurations first before using the System Connections app. Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF) Context You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data, which was manually copied or replicated from SAP S/4HANA or created from new using the app. Location master data can then be used by the System Connections app in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Master Data Replication in the Source System To set up master data replication, you must configure the replication of master data via the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S/4HANA source system. DRF uses SOAP service - LocationBulkReplicationRequest to replicate location master data from the source system to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. Define the business system for the SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant to which you want to replicate business partners. a. In the source system, go to Customizing for Data Replication using transaction DRFIMG. b. Go to Define Custom Settings for Data Replication Define Technical Settings Define Technical Settings for Business Systems . 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- c. There are two ways of making the location replication configuration: i. Create a business system using your LBN ID and Logical System ID as values. Concatenate LBN ID and the Logical System ID with delimiter “##”. For example, 100000000001##SYSCLNT001. ii. Follow the steps below: 1. Ensure that you are using a Cross Customising Client and run transaction drfimg. 2. Navigate to Data Replication > Define Custom Settings for Data Replication > Define Technical Settings > BAdI Determination of Local System Name. Execute this BAdI. 3. Provide a Z BAdI for Enhancement Implementation and fill other required information to create a BAdI. 4. Create a new BAdI implementation with BAdI definition as MDG_IDM_GET_LCL_SYSTEM and select Copy Sample Class. Ensure that the Active checkbox is selected. d. Select the newly created business system and navigate to Define Bus. System, BOs in the dialog structure. e. Enter 189 as the BO type and Location as the description. f. Enter 189 as the BO type and Location as the description. g. Create a new communication channel called Replication via Services.  Note Once these configurations are made, it would be applicable for all data replication settings via DRF. The logical system would be used in all these settings.  Note The logical system ID you entered here (string after the delimiter “##”) will also be used if you manually create individual location records in the Manage Locations app at a later time. For more information, see Creating a Location.  Sample Code METHOD IF_MDG_IDM_GET_LCL_SYSTEM~GET_LOCAL_SYSTEM. *! This method determines the local business system via the ALE logical system assigned to * If no business system is maintained, it returns an empty value. DATA: lv_own_logical_system TYPE logsys, ls_bs_tech TYPE mdg_s_bus_sys_tech, lv_not_found TYPE boole_d. CALL FUNCTION 'OWN_LOGICAL_SYSTEM_GET' IMPORTING own_logical_system = lv_own_logical_system EXCEPTIONS own_logical_system_not_defined = 1 OTHERS = 2. ev_local_system = lv_own_logical_system. ENDMETHOD.  Note Do not select the Disabled for Replication checkbox. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 49 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 2. Define a replication model by giving it a name and a description. a. Go to Define Custom Settings for Data Replication Define Replication Models . b. Create a replication model. c. Select the newly created replication model and choose Assign Outbound Implementation. d. Select the outbound implementation 189_1 and choose Assign Target Systems for Repl. Model / Outb. Impl to assign the target system (identified by its LBN ID – as maintained in the business system) to the outbound implementation. e. Optional: If you only want to replicate one default language description, select the outbound implementation and navigate to Assign Language. f. Choose Activate. 3. Optional: Set up filter object criteria. a. On the SAP Easy Access screen, choose Cross-Application Components Processes and Tools for Enterprise Applications Master Data Governance Data Replication Define Filter Criteria (transaction DRFF). b. In the worklist, search for the replication model name you have created in step 2, and define the filter criteria for including or excluding business objects. 4. Trigger replication. a. Go to transaction DRFOUT (Execute Data Replication). b. Select the newly created replication model and select the following settings under Replication Mode: To send an update of all locations, select Initialization. To send the lasted changed location, select Changes. If you have defined your own filter criteria, select Manual. The manual replication will either be based on the filter criteria defined in step 3, or be based on the filter that you manually maintained in the DRFOUT transaction. For more information, see SAP Note 3688060 . As part of our ongoing commitment to security and trust, SAP is updating the root Certificate Authority (CA). This update supports the broader adoption of our fifth-generation (G5) root CA and allows additional time for its inclusion in major browser 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 50 This is custom documentation. This change could impact B2B Connectivity: The sender systems must trust both the old root certificate ( DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate ( DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the inbound communication to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. For information about a possible impact on the end user UI, see Browser Support. Resolution for B2B Connectivity to BN4L: Case 1: When sender system is S/4HANA (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Upload this Root Certificate to all relevant SSL Client PSEs*. 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 3238733 - How to Import a Certificate Into a STRUST PSE's Certificate List In a NetWeaver AS ABAP. 4. [DigiCert Global Root G2] should remain as is. 5. ICM restart should be necessary post change in STRUST, only if you are running old releases of Netweaver 700/701 and 64x. See SAP KBA 2746647 - SSSLERR_PEER_CERT_UNTRUSTED after importing the target certificate. Since Netweaver AS ABAP 710 and AS ABAP 702, ICM restart is no longer necessary. Case 2: When sender system is SAP NetWeaver PI (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to TrustedCAs view of NetWeaver Java Key Storage. 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 2056672 - How to import server certificates in PI system. Case 3: When WebDispatcher is placed in front of Cloud Integration endpoint 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to Trusted Certificates through Web Administration Interface of SAP WebDispatcher. 3. See SAP Help - PSE Management in Web Administration Interface of SAP Web Dispatcher, section [Trusted Certificates]. Case 4: When sender system is a non-SAP service/software 1. Consult your vendor for confirmation that it should trust [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] for outbound TLS communication. 2. Particularly, in case of a customer written Java program, JDK version should be higher than the following: SAP JVM 8.1.097 SapMachine 11.0.22 SapMachine 17.0.10 SapMachine 21.0.2 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Oracle JDK 8u401 Oracle JDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 21.0.2 For more information, see the following SAP Notes: 3688060 3587968 3566727 3472211 Connecting Directly Between SAP Business Network for Logistics and Your SAP Backend System Perform the following steps: 1. Configuring Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics 2. Configuring in SAP Backend Systems via SOA Manager 3. Activate the connection in SAP Business Network for Logistics. (Refer to the document Activating the Connection.) Generally, you use a service user or RFC user to communicate with the SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system. This user processes the incoming B2B messages and must have the following authorization objects so that they can create or update the correct documents in the external system: In SAP TM, the user must have the authorization objects T_ADMIN and T_TM_ALL. In SAP S/4HANA, the user must have the authorization objects T_ADMIN, T_TOR_EXE and S_SERVICE. For more details, refer to the following SAP Note: 2890717 . Manage Alternate IDs (Solution Owner) You can maintain alternate identifiers of your other accounts in the network. These identifiers shall be used in specific integration scenarios or in specific transaction flows in the network. Additionally, the LBN ID of your tenant can be seen above the Manage Alternate IDs table as a read-only field. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following alternate identifiers (alternate IDs): DUNS ID (Data Universal Numbering System ID) SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Registration Number USDOT (US Department of Transportation) MC Number (Motor Carrier Number) Others GLN (Global Location Number) Technical User To create your own alternate IDs, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select an alternate ID type from the dropdown menu and type in the required value. 3. Choose OK. You can also delete or change existing entries. Configure Partner Connections You can use the Configure Partner Connections app to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners. Network partners will have many business partners in their network and have built integrations to business partner systems. Status: Active Enable EDIFACT IFTSTA for Event Tracking The message type EDIFACT IFTSTA supports both inquiries of shipment status and responses for consignment status, making it suitable for use in both inbound and outbound connections. This message type can be leveraged to track the following business events in the global track and trace solution: Code Code Description DEPARTURE Departure UNLOAD_END Unloading End ARRIV_DEST Arrival OUT_FOR_DELIVERY Out for Delivery LOAD_END Loading End DELAYED Delay Configuration The GLNID is crucial for identifying both parties in IFTSTA communication. To set up EDIFACT integration for the IFTSTA message type, this identifier for both parties must be consistently maintained in the following apps: Configure Partner Connections  Note For road FTL tracking, you can also choose other Business Partner ID types listed in Create Partner Connection, depending on the requirements of your carrier or visibility providers. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 76 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- System Connections Maintaining GLNIDs as Customer Headers in Configure Partner Connections Solution owners must maintain their GLNID and that of their data contributors. Use customer headers in the Configure Partner Connections app for this purpose. To maintain GLNIDs in Configure Partner Connections, follow these steps: 1. Open the partner connection in which you want to enable the EDIFACT IFTSTA message type. 2. Scroll down to the Custom Headers section and click the plus sign. 3. Enter SHIPPER_GLNID as the key and enter your GLNID as the value. 4. Enter CARRIER_GLNID as the key and enter the GLNID of the data contributor you work with as the value. 5. Save your changes. 6. Repeat these steps if you want to enable EDIFACT IFTSTA in other partner connections. Maintaining GLNIDs as Alternative Identifiers in System Connections Both solution owners and data contributors must maintain their GLNID in the System Connections app. To maintain GLNIDs in System Connections, follow these steps: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select GLN from the dropdown menu and enter your GLNID. 3. Choose OK. Limitations In an inbound connection, if RFF+ZZ8 (stopId) is not provided, the stopId is converted to an empty string, instead of NULL. If an EDI file contains more than one event types, multiple messages with the same message number are sent to the global track and trace solution. The address name field of a location is not supported in an IFTSTA message. UNLOCODE and IATACODE are not supported in an IFTSTA message. A delay event can only refer to an arrival or departure event, and no event reason code is available in the delay event. More information You can refer your data contributors to this implementation guide for B2B IFTSTA integration: https://help.sap.com/doc/df3dd1c3edd44250b0c27c9c71159459/LBN/en-US/SAP_LBN_EDI_HowToGuide_GTT.pdf For detailed information about the IFTSTA messages used in the global track and trace solution, see the following Message Implementation Guide: https://help.sap.com/doc/9cc21c6fda37437eaee763d114d5bbfe/LBN/en-US/SAP_LBN_IFTSTA_D01C_GTT.pdf 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 77 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Manage Notification Templates The Manage Notification Templates app enables you to create and maintain email notification templates that you can use to notify your business partner on the occurrence of an event. This app enables you to create a customized notification template and maintain language specific notification email texts for this template. You can also specify the recipients of these emails in these templates. Creation of a Notification Template To create a notification template, perform the following: 1. Choose Create. The Create Notification Template dialog box appears. 2. Enter a template ID and template description. 3. Select the Global Track and Trace application and choose OK. The system creates the template. When you select this template, you can view and maintain the email templates in different languages. You can use the Delete button to delete one or more templates. Note that you must set one of the templates as default and the default template cannot be deleted. To maintain email templates in different languages you must select the notification template, perform the following: 1. Choose Add. The Add Language dialog box appears. 2. Select a language from the drop-down menu. 3. Enter a value from the Insert Placeholder button. Note that when you choose this button, the system displays a list of placeholders. Choose the appropriate placeholder for the email contacts. 4. Choose OK. A new window appears. 5. Enter an email subject and email body in the respective fields. Note that you can also enter a value from the Insert Placeholder button. When you choose this button, the system displays a list of placeholders. Choose the appropriate placeholder. 6. Choose Save. The system saves the language specific email template text. Similarly, you can add multiple language email template texts to a template. Note that the system sets the first language template that you create as the default template. Once you create two or more language templates, you select a template and use the Set As Default button to choose a different default template. Manage Locations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 78 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see Configurations for Location Replication. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Viewing a Location To view a location, proceed as follows: 1. By default, you can use the following fields to filter locations: External ID Source System Object Type Description Country/Region City Data Processing Status Additional Information You can also adjust the filter bar by chooosing Adapt Filters. 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. The detail view of the location consists of a header and other sections.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 79 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. This includes the business purposes, the longitude/latitude coordinates, and the revision history. Geographical Coordinates and Map This section displays the geographical coordinates of the location. It also identifies the location on the map. Alternative Location IDs This section displays a list of type-specific alternative IDs of the location. Contact Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. Additional Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. More Information You can do the following with the filter bar: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for locations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens.  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 80 This is custom documentation. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. If you are importing a location from SAP Transportation Management (TM), set the Source System to the business system name of your TM system and set the External ID to the location ID in TM. For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. This is a mandatory field if you want to use the location in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. The logical system ID you enter here must be the same one that you used when configuring the replication of location master data via the Data Replication Framework. For more information, see Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF). Make sure you enter the logical system ID correctly so that it matches the source system of the location. Otherwise, there can be duplicate records in your location master data. Upload Locations You can fill the details of locations using an Excel template and then upload this template back to the app. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Choose Upload to open the Upload Locations page. 2. Click Upload on the up-right corner, then download the Excel template available by choosing Download Excel Template. 3. Fill the details of the locations you want to upload in the template. 4. In Choose File, locate the modified Excel template and then choose Upload. Editing a Location To edit a location, proceed as follows: 1. Use the following fields to filter locations: Location ID Description Location Type Country/Region City 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. 3. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner of the details page. Enable Risk Monitoring If you have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections, you can determine whether or not to use the service provider to monitor risks at a certain location in Manage Locations.  Note You can enter the geographical coordinates for the location records in the Longitude and Latitude columns manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you upload your file. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location records you are uploading is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo- coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 83 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Prerequisites You have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. Procedure To enable risk monitoring for a specific location, follow these steps: 1. Click the location record for which you want to monitor risks to open its details page. 2. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner. 3. Click to select the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox and then choose Save. Alternatively, you can enable risk monitoring for multiple locations at once. To do this, select the location records, and then choose Risk Monitoring Enable . Results The risk monitoring service provider starts monitoring risks at the location. If you’ve subscribed for the intelligent insights add-on, you can view the risk information on each target location in the Logistics Execution Insights app. To notify the service provider to stop monitoring risks at a location, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in the corresponding location record. To stop using the risk monitoring feature for all locations in your supply chain, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in each location record where you previously enabled the feature in Manage Locations and then deactivate the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. More Information Editing a Location Creating a Location Manage Custom Codes You can use the manage custom codes feature to extend the drop-down list for the following fields: Country/Region State Location Type Risk information is not displayed in Manage Locations. Instead, it’s displayed on the map view of the Logistics Execution Insights app. You use Manage Locations to specify a group of target locations where you want to monitor risks.  Note You can also configure this setting when creating a new location record. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 84 This is custom documentation. For example, you do not find the region code you need in the drop-down list of Country/Region. To create a custom code, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Manage Custom Codes button. 2. On the Manage Custom Codes page, select the field for which you want to extend the list, and then choose Create. 3. Specify the name, language, and description of the code, and then choose Save. Results After you create a custom code, you can find it from the Custom category when you expand the corresponding drop-down list. If needed, you can also remove it or edit its description on the Manage Custom Codes page. Global settings for Geo-Coordinates You can use Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box to define how the system handles geo- coordinates for all location records. In Generate geo-coordinates automatically, you have the following options: Off (Default): Do not generate geo-coordinates automatically even if they are missing. Generate: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. (Applies to all locations including the existing ones) Overwrite: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when coordinates are missing or overwrite them if they already exist. (Applies to locations created after you enable this option) Archiving Locations If you have location records that are no longer used regularly, you can archive these records for future reference or regulatory compliance.  Note Options in Generate geo-coordinates automatically only take effect for location records where you leave Calibrate coordinates when saving with the default option Apply global settings. The Calibrate coordinates when saving setting in location records takes precedence over Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box. For example, when you set Calibrate coordinates when saving to No in a location record, the system does not generate or calibrate coordinates for the record even if Generate geo-coordinates automatically is set to Generate or Overwrite.  Note To archive locations, you must have the LocationArchiveTemplate role. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 85 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- To archive location records, select the records you want to archive on the Locations list and then choose Archive. You can view the locations you’ve archived on the Archived Locations list by choosing Archived Items at the up-right corner. To restore archived location records, select the records you want to restore on the Archived Locations list, and then choose Restore. You can view the restored locations after you switch to the standard Locations list. Define Additional Information The Additional Information section contains a list of additional information associated to a location record. This section enables you to define necessary custom characteristics or references by adding your information items. An information item comprises a name, the type of the item, and the corresponding value. Type: Type of the additional information item. It can be either Text or Alternative ID. Name: Name of the additional information item. If you set Type to Alternative ID, the name of the item must be set to one of the following values: GLN DUNS UN/LOCODE IATA Airport Code Value: Value that corresponds to this additional information item. If you have a location that contains multiple ports or airports, you can maintain multiple UN/LOCODEs and IATA Airport Codes for this location in this section. But to ensure that the actual event matches with the correct planned/unplanned event, be aware of the following event match rules: For planned events, when multiple location records are found with the same UN/LOCODE or IATA Airport Code, the system will match the actual event with the planned event that has the same location alternative key. For unplanned events, the UN/LOCODE or IATA Airport Code maintained in the Alternative Location IDs section of the Manage Locations app is superior to the one maintained in the Additional Information section. For example, when two location records (A and B) are found with the same UN/LOCODE, but the UN/LOCODE in Location A is maintained in the Alternative Location IDs section and the UN/LOCODE in Location B is maintained in the Additional Information section, the system will take Location A as the superior one, and match the actual event with the unplanned event that has Location A. Discover Business Partners Finding the right business partners is always a challenge. However, this will be easier once your partners-to-be have joined SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a simple yet powerful app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, Discover Business Partners helps you search the network for logistics service providers, then from the results, invite suitable ones to be your business partners. Search for Business Partners 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 86 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- To search for business partners on the network, enter a key word, for example the company name, in the search box and then press Enter . You can also use faceted search on the left pane to narrow down your search results. When using faceted search, you can even leave the search box empty. This is useful if you want to explore your potential partners in a specific region or industry. Result A set of matched results are returned. You can click to open the details page of a matched result. Send Request for Connection To send a request for connection to your potential business partners, proceed as follows: 1. Click to select the company to which you want to send the request for connection from the Matched Results table. 2. Choose Request for Connection. The request for connection is sent to the selected companies. Results A request for connection is sent to the selected company. Once the company accepts your request, you will become business partners. After you’ve set up a partnership with a business partner via this app, you must update the business partner’s LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). To do this, see Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID. References Manage Business Profile Manage Invitations Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID To update the LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) for a logistics service provider who’s become your business partner, proceed as follows in SAP TM: 1. Go to the Manage Business Partner transaction (transaction BP). 2. Set the filter criteria to find the business partner for which you want to update the LBN ID and then double-click the business partner to open its Display Organization page. 3. Navigate to the Identification tab. In the Identification Numbers section, IDType field, enter LBN001. 4. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: SAP Business Network for Logistics- Best Practice This site is dedicated to collecting all best practices for SAP Business Network for Logistics.  Pre-Implementation Think about the solution as a whole rather than focusing on BN4L only. A back-end system (e.g. TM, S/4Hana, EWM, YL etc.) is a leading system that determines how various logistics processes, data flow and collaboration with trading partners via BN4L will look like. Build all these scenarios coming from the back-end system into the BN4L and not vice versa. Review Activate Road Map Viewer to get familiar with SAP Activate phases that provide clear guidance at every step of the implementation journey. Consider customer’s existing and future processes in their back-end system as well as back-end limitations and compatibility with BN4L. Review Tips and Tricks blog and this document with best practices prior the implementation. Telling the narrative from BN4L point of view quite often doesn't reflect the reality of projects where BN4L is implemented as it doesn’t reflect needs and scenarios of customer’s back-end. Supply Chain Logistics Maturity Model introduces a structured framework developed by SAP to help logistics leaders assess and improve their supply chain operations. This resource can be leveraged by our customers ahead of their IT transformation initiatives to assess their current maturity level and define strategic next steps.  Shipper Onboarding Shipper onboarding includes initial configuration of global BTP account which includes subaccounts creation and subscription to applications for BN4L, user management or establishing trust between subaccounts and Identity Authentication tenant. FC, GTT External  Network Partners There are two types of network partners that SAP collaborate with within BN4L solution. Tracking Collaboration Integrate with SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) for event reporting purpose. LSPs / carriers onboarded to this type of network partners are able to share tracking information and report events to customers through BN4L. Visibility service providers / visibility data aggregators Transacting Collaboration Integrate with SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) for transacting purpose. SAP Business Network for Logistics: Get your first, API integrated example from Shipper in 3 steps Saif Product and Topic Expert 2023 Aug 29 11:51 PM 15 Likes  6,668 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Getting started with Carrier API Integration in 3 simple steps The SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration solution connects shippers and their logistics partners on a secure network for optimized collaboration and insights, integrated tightly with core business processes for efficiency and resilience. More details can be found here. Carrier Integration involves 3 key entities/systems. S/4HANA Transportation Management system - owned by Shipper. SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) - Both Shipper and Carrier are part of this. Carrier / Network Partner's system - owned by Carriers or Network partners.   -- 1 of 7 -- As shown above, there are 2 integration patterns: Outbound from TM & SAP BN4L: Whenever there is a change or a business event in TM, it triggers the call to SAP BN4L which then routes it to a specific carrier webhook based on the configuration. Inbound into TM & SAP BN4L: This is triggered by Carriers or Network Partners when they call SAP BN4L's APIs. Note: SAP BN4L also supports EDI in addition to API and also a Web portal Interface. In this post, we will focus on the first pattern of receiving orders from a Shipper. 1. Preparing webhook - by Carrier As seen above, in order for carriers to receive the business events/changes, a webhook is required to be hosted by carriers and configured in BN4L. There are many platforms such as pipedream, webhook.site, Postman, Make, SAP's Integration Suite or even a simple nodejs application hosting a webhook on Business Technology platform (BTP). While there are a number of ways listed below to create a webhook, the intent of this blog is to give a quick turnaround for carriers to receive examples and messages from SAP BN4L to build the integration. For simplicity's sake, I use an iPaas provider pipedream. This is easy and convenient to create a webhook to test the end-end integration. -- 2 of 7 -- 2. Configure System Connections - by Carrier Pre-requisite: SAP BN4L provides a portal for carriers, which carriers receive access to once ordered via sapstore. The process is explained here. Carrier user will need the necessary authorization to be able to access and manage connections in the portal. Make sure you also enable Inbound communication. Make sure you have accepted the invitation from the Shipper. -- 3 of 7 -- Access the System Connections app and configure the webhook that you created in the previous step for the scenario that you wish to test. In the case below, I chose the "Freight Subcontracting All" option as an example. -- 4 of 7 -- 3. Configure Partner Connections - by Shipper Once you are done with Step 2, contact your shipper to configure the connection to your configured webhook. Pre-requisite: Shipper has access to SAP BN4L and has onboarded with one of the scenarios described. Shipper user has relevant roles to access "Configure Partner Connections" and ""app. Shipper sends an invite to the carrier and makes sure the tenants are connected. Shipper accesses the "Configure Partner Connections" app and establishes a connection with the scenario endpoint configured by carrier in their tenant in step 2 and also activates the connection. -- 5 of 7 -- Note: You can repeat steps 2 and 3 for other scenarios and operations. That's it..!! Ask your Shipper to send some test orders and voilà! you will receive the orders to the configured webhook. You can also access the "Manage Integration Logs" application to monitor the integration and also access the payload. Conclusion While the above may not be a productive setup, it allows the participants of the network(Shippers-Carriers/ Network Partners) to quickly understand the behavior of the system and enables you to develop and validate against production-like orders from your shippers in a very short time. -- 6 of 7 -- Comments For further questions and feedback related to the blog, please check the Q&A area and feel free to post your questions in the link with the tag SAP Business Network for Logistics.
