file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 1 INTERNAL ONLY SCC / Indirect Cross Training Purchase Order Collaboration -- 1 of 10 -- 2 Agenda 01 Purchase Order Collaboration 02 03 04 Practical Exam Scenarios Order Confirmation & Ship Notice Goods Receipt & Invoice -- 2 of 10 -- 3 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration Overview Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice Today we will be focusing on the SCC Process Purchase Order Collaboration. o PO Collaboration’s core function is facilitating the Buyer and Supplier’s Ordering, Shipment and Invoicing of Direct Materials required for their Supply Chain. This includes raw materials, finished goods, spare parts or components. o Normally PO Collaboration is not the only SCC process the Buyer would have in scope and is often used in combination with other SCC Process integral to the Buyer’s own Supply Chain. o It also provides a great starting point for Supplier Integration Specialists as it’s familiar in the sense of documents you may have worked with previously, but also extents it’s functionally and use of cXML elements to meet industry specific requirements within Supply Chain. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration Overview -- 4 of 10 -- 5 SCC Process Overview Consignment Collaboration In consignment collaboration, the supplier sends consignments to the buyer, but retains ownership of the consignments until the buyer pays for the assignment the buyer consumes. The transfer of ownership, and often of location, to the buyer at the time of consumption is called a consignment movement. The consignment movement information flows from Buyer to Supplier. Subcontract Collaboration This solution supports the following features for subcontract purchase orders and their associated documents, which are used in contract manufacturing collaboration. Forecast Collaboration Forecast collaboration allows buyers to send forecasts of future procurement to suppliers. Suppliers can send commitments to buyers based on forecast demand. Quality Collaboration Quality inspection collaboration supports buyer inspections of supplier facilities. Supplier Managed Inventory (SMI) This module provides suppliers with visibility into the buyer's inventory and demand levels so that they can replenish inventory based on established minimum and maximum stock levels. Schedule Agreement Collaboration Form of an outline agreement to procure items on predetermined dates according to an aligned Schedule. Returns Collaboration The returns process deals with the business process of returning goods to the Supplier. It also deals with receiving credit for the returned items. Material Traceability Capture complete material provenance from raw material to finished product to enhance safety, sustainability, and customer loyalty. Please note: Not a process for Supplier Integration but adds to the importance of correct Batch Information on Orders / Ship Notices. Supply Chain Collaboration Solutions Glossary A Supply Chain in the context of Buyers and Suppliers is the structured flow of materials, information, and commitments that allows suppliers to deliver goods, and Buyers to convert those inputs into finished offerings. This can be anything from; Electronics, Cars, Medicine, Food or Appliances. These are all industries that currently transact via SAP Business Network SCC. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration + Other SCC Processes Purchase Order Order Confirmation Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice o Please remember that when other SCC Processes are also in scope, the Purchase Order is often not the start of the procurement flow and other documents may be transacted (Integrated or Portal) before the PO even is sent to the Supplier. o A good example is the combination of Forecast Collaboration and Purchase Order Collaboration where the Forecasting of order quantity is completed before the PO is sent to the Supplier. This forecasting can either be integrated or completed via the Portal by Suppliers. o This is not limited to Forecast Collaboration and applies to all other SCC process that the Buyer may have in scope. Forecast Collaboration PO Collaboration Forecast Forecast Commit -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Purchase Order – Direct Materials -- 7 of 10 -- 8 Purchase Order Types – Quick Glance SCC Processes Purchase Order Type Comments Purchase Order Collaboration Direct Materials Purchase Order Ordering of direct materials based on the Material Master from the Buyer’s ERP. Subcontracting Collaboration Subcontract Purchase Order An order that contains Component Information for a Subtracting Supplier to create and/or finish the goods with. Consignment Collaboration Consignment Purchase Order Order of Consignment materials that are only purchased at time of movement / use. Returns Collaboration Returns Purchase Order Materials that are to be returned due to warranty or failed inspection. Schedule Agreement Collaboration Schedule Agreement / Schedule Agreement Release (JIT & Forecast) Order that’s based on a contractual agreement that outlines the frequency of deliveries. Service Process Service Orders Service Order for both planned and unplanned services. Indirect Processes Purchase Order Type Comments Buying and Invoicing Catalog Order, Free Text Order, Blanket PO Catalog Order based off Supplier Punchout or CIF. Not a part of SCC. Commerce Automation Catalog Order, Free Text Order, Blanket PO Not a part of SCC. Despite the overarching name, the use, information, and structure that defines the Purchase Order differs greatly per the process it’s a part of. Requirements that applies to the PO within the PO Collaboration may not be applicable to other processes. All POs within SCC are generated by the Buyer’s ERP. Please note: The below are just examples of the PO types only and is not representative of full SCC process. Please refer to appendix 2.a for a full overview of processes and documents. -- 8 of 10 -- 9 Supply Chain Terminology for PO Collaboration Term Explanation Material ID The material that is being procured by the Buyer from the Supplier. The material may be the stock / items required for the buyer’s production line, or the end-product itself. Normally this the Buyer PartID on the PO and used as the main identifier. It’s not common for the Supplier PartID to be maintained as well, only in specific cases. Production Plants, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store. Depending on the Buyer, ShipTo locations to them could mean a Production Plant, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store Front Location and would generally differ depending on the industry. • Some Buyer’s may have a combination of Production plants, warehouse and distribution centers that suppliers need to shipTo. • Production Plants should be treated as small entities within an organization. It’s common that a Buyer’s Production plant will have different requirements and processes in scope. For example: • Buyer Plant A: could be using Purchase Orders Collaboration as they just needs material parts for Repairs. • Buyer Plant B: could be using both SCC Processes Schedule Agreements and Purchase Orders as the plant is dedicated to mass production of the end product. Material requirements planning (MRP) Material requirements planning (MRP) is a software-based integrated inventory and supply management system designed for businesses. Companies use MRP to estimate raw material needs, manage inventory, and plan production and deliveries. This terminology is not specific to SAP Business Network SCC, but is general terminology used by Buyer’s that are experienced with Direct Materials Supply Chain. -- 9 of 10 -- 10 Purchase Order - Some differences, a quick glance Indirect SCC Buyer Part ID Usually optional. Mostly Supplier Part Ids are used. Free text Pos are also possible. Used by Buyer and supplier as main identifier of the materials. Data alignment of materials in scope are integral to the integration connection. Bill To , Ship To and Storage Locations Usually the buyer locations are head quarters / offices or delivery is indicted directly to the employee Each Buyer location has a unique identification code at the plant / shipTo level. For large plants or warehouses, the shipTo location may have designated locations where the Supplier / Carrier must deliver to once at the plant / warehouse location. For example; an order of vaccines can only be delivered to storage location “A” as it’s medical related. Batch Ids Not commonly utilized Used to identify specific production lots Revisions and Drawing numbers Not commonly utilized Used to identify different versions of product specifications Schedule Lines Not used. Usually the parent PO line is used. The PO Line is the parent of the Schedule lines. Used by Buyers to specify a schedule of deliveries for the PO line Quantity. Control Keys Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules Tolerances ( as per control keys ) date and quantity Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Used all the time In general for Supply Chain Collaboration, requirements are defined at either a material or plant level by the Buyer within their ERP. These requirements are shared with the Supplier using Purchase Order Control keys and Tolerances, when sent on the PO these supersede the Supplier level transaction rules. This allows Buyers the capability configure their requirements at either a material or plant level, which is extremally important for large or global organizations where these requirements will often differ throughout their various business entities, Supply Chain process, locations, material and vendors. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 11 SCC Specific Considerations on the Purchase Order SCC Flow Material / Plant Specific Revision ID Provides and indicator for both buyers and supplier to help identify the part version needing to be produced. New revisions may have accompanying design specifications sent as an attachment on the Purchase Order. Material Specific Control Keys Document Instructions and tolerances supersede what is defined at the supplier group level. Control keys and tolerances are defined by the Buyer’s ERP and would need to be altered in the Buyer’s system there if there are conflicting keys or tolerances set for the OC or ASN as it’s overriding all respective transactional rules in the network. Yes Purchase Order Schedule Lines PO line is the Parent of the Schedule Lines, you can have multiples schedule lines on one PO Line. This provides a delivery schedule that the supplier would need to adhere to when supplying the requested goods. The OC confirming the Delivery date would need to include each of the scheduled lines for PO Line 10. Normally the ASN Shipments would be as per Schedule Line requested Quantity and DeliveryDate. Please Note the Schedule Line: Date&Time Timestamp, Quantity and UOM must match exactly when it's returned on the Order Confirmation. Schedule Line reference requirement is determined by Supplier Transactional rules. Yes Handling Unit Flag PO Flag that specifies if Handling Unit Information is Required on the ASN for this specific material. This is a material level flag and may not apply to all materials within the supplier's scope. The material Master Data must be aligned between the Buyer and Supplier as this requirement could also differ between Buyer plant / locations as well. Yes Quality Process Flag Certain Materials require additional certification documentation or must follow an additional quality process flow. Commonly this in the form of a PDF document (Certificate of Analysis) that's attached to the ASN / Ship Notice cXML message. More complex process a part Quality Collaboration would require additional cXML messages to be sent. Yes Batch Required Flag Flag to specify if Batch Information is required on the ASN. Depending on the material, this information could include BatchID, ExpiryDate, ProductionDate or UseByDate. This may also impact the ASN structure as different material Batches / BatchIDs are usually split into sperate ASN Lines when sent on a single ASN. Yes Purchase Order Attachments Attachments on POs are commonly utilized in specific industries. The two common types of suppliers that utilize attachments are; • Packaging Suppliers: Labeling and information that needs to be on the box of the end product (For example; Pharmaceutical or Health products). • Parts Suppliers: it's utilized in combination with the material revision ID. Attachments would be additional documentation, specifications, product drawings and dimensions that would be needed by the supplier to manufacture. Yes -- 1 of 10 -- 12 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice As we go through each of the documents within the PO Collaboration process, we will be using an example of a Grocery Store (Buyer) purchasing cartons of Milk from their largest Milk Supplier. Cartons of Milk will be delivered by the Supplier to each of the Buyer’s Distribution Warehouses based on the Purchase Order. The Buyer then internally transfers the Milk to each of their store locations daily. This should help with visualizing how different technical aspects within the cXML documents can affect the process in the real world when it comes to Supply Chain. If you prefer, you can apply the same scenario for Oat Milk instead. Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts -- 2 of 10 -- 13 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag As per a Standard Purchase Order to Invoice process, the Buyer has sent a Purchase Order from their ERP to the Integrated Supplier via the SAP Business Network. The Supplier received the PO into their ERP and converted it into their internal Sales Order to start processing the order. The PO was for 550 2 Liter Cartons (EA) of Milk The Supplier was expecting this demand of quantity for this location. A month prior to receiving the PO the Buyer and Supplier had Collaborated on the Forecast of Orders via the Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 14 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Upon review of the Purchase Order the Supplier had identified that the ShipTo location for this Order is for the Buyer’s Distribution Centre. It’s an extremely large Distribution Centre (DC101) and has multiple entrances that lead to different storage locations for specific goods. o Milk must be constantly refrigerated so delivery must go to storageLocation ”C” at this Distribution Centre (DC101). o If you were using the example of Oat Milk. The Buyer may want it delivered to StorageLocation “A” as refrigeration is not needed. The Purchase Order would reflect this requirement using the ShipTo and StorageLocation. It is critical this information is captured by the Supplier’s ERP so it can be informed to their carrier for this shipment to ensure the full delivery is correct. Note: Depending on the Buyer, ShipTo locations to them could mean a Production Plant, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store Front Location and would generally differ depending on the industry. -- 4 of 10 -- 15 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Master Data Alignment It’s extremely important that the alignment of data between Buyer and Supplier is completed in addition to their integration, or on a regular basis as a part of their Business Relationship. This includes business specific information such as ShipTo / StorageLocation, BillTo, Material ID, UOM, Price ect... Within Supply Chain, there is a strong focus on Material level requirements, and business processes and logic based on each specific Material IDs. Any discrepancies lead to delayed materials that would impact the Buyer directly. If for example the shipTo and storage locations were not correctly aligned in the supplier’s system, delivery of goods may not have occurred, impacting available Milk for an entire city / region. -- 5 of 10 -- 16 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag For this specific DC Location, the Buyer would send Weekly orders for Milk every Thursday to the Supplier. If they received all 5500 cartons of Milk on Friday at the Distribution Centre, they would use valuable warehouse space to hold all the cartons until sold. Instead, the Buyer requests the delivery of PO Line 10 throughout the week using 3 different Schedule Lines. From past consumer trends, the Buyer knows that Monday and Friday are the busiest days at the Grocery Store locations, so the majority of the 5500 Cartons are split between those two days and is reflected as such at the Schedule Line level on the PO. -- 6 of 10 -- 17 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario - PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Scheduled Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Control Keys and and Tolerances can be defined at either the vendor, plant and/or material level. When sent on the PO they supersede the related supplier transactional rules. o The Buyer requires both OC and ASN to be sent for the Purchase Order to ensure accurate delivery information. o As noted, the Buyer’s DC space is limited so the upper limited of delivered quantities is 10%. o There is no allowed tolerance on Delivery Date as it’s vital that there is enough milk for specific days. It’s also to ensure the freshest possible Milk for the end customers and limit any spoilage. In combination with the scheduled lines and Material level tolerances, the Buyer has a lean Supply Chain that’s able to cater to all customers in the City on a weekly basis. Note: If for this specific material the Tolerance was outside of the agreed percentage causing the documents to fail (OC / ASN), this tolerance would need to be amended by the Buyer within their ERP and Change Order sent with the updated tolerance at the line level. -- 7 of 10 -- 18 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag o For food related Suppliers and Buyers, Lots / Batches are commonly documented by both the Buyer and Supplier. This is normally referred to as Batch Managed Materials. Batch Information is provided on the ASN for the shipped quantity. If there is a recall of Milk both parties know exactly what stores and locations are affected. o In accordance with local regulations, regular testing of the Milk is required. The Supplier is also aware of this Business requirement, so for this specific PO it’s flagged internally for testing and prepares the required Analysis documentation for the Quality Collaboration process. o To ensure that Buyer Distribution Centre (DC101) can efficiently unpack and receive the Milk delivery on the day, the Buyer requires Handling Unit / Packaging Information sent on the Ship Notice, this will detail in the cXML how the goods are shipped within the truck along with the order weight & dimensions. -- 8 of 10 -- 19 SCC PO cXML Examples / Comparison Purchase Order Line Example including; § Control Keys § Schedule Lines, § Handling Unit Flag § Quality Flag § Batch Managed Material Flag For the full comparison of an Indirect and SCC Purchase Order, please refer excel previously shared within the shared drive. -- 9 of 10 -- 20 Order Confirmation -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 21 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation The Order Confirmation provides the Buyer with an indication of what to expect and when. This is particularly important for materials that are relevant for material requirements planning (MRP) in the ERP because data in the Order Confirmation impacts the planning for that material. o Due to this, there are often a heavy focus on ensuring that provides the latest status via the Order Confirmation regardless of if the Purchase Order has already been confirmed. In turn this may result in multiple PO versions and Order Confirmations. In SCC many Buyer’s have implemented Supply Chain Monitor and Order Confirmation with Approval. This monitoring feature sits within the Buyer’s SAP Business Network Account and allows the Buyer to respond to Order Confirmations from their Suppliers. If the Supplier Confirms the Purchase Order outside the agreed tolerance for quantity, price, or delivery date, an Order Confirmation Deviation Approval feature enables the Buyer to review the confirmation deviation and decide whether to approve or reject the Order Confirmation. Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice -- 1 of 10 -- 22 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation Approval Flow Example Order Confirmation Approval is only in scope for specific SCC Buyers. Please be aware it’s common for SCC Buyer’s to deploy this functionality as a part of their SCC solution. For Hybrid Buyers that have both SCC and Indirect Suppliers under the same SAP Business Network Buyer account, only Order Confirmations for SCC Direct POs will trigger the approval flow. -- 2 of 10 -- 23 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Order Confirmation Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice Milk Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts -- 3 of 10 -- 24 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Order Confirmation Order Confirmation 1 (New)  Accept  Schedule Line reference The Milk Supplier has since processed the PO and is ready to confirm supply. As they were expecting this demand, they have enough Milk stock to ship as per the schedule lines on the PO. The OC was automictically approved by the Buyer as it’s all within OC tolerance. Order Confirmation 2 (Update)  Accept with Quantity Change  Schedule Line reference Unfortunately, the morning of delivery a 3 pallets of Milk cartons had fell over in the Supplier’s Warehouse and they are not able to meet the expected demand for Friday. The Supplier Creates an additional OC (Update) to notify the buyer with a new delivery quantity of 50 instead. As this is outside of Tolerance, the OC is sent for approval. The OC is approved by the Buyer and a Change Order with the new Quanty is sent. Supplier Confirms (Update) the Change Order before the warehouse starts packing the goods. Order Confirmation 3 (Update)  Accept  Schedule Line reference -- 4 of 10 -- 25 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation Over the coming month, an additional SI Training session will by lead by my colleague Isabelle. • This session will go into detail Order Confirmation logic and key considerations when confirming / requesting changes at the Schedule Line level for Integrated Suppliers. Today’s focus was to understand the Importance of the Order Confirmation and its practical use in the Supply Chain. Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice -- 5 of 10 -- 26 Advanced Ship Notice -- 6 of 10 -- 27 SCC PO Collaboration – Advanced Ship Notice Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice The ASN within SCC extends its current use to provide extra detail about the Shipped Quantity before it’s physically received by the Buyer’s Plant / Distribution Centre. This allows the Buyer’s warehouse to receipt the goods with reference to the ASN, thus automatically populating the details from the cXML ASN (IBD – In bound Delivery). o If the the ASN is not sent, the Buyer warehouse would have to check received stock and manually document the information into their own system to create the IBD internally. Batch Information is commonly utilized in many industries and includes additional for the shiped products such as BatchID, expiryDate, productionDate and Buyer batchID(Subcon). o For certain industries serialID for finished good may be used instead, or a GTIN / Barcode ID as an additional identifier for consumer products. Certificate Of Analysis (Quality Attachment) used by Buyer’s to ensure stock is periodically checked by Suppliers and meets certain industry standards before it’s shipped to the Buyer’s location. Handling Units / Packaging Information Provides the Buyer with a detailed packing structure of the goods being shipped on the ASN. This includes the SSCC ID of the Handling Units / Packages, Level of packing used (Pallet > Boxes > Goods), and the dimensions & weight for each of the packages. -- 7 of 10 -- 28 SCC PO Collaboration – Advanced Ship Notice Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice Technical Acknowledgments: For SCC Suppliers Integrating ASNs it’s extremely important that the Technical Acknowledgment (StatusUpdate) cXML message is enabled and integrated by the supplier. Majority of information sent on the ASN is not validated on the Business Network, but rather the Buyer’s Warehouse System so unless the the supplier checks each ASN history for each ASN or is setup to receive email notifications from the network to check, it’s incredibly difficult for the supplier to full visibility of their ASN status. Handling Units: An additional Training session will be designated to the structure of the ASNs with Handling Units / Packaging. -- 8 of 10 -- 29 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Advanced Ship Notice Milk Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice -- 9 of 10 -- 30 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Advanced Ship Notice Ship Notice 1 Quantity 50 • Single Batch Packaging • 1 Pallets > Crates Certificate of Analysis (Attached) The Supplier is now ready to Pick and Pack the Order before it’s shipped to the Buyer DC(101) As per the Change Order Friday’s Schedule quantity is now 50 instead of 200. The Milk is normally packed into re- usable crates and loaded onto a pallet supporting 50 cartons. • Certificate of Analysis is completed for this shipment of 50 and attached as a PDF to the cXML ASN. cXML ASN is sent via the SAP Business Network and received by the Buyer’s ERP successfully. The Buyer’s system automatically creates an IBD (Inbound Delivery Note) ready for the actual receiving of goods. Supplier Receives the cXML Technical Acknowledgement from the Buyer’s system that Ship Notice was successfully. Technical Acknowledgment (From Buyer) “ShipNotice 1 Accepted – IBD created.” -- 10 of 10 --

Technical Acknowledgment (From Buyer) “ShipNotice 2 Accepted – IBD created.” -- 1 of 10 -- 32 Goods Receipt & Invoice -- 2 of 10 -- 33 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – GR & Invoice Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice Both the GR and Invoice function in similar aspect to Indirect projects. • Please remember that depending on the Buyer there may be a Business Requirement to reference either the ShipNotice or Goods Receipt on the Invoice. For specific SCC processes, the Goods Receipt Message will contain additional information regarding the received goods for example, Supplier or Buyer Batch Information and may be useful for the Supplier to integrate as part of their process. -- 3 of 10 -- 34 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Final Comments These examples today are common scenarios with PO Collaboration based off first-hand experience with different Buyers and Suppliers from various industries. The scenario discussed today was for only a single supplier, plant and material ID. Please consider that it takes many individual suppliers and materials to supply a large country wide Grocery Store. Please note this not information that you have to know about your Buyer and Supplier. But you only need to understand how their processes within their Supply Chain transfers onto the cXML that we see in the Network. Buyers and suppliers will each have their own flavor of Supply Chain so as a Supplier Integrator it’s important discuss and document with your Buyer any specific requirements they have as a part of their Supply Chain process via the SAP Business Network. o These are business requirements that can not be assumed from just looking at the cXML file. file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 1 INTERNAL ONLY SCC / Indirect Cross Training Purchase Order Collaboration - PO Structure -- 1 of 10 -- 2 Agenda 01 Purchase Order Collaboration PO - Some differences at a quick glance 02 SCC PO Consideration03 cXML Examples Purchase Order Flow04 -- 2 of 10 -- 3 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration Purchase Order Order Confirmation Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice / Line Level Credit This document focuses on the Purchase Order structure for SCC Purchase Order Collaboration. o Other SCC Processes will have different requirements, fields and detail that is passed on the Purchase Order for the respective SCC process it’s a part of. o Please remember that when other SCC Processes are also in scope, the Purchase Order is often not the start of the procurement flow and other documents may be transacted (Integrated or Portal) before the PO even is sent to the Supplier. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 Purchase Order - Some differences – a quick glance Indirect SCC Buyer Part ID Usually optional. Mostly Supplier Part Ids are used. Free text Pos are also possible Used by Buyer and supplier as main identifier of the materials. Free text Pos are not used. Bill To , Ship To and Storage Locations Usually the buyer locations are head quarters / offices or delivery is indicted directly to the employee Each Buyer location has a unique identification code at the plant / shipTo level. For large plants or warehouses, the shipTo location may have designated locations where the Supplier / Carrier must deliver to once at the plant / warehouse location. For example; an order of vaccines can only be delivered to storage location “A” as it’s medical related. Batch Ids Not commonly utilized Used to identify specific production lots Revisions and Drawing numbers Not commonly utilized Used to identify different versions of product specifications Schedule Lines Not used. Usually the parent PO line is used. The PO Line is the parent of the Schedule lines Control Keys Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules Tolerances ( as per control keys ) date and quantity Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Used all the time Blanket Pos In use Not part of the scope Catalogues In use Not part of the scope. All material master data is locally stored by buyer and supplier -- 4 of 10 -- 5 SCC PO cXML Examples / Comparison Purchase Order Line Example including; § Control Keys § Schedule Lines, § Handling Unit Flag § Quality Flag § Batch Managed Material Flag For the full comparison of an Indirect and SCC Purchase Order, please refer to the excel below. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC Specific Considerations on the Purchase Order SCC Flow Material / Plant Specific Revision ID Provides and indicator for both buyers and supplier to help identify the part version needing to be produced. New revisions may have accompanying design specifications sent as an attachment on the Purchase Order. Material Specific Control Keys Document Instructions and tolerances supersede what is defined at the supplier group level. Control keys and tolerances are defined by the Buyer’s ERP and would need to be altered there if there are conflicting keys or tolerances set for the OC or ASN. Yes Purchase Order Schedule Lines This provides a delivery schedule that the supplier would need to adhere to when supplying the requested goods. The OC confirming the Delivery date would need to include each of the scheduled lines for PO Line 10. Normally the ASN Shipments would be split as per schedule line. Please Note: Date-Time Timestamp & UOM must match exactly when it's returned on the Order Confirmation. Quantity tolerance is per case. Yes Handling Unit Flag PO Flag that specifies if Handling Unit Information is Required on the ASN for this specific material. This is a material level flag and may not apply to all materials within the supplier's scope. The material Master Data must be aligned between the Buyer and Supplier as this requirement could also differ between Buyer plant / locations as well. Yes Quality Process Flag Certain Materials require additional certification documentation or must follow an additional quality process flow. Commonly this in the form of a PDF document (Certificate of Analysis) that's attached to the ASN / Ship Notice cXML message. More complex process a part Quality Collaboration would require additional cXML messages to be sent. Yes Batch Required Flag Flag to specify if Batch Information is required on the ASN. Depending on the material, this information could include BatchID, ExpiryDate, ProductionDate or UseByDate. This may also impact the ASN structure as different material Batches / BatchIDs are usually split into sperate ASN Lines when sent on a single ASN. Yes Purchase Order Attachments Attachments on POs are commonly utilized in specific industries. The two common types of suppliers that utilize attachments are; • Packaging Suppliers: Labeling and information that needs to be on the box of the end product (For example; Pharmaceutical or Health products). • Parts Suppliers: it's utilized in combination with the material revision ID. Attachments would be additional documentation, specifications, product drawings and dimensions that would be needed by the supplier to manufacture. What is the purpose of the training and organization 02 SCC and Indirect Some general aspects 03 SCC Complexity Buyer and Supplier Complexity Examples 04 Direct Purchase Order Collaboration Indirect and SCC differences 05 Next steps Next Session Info -- 2 of 10 -- 3 Training purpose and Info -- 3 of 10 -- 4 ▪ All sessions will be recorded ▪ All materials presented or offered before/after sessions will be made available ▪ Location of all materials will be communicated later on ▪ Sessions will cover : methodology, procedures, business aspects, SBN functional topics and technical ▪ We aim for approximately 10 sessions followed by a Q&A Training purpose SCC Process in scope SI type Activity - as per SCC DD and methodology Outcome Purchase Order Collaboration Buy Side Education of the Buyer SIFL resource for SCC SI methodology ( includes buyer consultation ) Able to articulate / educate Buyer team / SIFL and /or internal teams on SCC methodology Purchase Order Collaboration with Order Confirmation Flow ASN with Handling Units Buy Side Guidelines creation - new Able to create / review/ revise / update SCC Guidelines OC Deviations , Tolerances , OC with Delivery lines reference , Invoices with ASN / GR reference Guideline update / modification Sell Side SCC SI project activities, calls, notes Able to conduct SCC SI projects as per SCC methodology Today’s session is meant to be an intro, a first step -- 4 of 10 -- 5 Indirect and SCC -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC • Purchased materials are directly part of the produced finished goods and the production process • Direct and critical impact in the production lines / finished goods / distribution / logistics • Buyers have multiple Locations / Plants with different scope flavors - impacting Scope, timelines, Go lives strategies • Multiple SCC processes covering different parts of production, manufacturing, planning, etc • Each buyer implements different combinations of the SCC processes • Buyers and suppliers have different teams/ procedures / materials etc per each SCC process Indirect • Purchased materials are not part of the produced finished goods • No direct impact on the production lines / finished goods • Buyer Locations have more impact when Invoices are in scope • One single Process Some differences – a quick glance Consultancy mindset & Pro- active approach -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Context: 2 Solutions Providing different value propositions and addressing different business work streams and requirements for our customers Supply Chain Collab ✓ Increasing visibility along the supply chain enabling margin growth and Inventory stock levels optimization. ✓ Enabling Business Transformation and driving operational excellence by optimizing manufacturing and asset performance and elevating product quality ✓ Business Critical operations Indirect Procurement ✓ Enabling control and monitoring allowing the Buyers to standardize their indirect procurement operations. ✓ Reducing error handling enabling faster invoice reconciliation and cash flow optimization Over 35 SCC processes combinations and 100+ document types variants One set of documents with approx 5+ types variances Specific Indirect : - Buyer Org and resources - Buyer internal procedures - Buyer compliance message - Buyer Supplier communication - Buyer Flight plan Specific SCC : - Buyer Org/resources and internal procedures, business and logistic requirements (+flavors per buyer location) - Buyer compliance message - Buyer Supplier communication and change management - Buyer Flight plan & Supplier segmentation per SCC process and per Buyer location Where ? Official list of all SCC processes and documents per each together with the availability in multiple file formats: Standard B2B Formats on SAP Integration Suite managed gateway.xlsx -- 7 of 10 -- 8 What are the Criteria that impact the effort/project plan/timeline of the BUYER and Suppliers during the entire project ? Change management and Business Transformation ▪ Change management is CRITICAL to the success of the project ▪ SCC projects have a critical Transformation Added Value within the Buyer and Supplier organizations. ▪ Day to day operations are changed / optimized and/or completely renewed ▪ We have noticed that the change management activities deeply impact a project timeline and require multiple resources on both BUYER and Supplier side Number of BUYER Plants in scope ▪ It is very usual that SCC buyers have multiple Locations in scope ▪ From our experience we noticed that it is very often that different flavors of business/logistic requirements are in scope Per Each Buyer Location ▪ Please note that Buyer / Supplier SIT/UAT testing needs to be done per each Buyer Location in conjunction with each SCC process in scope Number of SCC Processes in scope ▪ A Buyer may have in scope one ( e.g. Po collab ) or more processes ( e.g. SMI, Po Collab, Forecast Collab ,etc ) at the same time. ▪ From our experience we noticed that each SCC process has on the Buyer side different requirements that need to be designed/mapped and tested separately ▪ The more processes are in scope the larger the timeline SCC Business Scope Buyer locations Change management Number of Document type per SCC Process in scope ▪ The buyer may chose to implement a certain number of documents per SCC process or all. ▪ Impact in the number of needed mappings and the timeline ▪ Buyer may have internal requirements/ technical limitations that dictate his choice -- 8 of 10 -- 9 SCC Projects – Supplier integration – One glance Buyer Dedicated resources for supplier Integration Buyer SIFL resource as part of standard SCC DD Buyer SIFL resource is not technical and is leading the supplier integration project Supplier interest in supplier Integration approach Due to strategic collaboration with the buyer suppliers often pursue themselves the integration project and have internal commitment for resources and necessary budgets SCC Direct impact – day to day operations Supplier and Buyer resources Buyer Interest / commitment / strategy About 60 to 70% of SCC Buyers come to the network already having a plan/pipeline for integrated suppliers. Usually the strategic suppliers are pilots Buyer compliance message 60 to 70% of SCC Buyers have the necessary leverage to deliver strict compliance messaging to their suppliers Buyer internal interest Change management and Business Transformation About 70 to 90% of SCC Buyers implement /deploy completely NEW Business scope / processes/ requirements as part of an SBN project. New scope may come as part of : ✓ New / legacy Buyer locations / regions ✓ S4 projects / migrations from other back-end systems ✓ Buyer Internal business requirements Strategic impact within the buyer organization Critical impact in day to day operations. Buyers are committed and treat each supplier as an individual project that is basically a mini version if the Buyer deployment project with average durations of 6 moths to 1 year or more depending on scope complexity 1 2 Critical Business Transformation projects 90% of SCC Buyers / partners have the wrong expectation that change management for new Business scope/requirements is covered by the technical deployment project / SAP, both on buyer and supplier side -- 9 of 10 -- 10 SCC Complexity -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Training Session 2 SCC.content: SCC Indirect Cross training – Session 2 SCC Supplier Integration Roles and responsibilities Name, SAP Business Network May, 2026 -- 1 of 10 -- All sessions will be recorded All materials presented or offered before/after sessions will be made available Sessions will cover : methodology, procedures, business aspects, SBN functional topics and technical We aim for approximately 10 sessions followed by a Q&A Training purpose Location of all materials : And in the On24 application as part of the sessions – access is provided individually after you register Please note that all materials are MANDATORY and INTERNAL -- 2 of 10 -- Focus for today What we aim to cover ? Session 1 covered more business aspects impacting the projects Today’s session will focus on SAP SCC Methodology General aspects valid for both Buy – side and Sell Side More focus on the Sell-side activities What is Buyer Solution Deployment ? SCC Buyer dedicated roles Responsibilities of Buyer, Supplier and SAP Supplier Integration KO CALL and general process Please note that Buy – Side activities and methodology ( including Buyer Integration SCC KO call ) will not be covered today . A separate session will be dedicated to this subject. Have in mind the bigger picture – facilitating continuous Adoption and project growth ( adopting new SCC processes for example ) is the target -- 3 of 10 -- SCC Buyer Solution Deployment Services Include SAP Roles like : Delivery Executive and Product Expert along side Buyer Integrator SCC Enablement Deployment Description Stipulates that : - Buyer needs to have Dedicated resources for Supplier Enablement and Supplier Integration - Supplier Integration ( and Enablement ) are driven by the Buyer resources - Pilot suppliers are pre-defined : maximum 7 for portal and maximum 3 for Supplier integration - Supplier Integration KO call is lead by the Buyer resources – Buyer SIFL ( not by the SAP SI ) End to End testing is lead by the Buyer SIFL ( SAP SI is only covering initial technical testing ) Due to business/ operational impact the buyer is deeply involved and driving the process Most suppliers using Supplier Managed Gateway Change management should be aligned between buyer and supplier BEFORE starting the actual supplier integration Indirect Buyer Solution Deployment involves the SAP Buyer Integrator There are no dedicated and official Buyer resources for supplier Integration SAP SI is usually driving the Supplier Integration SAP SI is usually trying to advertise the advantages of supplier integration SAP SI leads the Supplier Integration KO call Usually SAP SI is driving end to end testing between Buyer and supplier More focus on buyer hands-off approach More suppliers using legacy connection -- 4 of 10 -- Buyer Solution Deployment What is a Deployment Description and why it is important ? -- 5 of 10 -- Buyer Solution Deployment defines the full Buyer Scope in SAP Business Network (SBN) – across business, operational, logistic, functional, and technical dimensions. It outlines how the buyer will use SBN and applies uniformly to all suppliers – portal and integrated suppliers. For example, if Purchase Orders weren’t inlcluded in the Buyer Solution, no supplier – integrated or portal – will receive them via SBN. The Buyer Solution acts as the foundation for all supplier interactions on the Network. The Buyer Solution Design Document captures the entire Buyer Scope on SBN, covering both the buyer’s back-end systems and how these are integrated with SBN. It serves as the source of truth for both portal training materials and Supplier Integration Guidelines. For more detailed information, consult your SCC deployment description. What is Buyer Solution Deployment/Implementation? -- 6 of 10 -- IDoc or proxy Native connection Pre-defined mappings & customizations cXML cXML Translation CXML or EDI Supplier Managed Gateway Buyer Managed Gateway Buyer Solution Deployment Supplier Message Flow And Translation Points for Integrated (B2B) Documents Buyer’s ERP Supplier’s ERP Supplier Managed Gateway for Spend & Network does not “touch” the supplier’s internal back-end systems. For inbound documents (e.g., PO), the supplier provides a URL endpoint to receive files in real time. For outbound documents (e.g., ASN), the supplier prepares the file according to BUYER* Seller Integration Guidelines. Buyer Managed Gateway and Supplier Managed Gateways do not perform the same functionalities. If Buyer uses SAP – Buyer Managed Gateway will act as an out of the box product and includes Services with pre-defined duration as per purchased licenses -- 7 of 10 -- 01 SAP roles included in the SCC Buyer Solution Deployment Services, and only during purchased period : Delivery Executive, Product Exert centre of excellence ), BI, Functional / Technical Consultant 02 SAP Roles included in the Embedded Services : NxLs ( digital or none in some cases ), Sis ( Buy side and sell side ), CSM ( as per case ) 03 In SCC The Buyer resources are driving the Supplier Integration projects. file://SBN/split/Training Session 2 SCC.content: Seller Integration - Participating Roles Who are the key players that have a mandatory role in the integration project? -- 1 of 10 -- The same contact may take on multiple roles Assists in troubleshooting document failure on BUYER* side back-end system. Attend supplier calls as needed. Performs data mapping or modifications on BUYER* side back-end system if needed (on case by case basis). Provides technical details for the integration to BUYER* back-end systems Together with the BUYER* SIFL organizes the regular calls with the suppliers . Reviews and confirms test plan per supplier. Attends supplier calls as needed. Generates test documents. Downloads & validates applicable test transactions; load & process through ERP. Assists in other testing activities, coordinate go-live The main contact for supplier integration project coordination within Customer organization and with the suppliers. Participates in Customer enablement meetings, drives kick-off and regular status calls for supplier integration projects, creates custom reporting. Creates and approves Identified Supplier communications, education content and project plan Participates in Customer requirements gathering and Customer design workshops. Supports Internal Customer training sessions needed for the seller integration project as well with the integrated suppliers themselves. Reinforces Solution compliance with Identified Integrated Supplier and internal Customer department stakeholder as part of the change management program. Participates in the Customer User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and drives the individual end to end testing within the supplier integration projects. Conducts enablement related activities in the SAP Business network and Customer back-end system. Obtains supplier’s commitment for project Scope and Timeline. Coordinates, during pilot phase, internal activities with the Functional Lead to facilitate the project progress. Coordinates, during pilot phase, with the Technical Lead if technical issues from integration supplier testing require trouble soothing. Coordinates with Customer’s purchasing department to address Integrated Suppliers that are not following agreed upon integration Testing Contact -- 2 of 10 -- BUYER* SIFL - Activities - general overview - Project holistic activities Please note that we can not estimate all the activities needed on the BUYER* side since each Buyer project represents a specific case. file://SBN/split/What is Buyer and Suppl.content: 1 SCC Supplier Integration INTERNAL What is Buyer SCC SI KO call and SCC SI Supplier KO call -- 1 of 6 -- 2 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What is it? • As part of the SCC Buyer SE call the SI part should be an Introduction to Seller Integration in general – focused on SCC SI methodology and Buyer dedicated resources/responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description • It should NOT be a Technical presentation • Buyer SCC SI KO call is done per each buyer scope/case • Buyer SI ko call is NOT a technical call • It is means to Introduce the SCC Seller Integration methodology to the buyer’s team, including the Buyer dedicated role and its responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description (Please see the related screenshot below from Deployment Description) • It should continue the message that was delivered during the buyer SE KO call either by our NxL colleagues, DE or, if there was an Intro session, directly by the SCC SI • The Buyer SI KO call is supposed to mark the moment when the Buyer will start to work/commit/start consider seller integration as part of his entire project • During the call the SCC SI will present the seller integration methodology/best practices to the team of the buyer • KO call is done per each supplier in scope for SCC integration and will reflect the specific relation of that specific supplier with the buyer • Supplier SCC SI KO is NOT a technical call • Ko call represents the official start of the integration project for that specific supplier Pre-condition: buyer SIFL should have already discussed and agreed with the supplier on the Business change management / Business requirements / SCC processes in scope (and document types per process) per each buyer Location / Plant When? • When a buyer is interested to know more about supplier Integration but does not have a definitive commitment to start it, does not have allocated resources to the Si part, is confused on what supplier integration is. • Usually in the Explore phase of New Buyer Deployments but it is possible that the interest of the buyer appears in different stages and / or after the completion of the initial Go live • When a buyer already has a declared interest / commitment to start the SCC SI part • Buyer should already have a dedicated buyer SIFL resource allocated Usually in the Explore phase of New Buyer Deployments but it is possible that the interest of the buyer appears in different stages and / or after the completion of the initial Go live • For each Supplier Pilot • For each supplier in the run phase -- 2 of 6 -- 3 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session - consultation Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call How is the KO call slide deck created per each buyer project? • Buyer ko call deck is updated (from the general template) per each buyer case/scope • We should start with the general standard slides and customize per buyer scope / case • Customizations/adaptations; add the logo of the buyer, remove / add SCC processes / documents that are in scope (based on whatever information is available to the SI at that point in time). Consult with NxL, DE and COE involved with the buyer to obtain any information available at the time • Buyer KO call deck is adapted per each buyer scope / case • We should start with the general standard slides and customize/ adapt per buyer • Customizations/adaptations; add the logo of the buyer, remove / add SCC processes / document’s types that are in scope (based on whatever information is available to the SI at that point in time) etc. It is critical for a successful approach to adapt as per the case of the buyer and focus during the session on what seems to be more fitted: buyer role / responsibilities, methodology, expectations, scope, change management, etc. • Buyer SIFL has the responsibility to create the needed documentation / decks - general and adapted per each supplier case / scope • SBN SCC SI – usually offers best practices as part of the SCC SI methodology sessions Typical duration 1 hour Can be reduced to less according to case / time available etc. 1 hour Please note that multiple sessions may be needed on a case-by-case basis 1 hour (but multiple sessions may be needed on a case-by- case basis) -- 3 of 6 -- 4 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What is the aim of the call? At the end of the call the buyer’s team should know that: • There is something called Seller Integration that needs to be included in the general project plan in the Buyer wishes to have it in scope • That Seller integration might impact their timelines / targets What are the dependencies between buyer Solution Deployment and the Seller Integration part • The Buyer is responsible for allocating dedicated resources that will take ownership of the responsibilities mentioned in the SCC Deployment Description • That a separate call will be organized to get in detail and they should expect it Recommendation: ask buyer if they are comfortable to record the session. Buyer team should archive the recording for internal KT sessions At the end of the call the team of the Buyer should be clear on the following points: • what is SCC supplier integration • what is the difference between a supplier working on the portal and an integrated supplier • enablement for integrated suppliers, who do what, integration and portal work are possible for the same supplier. • what resources are needed from buyer side and what are the responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description • what are integration guidelines, why they are needed and when they are created • what is the process that is followed together with the buyer’s team for each supplier. • best practices Important: the buyer should be clear that it is their responsibility to discuss and agree with the supplier on the business scope AND the Change Management part (ideally before the supplier ko call) Recommendation: ask buyer if they are comfortable to record the session. Buyer team should archive the recording for internal KT sessions 1. Buyer SIFL and supplier team Review and re-confirm the scope of the project based on the individual business relation between BUYER and SUPPLIER • Business change management / Business requirements / SCC processes in scope (and document types per process) per each buyer Location/Plant • From these documents, are there some that are completely new (change management)? • Also, from these documents some will be handled in the portal, and some will be integrated? which are the actual documents in scope of the integration? • Locations on buyer and supplier that we have in scope 2. Define the roles and contacts involved (buyer and supplier) 3. Buyer SIFL has the responsibility to Review and agree/commit the supplier to project scope, timeline and start moment 4. Discuss about the testing approach as per Business requirements and business cases 5. Agree on the regular calls 6. Agree on the next steps 7. At the end of the call buyer and supplier need to be crystal clear and completely in sync on the business scope, the integration scope, the portal scope, the change management and timelines -- 4 of 6 -- 5 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What should be the next step? The next step should be: • Buyer team to allocate necessary resources SAP SCC SI organizes the separate Buyer SI KO call Please note that it does happen often that Buyers do not follow/ respond/restart discussions after such an Intro call. From experience/lessons learned we have noticed that buyers requesting Intro calls (information calls) are not really interested in suppliers, are not in a position to allocate resources, do not have budgets/internal buy in or have other situations that prevent them to commit/start a seller integration at that moment in time. The next steps should be: • Buyer SIFL and SCC SI agree on following regular sessions to review in details SCC methodology and best practices, Buyer Scoping file, SCC SI guidelines creation, Please note that it is possible to Buyer will change the buyer resources and there will be a need to repeat the buyer KO call session multiple times The next steps should be: • Buyer SIFL should set in place the regular project management calls • SCC SI usually agrees with the supplier on the technical call or calls • It is possible that sometimes SCC SI has one technical intro with the supplier team prior to the o call – just to give a macro image on the cXML and HTTPS connection for example. Owner/ organizer NxL/DE - usually informs SCC SI manager of the interest of the buyer NxL/DE usually facilitate the session – this may vary per case SCC SI will drive the presentation / session and provide notes NxL/DE - usually informs SCC SI manager of the interest of the buyer NxL/DE may facilitate the session or just introduce the SCC SI to the buyer team/resources – this may vary per case SCC SI will drive the presentation/session and provide notes Buyer SIFL will drive the call and take notes – as per RACI mentioned in the SCC Deployment Description Buyer SIFL should inform the SCC SI prior to the call and provide the Scoping file agreed with the supplier -- 5 of 6 -- 6 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call Mandatory participant resources Buyer resources: Technical, business, decision makers, Buyer Service provider SAP SBN resource: SI and the NDL/DE optional CSM and COE according to each case Note: the SCC SI is not necessarily the same resource that will actually take over the project. At this moment in time the Buyer is not yet committed to the SI part, so we allocate a resource that is available for a one-time session Buyer Resource: SIFL Optional: Buyer technical, business, decision makers, Buyer Service provider SBN SCC SI resource: SCC SI and the NDL/DE Optional: CSM and COE according to each case Buyer SIFL and supplier team are mandatory in the call. Buyer Resource: Buyer SIFL, also Buyer Business resources are often a part of the call. Supplier Resource: Supplier Business and technical resources are required.
